groups.name: Elections & decision making
groups.question: Can people choose their representatives through genuinely competitive, well-run elections, and take binding collective decisions - at every level of government?

groups.name: Government & accountability
groups.question: Can democratically authorised institutions exercise their powers effectively, within appropriate limits, and be held answerable for doing so?

groups.name: Rule of law & justice
groups.question: Is public power exercised under known and predictable law, with independent adjudication and effective means to challenge wrongdoing and obtain redress?

groups.name: Rights, freedoms & civic space
groups.question: Can people exercise the freedoms necessary to participate in, criticise and challenge democratic power - and is there space to organise without unjustified interference?

groups.name: Information & public debate
groups.question: Can people obtain meaningful information about public affairs and encounter a genuinely plural range of political arguments without either state or private actors exercising unaccountable control over the information environment?

groups.name: Participation & civic life
groups.question: Are people able and willing to take part in political and civic life, and are the resources and opportunities to do so distributed on fair terms?

groups.name: Not a democracy story
groups.question: Items the classifier ruled out of scope: jobs, events, funding calls, logistics and general news.

items.h: Data and AI Public Engagement Community of Practice, 11 March
items.b: At 2pm next Wednesday, Connected by Data will be hosting the next meeting of the Data and AI Public Engagement network, focusing on the latest work and discussion on public participation and engagement around data and AI. Find out more.
Apply by 20 March: Head of External Affairs — Demos (£50,000)
items.sec: Featured Job Listings across the Democracy Sector

items.h: Baden-Württemberg citizens assemblies booming
items.b: In the German state of Baden-Württemberg, 10 of the 21 parties running in the March state elections are promising more citizens assemblies . Since 2011, following disputes around a major rail project, the state government has been practising what it calls ‘a policy of being heard’ focused on maximising dialogue-based participation formats — see more .
items.sec: And now for something completely different …
items.why: it is comparative evidence about how deliberative and direct-democracy machinery like citizens' assemblies is being expanded as a form of collective decision-making, relevant to UK debates on the same mechanisms
items.note: Citizens' assemblies are classified under elections & decision making per the framework's reassignment, treated here as comparative international evidence.
links: 10 of the 21 parties running in the March state elections are promising more citizens assemblies

items.h: Experimenting with paying young people for campaign contributions
items.b: During the 2021 elections Raise Your Voice (RYV), funded by the UK Democracy Fund, worked to amplify the voices of young people in Wales, educating and empowering them about the Senedd Election. RYV paid young people to create digital content on a range of topics, from calling for improved political education to sharing the experiences of young people of colour — take a look at their spoken word , podcasts and blogs .
items.why: a new programme was created to build young people's capacity and willingness to engage in an election, expanding the practical means of civic participation

items.b: Women deceived into relationships with spycops send clear message. As the delayed public inquiry into undercover policing proceeds, Police Spies Out of Lives hire a van to emblazon their message across Central London. The van parked up outside key venues, such as the inquiry venue, the Houses of Parliament, the Home Office, the RCJ and New Scotland Yard.
items.why: it concerns a public inquiry providing redress for state wrongdoing (undercover policing abuses), a mechanism for holding public power accountable under law
items.note: Public inquiry framed around redress rather than scrutiny is classified as rule of law & justice.

items.h: Democracy Drinks: Election Edition special event, tonight 20th June in London
items.b: It’s not too late to sign up for our special Democracy Drink: Election Edition event at the Wellcome Collection. This is a joint event with The Civic Power Fund and the Joseph Rowntree Reform Trust , and an opportunity for you to both share your work, updates and what you’ve achieved so far this election — and also an opportunity to let your hair down for a night with free drinks and nibbles.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
links: special Democracy Drink: Election Edition event

items.h: Did you miss TiCTEC — the world’s key conference on civic technology?
items.b: Don’t fret, mySociety , who host and organise the major conference on pro-democracy technology have published a full range of talks online via their YouTube .
items.note: Publishing conference talks online is organisational content promotion, not a new participation mechanism.

items.h: YouGov poll finds majority of Brits do not support votes for 16 and 17 year olds
items.b: Over half of Brits do not support extending the right to vote to 16 and 17 year olds, according to recent YouGov polling . In fact, Labour voters are the only group to overall support the policy (46% support vs 43% oppose), whilst 55% of Liberal Democrats, 83% of Conservatives and 85% of Reform voters oppose the change.
items.why: it reports public attitudes toward extending suffrage to 16 and 17 year olds, a core question of who is entitled to vote in UK elections

items.h: Democracy Network considers switching away from X/Twitter, launches new Comms WhatsApp Group
items.b: Adam Mendum, Comms Lead at the Democracy Network and Involve , is planning to host a conversation on what action others in the sector have taken, or are planning to take, if any, with respect to X and the recent riots. As part of this, Adam is promoting the Network’s new Democracy Amplifiers WhatsApp Group for comms leads and others in the sector to explore ways to collaborate, share skills, resources and ideas with one another — and have the conversation about switching away from X. So if you’re responsible for, or are interested in comms collaboration — join the group now .
items.sec: Reconsidering your use of Twitter / X?
items.note: This is internal sector comms organising, not a new mechanism affecting public participation or debate.

items.b: View the database here — Have we missed something? Add it here !

items.h: Government to postpone local elections in nine regions
items.b: Angela Rayner has delayed local elections in nine regions across England as the government develops their plans for devolution across the country. The one year delay was criticised by Conservative Party Shadow Minister Kevin Hollinrake however who said the ‘mass postponement’ was a ‘worrying day for democracy’. Democracy Club has run the numbers and says that the councils affected were due to elect 599 councillors, reducing the number up for election on 1 May by 26.6%. 1,657 council seats still remain up for grabs.
items.why: postponing local elections directly affects citizens' ability to choose representatives on a fixed timetable and reduces the number of councillors up for democratic mandate this cycle.
items.note: Local government electoral timing falls under elections & decision making per boundary rules.

items.h: New children’s book to excite children to consider their place in the world and politics
items.b: How to be a Revolutionary is a new book by BBC 6 Music journalist Lucy Ann Unwin . Set during a general election, the book starts with a child excited by the glossy red leaflets coming through the door, a quest to smile at strangers in a park and a curious team of rats leading a crew of passionate kids to inspire their school to change the world — one small step at a time. A book for the school library perhaps? See you next time,
items.sec: And now for something completely different…
links: How to be a Revolutionary is a new book by BBC 6 Music journalist Lucy Ann Unwin

items.h: Labour confirms plans to reform Mayor and PPC voting system with upcoming White Paper
items.b: At the Local Government Association conference earlier this month, government minister Jim McMahon suggested that the upcoming White Paper on Devolution will address the use of First Past the Post for electing Mayors and Police and Crime Commissioners. Labour for a New Democracy celebrated this ‘a small step in the right direction’, adding this should create further opportunities to engage with the government about First Past the Post at other elections.
items.why: changing the electoral system used to elect mayors and PCCs alters how votes translate into representation and political competition.
links: Labour for a New Democracy celebrated this

items.h: Labour MPs demand government leaves Musk’s X platform in leaked WhatsApp messages
items.b: Leaked messages show backbench MPs believe the government should ‘show direction to others in the UK’ by leaving X . MPs in the leaked Whatsapp group complain that they are still expected to share content on the platform, despite the fact that many in the group see X owner Elon Musk as a ‘fascist’ and that the platform’s AI tool, Grok, had put ‘children in harm’s way’.
items.why: government presence on a platform accused of spreading harmful AI-generated content bears on the plurality and safety of the public information environment.
items.note: Focus is on the information environment rather than an individual's speech rights, so filed under information & public debate.
links: Leaked messages show backbench MPs believe the government should ‘show direction to others in the UK’ by leaving X

items.h: Democracy Sausage
items.b: You can thank Trin Gong at Radix Big Tent for this one. Trin says in Australia it’s all about ‘democracy sausages’ at polling stations, rather than dogs. Whilst fundraising outside polling stations has apparently been on the go since the 1930s, hot sausage fundraising stands have apparently been going strong since the 1980s with the advent of the portable grill. On federal election day in 2016, Twitter even changed it’s emoji for #ausvotes to a piece of white bread topped by a sausage and red sauce!
Apply by May 18–31: Various roles available at Advocacy Academy
View current open grants and paid fellowships — Add a new grant or funding opportunity

items.h: New report in an upcoming series from IPPR suggests democracy needs major reform
items.b: IPPR have teamed up with Compass , ERS and Unlock Democracy to publish a major new report on the decline of democratic engagement in the UK. One of the key findings is that age and class have a significant impact on perceptions about whether democracy serves individuals well. The report is part of a new programme at IPPR focusing on democracy and justice, so keep an eye out for future updates about its development.
items.why: new research on how age and class shape perceptions of and engagement with democracy speaks to unequal conditions for civic participation.

items.b: This is your chance to let us know what you think about our work so far . Your feedback is really important to us — but there’s a twist. This time, we’re using pol.is — an online deliberation tool developed for open ended feedback from large groups of people. It is well suited to gathering organic, authentic feedback while retaining minority opinions. Find out more about Pol.is and how you can use it in your work. Take part in the survey.
items.note: Internal organisational feedback survey, not a public democratic mechanism, despite using a deliberative tool.
links: This is your chance to let us know what you think about our work so far

items.h: Climate and Nature Bill advanced in Parliament by Roz Savage MP
items.b: ​​The Climate and Nature Bill has been selected to advance the private members’ bill ballot in parliament. Unlike earlier presentations of the bill, it will now be allocated parliamentary time for reading and debate in the 2024–2025 session. The bill lays forth provisions for a citizens’ assembly to recommend measures for inclusion in an all-of-government strategy — See more via Zero Hour .
items.why: the bill would establish a citizens' assembly to feed into government strategy, creating new deliberative decision-making machinery.
items.note: Citizens' assembly provisions are classified under elections & decision making per the revised framework.

items.b: Apply by May 29: Programme Associate at People Powered ($60–74k)
items.note: Job advert, sector logistics.

items.h: Vote now for the annual Civility in Politics Awards
items.b: Returning for their second year, the Civility in Politics Awards shine a spotlight on the people working in politics who have shown the possibility of civil, thoughtful and reflective public debate that spans across political divides. The awards are judged in four categories, Politician of the Year, Bridge-Builders of the Year, Campaigner of the Year and The Daniel Stevenson Award. Shortlists will be announced in late December, with the awards themselves taking place in January. Nominate and vote now — voting closes 8th December.
items.note: Award nomination/voting is organisational admin, not a democratic mechanism.

items.h: Liberal Democrats write to Ofcom over BBC’s Reform UK coverage bias
items.b: The Liberal Democrats have written to Ofcom over what they claim is unfair and excessive coverage of Reform UK by the BBC. They took particular issue with the broadcaster’s coverage of a Reform UK press conference in which Farage announced his immigration policy, with coverage running all day on the BBC’s home and politics page. Best for Britain lodged a similar complaint over Sky News’ coverage of Reform’s press conference in early August.
items.why: a regulatory complaint over broadcaster coverage balance bears on whether the media environment gives voters a plural, undistorted view of competing parties
items.note: Focus is on broadcast impartiality/regulation rather than the electoral competition itself.
links: Best for Britain lodged a similar complaint

items.h: Directory of Social Change launches new Governance App
items.b: The new free platform helps you review and improve your organisation’s governance. You can use it to gather responses from your board, generate performance scores of your campaign or org, highlight differing views across the board and have targeted discussions about what’s going well and where to improve.
items.note: Tool is for internal organisational governance, not for public democratic participation.

items.h: Telegraph accuses UK Government of ‘trying to rig elections’ with Votes at 16
items.b: According to Telegraph journalists Ethan Croft and Ollie Corfe, the Labour Government is working to rig elections through the introduction of lowering the voting age. Read more (paywall).
items.why: changing the voting age directly alters the franchise and who can participate in choosing representatives

items.h: mySociety are providing three £5k grants to innovators and councils for new climate projects
items.b: To be eligible to bid for one of the grants, you must either be a council that wants to trial an idea, or an organisation that wants to work with a council to trial your project. Find out more about the climate partnership grants .
items.note: Funding call for climate innovation trials, not democratic participation infrastructure.
links: Find out more about the climate partnership grants

items.b: Irish far-right activity on Telegram has real life consequences. The Institute for Strategic Dialogue publishes a new report on the activity of the far-right on Irish Telegram and how this form of organising and propaganda distribution is impacting on real life in communities across Ireland.
items.note: Concerns Irish far-right activity with no stated bearing on UK democracy.

items.h: Local Government Association share their seven principles for safer canvassing
items.b: The guidance by the Local Government Association (LGA) sets out practical hints for canvassers during the pre-election period and is openly available on the LGA website . In addition, they have a range of other advice for councillors and councils on preventing and handling abuse and intimidation available through the LGA Civility in Public Life Hub — Would you like to know more?
items.why: guidance to keep canvassing safe protects candidates' and campaigners' practical ability to compete for votes during elections
links: Would you like to know more?

items.h: Northern Ireland elections deferred to 2023
items.b: The UK Government has pushed back fresh elections to the Northern Ireland assembly amid reports that a breakthrough has been found in the controversial Brexit arrangements that have caused the Democratic Unionist Party boycott of Stormont. NI Secretary Chris Heaton-Harris claims PM Sunak has overruled his authority and stepped in to take direct control after meetings between Rishi Sunak and Irish Taoiseach Michael Martin.
items.why: postponing scheduled assembly elections directly affects when and whether voters can renew their elected representatives
links: pushed back fresh elections to the Northern Ireland assembly

items.h: New Byline Times polling shows decline of mainstream news outlets
items.b: New polling by We Think for Byline Times shows that for most voters under 40, newspapers and broadcasters are no longer their main source of news. 52% of UK under 40s now say social media is their main source, with 25% specifically listing TikTok as their primary source of news. See the full Byline story here .
items.why: a shift away from traditional news outlets toward social media changes how citizens obtain information about public affairs and encounter political debate

items.h: Welcome to the post-election edition of the Democracy Bulletin,
items.b: This email is a weekly roundup of activities from across the democracy sector, including a summary of updates, job listings (at the bottom!), news and even the odd bit of gossip from our Thursday meetups . Please do share your ideas, feedback and any questions you might have about the Democracy Handbook, meetup and newsletter via our survey or send us an email . We’ve set up a new recurring calendar event for the Democracy Meetup, you can add it to your calendar here . You can also sub to a new wider UK Democracy Calendar which adds every event from the democracy sector to your calendar as the…

This week a coalition of civil society orgs urged the government to drop Voter ID. 17 organisations came together this week to urge the Prime Minister to abandon plans to implement Voter ID in upcoming elections.
items.why: this concerns voter identification requirements that affect who can exercise their franchise and how elections are administered.
links: abandon plans to implement Voter ID

items.b: Two new by-elections. By-elections are due to be held in Chesham and Amersham and Batley and Spen in coming months.
items.why: by-elections determine who holds representative office and give voters a fresh chance to choose their representatives.

items.b: Councillors across England renew calls to allow online meetings . As the emergency legislation ran out last week, online council meetings are no longer allowed. A high court action by Hertfordshire Council was rejected and the government pledges a consultation on the issue.
items.why: the legality of remote council meetings affects the functioning of local democratic decision-making structures.
items.note: Local government meeting procedures treated as decision-making machinery per boundary rule.

items.b: 2021 Chesham and Amersham by-election . Following the passing of local Conservative MP Cheryl Gillan early last month, a by-election will be held in the near future. The two main contenders for the South Bucks seat, the Lib Dems and Conservatives have selected their candidates, Sarah Green, and Peter Fleet.
items.why: candidate selection for a parliamentary by-election shapes voters' choice of representative.

items.b: By-election called for Batley and Spen. Tracy Brabin MP stands down to take up their new post as Mayor of West Yorkshire, triggering a by-election . Jo Cox’s sister Kim Leadbeater announces her aim to stand for Labour in the seat.
items.why: a triggered by-election and candidate announcement directly concern how a parliamentary seat is contested and filled.

items.b: Conservative Party refuses to sign joint pledge against abuse and intimidation of election candidates. In a rare intervention, the Committee on Standards in Public Life wrote a report detailing its “concern” at the government’s failure to respond to its earlier recommendations written in the wake of the murder of MP Jo Cox. The 2019 review made a range of recommendations to clean up politics and keep candidates safe, but two years later, the government still says it is considering the report.
items.why: the government's failure to act on standards recommendations shows a lack of accountability to independent oversight bodies meant to safeguard political conduct.
items.note: Standards in public life falls under government_accountability, though candidate safety also touches elections.

items.b: UK-wide elections break records for female representation and diversity. The Scottish election produced the most diverse parliament ever . Pam Duncan-Glancy becomes first wheelchair user elected to Holyrood. Natasha Asghar is the first woman of colour elected to the Senedd. Hina Bokhari, Marina Ahmad and Sakina Sheikh are the first female Muslim London Assembly Members . Jill Mortimer is the first female MP for Hartlepool. Tracy Brabin is the first female metro mayor . Liverpool elects Joanne Anderson, the UK’s first directly elected black female mayor .
items.why: the representativeness of elected institutions determines whether historically underrepresented groups can genuinely access democratic power.
links: first female Muslim London Assembly Members

items.b: Paltry turnout figures across England and Wales. Besides Scotland, voter turnout across England and Wales last week was pitifully low, a cursory google search of “local election turnout” will reveal stories from local papers up and down the country reporting on dismal turnout figures — Bradford, 37% — Bristol, 40% — Isle of Wight, 36% — West Northamptonshire, 29%. As the Bristol Cable report , these average figures across an area hide the range of turnout, often mirroring inequalities. In Bristol for example, turnout fell to 20% in Hartcliffe and Withywood, to 57% in Westbury-on-Trym and Henle…
items.why: turnout reflects the legitimacy and breadth of participation underpinning elected mandates, and is always classified under elections regardless of framing.
items.note: Turnout is filed under elections per the standing rule even when the framing is about willingness/non-voting patterns.

items.b: Record number of rejected ballots in London elections. 114,000 first preference votes were rejected in the London Mayoral ballot last Thursday, a significant increase on the 49,871 rejected votes recorded in 2016’s mayoral vote. A confusing ballot paper design is being blamed for the record rejection. Speaking to the BBC, Mary Harpley, as the Greater London Returning Officer reports it was necessary to split the ballot paper in this way to accommodate the record 20 candidates on the ballot.
items.why: a record rise in rejected ballots signals a failure in ballot design and election administration that undermines accurate vote counting.

items.b: AEA calls for a new Electoral Administration Act . In response to this week’s Queen’s Speech provisions for Voter ID and the abolition of the Fixed Term Parliaments Act, the Association of Electoral Administrators makes recommendations to ensure Voter ID does not add additional load and financial burden on councils and local election officials, that local ID schemes are funded by central government and schemes run by local authorities. AEA also strongly opposes the proposed reduction of the current 25-day general election timetable, as recommended by the Joint Committee on the Fixed-term Parli…
items.why: rules on voter ID and election timetables directly shape who can practically cast a vote and how elections are administered.
links: Joint Committee on the Fixed-term Parliaments Act

items.b: Democracy Club doubles their userbase with record stats . With 2,087,285 postcode searches recorded on Democracy Club’s database during election week, double that of both the roughly 1,000,000 searches polled during the 2019 local and EU elections. Democracy Club also recorded their best ever data coverage on the polling station finder tool WhereCanIVote, with 90% of councils sending in data.
items.why: tools that help voters find polling stations affect the practical accessibility of voting, a core element of election administration.
items.note: Treated as elections machinery (voting access) rather than general civic capacity-building.

items.b: New international best practice for vote counting from South Norfolk. Election staff in the region produced this energetic guide for vote counts.
items.why: vote-counting practice affects the accuracy and trustworthiness of election administration.

items.b: EquipHer . Activate, along with Elect Her and Glitch UK are creating Equip Her, a project to support a wider pipeline of politically active women from under-represented communities with the knowledge, skills and resources they need to get elected. EquipHer is supported by the Joseph Rowntree Reform Trust.
items.why: building a skills and resource pipeline for underrepresented women expands who can practically compete for elected office, a new means of participation.
items.note: Classified as sector capacity-building under participation, though it bears on candidate representativeness too.

items.b: Updated Twitter List of MSPs. Vonnie Sandlan , Comms Manager at Equality and Human Rights Commission (Scotland), has created a Twitter List of all members of the Scottish Parliament and updated it with 2021 additions.

UK rurality and deprivation dataset published . Alex Parsons’, Researcher at mySociety, has completed their work on a UK-wide rurality and deprivation dataset . As Alex explains, devolution in the UK means that some core datasets are produced separately by the statistics authorities in different nations. The new unified dataset brings together a complex arrangement of thresholds and definitions, providing a key resource and benchmark for UK-wide services such as mySociety. Alasdair Rae updates their UK Constituency Deprivation chart based on this new data.
items.why: a unified deprivation dataset underpins analysis of unequal conditions bearing on people's practical ability to take part in political life.
items.note: Borderline sector capacity-building resource whose direct link to participation is indirect.

items.b: Unlock Democracy supporters “angry”. With the government mired in corruption scandals, moves towards a ‘digital police state’ , the criminalisation of protest and dissent and a Queen’s Speech outlining new ways to make it more difficult to vote, Shaun Roberts , Head of Campaigns & Digital at Unlock Democracy, reports that UD members and supporters are angry, with a marked uptick in engagement across their activities.
items.why: a reported uptick in public engagement and mobilisation reflects people's willingness to take part in civic and campaigning activity.

items.b: Polimonitor to launch ‘virtual hansard’. Sam Cunningham , CEO of automated political monitoring platform Polimonitor , details plans for a new ‘virtual hansard’ tool. The new feature for the Polimonitor platform will provide Hansard information in near-real time, compared to the often long waits for Hansard data and transcripts for committees and activity away from the parliamentary floor.
items.why: faster access to Hansard and committee records strengthens the public's and researchers' ability to scrutinise Parliament's work and hold it accountable.
items.note: Treated as accountability tooling since it targets scrutiny of parliamentary proceedings rather than the wider media environment.

items.b: Prototype policy impact and news aggregation platform in the works. This week Josh Russell secured funding for a prototype news aggregation platform to be used by people researching the impact of government policies. They’re hiring — see jobs section below for more info, or Josh’s post on Democracy Club Slack, here .
items.why: a new tool helping people research the impact of government policy expands civil society's practical capacity to engage with and scrutinise public affairs.
items.note: Sector capacity-building creating a new means of engagement, per the capacity-building rule.

items.b: Neal Lawson calls for Labour to be re-founded. The party is trapped in an industrial era mindset and must burnish itself with a new name, a new identity and form the core of a progressive alliance, Lawson argues in the Guardian this week. The refounding, they say, will require a deliberative, intentional process and could involve a citizens’ assembly of the public, building new foundations for a party based in the vitality of the networked 21st century.
items.why: the proposal concerns restructuring a political party and using a citizens' assembly as a deliberative decision-making process, both of which bear on political competition and collective decision-making machinery.
items.note: Citizens' assembly component routed to elections_decision_making per framework rule, though this is an opinion/proposal rather than an enacted change.

items.b: New micro-local community building course. Village in the City are offering a new village builder course starting later this month. Facilitated by Mark McKergow, founder of Village in the City, the course explores six key elements for the successful development of micro-local communities, including Asset Based Community Development.
items.why: a new course builds people's practical capacity to organise and participate in civic life at the local, community level.

items.b: New briefing paper on constituency boundary reviews . Published by Neil Johnston at the House of Commons Library, the paper summarises current rules and procedures for boundary changes and how they’ve changed over time. It also gives an overview of how the number of MPs has reached the current level of 650.
items.why: constituency boundary rules determine the shape and size of electoral districts, directly affecting the representativeness of elected institutions.

items.b: Democracy Alliance. Liz Crosbie of Reboot GB is working on getting the Democracy Alliance community to commit whether or not it wants to actively collaborate on a Progressive Alliance pro-democracy campaign between now and the next general election.
items.note: Internal coalition-building process with no concrete mechanism or change reported; reads as sector logistics.

items.b: Democracy Handbook launches new funding tracker . James Moulding and the Democracy Handbook team are now tracking grant funding opportunities , in addition to jobs and events . Click here to add a grant , jobs and events to the Democracy Handbook database. Check these out and more on the UK Democracy Handbook .
items.note: Funding/jobs/events tracker is sector logistics, not a democracy story.

items.b: Koreo delivering Government Kickstart Scheme placements. Does your project or organisation require additional resource? The Government’s Kickstart Scheme creates placements for those aged 16–24 on Universal Credit and at risk of long-term youth unemployment. Apply now for a government sponsored placement in your organisation via Charityworks.
items.note: Job placement scheme promotion is sector logistics.

items.b: Coalition of democracy orgs urge government to drop Voter ID. With the news that polling stations will now require a form of photo ID to vote in future general elections to ‘prevent electoral fraud’, a group of 17 organisations have urged a rethink on the issue. Signatories included the Electoral Reform Society, Fair Vote UK, Stonewall and Operation Black Vote. Almost 3.5m voters have no passport or driving license by the government’s own estimate , with the Electoral Commission recording just 164 cases of electoral fraud in the 2019 General Election, out of 47m registered electors. Former Sco…
items.why: voter ID requirements affect the practical ability of eligible citizens to exercise their franchise, bearing directly on inclusive suffrage and electoral integrity safeguards.
links: require a form of photo ID

items.b: Unlock Democracy, Electoral Reform Society and Fair Vote UK publish their own version of the Government’s ‘Electoral Integrity Bill’ . The alternative bill demonstrates a potential alternative approach, they say.
items.why: publishing an alternative electoral integrity bill directly engages with how elections are administered and safeguarded, a core electoral machinery question.

items.b: New paper on the women members of Parliament. Richard Kelly at the House of Commons Library, has produced a research briefing and list of all female members of Parliament who have ever been elected. A similar paper was published back in February covering the Lords.
items.why: it documents the historical representativeness of Parliament by tracking women's presence among elected members.
links: list of all female members of Parliament

items.b: Number of appointments has ‘undone progress’, says report . Much of the substantial progress made by the House of Lords in reducing its size has been undone by recent appointments, the Lord Speaker’s committee on the size of the House has concluded .
items.why: the composition and scale of the House of Lords, filled through appointment rather than election, affects legislative scrutiny capacity and standards around public appointments.

items.b: Who Targets Me publish large dataset of UK political Facebook advertisers. Sam Jeffers, Founder of Who Targets Me , has published an open list of more than 5,000 UK political Facebook advertisers, tagged by party affiliation, in addition to several thousand non-party affiliated.
items.why: public disclosure of political advertisers on social media increases transparency of the information environment in which political persuasion occurs.
items.note: Touches campaign finance transparency but centres on the social-media information environment, so filed under information_debate.

items.b: Fair Vote UK develop strategy to take on the Online Safety Bill and Electoral Integrity Bill. If anyone is interested in engaging with either of these, speak to Kyle Taylor at Fair Vote, they are developing a coalition around the bills.
items.note: A call to join a coalition/advocacy effort, treated as sector organising rather than a reported democratic development.

items.b: The People Vs Climate Change. A new BBC documentary about the UK Climate Assembly , supported by Involve, mySociety and Sortition Foundation, is now available on iPlayer, Asha Pond from mySociety reports.
items.why: it raises public awareness of the UK Climate Assembly, a deliberative decision-making process that the framework treats as part of collective decision-making machinery.
items.note: Citizens' assemblies are filed under elections_decision_making per the framework's boundary rule.

items.b: Councillors call for online meetings to continue post-pandemic. As previously reported several weeks ago in this newsletter (and in greater depth), the emergency legislation allowing the move for council work to move to remote meetings has now run out, ending on 6th May. Councillors have taken to the High Court to see if existing law would enable them to continue meeting online, but their attempt has now been dismissed with judges saying MPs need to pass a new law to allow remote council work to continue. The government has launched a consultation to look at “next steps”.
items.why: the legal ability of local councils to meet and take decisions remotely affects the functioning of local democratic decision-making structures.
items.note: Local government structure/powers filed under elections_decision_making per boundary rule, though a court ruling is also involved.
links: their attempt has now been dismissed

items.b: Local Government explained . Jessica Studdert unpacks the structure of local government and councils in England in this new series by New Local. This piece is a must-read refresher for democracy wonks and serves as a reminder of how power is exercised throughout local government structures.
items.why: understanding how power is structured and exercised within local government affects citizens' ability to engage with that tier of decision-making.
items.note: Explainer on local government structure filed under elections_decision_making per boundary rule.
links: unpacks the structure of local government and councils

items.b: Towns Fund reports on their work in Boston. The £3.6 billion towns fund is aimed at ‘levelling up’ towns and cities across the country. The delivery team for the Town Deal for Boston report a palpable sense of optimism .

items.b: The Scottish Independence Library is looking for volunteer librarians. For more info, speak to Becki , Common Weal’s Communications Officer.
items.note: A volunteer recruitment notice for an organisation rather than a change affecting public participation.

items.why: a media literacy campaign on a major platform aims to help users critically assess the political information they encounter online.

items.note: Recommends an academic article, not a report on an actual mechanism change.

items.h: Welcome to the Election Week edition of the Democracy Bulletin,
items.b: It’s all go across the country (except in Northern Ireland) as covid-safe election counts continue. Yesterday was the largest set of elections for over 50 years in the UK, with 4,310 separate ballots and over 5,166 representatives up for election, with the vote held in over 35,500 polling stations! A huge and complex exercise, as noted by Democracy Club. While we wait, we’ve got a great haul of news, updates, project plugs and election glamour from across the democracy space for you. If you’re new — this newsletter is a weekly roundup of activities from across the democracy sector, including a…
items.note: Mostly newsletter welcome/admin text; the election-scale description is incidental colour rather than a reported mechanism-focused story.
links: taking a look at the meetup notes directly

items.b: Labour suffers catastrophic defeat in Hartlepool . The by-election has been the focal point of election coverage over the last few weeks. The crushing result in the so-called ‘red wall’ seat with more than 51.9% of votes going to the Conservative candidate is expected to cause angst and head-scratching within the Labour Party.
items.why: the result reflects genuine electoral competition and the public's ability to remove or reject representatives via a by-election

items.b: Hold the press, Election Leaflets is back! You can now photograph and upload your election leaflets, reports Peter Keeling of Democracy Club. Uploaded leaflets form an archive of useful data used by academics, journalists, campaigners and investigators. Since 2010 over 18,136 leaflets have been uploaded to the platform. Peter also wrote a piece about elections in the last pandemic for History Today.
items.why: an archive of campaign leaflets improves the public information environment around elections, aiding journalists, academics and campaigners in scrutinising political communication
items.note: Treated as information environment tool rather than election administration since its function is public-interest archiving of campaign material.

items.b: Fair Play. With the 2021 elections now in the rearview mirror, the Fair Play Pledge is wrapping up, writes Kyle Taylor . In recent days the Scottish Labour Party, Scottish Lib Dems and English Lib Dems committed their regional parties as a whole to the pledge. They also succeeded in signing up Sadiq Khan, Luisa Porrit and Sian Berry from the London mayoral race, as well as Paul Williams’ Hartlepool by-election campaign. In other news, the Fair Play Fact Check is now available in web browser extensions stores, with a showcase launch event coming soon.
items.why: parties and candidates committing to fair campaigning pledges bears on broadly equal campaigning opportunities and political competition in elections
items.note: Fact-check browser extension also touches the information environment beat as a secondary element.

items.b: Improving transparency in England’s patchy local elections data. Lucy Zhu at the Local Government Information Unit reports on their work compiling local elections data for the LGIU’s Ones to Watch Guide . They state there has been an improvement in transparency from both councils themselves and from other sources.
items.why: transparent local election data lets voters and researchers scrutinise how councils are elected and administered.

items.b: Community Manifesto. Similar to the recent Bristol Citizens’ Agenda, Gavin Barker at the Centre for Welfare Reform has been focusing on a community manifesto for the Cornwall Independent Poverty Forum , gathering local submissions of policy ideas and initiatives for new incoming candidates to consider following the local elections.
items.why: it creates a new channel through which community groups compile and press policy priorities onto newly elected local representatives.
items.note: Manifesto-gathering is civic organising rather than election administration or candidate selection.
links: community manifesto for the Cornwall Independent Poverty Forum

items.b: Compass cross-party post-election debrief . Colin Miller of Compass recommends their event next Tuesday 11th May . Compass is playing host to John Curtice, Caroline Lucas, Layla Moran, Clive Lewis, Tommy Sheppard and others for a post-election debrief. The event will likely cover talk of a progressive alliance, PR and the potential breakup of the UK.

The Wonk’s Guide to Hartlepool . Whilst we wait patiently for the results of elections across England, Wales and Scotland, Aveek Bhattacharya, Chief Economist of the Social Market Foundation, writes about the challenges facing the town of Hartlepool, centre of election attention over the last few weeks.

Innovation in Politics Awards. Josef Zehetner of the Innovation in Politics Institute joined us at the Democracy Meetup to welcome those in the sector to submit their most outstanding political initiatives as nominees for the prestigious award. A jury over 1,000 citizens from across Europe will select the winning projects in nine categories.
links: submit their most outstanding political initiatives

items.b: Apply now for CCC’s 2021 Summer School. Looking for career advice from leading scholars in territorial politics? Looking for feedback on your research? The Centre for Constitutional Change’s Sovereignty, Independence and Constitutional Change Summer School is now open to applications. Apply by 10th May .

FOI & WasteWorks . Myfanwy Nixon from mySociety reports you can now watch the video of mySociety’s FOI policy launch , Alex Parsons has also been adding nerdy bits of detail into subsidiary blog posts on things that didn’t make it into the policy paper, like how Network Rail became subject to FOI . mySociety’s trading arm SocietyWorks also launched their new council waste platform, WasteWorks .
items.why: the FOI policy work and the extension of FOI coverage to bodies like Network Rail strengthen mechanisms for holding public functions answerable.
items.note: WasteWorks is a secondary participation tool distinct from the primary FOI accountability story.
links: video of mySociety’s FOI policy launch
how Network Rail became subject to FOI

items.b: Rebooting Democracy. Liz Crosbie of Reboot GB soft launched the Reboot Pledge this week, calling on opposition party leaders to work together, tackle the climate crisis and commit to electoral reform.
items.why: it launches a new pledge campaign mobilising public pressure on party leaders toward cooperation and electoral reform.
items.note: Campaign launch is participation; its substantive ask concerns electoral reform.

items.b: Applications now open to NCCPE Engage Academy . The NCCPE announced this year’s applications for their Engage Academy are now open. Running for seven years, the Engage Academy is a nine month development programme for public engagement professionals. Find out more here .
items.why: a development programme for public engagement professionals builds capacity in the sector that facilitates citizen participation.
items.note: Borderline: this trains practitioners rather than directly creating a citizen-facing participation channel.

items.b: Tory activists decry use of Party funds for private costs. ConservativeHome found that 7 in 10 Conservative activists believe that money raised by the party shouldn’t help fund the leader’s private costs.
items.why: activist concern over misuse of party funds bears on standards in public life and the transparency of party financing.
items.note: Party finance transparency sits at the boundary of accountability/corruption and the elections anchor on transparent financing.

items.b: “Please honour us and give us a voice”. Last week we covered #NewScots , this week we highlight the reverse reality in England. This week in the Bristol Cable , Priyanka Raval talks to Asli Tatliadim, Manager at Bristol Refugee Rights (BRR) who’s lived in Bristol since moving to the UK in 2017. Despite her keen interest in local politics, she is unable to vote. Although there is an escalating campaign for similar rights to those in Wales and Scotland, the Government has not been forthcoming. Chloe Smith MP, Conservative Minister of State for the Constitution and Devolution rejected any further…
items.why: it concerns who is included in the franchise for local elections, a core determinant of who can choose representatives.

items.b: Thematic groups underway. Thematic groups bringing together civil servants and civil society as part of the development of the new National Action Plan for Open Government have started, with the first of four Open Procurement and Open Health workshops taking place this week. Open Justice will start on May 10th, reports Kevin Keith , Chair of UK Open Government Network. Sign up here to get involved in this vital process.
items.why: it creates structured channels for civil society to shape government policy through the Open Government Action Plan process.
items.note: Treated as capacity-building for participation rather than an event listing, since it launches a new engagement structure.
links: National Action Plan for Open Government

items.b: Senior Tory backs Votes at 16. Tobias Ellwood MP signals their support for expanding the franchise to 16 and 17 years olds in England, following on the coattails of Scotland and Wales.
items.why: expanding the franchise to 16 and 17 year olds changes who is entitled to vote.

items.b: Celebrating Votes at 16 in Wales . Yesterday’s Senedd election was the first time in Wales that 16 years olds had the right to vote. Writing for ERS, Kelly Harris, a youth worker involved in the evolution of the issue over the last 20 years, looks back on the campaign , from the Funky Dragon (the Children and Young People’s Assembly for Wales, at the time) to Welsh Senedd itself.
items.why: it reports the first exercise of an expanded franchise, directly affecting who could vote in the Senedd election.

items.b: Newly relaunched ElectHer promotes Peer Circles. Structured as a 7-session programme, Peer Circles will run three times a year to create a safe and constructive space for women who are considering standing for elected office.
items.why: supporting more women to stand for elected office affects candidate access and the representativeness of elected institutions.
items.note: Classified under elections as candidate access rather than participation, per framework anchors on parties and candidates.

items.b: Unlock Democracy calls for independent inquiry into Conservative Party donations linked to COVID-19 contracts. Their petition calls on the Tory Treasurer to hand over donations received from individuals and companies that benefited from COVID-19 contracts.
items.why: it concerns potential conflicts of interest between political party donations and public contracting decisions, a core accountability and corruption issue.

items.b: Institute for Government calls for full statutory public inquiry into government action during the pandemic . Whilst the Prime Minister continues to claim an inquiry would distract from managing the crisis, the IfG’s report details why now is the time for the promised inquiry. Another new IfG paper sets out the changes needed to restore trust in government and reduce the risk of conflicts of interest undermining public confidence.
items.why: a statutory public inquiry is a scrutiny mechanism for holding the executive answerable for its pandemic decisions.
items.note: Public inquiry framed as scrutiny (accountability) rather than redress (rule of law).

items.b: Governing for the future. The RSA publishes a new report examining lessons for the future, thinking about democracy in particular. The report says that due to a string of high-profile scandals and untransparent decision making during the crisis, responses are urgently needed to restore public trust and confidence in UK governance. The report recommends a deliberative assembly to discuss the COVID-19 response, radical transparency approaches and a new lobbying tax.
items.why: proposals for transparency, lobbying regulation and deliberative processes aim to restore checks on executive power and public trust in governance.
items.note: Deliberative assembly recommendation touches elections_decision_making, but overall report centres on trust and accountability.

items.b: Constitution Unit webinar on Ministerial Standards. Don’t miss the Constitution Unit’s upcoming webinar on May 24th on Ministerial Standards, with Sir Alex Allan, former Independent Adviser on Ministers’ Interests, Susan Deacon, former Minister for Health in Scotland and Prof Robert Hazell, Professor of Government and the Constitution at the Constitution Unit.
items.note: An event/webinar listing rather than a reported development.

items.b: Connecting for Good . Act Build Change Director Stephanie Wong shares their thoughts on organising methods and observations from their work on Connecting for Good, a movement against social isolation in Coventry.
items.why: community organising to build local connection and combat isolation strengthens the civic capacity underpinning collective participation.
items.note: Borderline: primarily social rather than explicitly political organising, but framed as civil-society organising practice.

items.b: Building up Win-Win Democracy. Perry Walker at TalkShop looks to offer facilitation training and workshops on their win-win democracy methodology to Flatpack councillors after the election. Win-win democracy provides a means for competing groups and factions to find compromise and emerge from discussions with ‘wins’ for everyone involved.
items.why: it creates a new facilitation tool intended to help elected councillors and communities resolve disputes and take part in local decision-making more effectively
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new means of participation, not standard news.

items.b: The Great Get Together. Between June 18th to 20th Great Get Together are encouraging communities to come out of isolation, share time together and celebrate what we have in common. You can find out more here .

Bridge Builder’s Handbook. The Relationship Project teamed up with the After Disaster Network this week to publish their new handbook , a step-by-step guide to building more connected communities. The work draws together mediation, peace building theory and conflict transformation work.

Over £400,000 crowdfunded by Scottish political parties ahead of the Holyrood elections. Across Scotland 13 parties and candidates raised twice the amount raised back in the 2017 General Election. 16 of the 108 funding campaigns failed to provide the necessary legal information on their pages, risking parties accepting donations from “impermissable sources”.
items.why: it concerns campaign finance transparency and compliance with rules on permissible donation sources ahead of Holyrood elections

items.b: Scrap the Bristol Mayor? Lib Dem and Tory candidates agreed on one thing this election, both want to hold a referendum on scrapping the Bristol Mayor. They argue that councillors have been sidelined with the rise of the mayoral system, the Bristol Cable reports.
items.why: it concerns a proposed referendum on the structure of local government decision-making in Bristol
items.note: Referendums and local government structure are filed under elections & decision making per framework rule.

items.b: North for the North. New grassroots campaign Campaign for Northern Democracy launches. The group, an umbrella organisation, aims to raise the profile of the North’s democratic deficit. CfND is sponsored by Compass and the Hannah Mitchell Foundation.
items.why: it launches a new grassroots campaign network intended to organise civic pressure around regional democratic representation
items.note: Civil society capacity-building primary; underlying devolution/regional governance issue is secondary.

items.b: Sturgeon rules out wildcat illegal indy vote. During the final Scottish leaders election debate, First Minister Nicola Sturgeon MSP ruled out holding an illegal referendum vote, in response to Scottish Tory leader Douglas Ross MP. Prime Minister Johnson must transfer reserved powers to Scotland via a Section 30 order in order for the SNP to hold a referendum. The SNP have maintained they are only in the business of legal referenda, learning from Catalonia’s failed and violent independence bid.
items.why: it concerns the legal mechanism required to hold a binding independence referendum and the constraints on that direct democratic decision
links: ruled out holding an illegal referendum

items.b: The Cost of One Party Councils. Yesterday’s election is likely to produce swathes of ‘one-party councils’, Josiah Mortimer, Head of Comms at the Electoral Reform Society (ERS) argues , under the England and Wales one-party takes all local electoral system. ERS published a study back in 2015 that found councils dominated by single parties could waste the UK as much as £2.6bn a year through a lack of scrutiny of their procurement processes.
items.why: it concerns how the first-past-the-post local electoral system produces one-party councils, weakening competitive representation and scrutiny

items.b: Break-Up Britain. Forty-four years ago, Tom Nairn predicted the break-up of the United Kingdom. Writing for Verso ahead of this week’s historic Scottish election, James Foley of Common Weal, revisits Nairn’s prognoses for the break up of the British state.
items.note: A historical/literary retrospective on predictions of UK breakup, not a reported mechanism or change.

items.b: The Union’s Promise. Charlotte Alldritt of the Centre for Progressive Policy writes in The Times (paywall) that the promise of the Union is vanishing with the British Government increasingly serving England alone. The potency, legitimacy and sustainability of the UK government is threatened by apathy and incompetence as well as Westminster’s grating superiority complex, they write.
items.why: it concerns the legitimacy and accountability of the UK government in representing and serving all nations of the Union equally
items.note: Borderline opinion piece on political legitimacy rather than a concrete mechanism change.

items.b: Parliament and Northern Ireland. David Torrance of the House of Commons library has written a brief on the history of the relations and constitutional developments between Northern Ireland and the British Parliament since the 1920 Government of Ireland Act.
items.why: This matters democratically because it concerns the constitutional structure governing how Northern Ireland's devolved institutions relate to and derive authority from the UK Parliament.
items.note: Treated as devolved government structure under elections & decision making rather than participation.

items.b: Public Interest News. Congrats to Joe Mitchell who starts in their new role at the Public Interest News Foundation this week, working to provide financial support for indie local news publishers alongside research into independent publishing and experimentation and innovation in non-traditional news provision.
items.note: Staff appointment news about an organisation, excluded per rules.

items.b: Reporting on election polls, results and surveys? Back in November 2019, IMPRESS and the Market Research Society produced this resource on reporting statistical data responsibly. IMPRESS is also hiring for a new Regulatory Executive .
items.why: This matters democratically because responsible reporting of election polls and statistical data shapes the public information environment voters rely on to understand political competition.
items.note: Job listing portion excluded; focus is on the resource for responsible election data reporting.

items.b: BBC and Beyond . The Media Reform Coalition’s new campaign, ‘ The BBC and Beyond : Reimagining Public Media’, launched this week, aiming to defend and re-envision public media in the digital age.
items.why: This matters democratically because a campaign to defend and reimagine public service media addresses plurality and quality of the public information environment.

items.b: Embracing complexity in government . Thea Snow of the Centre for Public Impact on complexity and government . The piece is part of City of Melbourne’s upcoming City of the Future event by Participate Melbourne.
items.note: Abstract international public-administration commentary without a UK democratic mechanism.

items.b: Office politics. Titus Alexander recommends a Guardian piece on Biden’s office politics , which resembles a chapter from their book Practical Politics .
Worlds apart . In this week’s Act Build Change mailer Sotez Chowdhury recommends Heineken’s Worlds Apart short film, not the brand, but their approach.

items.h: Welcome to the 26th May issue of the new Democracy Bulletin,
items.b: For our flurry of new readers joining us this week, this bulletin is a fortnightly roundup of activities from across the democracy sector, including a summary of updates, job listings (at the bottom!), news and even the odd bit of gossip from our meetups . We’d just like to say a word or two of apologies for our technical issues at Monday’s meetup, it seems we’re still having some teething troubles with the new AddEvent calendar integration (gremlins in the system!). Please do share your ideas, feedback and any questions you might have about the Centre for Democracy’s programmes: UK Democracy …
items.note: Newsletter administrative/meta content about its own operations, not a democracy story.

items.b: See all current job adverts — Add a new role or paid internship to our database
links: Add a new role or paid internship

items.b: View a list of upcoming events — Add a new event to our database
View current open grants and paid fellowships — Add a new grant or funding opportunity
