items.h: MPs Research Matrix
items.b: The growing collaboration through the Elections Bill coalition needs 5–6 orgs who can take 15 MPs each from this list and research them to divvy up the workload. Email matt@fairvote.uk if you can help.
items.note: Internal coalition workload-sharing logistics, not substantive democracy content.

items.h: Elections Bill coalition to start to maintain a shared calendar from September
items.b: Starting in September, organisations taking part in the coalition will be able to view a shared calendar to provide greater awareness of what organisations are doing across the space in response to the Bill.
items.note: Coalition scheduling/coordination tool, sector admin only.

items.h: Fair Vote setting up a new centralised folder to host Elections Bill policy/research work
items.b: Nico Docherty at Fair Vote UK is pulling together briefing notes, policy pieces and research on areas affected by the bill. If you know anything useful that should be added, send it to nico@fairvote.uk .
items.note: Internal resource-sharing folder, sector admin only.

items.h: Recent roundtables held by Cat Smith MP suggest the Government may be open to expanding acceptable ID
items.b: Recent meetings with civil society organisations revealed that the Government intends to include blue badges as an acceptable form of ID, which promisingly suggests the Government may be open to expanding to include other forms of ID, reports Fair Vote UK .
items.why: government decisions about which forms of ID are acceptable directly determine who can practically exercise their right to vote.

items.h: Voter ID distribution to be managed at the local council level, not via a central government portal
items.b: Meetings of the Elections Bill coalition with the Cabinet Office and Electoral Commission have confirmed that the Government is committed to distribution and management of the new voter ID at the local council level. Peter Stanyon, Chief Executive of the Association of Electoral Administrators , has repeatedly warned the Government of additional cost burdens being pushed onto already cash-strapped councils , that national funding should be made available to roll out and maintain the scheme.
items.why: the administrative arrangements and funding for implementing voter ID affect whether elections are run fairly and accessibly across all council areas.
links: additional cost burdens being pushed onto already cash-strapped councils

items.h: Elections Bill policy deep dive
items.b: Electoral Reform Society, Open Britain, Fair Vote, Unlock Democracy, Hands Off Our Vote and others as part of the coalition are focusing on the detail of the bill at the moment, as well as compiling policy positions from across different organisations into one place. Jess Garland, Director of Research and Policy at ERS, suggests that if anyone has amendments or has policy concerns that they get in touch .
items.note: Sector coordination call for input on the bill, not a substantive policy development itself.

items.h: The3million draft a new motion for councils on Residence-Based Voting Rights
items.b: Maria Milenova and Lara Parizotto of the3million , in partnership with Polish Migrants Organise for Change , have prepared a model council motion on Residence-Based Voting Rights and voter ID and have begun disseminating it to local councillors in their network. Lara is also keen to find out more about how the Scottish and Welsh campaigns for RBVR developed and successfully expanded the franchise.
items.why: the campaign seeks to expand the franchise to residents who are currently excluded from voting, directly affecting who can participate in elections.

items.h: SNP councillors in Renfrewshire receive Government reply to their letter to Chloe Smith MP opposing voter ID
items.b: SNP councillors wrote to the government back in June to demand the Prime Minister scrap plans for voter ID on the basis of alienating deprived communities. Chloe Smith MP responded saying voter fraud was “ a crime we cannot allow room for ” and that the government would be continuing with its plans.
items.why: the dispute concerns whether new voter ID rules will restrict ballot access for deprived communities.
links: a crime we cannot allow room for

items.h: Mayor of London writes to Minister of the Constitution, Chloe Smith MP, over Election Bill concerns
items.b: Elisabeth Pop highlights this letter the Mayor’s Office has sent to Chloe Smith MP, raising concerns over the bills impact on the ability of Londoners to fully engage in the democratic process. The stats and background research included in the letter may be useful to other organisations, they mention.
items.why: the letter raises concerns that the Elections Bill's provisions could reduce Londoners' practical ability to vote and take part in elections.

items.h: Updates on the Police Bill coalition, looking for open letter co-signatories
items.b: Joseph Rowntree Charitable Trust (JRCT) has provided funding to contract a new Police Bill coalition convener, Kathleen Christie . Thanks to funding from JRRT, the Quakers have contracted Jessica Metheringham to work on influencing the bill as it passes through the Lords, they’re also looking to hire a comms consultant. Kathleen is asking democracy organisations to co-sign a new open letter against the bill. The deadline for the open letter is August 31st, you can co-sign the letter here . The PCSC Bill will start its passage through the Lords on 14th September. If you’re interested in joining…
items.why: the coalition's advocacy and open letter target legislation that could restrict the legal space for protest and assembly.
items.note: Mostly reports coalition funding/staffing, but purpose is organised opposition to a bill affecting protest rights.
links: you can co-sign the letter here

items.h: Democracy and human rights groups come together to sign shared position paper
items.b: More than 230 organisations including Index on Censorship, Best for Britain, Fair Vote, Travellers Movement and Unlock Democracy have signed a shared position paper in defence of the Human Rights Act and judicial review. If you would like to add your organisation, please contact Rachel at Humanists UK with your logo and a two sentence description of your organisation.
items.why: a broad civil-society coalition publicly defending the Human Rights Act and judicial review protects the mechanisms by which individuals can challenge and constrain public power

items.h: I Have A Voice prep for their event launch and experiment with a new application process
items.b: Rebecca Deegan, Founder at I Have A Voice, is preparing for the launch of their first policy paper . The new paper goes into depth on the need to diversify the political sphere and widen participation in democratic processes — don’t miss their launch on 1 September ! They’re also hiring for a new Education Partnership Manager , and in an experimental turn have asked potential applicants for a 60-second video clip of what they’d do if they were stuck in a lift with Boris Johnson, much more exciting than just reading CVs!
items.note: Event launch and hiring process are organisational logistics, not a democracy mechanism story.
links: launch of their first policy paper

items.h: Represent.me is looking for a new owner
items.b: The civic-centric political engagement platform, Represent, is looking for a new lease of life. Whilst it grew quickly in 2015–2016 with over 20,000 registered users, it has been dormant for the last 3 years due to the change in political sensibilities and founder burnout. Represent.me would benefit an organisation seeking national or international engagement: campaigns, political parties, unions, civic foundations, etc. The founder is also interested in making it fully open-source. For more information see http://go.eddowding.com/represent . You can contact the founder, Ed Dowding, at ed@repr…
items.note: A platform seeking a new owner is organisational/sector logistics.

items.h: Pol.is are working to build more effective and accessible consultations
items.b: Rutter Wetters, researcher at the digital democracy platform Pol.is , is working on their Computational Democracy Project, to develop a more effective, fair and accessible method of public consultation designed to promote consensus and minimise trolling. For those unfamiliar with the platform, Pol.is has a long track record of successful deployments, and is the tool of choice for the Digital Minister of Taiwan, Audrey Tang .
items.why: developing more effective, accessible consultation methods shapes how public deliberation and collective decision-making can be conducted
items.note: Deliberation and consultation tools fall under elections & decision making per the framework's boundary rule, not participation.

items.h: Artcry — the new fund to support artists to make politically response work
items.b: Artcry give small grants up to £2.5k to support artists who want to make an immediate artistic impact in response to social and political events. They’re keen to get involved in the campaigning of democracy organisations in this space. You can find out more about Artcry on their website , or by contacting their Director, Kathryn Bilyard .
items.note: This is a funding call for artists, sector logistics rather than a democracy mechanism.

items.h: Upskilling activists with the School of Social Justice
items.b: Alvin Carpio has started working with a small team to experiment with delivering content to upskill activists, through a new YouTube channel and podcast. They’re currently recruiting and on the lookout for a videographer, video editor, graphic designer and animator.
items.why: creating new training content and channels to upskill activists expands the practical means by which people can take part in civic and political life

items.h: What makes a campaigning organisation ‘people-driven’?
items.b: In this latest piece for Sheila McKechnie as part of a collaboration with the Power Sharing Project , Lianna Etkind unpacks their experiences from community organising. Bookings for SMK’s next Campaign Carousel in January are now open.
items.note: An opinion piece and event booking notice rather than a reported change or new participation mechanism.

items.h: Women’s Equality Party table amendment to recall MPs guilty of sexual harassment
items.b: After successfully campaigning to stop Mark Field being selected as a candidate after he infamously grabbed a female climate protestor in 2019 and standing candidates against MPs under investigation for misconduct, WEP have worked to successfully table an amendment in Parliament to recall sex pest MPs .
items.why: a recall mechanism for MPs guilty of sexual harassment changes how elected representatives can be removed and held accountable outside of general elections
items.note: Recall of MPs sits at the boundary between electoral mechanics and standards-in-public-life accountability.

items.h: Make Votes Matter are hiring a new Media Manager and working to build their Alliance
items.b: The MVM Alliance for Proportional Representation started back in 2016 and is a cross-party grouping of 71 organisations and parties, ranging from Conservative Action on Electoral Reform to Plaid Cymru. Holly Morgan-Davies has just joined MVM and is now working to build up the Alliance and welcome new members. Make Votes Matter are also hiring a new Media Manager, you can find out more and apply here .
items.note: Hiring and alliance-building news about the organisation itself, not a reported change to democratic mechanisms.

items.h: New House of Commons Library briefings on Parliamentary Recall and Unitary Local Government
items.b: Richard Kelly has written up a detailed briefing on the process and history of recalling Parliament, whilst Mark Sandford provides a comprehensive overview of unitary local government in England.
items.why: authoritative briefings on the process of recalling Parliament and the structure of unitary local government inform understanding of core decision-making machinery
items.note: Local government structure and parliamentary recall fall under elections & decision making.

items.h: National Union of Journalists members prevented from reporting on latest XR demonstrations
items.b: With Extinction Rebellion back on the streets of London this week ahead of COP26 in November, the National Union of Journalists report their members being unable to access protest areas this week after being turned away by the Metropolitan Police.
items.why: journalists being blocked from reporting on a protest restricts the public's access to information about how state power is being exercised and challenged
items.note: Journalists' access to report is treated as press freedom (information_debate) rather than protest policing itself.
links: report their members being unable to access protest areas

items.h: SNP and Scottish Greens confirm power-sharing deal in historic first for UK Greens
items.b: Lorna Slater and Patrick Harvie will become ministers under a confidence and supply agreement between the party and the SNP. The deal marks the first time the Green Party has entered government in the UK. The Scottish Tory party took aim at the Greens calling them “ extremists ” (paywall). View the shared policy programme here and the Cooperation Agreement here .
items.why: the formation of a governing coalition following an election determines who exercises executive power and under what policy programme

items.h: Green Party leadership election experiencing a last minute flurry of candidates
items.b: New candidates for the top job include Ashley Gunstock — an actor best known for a stint in the police drama The Bill , Shahrar Ali — who is centering the party’s internal conflict over trans rights as the core of his campaign. Other candidates include co-leader candidates Amelia Womack and Extinction Rebellion activist Tamsin Omond , Carla Denyer and Adrian Ramsay and Tina Rothery and Martin Hemingway .
items.why: a contested leadership election determines who leads a political party that competes for public office
items.note: Internal party leadership contest treated under elections_decision_making per free-political-parties anchor.
links: Amelia Womack and Extinction Rebellion activist Tamsin Omond

items.h: New briefing on UK elections from the House of Commons Library
items.b: The paper by Richard Cracknell and Sam Pilling presents an overview of elections in the UK since 1918 , including elections to the European Parliament, local government and devolved legislatures.
items.why: an authoritative reference on the history and administration of UK elections informs understanding of how electoral machinery has functioned and changed
items.note: Treated as elections_decision_making despite being a reference document rather than a change.
links: overview of elections in the UK since 1918

items.h: Bureau Local launches new People’s Newsroom to support community journalism
items.b: The new initiative will begin on an experimental basis in Swansea , providing hands-on startup support to design innovative journalism initiatives and invest in community newsroom leaders traditionally marginalised by the media. The Swansea newsroom project brings together the Ethnic Minorities and Youth Support Team Wales (EYST) , Lankelly Chase and Clwstwr to research, design and build the new community journalism project, which will then inform the UK wide rollout of the People’s Newsroom project next year. Find out more about the People’s Newsroom at the Bureau Local’s project launch event…
items.why: building new community journalism capacity in underserved areas expands the plural sources of public-interest information available to citizens
links: new initiative will begin on an experimental basis in Swansea
Ethnic Minorities and Youth Support Team Wales (EYST)

items.h: Manchester local news startup The Mill reaches 925 members and £65,000 annual income
items.b: The Mill ’s four-strong team produce a well-researched advertising-free article every weekday to its paying members, whether investigating online allegations of local government corruption or analysing the future of the iconic Piccadilly Gardens. The Mill is in direct competition with the Manchester Evening News , owned by Reach, Britain’s largest newspaper group.
items.note: Reports on an existing outlet's membership and revenue growth, which is organisational news rather than a new mechanism affecting participation.

items.h: DCMS’ Online Media Literacy Strategy, PINF’s Joe Mitchell takes a look
items.b: DCMS’ Online Media Report outlines the context and the challenges facing those working on media literacy reform, which includes better coordination of the 170 organisations identified in the strategy. The paper goes on to describe (some very familiar) problems faced by those orgs, of funding, evaluation etc. Joe Mitchell of Public Interest News Foundation asks whether there are any lessons here for any attempts at political/civic literacy strategy?
items.why: assessing a government media literacy strategy bears on how well citizens can navigate the public information environment

items.h: GB News stalls, Andrew Neil likely to quit role
items.b: GB News has seen its viewership drop to zero on some shows after presenter takes the kneee, as Chairman and former BBC presenter Andrew Neil reconsiders his role .
items.note: Reports on a broadcaster's viewership and staffing troubles rather than a mechanism of press freedom or media plurality.

items.h: Major new funding opportunity for participatory processes launched by Open Society Foundations
items.b: Open Society Foundations (OSF) has launched a call for proposals to fund a piece of participatory design work, with quite a short deadline (7 October). They’re looking for a UK-based non-profit organisation to lead a group of partners/stakeholders to develop a participatory process to design a new approach to community safety and policing resource allocation. The purpose is to design a participatory and multi-stakeholder (including police) process, where the process itself educates the public and other actors about policing and community safety budgets and outcomes. The process will result in …
items.why: funding a new participatory process for policing and community safety budgets creates a mechanism for citizens to take part directly in resource-allocation decisions
items.note: Participatory budgeting is explicitly participation_civic_life territory rather than elections_decision_making.

items.h: Journalism failed in Afghanistan too
items.b: Peter W Klein, Executive Director of the Global Reporting Centre, an independent non-profit newsroom, reflects on the troubled role of journalism during the long 20 years of the Afghanistan occupation.
items.note: A reflective piece on journalism in Afghanistan, not bearing on UK democratic mechanisms.

items.h: How did democracy fare under lockdown?
items.b: Ariane Gottlieb writing for National Endowment for Democracy’s Power 3.0 project goes into some depth on how COVID-19 has affected and continues to play havoc with democratic processes , cultures and electoral calendars around the world.
items.why: it examines how COVID-19 disrupted electoral calendars and democratic processes globally, bearing on electoral integrity and continuity.
links: COVID-19 has affected and continues to play havoc with democratic processes

items.h: Elections Bill Coalition Delivers Petitions to Downing Street
items.b: On Tuesday 5th representatives from the Democracy Defence Coalition delivered a myriad of petitions and a civil society sign-on letter to Downing Street opposing the introduction of Voter ID. They were also able to meet with Angela Rayner to reinforce the importance of the issue. The coalition is now in full swing, with 61 organisations participating. They hold weekly “office hours” for any orgs interested in the bill and are running an array of joint campaigns across the range of issues raised by the bill. If you’d like to get on the weekly digest email list or attend the office hours please …
items.why: This matters democratically because civil society campaigning against Voter ID concerns who can exercise the right to vote and how electoral access is regulated.
items.note: Campaign/coalition activity treated under elections since the substantive issue is voter ID.
links: delivered a myriad of petitions and a civil society sign-on letter to Downing Street

items.h: Elections Bill Coalition issues new must-read civil society briefing
items.b: The comprehensive joint document outlines the problems of the Elections Bill, the current groupings opposing the bill and the objectives and strategy of the coalition opposing the bill. The briefing also includes a parliamentary timetable for the bill and messaging guidance.
items.why: This matters democratically because the briefing is a new resource enabling civil society to engage effectively with legislation affecting electoral access.
items.note: Treated as capacity-building resource per the sector capacity-building rule, though the underlying topic is voter ID.

items.h: RebootGB identify loophole in Elections Bill potentially stalling a future snap election
items.b: An unintended consequence of the required 365-day registration period for the new £700 spend limit would mean ‘backdating’ the law to hold an election whilst that 365-day period ticks down, which may be subject to legal challenge, according to RebootGB’s PACAC inquiry submission .
items.why: This matters democratically because a drafting flaw in election spending rules could affect the timing and legality of calling a general election.

items.h: Unlock Democracy launches Elections Bill Action Centre
items.b: The new portal provides key links to how supporters and citizens can take action to aid the campaign against the Elections Bill.
items.why: This matters democratically because the new action centre gives citizens a concrete channel to engage with legislation affecting their voting rights.

items.h: MP Research Matrix — if you have any intel or org connections to add, please do so
items.b: The Elections Bill coalition is compiling intelligence on MPs ties and notable votes to aid in the campaign. Add any information you have to the shared spreadsheet to help the work of the coalition..
items.note: Internal coalition lobbying spreadsheet, not a public-facing participation tool.

items.h: New tool asks the media to cover the Elections Bill
items.b: Josh Russell, Co-founder of Forward Democracy , has launched a new site to ask news media orgs to report on the Elections Bill, check it out here: heynews.org/uk/electionsbill/
items.why: This matters democratically because the tool creates a new means for citizens to press media outlets to cover legislation affecting electoral access.

items.h: ERS Cymru coordinating Welsh civil society opposition to voter ID
items.b: Jess Blair and ERS Cymru are working to coordinate 18 Welsh civil society groups against voter ID .
items.why: This matters democratically because civil society coordination in Wales is contesting voter ID rules that could restrict electoral access.

items.h: Updated costings on voter ID
items.b: Voter ID is expected to cost as much as £180m per decade under the new plans, with £15m alone being spent on the plastic ID cards themselves for voters without ID.
items.why: This matters democratically because the cost of implementing voter ID has direct implications for electoral administration and practical access to voting.

items.h: Joint Committee on Human Rights release report on the Elections Bill
items.b: The new report provides a good analysis of the impact of voter ID on marginalised groups protected under human rights law.
items.why: This matters democratically because the report examines whether voter ID requirements will disproportionately restrict marginalised groups' right to vote.
items.note: Substance is voter ID (elections) though the analytic lens is discrimination/rights.

items.h: Involve appoints Coordinator of new Democracy Network
items.b: Jessie Joe Jacobs is a social entrepreneur with 18 years experience of network development, campaign and project management, fundraising and campaigning for a diversity of organisations and causes. As Regional Director of the Stronger In campaign, Director of the Northern Inclusion Forum and Campaigns Officer at the TUC, Jessie brings a wealth of experience and passion to the role. Jessie will begin their new role at the end of the September and we look forward to more updates about the development of the new network. Welcome Jessie!
items.note: Staff appointment news about an organisation, excluded per framework.

items.h: Mark the UN International Day of Democracy with Democracy Day Live
items.b: The team at Open Britain and Democracy Unleashed have brought together a fantastic panel to celebrate the International Day of Democracy on 15th September, including journalist Gavin Esler, Peter Jukes, Founder of Byline Times, Dominic Grieve, former Attorney General, Klina Jordan, Director of Make Votes Matter, Tom Brake, Director of Unlock Democracy. Sign up on Facebook here .
items.note: Event/listing announcement, not substantive reporting on a democratic mechanism.

items.h: I Have A Voice launch publish first discussion paper
items.b: Rebecca Deegan , Director at I Have A Voice , is celebrating the launch of their first discussion paper and moving on to focus on next steps — including working out how to measure political literacy in a way that supports targeted intervention.
items.note: Organisational news about a paper launch and future plans, not yet a tool or change affecting participation.

items.h: Centenary Action Group submits paper to the APPG on Disability’s inquiry into Access for Elected Office
items.b: Informed by the Elect Her and CAG’s bi-monthly roundtables for Deaf and Disabled women active in politics, the evidence paper concludes:
items.why: public office must be genuinely open to all citizens, and this evidence documents structural barriers preventing disabled people from standing for or serving in elected office.
items.note: Access to elected office is anchored in elections_decision_making (public office open to all citizens) even though disability equality also touches rights.

items.b: That there are numerous barriers that prevent Disabled people from becoming elected representatives and more barriers still that make participation difficult once elected.
items.why: barriers to becoming and remaining an elected representative directly affect who can exercise democratic office.

items.b: An intersectional approach must be taken, that Disabled people are not a homogenous group and that a Disabled person may have multiple protected characteristics.
items.why: recognising intersecting characteristics among disabled people shapes how barriers to elected office should be addressed.
items.note: Part of the same evidence paper on access to elected office.

items.b: That efforts cannot be down to political parties alone, the Government must take the lead in measures to remove barriers for Disabled people.
items.why: who bears responsibility for removing barriers to elected office is a question of institutional design for democratic access.

items.b: Through ensuring Disabled women, and men, have a seat at the decision-making table, we will improve governance and change society for the better.
items.why: ensuring disabled people have seats at decision-making tables bears directly on representativeness of elected institutions.

items.h: Elect Her are now preparing for their eighth cohort
items.b: Elect Her’s Peer Support Circles are structured as a 7-session journey, each composed of peers from across the political spectrum who want to create a safe space to support one another and encourage new voices and ambitions. The programme is free — Join the new cohort from 6th October and share the opportunity via your social media feeds.
items.why: a peer support programme building capacity for underrepresented people to stand for office creates new means for them to take part in democratic life.
items.note: Capacity-building programme counts as participation under the sector capacity-building rule, though it also bears on candidate access to office.

items.h: Make Votes Matter launching new ‘Democracy Loves’ event series
items.b: The series kicks off on w/c 20th September with the first event focusing on the link between representation and climate justice. MVM are also launching their Activist Toolkit for conference season this Thursday and are preparing for their new film with acclaimed director Amir Amirani about the need for PR.
items.why: campaigning for proportional representation concerns the electoral system that determines how votes translate into political power.
items.note: New toolkit and event series are also capacity-building for participation, but the substantive focus is electoral reform.

items.h: Democracy Club looking for partners for new project to build a UK-wide database of elected representatives
items.b: Approximately 400 organisations with 22,000 elected people make decisions every day about things that directly affect our lives. Whilst most of the work of local government is transparent, that doesn’t mean it’s accessible. Democracy Club want to partner with organisations who are trying to research, lobby or better understand the people who run local governments — if you are interested, get in touch to discuss.
items.why: a public database of the thousands of elected representatives who make local decisions makes local democratic structures more accessible and accountable.
items.note: Concerns structure and accessibility of local government, which the framework files under elections & decision making.

items.h: The House of Commons has reverted back to in-person sessions
items.b: The House of Commons is abandoning virtual sessions and proxy voting as it returns to pre-pandemic ways. Whilst many MPs are celebrating the change, this will make for a difficult situation for those MPs that benefited from the more flexible arrangements which included those with health issues, childcare demands and problems with commuting distances.
items.why: This matters democratically because the working practices of the House of Commons affect which MPs can effectively participate in legislative scrutiny and representation.
items.note: Treated as Parliament's own functioning rather than participation, since it concerns legislative procedure.

items.h: mySociety looking for new Policy & Advocacy Manager and Front End Designer
items.b: mySociety are in a period of growth at the moment and have been hiring throughout the summer. Their latest open roles include for a new policy position and a Front End Designer . To keep up with the latest jobs releases from mySociety, subscribe to their jobs mailer here , or check the UK Democracy Jobs Board .

items.h: Compass hiring new Campaigns and Projects Office
items.b: There are some really good roles opening up in the democracy sector this fortnight, this one’s from Frances Foley and the team over at Compass with a key focus on building a Progressive Alliance and campaigning for a basic income. Apply and find out more here .
links: Apply and find out more here

items.h: Speakers’ Corner Trust looking for new early career Trustee
items.b: Founded in 2007, the Speakers’ Corner Trust works to develop a more active citizenry, in the fullest sense of the word and true to their namesake. The new Trustee should be between 18–30 years. The post is a great opportunity for someone in their early career to leap into a new space, to flex their creativity and take on new projects, supported and mentored by the Trust board.

items.h: Compass and Unlock Democracy team up to launch new campaign Powering Up
items.b: Powering Up aims to secure public and political support for a programme of wide democratic reform ahead of the next general election. The work follows four phases, identifying a package of reforms commanding broad support, building a network of influencers, creating public awareness and securing commitments from political parties. The project is set to run for a year initially and is funded by Joseph Rowntree Reform Trust .
items.why: This matters democratically because launching a campaign to build public and political backing for democratic reform creates a new organised means for citizens and parties to shape decision-making structures.
items.note: Classified as capacity-building/campaigning rather than the reform content itself.

items.h: As conference season approaches, ERS doubles down on securing party support for PR
items.b: Josiah Mortimer and the team at the Electoral Reform Society are working busily with Labour for a New Democracy and other partners such as Make Votes Matter to boost the case for electoral reform as a record 250 Labour CLPs sign up to back PR.
items.why: This matters democratically because building party support for proportional representation concerns the electoral system that structures political competition.

items.h: Demos running trial of their ‘Combined Choice’ digital democratic method
items.b: Combined Choice represents decisions, not as a series of proposals, but as a whole, they argue. Instead of voting on each proposal in series, decisions are combined in one digital file, decision makers can then put forward an alternative version of the file with the file with the most support enforced. The trial is beginning now in an English town. Find out more about Demos’ Combined Choice method here .
items.why: This matters democratically because trialling a new digital method for aggregating collective choices creates an alternative mechanism for binding decision-making.
items.note: Deliberative/decision-making tools are filed under elections & decision making per framework rule.

items.h: The House of Commons Library has released new briefing papers on the Ministerial Code and Online Harms
items.b: Researchers Chris Rhodes and Hazel Armstrong publish a new briefing paper looking at the UK Ministerial Code and the role of the Independent Adviser. John Woodhouse and Maria Lalic have released new papers on Regulating Online Harms and a reading list of the public reactions to the draft Online Safety Bill.
items.why: This matters democratically because the Ministerial Code briefing concerns executive accountability and standards in public life, while the Online Harms briefing bears on the public information environment.

items.h: Sharon Graham has been elected as Unite’s General Secretary
items.b: After an intense battle to replace the outgoing Len McLuskey, Sharon Graham has come out on top. Graham is the first woman to hold the position in the history of the union and has previously served as the union’s executive officer and as head of its organising and leverage department. Their election marks a return to industrial struggle to advance the union’s cause, over access to politicians and lobbying.
items.note: Internal union leadership election does not materially affect public political power or democratic participation mechanisms.

items.h: Green Party Executive (GPEx) results announced
items.b: Whilst we’re still waiting on the leadership election, the results of this year’s GPEx elections are in , with Green members selecting representatives for the six positions available. View the results here.
items.note: Internal party executive committee results are organisational administration rather than a democracy mechanism story.

items.h: UK Government softens rigid rejection of Scottish referendum demands
items.b: Signalling a partial climbdown , the Scotland Secretary Alistair Jack MP states if Scotland is able to maintain support for a referendum above 60% for an extended period, then “I would acknowledge that there was a desire for a referendum.” Current polling has support for a referendum at around 51%. Previously the UK Government had outright rejected calls for a second independence referendum with the PM stating such suggestions as “ irresponsible and reckless .”
items.why: it concerns the conditions under which a binding collective decision (an independence referendum) might be authorised, a core mechanism of direct democracy.
items.note: Referendums are classified under elections & decision making per the revised framework.

items.h: People’s Newsroom launches
items.b: Megan Lucero and the team at The People’s Newsroom celebrated their launch event today. The new initiative will begin on an experimental basis in Swansea , providing hands-on startup support to design innovative journalism initiatives and invest in community newsroom leaders traditionally marginalised by the media.
items.why: it creates new local journalism capacity, supporting the plural information environment communities need to scrutinise public affairs.

items.b: Government consultation on the privatisation of Channel 4 — closes September 14
items.why: the ownership and public-service status of a major broadcaster bears directly on media plurality in the UK's information environment.
links: Government consultation on the privatisation of Channel 4

items.b: Ofcom consultation on How Ofcom regulates the BBC — closes September 15
items.why: how the BBC is regulated affects the plurality and independence of public-service media central to public debate.
links: Ofcom consultation on How Ofcom regulates the BBC

items.h: We Own It, Media Reform Coalition and others publish briefing on Channel 4 privatisation
items.b: Despite having become more commercialised since the 1990s, Channel 4 still plays a vital role in the UK media landscape. The briefing document by We Own It, Voices of the Listener and Viewer, British Broadcasting Challenge and the Media Reform Coalition, aims to help individuals and organisations respond to the consultation (above).
items.why: the briefing addresses media ownership concentration risk from Channel 4 privatisation, a core information-environment concern, while also equipping people to take part in the consultation.

items.h: Economic scale of misinformation revealed in new report by NewsGuard
items.b: The report shows that fake news sites are being unintentionally funded by major advertisers’ programmatic advertising to the tune of $1 for every $2.16 in digital ad revenue.
items.why: it exposes how commercial advertising structures inadvertently fund disinformation, degrading the reliability of the public information environment.

items.h: Less than one month to apply for major democracy funding opportunity
items.b: Open Society Foundations (OSF) has launched a call for proposals to fund a piece of participatory design work, with quite a short deadline (7 October). They’re looking for a UK-based non-profit organisation to lead a group of partners/stakeholders to develop a participatory process to design a new approach to community safety and policing resource allocation. The purpose is to design a participatory and multi-stakeholder (including police) process, where the process itself educates the public and other actors about policing and community safety budgets and outcomes. The process will result in …
items.note: This is a funding call, sector logistics rather than a reported democratic development.

items.h: New report from Involve and Institute for Government
items.b: The report calls for greater government engagement with the public in designing net zero policies.
items.why: it advocates for greater public engagement in shaping net zero policy, addressing people's practical opportunity to take part in policymaking.

items.h: Elections Bill passes second reading
items.b: The Elections Bill has passed its second reading in the House of Commons by 327 votes to 228.
items.why: it reports a legislative step that will reshape the rules governing how UK elections are administered and contested.

items.h: New shared calendar now available — add your orgs events & operations
items.b: The Election Bill Coalition now hosts a shared operational calendar . Add upcoming events, social media pushes and anything else that is useful for collaboration.
items.note: Internal coalition logistics tool, not a change affecting public participation.

items.h: Elections Bill Democracy Defence Coalition fully operational
items.b: With open Office Hours every Thursday at 12pm, this is the weekly forum to share intel, raise questions, make connections and participate in multi-organisation sessions to draft amendments, coordinate activity and engage with over 60 orgs. To get on the contact list, email matt@fairvote.uk
items.note: Coalition coordination among organisations rather than a new means of public participation.

items.h: Are you a third party campaigner? Answer this survey by Bond, NCVO, SMK and others
items.b: The third party campaigner survey aims to generate an idea of the potential impact of the Elections Bill on affected campaigning groups. Bates Wells have published a briefing covering the impact of the bill on charities and issue-based campaigners.
items.note: A call to complete a survey/briefing announcement, sector logistics rather than a reported democratic change.

items.h: Labour tabling amendments to iron out inconsistencies in accepted forms of voter ID
items.b: Currently the legislation will allow for Oyster 60+ cards and pensioner bus passes, but excludes 18+ Oyster cards and student ID. Kate Robson , Political Adviser to Cat Smith MP, and their team are expected to table amendments this week in an attempt to add these forms, as well as Rail Cards, Young Scot Cards and other forms of non-photo ID cards.
items.why: it concerns which forms of identification will be accepted to vote, directly affecting access to the franchise.

items.h: UK Government announces they are proceeding with legislation to replace all SV elections with FPTP
items.b: The government has announced its intention to bring forward an amendment at committee stage which would extend FPTP to all elections currently held under Supplementary Vote, as originally floated by the Home Secretary in March.
items.why: changing the electoral system used for certain elections alters how votes translate into representation.

items.h: Traveller Movement highlights impact of voter ID on nomadic communities
items.b: An array of reports and briefings in recent months have detailed concerns about the impact of voter ID legislation on poor and minoritised voters. Traveller Movement’s latest research shows that the proposals will have a particularly pronounced impact for Nomadic Travellers who live on sites where access to basic infrastructure is not guaranteed.
items.why: voter ID requirements risk disenfranchising nomadic and minoritised communities, directly affecting inclusive suffrage and access to voting.
items.note: Voter ID accessibility is filed under elections per the franchise/suffrage anchor even though it also touches equality concerns.

items.h: Who’s who on the Election Bill committee?
items.b: If you haven’t seen it already, the parliamentary committee for the Election Bill has been listed here .

items.h: Welsh Government refuses legislative assent for Elections Bill
items.b: The Welsh Government is calling for the Senedd to vote against the bill and have said two sets of election rules on voter ID, one for UK elections and one for Welsh Senedd and council elections, will cause confusion and lower already poor turnout. Welsh Counsel General, Mick Antoniw , is pushing for amendments to the bill.
items.why: a devolved government refusing legislative consent over voter ID rules raises questions about who controls election administration and how that affects turnout across jurisdictions.
links: calling for the Senedd to vote against the bill

items.h: Online Safety Bill: What to expect in Parliament in the coming months
items.b: Carnegie Trust have published a new blog detailing what we can expect to see in Parliament over the next few months as the OSB picks up momentum.
items.note: Forward-looking procedural preview with no substantive content, treated as sector logistics.

items.h: First session of new Joint Committee on the Online Safety Bill
items.b: Last week’s session saw Imran Ahmed — Center for Countering Digital Hate, Danny Stone — Antisemitism Trust, and others including Rio Ferdinand giving evidence. Meanwhile, the call for evidence in the DCMS Select Committee inquiry into Online Safety and Online Harms has now closed.
items.why: parliamentary committee scrutiny of a bill regulating online speech is a mechanism for checking executive-proposed legislation before it becomes law.
items.note: Treated as legislative scrutiny (accountability) given the bill's information-environment subject matter as secondary.

items.h: Stop the Hate — new website to log harms ahead of parliamentary proceedings
items.b: To help collect public testimony for the Pre-legislative Scrutiny Committee, Digital Action have teamed up with Compassion in Politics to create a new site where people can log their experience of social media, providing examples of the harm they currently face. Please do share with your communities and networks, if you would like to add your organisation please reach out to Ruth Price at Digital Action.
items.why: launching a new tool for the public to submit evidence ahead of parliamentary scrutiny creates a new means for people to participate in shaping legislation.
items.note: Sector capacity-building rule applies: a new tool created to help people take part in the legislative process.

items.h: Big Brother Watch launches new report: The State of Free Speech Online
items.b: The report concludes that the Online Safety Bill threatens “state-sanctioned censorship of lawful expression online in a magnitude never previously possible in a liberal democracy”.
items.why: the report assesses whether new legislation would enable state censorship of lawful online expression, bearing on the plurality and freedom of the information environment.

items.h: Snapshot of public and civil society debate on the Online Safety Bill
items.b: Stephen Fry and a large number of LGBTQ+ campaigners have called for changes to the bill arguing that it would “censor” legal free speech. Meanwhile, the LSE’s Prof Damian Tambini says that despite objections on the grounds of free speech the bill needs to pass. UK Human Rights Blog have published their analysis on the bill. The Internet Commission have also done a writeup on their recent event on the OSB.
items.why: public and expert debate over whether the bill censors legal speech reflects contestation over the boundaries of political expression in digital media.
links: despite objections on the grounds of free speech

items.h: Panel discussion and Q&A: The Online Safety Bill’s Impact on Elections and Democracy
items.b: Fair Vote UK and Centre for Democracy will be co-hosting a panel discussion around the OSB’s impact on political discourse and debate in the digital arena, as well as highlighting how civil society can successfully cooperate to make this bill a boon for the health of UK democracy.
items.note: Event/panel listing rather than reported content, treated as sector logistics.

items.h: Police Bill Coalition circulate new parliamentary briefing
items.b: The coalition requests assistance in circulating the document amongst potential Conservative rebels, peers who are former judges, lawyers and campaigners. The document was collaboratively written by a range of the coalition member organisations.
items.why: civil society lobbying to shape legislation affecting policing powers bears on the legal space available for protest and assembly.
items.note: Police Bill concerns protest/assembly restrictions, so filed under rights and freedoms rather than participation.

items.h: Police Bill coalition members stage week of action 11–17 October
items.b: Liberty, Amnesty UK, Stonewall, British Institute for Human Rights, the Quakers and others are holding a Week of Action for human rights in the UK. The arrayed organisations plan to meet as many MPs at a constituency level as possible. To get involved email the team Amnesty here .
items.note: This is an event/campaign notice (week of action) rather than a reported development, treated as sector logistics.

items.h: Conference season is here
items.b: The Labour Party Conference kicks off this weekend with the party likely to debate PR, after more than 314 (almost half) Constituency Labour Parties backed the move and 144 sent motions to conference — making this the highest-known number of motions or expressions of interest in a single topic in recent party history. Holly Morgan and the team at Make Votes Matter are looking forward to releasing their new film Equal Votes ahead of the Labour Party Conference.
items.why: a major party debating proportional representation bears directly on the electoral system through which representatives are chosen.
links: highest-known number of motions or expressions of interest

items.h: Labour Party leadership announces return to electoral college system for leadership elections
items.b: In a move that will likely inflame factional divisions across the party , Keir Starmer’s leadership is pushing for a vote on a return to the electoral college system. Back in 2014, the One Member One Vote system was introduced, giving party members votes equal value — the system was endorsed with 86% of conference delegates backing the measure. The new system, if confirmed by conference, will see the return of a college system, with a third of votes given to Labour MPs, a third to affiliates and unions and a third to members.
items.why: changing how a major party elects its leader alters the internal competitive and representative processes that shape who can seek power.
items.note: Internal party electoral mechanics fall under free political parties within elections & decision making.
links: move that will likely inflame factional divisions across the party

items.h: The Constitution Society publishes new report: The Constitution in Review
items.b: The UK Constitution Monitoring Group (UKCMG) published its first report this fortnight. The report examines legislation, decisions and events over the first 6 months of this year against a set of 20 principles the Group identified as core to the proper operation of the UK constitution. The UKMCG report notes the scale, speed and piecemeal character of the Electios B This report is the first in a recurring series of six-monthly reviews.
items.why: a systematic review of legislation and events against constitutional principles is a scrutiny mechanism holding government conduct to account.

items.h: Reshuffle fallout: Chris Pincher replaces Chloe Smith, Gove retains elections brief
items.b: According to Matt Gallagher, Policy Officer at Fair Vote UK, Michael Gove’s new list of titles from the reshuffle includes mention of elections, so he appears to retain his overarching role in this area. Meanwhile, Chloe Smith MP has been replaced by Chris Pincher MP on heading up the Elections Bill.
items.why: a change in the minister responsible for the Elections Bill affects who controls the machinery shaping electoral law.
items.note: Reshuffle is reported through its effect on control of elections legislation, not general executive scrutiny.

items.h: Can you take a couple of quick surveys to help I Have A Voice Youth Ambassadors with their campaigns?
items.b: Two of their youth ambassador groups are surveying 16–25 year olds, they’d appreciate any efforts to share their surveys with audiences in this bracket. The links to the surveys are below: 1. What do you think we should all be taught about politics? 2. Have you ever experienced or witnessed discrimination in your classroom or curriculum?
items.note: A request to share surveys is sector logistics rather than a reported democratic development.
links: What do you think we should all be taught about politics?
Have you ever experienced or witnessed discrimination in your classroom or curriculum?

items.h: PINF kicking off their new leadership programme
items.b: Joe Mitchell and the team at the Public Interest News Foundation are spending the next 8 weeks developing the leadership capacity of 16 people from indie newsrooms from across the UK. PINF’s Impact Fund received 11 eligible expressions of interest, who will now work with a research expert to discuss and develop their ideas before making final proposals. PINF expect to announce the final grantees by the end of the year.
items.why: building leadership capacity in independent local newsrooms strengthens the plural local journalism that underpins public debate.
items.note: Capacity-building for journalism organisations counts as a democracy story under information & public debate.

items.h: The case for electoral reform from Scotland
items.b: William Bain, former Chair of Labour Campaign for Electoral Reform and former Labour MP for Glasgow North East, argues the case for electoral reform from a Scottish Labour perspective .
items.why: arguing for a different electoral system speaks directly to how competitive and representative UK elections are.

items.h: Upcoming two day democracy event: Innocracy 2021
items.b: Innocracy is a Berlin-based civil society conference running yearly since 2017. The conference is largely focused on democratic innovation.
items.note: Event listing for a non-UK conference, not bearing directly on UK democracy.

items.h: Latest House of Commons Library briefings: election turnout
items.b: Elise Uberoi has published a new briefing on turnout at elections .
items.why: new evidence on election turnout speaks to the extent of electoral participation, which is always filed under elections & decision making.
items.note: Turnout is always classified as elections & decision making per the standing rule.

items.h: New course from Trust The People
items.b: Extinction Rebellion offshoot Trust The People have launched a new free course on democratic transformation through community power. Find out more here .
items.why: it creates a new educational resource intended to build people's capacity to exercise community power in democratic life.
items.note: Sector capacity-building counts as a participation story under the framework's rule.

items.h: mySociety celebrating FOI achievements across Europe with Right to Know Day on Sept 28
items.b: They’re marking Right to Know Day with an online TICTeC, with campaigns and journalists talking about what they’ve achieved through FOI. Check out the event here .
items.note: This is an event listing/celebration rather than a report of institutional accountability or a change in the information environment.

items.h: Rebalancing upstream and downstream scrutiny of government
items.b: Writing for the UK Constitutional Law Association Richard Mackenzie-Gray Scott, Research Fellow at the Bingham Centre for the Rule of Law, highlights the marginalisation of Parliament and judicial deference to Government decisions during the period of pandemic national emergency. That these trends risk the erosion of public trust in government and more widely, in the processes and institutions that are meant to uphold the rule of law and democracy.
items.why: it concerns the marginalisation of parliamentary scrutiny and judicial deference to the executive during an emergency, both core checks on government power.
links: marginalisation of Parliament and judicial deference to Government decisions

items.h: Electoral Commission publish report on the May 2021 elections
items.b: The report covers how the elections were run, how voters found participating in the elections and the experience of campaigning. The EC found that despite the unusual conditions and considerable pressure on election delivery staff and volunteers, the polls were well run.
items.why: it evaluates how well elections were administered and experienced by voters and campaigners, bearing on electoral integrity and accessibility.

items.h: New Welsh proposals for multi-day polling and polling stations in shops and schools
items.b: The Welsh Government is keen to make it easier for people to vote , with new ‘flexible voting’ options being proposed including allowing voting to take place over multiple days, as well as seeing shops and schools hosting polling stations to boost turnout.
items.why: it proposes changes to voting mechanics and polling access intended to make casting a vote easier and boost turnout.
links: keen to make it easier for people to vote

items.h: Saving candidate websites after elections
items.b: Websites for local candidates tend to disappear after elections, this new archiving project is trying to save them. If you’re interested in election archiving, the British Library tried something similar in 2019.
items.note: An archiving project for candidate websites does not itself affect how public power is acquired, exercised or contested.

items.h: London celebrates London Voter Registration Week
items.b: A whole host of democracy orgs including Shout Out UK, the Greater London Assembly, Hope Not Hate and the Association for Citizenship Teaching, have come together to boost registration efforts across the capital.
items.why: it is a campaign to raise voter registration and turnout, which the framework places under elections regardless of framing.
items.note: Turnout and registration campaigns are always elections_decision_making per the framework's settled rule.

items.h: Royal Society of the Arts Catalyst funding applications open 27th September
items.b: The RSA’s Catalyst programme is designed to help seed and scale eligible projects with funding available up to £10,000. Find out more on the RSA website .
items.note: This is a funding call, treated as sector logistics rather than a democracy story.

items.h: Dark Matter Labs on balance governance and ‘behaving well’
items.b: Good long read on the system of governance, risk-holding, autonomy, accountability and power from the #BeyondtheRules project.
items.note: Too abstract and not tied to a specific mechanism of UK democratic power to qualify.

items.h: Firming up democracy’s soft underbelly
items.b: The International Forum for Democratic Studies has launched their final report in their series on sharp power and democratic resilience. The paper, authored by Christopher Walker, Vice President for Studies and Analysis at the National Endowment for Democracy, reviews the findings of eight papers that highlight serious vulnerabilities in the pillars of open societies.
items.why: it reviews evidence on foreign sharp-power tactics that seek to distort the information environment and undermine democratic institutions.
items.note: Content spans several beats generically framed as 'resilience', a non-beat lens; classified by its closest concrete anchor, foreign information operations.

items.h: Scottish Government joins Welsh Government in their refusal to provide consent for Elections Bill
items.b: The Scottish Government recommends that Holyrood does not give consent to the legislation , noting that there is “no evidence of significant electoral fraud to justify voter ID measures in Scotland” . Last month also saw the Welsh Government refuse to support the legislation in the Welsh Senedd . Scottish law makers are acutely aware that the Elections Bill will lead to a two-tier franchise in Scotland, with UK elections requiring ID, and Scottish elections remaining open and free, creating voter confusion and likely depressed turnout. According to Willie Sullivan, Senior Director at Electoral…
items.why: devolved legislatures withholding consent for national electoral legislation affects the structure and legitimacy of voting rules and franchise across UK jurisdictions.
links: Scottish Government recommends that Holyrood does not give consent to the legislation
Welsh Government refuse to support the legislation in the Welsh Senedd
refusal of Legislative Consent is very rare and thus highly signifi

items.h: Confusion over new Minister for the Elections Bill
items.b: Chris Pincher who had apparently replaced Chloe Smith in the recent reshuffle, was thought to be holding the brief for the Elections Bill, but we’ve learned that formally, there is currently no replacement. In other news, Pincher has never rebelled against his party.
items.why: ministerial responsibility for major electoral legislation being unclear affects accountability for how that legislation is scrutinised and implemented.

items.h: Amendments proposed by the Election Bill coalition have all been tabled
items.b: Cat Smith’s office reports that all amendments proposed by the Democracy Defence Coalition have been tabled. Though several amendments are still due in, they are likely to be submitted no later than October 15th according to Matt Gallagher and the team at Fair Vote.
items.why: the tabling of amendments to electoral legislation is part of the process by which the rules governing elections are contested and shaped.

items.h: Elections Bill bad news for Disabled voters
items.b: According to the Disability Rights UK ’s Head of Policy, Fazilet Hadi, the bill removes provisions in the Representation of the People Act 1983 relating to “prescribed equipment” such as tactile voting devices, which currently should be held and offered by all polling stations. Instead, the Bill allows for differential practices and equipment at each polling station. Fazilet outlined the domestic and international laws requiring equality of participation in the electoral process by Disabled people.
items.why: removing mandated accessible voting equipment affects disabled citizens' practical ability to exercise the franchise on equal terms.
links: the bill removes provisions in the Representation of the People Act 1983 relating to “prescribed equipment”

items.h: Voice4Change England hosting voter ID workshop and and drinks in London
items.b: On Monday 18th at the Royal Society of the Arts, Voice4Change England will be hosting a panel discussion and networking party focused on voter ID, particularly with reference to the electoral impacts on BAME communities across the UK.
items.note: Event/networking listing, not itself reporting a democratic development.

items.h: Dr Alan Renwick: Electoral Commission governance changes risk electoral integrity and devolution
items.b: In a new blog for the Constitution Unit, their Deputy Director, Dr Alan Renwick, analyses the proposed changes and subsequent political, electoral and constitutional impacts of the changes. Dr Renwick suggests that elements of the bill relating to the Electoral Commission are concerning and should be significantly changed as the bill works its way through parliament.
items.why: changes to the governance and independence of the Electoral Commission affect the integrity and impartiality of election administration.

items.h: Bates and Wells have released a briefing for third party campaigners
items.b: The briefing goes into detail on the impacts and implications for charities and third parties, including a breakdown of the new spending rules and new digital imprint requirements. We’ve uploaded the briefing to a dropbox link here .
items.why: new spending and imprint rules constrain the ability of civil society and campaigners to associate and campaign around elections.
items.note: Concerns freedom of association/campaigning for third-party civic organisations rather than parties themselves.

items.h: New Democracy Drinks!
items.b: Last Thursday a handful of us got together in a pub in South London for Democracy Drinks, which will hopefully become a new regular event for those of us in the London area. Jessie Joe Jacobs, the new Democracy Network Coordinator, joined us, with their colleague Callum Green, the new Director of Advocacy and Communications at Involve, alongside Ruth Price (Digital Action) who had organised the event, and folks from Best for Britain, the Royal Society, Newspeak House, the3million and more.
items.note: Social event report, sector logistics.

items.h: Jessie Joe Jacobs settles into their new role as Involve’s new Democracy Network Coordinator
items.b: Recently appointed as the new Network Coordinator , Jessie is spending most of their time reaching out to as many of us across the democracy space as possible over the next month. You can find out more about their mission here .
items.note: Staff appointment/role news about an organisation, not a change to democratic participation itself.

items.h: Upcoming joint event on the democratic and electoral impact of the Online Safety Bill
items.b: Teaming up with Fair Vote UK, the Centre for Democracy are co-hosting an upcoming event on the Online Safety Bill (OSB) and its impact on our democratic systems. The panel discussion and Q & A will be held on Zoom on October 13th, register now .
items.note: Event listing/sector logistics, not a substantive democracy story.

items.h: Democracy Club on the lookout for new Non-Executive Directors
items.b: Democracy Club are on the hunt for Non-Executive Directors (NED) that are a step removed from the usual suspects, beyond the democracy space. The team are thinking about how businesses and wider society can help play a role to promote voter turnout and distribute key election information, they’re hoping the NEDs might be able to help them achieve this. In other news, Democracy Club’s Peter Keeling is thinking about Northern Ireland ahead of the region’s upcoming Assembly elections in May 2022.
items.note: Organisational recruitment notice, not a change to democratic participation.

items.h: Powering Up project begins first stage of polling
items.b: Recently funded by JRRT, Unlock Democracy and Compass have partnered on a new project — Powering Up — to push for democratic reform. They are currently taking their first steps with polling to help identify target voter demographics, working with IPPR and ERS.
items.note: Reports on a project's internal polling activity rather than a change affecting public participation.

items.h: The Bakers’ Union has disaffiliated from the Labour Party
items.b: The Bakers Food and Allied Workers Union (BFAWU) announced during the Labour Party Conference that it has decided to disaffiliate from the Labour Party , accusing Labour leader Keir Starmer of waging a “factional war”. The Bakers’ Union helped found and fund the Labour Party in 1902.
items.note: Internal party-union affiliation dispute does not clearly engage a democratic mechanism of public power.

items.h: Reboot GB developing new Democracy Hubs
items.b: Liz Crosbie and the team at Reboot GB are developing a new practice of Open Source Democracy, based around Democracy Hubs , new local bases for activists to team together, disconnected from national campaigns and with the intention of outfoxing potential campaigning restrictions in the Elections Bill.
items.why: the creation of new local activist hubs changes people's practical capacity to organise and campaign, including around anticipated legal restrictions.
items.note: Sector capacity-building creating new means of participation.

items.h: Demos looking at the future of activism
items.b: The last few years have seen radical changes to activism, from the rise of precarious worker unions, the proliferation of direct action tactics from XR to Stop the Coup to GND Rising, the mass takeup of mutual aid groups across the country as a result of COVID-19 and the changing and intensifying political and legislative climate. Ciaran Cummins , Researcher at Demos, is about to start a new project at Demos looking into the role of activism during the pandemic and its future and is keen to talk to anyone interested.
items.note: A research project call for interviewees, not a new participatory capacity created.

items.h: Shout Out UK preparing for Political Literacy Week 2021
items.b: Shout Out UK’s Political Literacy Week will be held from November 4th.
items.why: the launch of a political literacy programme creates a new resource for people to understand and engage with democratic life.
items.note: Sector capacity-building programme aimed at civic engagement.

items.h: Labour Party Conference soundly rejects motion committing Labour to PR
items.b: The vote at conference was declared too close to call and a card vote was declared. Whilst 79.5% of CLP delegates backed the motion, 95% of affiliates — trade unions — voted against the motion. Campaigners seem to have expected this result, as trade unions have not held their annual conferences as usual due to COVID-19, and as a result similar supporting motions have not had time to progress through the unions. Campaigners at Make Votes Matter are confident they will return with the unions on board in the future. The rejected motion on PR was the most widely supported single topic ahead of con…
items.why: the vote reflects a major party's internal decision on whether to pursue changing the electoral system that determines how votes translate into seats.
links: was declared too close to call

items.h: Labour for a New Democracy: What to do after Labour Conference
items.b: L4ND are holding an event this Thursday on what to do now after the Labour Party Conference . L4ND and their allies were instrumental in getting the PR vote onto the conference floor last week.
items.note: Event listing/sector logistics.
links: L4ND are holding an event this Thursday on what to do now after the Labour Party Conference

items.h: Forward Democracy lights up Labour Conference with #LabourLovesPR projection
items.b: Teaming up with the Led By Donkeys projection team, Forward Democracy raised the stakes for last Monday’s Labour Conference vote on proportional representation with a huge 100ft message to Keir Starmer and attending delegates.
items.why: the campaign stunt aims to mobilise public and political support for reforming the electoral system used in UK elections.
items.note: Campaigning action tied to an electoral-system reform debate.

items.h: New poll finds 52% in favour of PR
items.b: The survey found 52% back PR, 17% oppose, with 31% don’t knows, finding broad enthusiasm for electoral reform. The poll was conducted by Number Cruncher Politics and commissioned by Labour for a New Democracy.
items.why: it reports public opinion on changing the electoral system used to choose representatives, which shapes how votes translate into seats.

items.h: Stir to Action release new report on ‘Building democratic culture, skills and partnership in policy-led regions’
items.b: Sharing the direct experiences of the democratic business community, the report poses questions around how we can overcome the lack of strategic leadership surrounding democratic business, in short — how policy commitments by local government can be translated into practical action and new opportunities .
items.why: it addresses building civic capacity and skills to translate local democratic policy into practical participation opportunities.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building report on civic participation rather than local government structure.

items.h: Green Party of England and Wales unveils new leadership pair
items.b: Succeeding Sian Berry and Jonathan Bartley, Carla Denyer and Adrian Ramsay are taking over as joint-leaders at a key time for the party, with rising membership figures following the continuing exodus from the Labour Party, climate and environmental concern hot in the national consciousness, healthy local election results and national polling higher than the Lib Dems and growing fortunes for sister green parties across the EU in France and Germany. Denyer is the Green Party’s MP for Bristol West. Ramsay formerly served as Deputy Leader and worked with Caroline Lucas MP on their successful bid f…
items.note: Internal party leadership change is organisational news, not a democracy mechanism story.
links: national polling higher than the Lib Dems

items.h: Over half of Conservative Party members want to elect their Chairman directly
items.b: In a new survey of the Conservative membership run by ConservativeHome, 56% believe that the post of Party Chairman should be elected by the membership, 70% want the power to directly elect “at least some” of the Party Board, and 75% believe that the leadership should be more accountable to members.
items.why: it concerns whether party members can directly elect party officials, a form of internal political competition and party democracy.
items.note: Party internal democracy filed under elections per the political-parties anchor.

items.h: Germany enjoys huge 76.6% electoral turnout in their recent federal elections
items.b: Back in 2019, the UK recorded a 67.3% turnout rate, having last broken the 70% mark back in 1997 with 71.3%. The CDU met with disappointing results in their first federal election without Angela Merkel since 2005. SPD leader Olaf Scholz has indicated they want to broker a coalition agreement by Christmas and are currently exploring their options .
items.why: it compares national turnout rates, a direct measure of electoral participation.
items.note: Turnout is always filed under elections & decision making per framework rule.

items.h: Hacked Off launches new campaign asking the question why IPSO hasn’t launched any investigations yet
items.b: The regulator IPSO was set up in 2014 in the wake of the phone-hacking scandal, reportedly with the power to commence standards investigations and to issue serious “million pound” fines. Hacked Off highlight that seven years later we haven’t seen any investigations or fines issued , despite the serious failure of a range of news publications, they argue.
items.why: it concerns whether the press regulator is holding news publications to account for standards failures, affecting the reliability of the public information environment.
links: we haven’t seen any investigations or fines issued

items.h: Centenary Action Group release new briefing on Online Safety Bill
items.b: The briefing by the coalition is focused on online harms against women and makes recommendations to include specific measures to address online harms against women and girls.
items.why: it seeks legal protections against gendered online harms, a matter of equal protection and freedom from discrimination.
items.note: Gender equality as a rights issue filed under rights & freedoms rather than information despite the legislative vehicle being the Online Safety Bill.

items.h: The Guardian no longer disclosing their print circulation figures
items.b: Joining the ranks of the Telegraph and News UK, the Guardian will no longer be transparent with regards to its print circulation metrics . The paper claims that this decision is due to a focus on diversity in their metrics, though Press Gazette suggests this may be due to dwindling figures.
items.why: reduced transparency about circulation undermines public and analysts' ability to assess media reach and plurality.
links: the Guardian will no longer be transparent with regards to its print circulation metrics

items.h: Facebook is starting to share how its algorithms demote items in news feeds
items.b: The social giant has released new “ content distribution guidelines ” providing some information on how the platform’s algorithm’s work.
items.why: greater transparency about algorithmic curation affects the public's ability to understand how political information is filtered and encountered.

items.h: Goodbye Social Democracy, James Plunkett on the future of government
items.b: In this Medium long read the author of End State , James Plunkett, takes a deep dive into the problem of the social settlement in the digital age.
items.note: A speculative essay on the social settlement lacks a concrete democratic mechanism.

items.h: Latest YouGov research shows Labour & Conservatives neck and neck in the Red Wall
items.b: According to the results of YouGov’s latest MRP polling , the Conservative Party’s influence in Red Wall seats has reduced to levels last seen during the 2017 General Election.
items.why: This matters democratically because polling on party support reflects the state of electoral competition between parties for representation.
