The amendments provide updates to the hastily passed Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022 , which attempted to crack down on the prevalence of dirty money within London.
items.why: this matters democratically because it concerns legislative measures to close loopholes enabling economic crime and corruption that undermine institutional accountability and transparency.
links: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Bill

items.h: Voters reject plans to leave European Court of Human Rights
items.b: Rishi Sunak is reportedly considering plans to leave the European Court of Human Rights at the next general election despite wide condemnation from legal experts and human rights groups, as well as the Conservatives’ political opponents. However, according to a poll run by the Byline Times , 54% of voters want the UK to remain within the ECHR compared to just 23% who want to leave.
items.why: this matters democratically because withdrawing from the ECHR would remove an external judicial constraint on UK executive power and alter how rights are adjudicated and enforced.
items.note: Classified under rule of law because the mechanism at issue is judicial constraint via an international court, not the rights themselves.

items.b: 14th Sept 2.30pm, How To Workshop: Improving Disabled Political Representation & Participation, Register
items.note: Treated as an event listing rather than a new participation resource or programme.

items.b: 18th Oct 2.30pm, Lunchtime Briefing with My Vote My Voice, Register

items.h: Are you getting ready for the party conference season? Democracy Network want to know
items.b: Democracy Network are tracking who’s doing what across the democracy sector this conference season. Are you organising an event, canvassing party members, organising a conference vote? We’re looking to understand who’s doing what, to better understand how the wider democracy movement can help support them, the Network are looking to partner on events, contact Democracy Network Director Jessie Joe Jacobs if you’d like support, speaking opportunities or sponsorship — add your party conference activities into this sheet .
links: contact Democracy Network Director Jessie Joe Jacobs if you’d like support, speaking opportunities or sponsorship

items.h: Prepare for the first ever mySociety Awards
items.b: Celebrating their 20th year as an organisation, mySociety wants to give a little back to those who’ve used their services to make positive change over that whole period . So if you know someone who used mySociety services and made an impact, now or as far back as the 2000s, go ahead and nominate them with this form .
items.note: Organisation's own award nomination, excluded per framework guidance.

items.h: Operation Black Vote launch new Civic Leadership Programme
items.b: In partnership with Westminster City Council, Operation Black Vote is launching a new and unique civic leadership programme aimed at nurturing future Westminster leaders and encouraging people from black and minority ethnic communities to get more involved in civic and political leadership — find out more (deadline has been extended).
items.why: this matters democratically because it creates a new programme building civic and political leadership capacity among underrepresented communities, expanding practical means of participation.
items.note: Counted as sector capacity-building since a new programme was launched, not organisational news.

items.h: Labour appoint new Shadow Minister for Democracy
items.b: The new Shadow Minister for Democracy Florence Eshalomi MP will sit within the Levelling Up dept.
items.note: Personnel appointment within a political party, not a change to democratic mechanisms.

items.h: Business and Democracy Commission to launch interim report
items.b: On 12th September, the Business and Democracy Commission are to hold their inaugural meeting, asking the question: when it comes to the relationship between democracy and business, what does good or bad look like? Register for the Zoom launch and crowdfund the effort here .
items.note: Launch of an exploratory commission and crowdfund/registration event, not a new participation mechanism or reported change.

items.h: I Have A Voice public new report on political literacy in the UK
items.b: Capturing Political Literacy? Towards a nationwide measure in the UK is a new report published by I Have A Voice (IHAV), in partnership with thinktank The 89 Initiative . The report is the first output of a plan of work to better define and understand what a nationwide measure of political literacy might look like. Email Rebecca Deegan , Co-founder of IHAV, with any questions.
items.note: A research report proposing a future measure of political literacy, not itself a tool or change affecting participation.
links: Capturing Political Literacy? Towards a nationwide measure in the UK

items.h: Carnegie UK kickstart new Democratic Wellbeing Champions programme
items.b: Whilst the open call is closed now, until last week Carnegie UK were looking to identify 12 new ‘democratic wellbeing champions’ . Envisioned as critical friends and advisors for their new Engaging Democracy programme, the small cohort will assist Carnegie in the conception of their ongoing work around better understanding democratic wellbeing in relation to participatory democracy in Scotland. So if you’re into democratic wellbeing research, get in touch with Hannah Paylor at Carnegie for more info.
items.why: this matters democratically because it creates a new advisory network intended to shape work on participatory democracy and democratic wellbeing in Scotland.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building since it launches a new champions programme feeding into a participatory democracy initiative.
links: were looking to identify 12 new ‘democratic wellbeing champions’

items.h: Democracy Box prepare to upscale their prototype proof of concept
items.b: Yvonne Murphy of Omidaze Productions is on the cusp of publishing their new report on their proof of concept Democracy Box prototypes , after which they’ll begin a year of partnership work with the Electoral Commission, and conversations with the BBC to upscale their prototypes. In addition to all of this, Yvonne and the team are trying to secure multi-year core funding — and finalise their last trial of The Talking Shop in Caerphilly this winter. Interested? Contact Yvonne for more information.
items.why: this matters democratically because it develops and scales new tools (Democracy Box, Talking Shop) intended to expand people's practical means of civic engagement, in partnership with the Electoral Commission.

items.h: DemocracyNext publish new Assembly Guide
items.b: The Democracy Next Assembly Guide breaks down a citizens’ assembly into phases, examples and downloadable templates. They’re aiming to expand their guide in coming months, being published in more languages and with advice on utilising it in different settings, ie schools, unions and workplaces. Download the guide now .
items.why: this matters democratically because it publishes a practical guide expanding capacity to run citizens' assemblies, a deliberative decision-making mechanism.
items.note: Citizens' assembly resources are classified under elections & decision making per the framework's boundary rule, not participation.

items.h: UPPER Coalition release report calling on the UK government to urgently publish a public engagement strategy.
items.b: The UPPER coalition, which includes Climate Outreach , Ashden , Involve and the Climate Citizens research group at Lancaster University has this week called for the UK government to publish its strategy urgently after committing to produce a public engagement plan at Cop26 in 2021. As part of their calls, the group has released two reports. The first report , led by Climate Outreach, makes four key asks and outlines the vital components for a public engagement strategy to succeed, whilst the second report , led by Involve, brings together thinking from the different fields of public engagement…
items.why: this matters democratically because the coalition is campaigning for the government to establish a formal public engagement strategy that would create new channels for citizen input into policy.
items.note: This is an advocacy campaign for a future mechanism rather than a report of one already created.
links: Climate Citizens research group at Lancaster University

items.h: Constitution Unit looking for a Research Assistant for new project on parliamentary procedure
items.b: The Constitution Unit has recently launched a new project — ‘The Politics of Parliamentary Procedure’ — funded by the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC). They are now looking to recruit a Research Assistant for that project. The project will explore the role of different actors in choosing and changing procedures in the UK House of Commons, with a particular focus on understanding the extent, causes, and consequences of government influence.
items.note: A job advertisement for a research post, which is sector logistics rather than a reported democratic change.

items.h: Heading to Labour Conference? Don’t miss Politics for the Many’s Democracy Fringe
items.b: The Politics for the Many event will see former Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell MP in conversation with democracy heavyweights from across the Labour movement. The event is supported by Unlock Democracy, Make Votes Matter, Labour Campaign for Electoral Reform and Labour for a New Democracy. Register now .
items.note: Event listing/fringe promotion, not a substantive democracy development.

items.h: 50:50 Parliament launch new Labour-focused public speaking training
items.b: The 50:50 Parliament training will run on 12th September at 8pm, delivered by the Lord Mayor of Oxford, Cllr Lubna Arshad. Find out more .
items.why: this creates a new training resource that builds people's capacity and confidence to take part in political life.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building since it launches a new means of participation rather than reporting org news.

items.h: Recursive Public awarded 100k grant from OpenAI
items.b: As part of their $1M grants programme Democratic Inputs to AI , OpenAI have awarded 10 applicants $100k. Recursive Public, a new collaboration between a set of independent researchers, including Carl Miller and Flynn Devine, Chatham House and vTaiwan, has been awarded one such tranche of funding. Their project aims to develop participatory methods for AI development, identifying areas of consensus and disagreement among the international Artificial Intelligence (AI) community, policymakers, and the general public on key questions of AI governance. Find out more .
items.note: Grant funding news for an international AI-governance research project, not clearly tied to UK democratic mechanisms.

items.h: Blagrave announce new Pathways Fund for youth-led changemaker orgs
items.b: The fund aims to offer 5–7 grants between £60–90k over three years to emergent youth-led groups and collectives across England. Find out more and share it with your network .
items.note: A funding call/grant announcement, treated as sector logistics.

items.h: UK Democracy Fund seeking digital expertise for new voter participation campaign
items.b: Ellen Berry at the UK Democracy Fund is looking for ambitious and effective non-partisan digital campaigns focused on voter participation. The Fund is looking to potentially fund and seriously scale up their work to hit their target goal of one million more people from lower propensity voting groups to register and vote in the next General Election — contact Ellen for more information .
items.note: Recruitment/funding call seeking a partner, not a reported change in participation mechanisms.

items.h: Newspeak House spinning up project to help new MPs set up their offices effectively
items.b: Newspeak House — the London College of Political Technology , report that they are undertaking the first phase of work on a new project to update and maintain best practice around setting up new MPs offices effectively, in light of changing technologies and organisational practices. The first phase, user research with MP office staff has started this month — so if you know any MP staffers that might be up for a chat, let them know — whilst they’ve received some small seed funding for this first phase, they are looking for funding opportunities for the remaining £85,000 to complete the project,…
items.note: Funding call for organisational capacity work, treated as sector logistics.
links: Newspeak House — the London College of Political Technology
if you know any MP staffers that might be up for a chat, let them know

items.h: Greater London Authority Democracy Hub announce successful grant applicants
items.b: GLA Democracy Hub have announced their recent awards for work in reaching out to under-registered and under-represented communities across London. 14 successful applicants were chosen, including The Politics Project , Disability Action Haringey and the Bulgarian Centre for Social Integration and Culture . Award recipients will receive between £25–50k and will now work to deliver impartial voter registration and voter ID informational activity and awareness raising across the capital. Congratulations to the successful applicants! Find out more about the GLA Democracy Hub Phase Two grant .
items.why: this funds new voter registration and voter ID outreach work aimed at increasing electoral participation among under-registered communities.
items.note: Voter registration and turnout work is filed under elections per the standing turnout rule.
links: Bulgarian Centre for Social Integration and Culture

items.h: SMK launch new report and ask, is our democracy at a tipping point?
items.b: Launching their new report Defending our democratic space: a call to action , Sheila McKechnie and Civil Exchange argue that the UK is now approaching a tipping point with regards to the democratic health of the United Kingdom. The report urges civil society organisations to speak out about this impending crisis before it is too late. Read the press release here .
items.why: the report addresses shrinking operating space for civil society organisations to organise and speak out on public affairs.
items.note: Framed around 'democratic space' for civic organisations, mapped to civic space rather than participation capacity.
links: Defending our democratic space: a call to action

items.h: VocalEyes looking for funding to upgrade their platform
items.b: VocalEyes CIC runs an amazing and long-running community participation and engagement platform. With a decade of success behind them they’re looking to the future and — importantly — a tech upgrade for their 10 year old platform. They’re looking for funding to expand, as well as to develop their tech stack, including the use of new generative AI. Can you assist them, or any have leads for them to follow up? Contact Arthur at VocalEyes .
items.note: Funding appeal for an existing organisation's platform upgrade counts as org-as-organisation news, not a new participation mechanism.

items.h: Catalyst publish list of third sector funding opportunities
items.b: Catalyst has published a full list of third sector funding organisations — check it out now.
links: published a full list of third sector funding organisations

items.h: My Vote My Voice urge govt to focus on accessible voting ahead of next year’s election
items.b: Members of the accessible voting coalition My Vote My Voice handed in their petition calling on the UK Government and Parliament to urgently focus on accessible voting measures ahead of the next elections. Hannah Molloy of United Response said ‘this means a lot to me, as I’m autistic and struggle a lot due to voting barriers’. Niamh Mitchell from Ambitious About Autism remarked the campaign is really important as it will ‘give individuals like me who are autistic or who have a learning disability the opportunity to vote just like everyone else’. Tom Pursglove MP, Minister of State for Disabled…
items.why: accessible voting measures determine whether disabled and neurodivergent people can practically exercise their suffrage on equal terms
items.note: Advocacy/petition stage, not yet an implemented change.

items.h: Mid-Bedfordshire by-election could be a watershed moment for tactical voting
items.b: With both Labour and the Liberal Democrats planning to fight hard for Nadine Dorries’ former seat, the upcoming Mid-Beds by-election could see the Tories hang on to control despite local anger with the former Secretary of State. But Professor Roy Lowe suggests this could be the moment to clarify once and for all that tactical voting is the only way to remove the Tories from power given the flaws of our electoral system.
items.why: tactical voting behaviour interacts with the electoral system to shape whether elections are genuinely competitive and how votes translate into political power
items.note: Largely opinion/analysis of a by-election but engages the mechanics of the electoral system.

items.h: Newspeak House begin planning Election Tech Handbook
items.b: Edward Saperia, Director of Newspeak House, has begun planning for next year’s Election Tech Handbook, the successor initiative to the 2017 and 2019 Election Tech Handbooks which functioned as a central repository, convening hub and signpost for projects, election data, communication channels and events during those general elections. Get in touch with Ed to find out more or join their WhatsApp Group .
items.why: building a shared repository and coordination hub for election-tech projects creates new practical means for civic groups to engage with and support elections
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building (new hub/resource) rather than the electoral machinery itself.

items.h: The Bristol Cable ask their readers to help them with local election monitoring
items.b: In 2019 The Bristol Cable worked with readers to monitor election advertising by asking them to submit pictures of campaign material they received physically and via social media. In the run up to the next general election they will be repeating the process, asking voters to send them content so they can analyse dodgy bar charts and call out misinformation wherever they see it. Relatedly, see Electionleaflets.org .
items.why: crowdsourced monitoring of campaign material helps expose misleading political advertising and improves the public information environment around elections
items.note: Also involves readers actively participating, but the core mechanism is scrutiny of political messaging.
links: worked with readers to monitor election advertising

items.h: National Policy Forum declares ‘FPTP flawed & damaging’
items.b: The Labour Party’s internal policy process, the National Policy Forum, has formally announced that the UK electoral system is a ‘driver of the distrust and alienation we see in politics’. The statement was made following weeks of extensive consultation across the whole party, including the membership, affiliated trade unions and elected NPF reps. Labour for a New Democracy remarked that ‘this is a significant turning point’ .
items.why: a major party formally adopting a critical stance on the electoral system signals a potential future change to how votes translate into political power

items.h: New research suggests the public back expanding electoral franchise to 16 year olds
items.b: New research commissioned by The Body Shop and The British Youth Counci l has found that 64% of adults would have liked to have had the vote at 16. The findings build on existing evidence that suggests that if a younger person is engaged in the democratic process during such formative years in their development, the more likely they are to participate in later life.
items.why: new evidence on public support for lowering the voting age bears directly on who is entitled to vote and thus who can shape political power

items.h: Institute for Government and Bennett Institute publish new report on electoral reform
items.b: The new report Electoral Reform and the constitution: What might a different voting system mean for the UK? , published as part of the Institute for Government / Bennett Institute ‘Review of the UK Constitution’ looks at the potential implications of electoral reform for the House of Commons for the functioning of the UK Constitution.
items.why: it examines how changing the electoral system for the House of Commons would reshape political competition and representation in the UK constitution
links: Electoral Reform and the constitution: What might a different voting system mean for the UK?

items.h: Liz Truss’ resignation honours list signals turning point for Lords reform, says Electoral Reform Society
items.b: The House of Lords has hit rock bottom support among the public according to recent research by the think tank Labour Together . Their report found that only 21 per cent of people trust Peers to act in the best interests of the people, behind journalists (22%), MPs (24%) and business leaders (34%). Now that Truss is handing out 49 honours despite her short and tumultuous tenure in №10, Mike Wright at the Electoral Reform Society says the UK could be reaching a turning point in terms of attitudes to the second chamber.
items.why: it concerns public trust in and appointments to the unelected second chamber, a standards-in-public-life and accountability issue
items.note: Treated as government accountability (appointments/standards) rather than elections since the Lords are not elected.
links: recent research by the think tank Labour Together

items.h: Talk Shop plan new Win-Win Workout on local transport planning
items.b: Last week Perry Walker, Bob Bollen and the Talk Shop team ran a Win-Win Workout on homelessness, now they’re turning their attention to how consensual solutions can be applied to the tricky issue of local transport planning.
items.why: it creates a deliberative process for reaching consensual local transport decisions, which the framework treats as decision-making machinery
items.note: Deliberative/consensus-building processes are classified under elections & decision making per framework rule, not participation.

items.h: Global People Power invite comment on their 2023–2025 strategic plan
items.b: Barnaby Flynn of Global People Power is working to find agreement between a range of global democracy organisations from The Alternative to Extinction Rebellion on what daily act like Clap for Carers might find traction. Barnaby is also seeking comment on their strategic plan .
items.note: Organisational strategic-plan consultation, not a change to democratic participation itself.

items.h: Research for Action launch new report on local government auditing
items.b: The new report Local Audit: Why Public Interest Needs to Count by Gloria Dawson and the team at Research for Action looks at the collapse of the local government auditing regime over the past decade and its wider impact on local democracy. The report argues that audit should be treated as an exercise conducted in the public interest and for the public good, but has largely been sidelined over the last decade due to austerity impacts and the abolition of the Audit Commission in 2015. Find out more about the report by contacting Gloria and the team at Research for Action .
items.why: it examines the collapse of local government audit oversight, a mechanism for holding local authorities answerable for public spending
links: Local Audit: Why Public Interest Needs to Count

items.h: This Is The North 2023 coming to Preston
items.b: People’s Powerhouse’s annual convention will be coming to Preston later this year — follow them on X (formerly known as Twitter) for updates.
items.note: Event listing/announcement only.

items.h: Civic Power Fund reflect on their efforts to embed community organising in Warm Welcome spaces
items.b: Last winter Good Faith and Civic Power Fund worked to experiment with building community power through supporting organisers around Warm Welcome spaces. Explore the findings of their community organising pilots in this blog by CPF Director, Martha Mackenzie. Funding for the pilots was provided by JRF , Trust for London and JRSST-CT .
items.why: it reports on efforts to build community organising capacity, creating new means for people to take part in local civic life

items.h: People’s Powerhouse, CLES and others consider a Northern Manifesto
items.b: Last week’s brilliant New Economy North Social (#NENSocial) in Manchester focused on what a Northern Manifesto might look like. See here for the full range of suggestions from the event. #NENSocial is supported by CLES , People’s Powerhouse , IPPR North and NEON .
items.note: Event report without a clear democratic mechanism beyond networking and idea-sharing.
links: See here for the full range of suggestions

items.h: Fabian Society calls for greater devolution to tackle inequality
items.b: The Fabian Society’s Commission on Poverty and Regional Inequality has published its final report A Good Life In All Regions: Uniting Our Country To End Poverty , calling for greater devolution of power to mayors and councils to strengthen the fabric of regional governance. In response to the report, Local Trust’s policy officer Steven Barclay has gone further in arguing that a hyperlocal focus also needs to exist to rebalance power and prosperity within specific regions .
items.why: it concerns the structure and powers of local and regional government tiers, which shape how binding collective decisions are made closer to citizens.
items.note: Devolution of powers to local/regional government falls under elections_decision_making per the framework's boundary rule.
links: Fabian Society’s Commission on Poverty and Regional Inequality
A Good Life In All Regions: Uniting Our Country To End Poverty
rebalance power and prosperity within specific regions

items.h: Scoping of £10m community wealth fund for Cornwall
items.b: With potential funding from the Public Works Loan Board and UK Infrastructure Bank, and with advice from the UCL Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose, the project — currently in a scoping phase — aims to be co-owned with Cornwall Council. The proposal is to include citizens’ assemblies and panels for the region, with governance of the fund drawn from representatives of the assembly.
items.why: it proposes citizens' assemblies as decision-making machinery to govern a public fund, directly engaging deliberative democratic structures.
items.note: Citizens' assemblies are classified under elections_decision_making, not participation, per the revised framework.

items.h: Electoral Commission suffers massive cyber attack targeting electoral registers
items.b: The attack took place in August 2021 and was identified in October 2022 after suspicious activity was detected on Electoral Commission systems . The perpetrators accessed servers containing the EC’s email, control systems and copies of electoral registries — including personal data of all of those who registered to vote between 2014–2022.
items.why: a breach of electoral registers threatens the security and integrity of the electoral administration system that underpins voter registration.
links: suspicious activity was detected on Electoral Commission systems

items.h: Unlock Democracy demands voter protection in the wake of EC hack
items.b: Russia has been widely reported as the actor behind the hack (above) with fears the data could be weaponised and used to fuel disinformation efforts. Unlock Democracy has written to the Electoral Commission asking them to take urgent action to prevent this — add your name here .
items.why: it concerns calls to protect voters and electoral data integrity following a breach of the electoral register, a core electoral administration issue.
links: fears the data could be weaponised

items.h: Royal Society of the Arts enters dispute with staff over pay rises
items.b: Staff at the Royal Society of the Arts who have been attempting to unionise since at least last October, have overwhelmingly voted for strike action by 93%, on a 79% turnout of members. The RSA have so far resisted acknowledging the union, with staff reporting a ‘toxic culture of fear’ around unionisation. Another staff member said ‘negotiations have been totally dismissive, anti-democratic and hypocritical. The RSA talks a lot about collaboration, openness, participation but they are failing to put this into practice’. The RSA responded with a press statement on their website.
items.why: it concerns workers' freedom of association and ability to organise a union without employer interference.
items.note: Freedom of association for a civic/professional organisation's staff falls under rights_freedoms_civic_space.

items.h: Conservative Party attempt to spoof local papers in pre-election push
items.b: As reported in Private Eye recently, the Conservative Party has spent considerable resources distributing party campaigning leaflets to residents across the country, with the leaflets designed to resemble local newspapers including convincing looking mastheads featuring the local constituency name. However, the Party has fallen foul again (they’ve tried this before) in their attempts, with genuine local newspapers of the same name, including the Wolverhampton Chronicle, Dudley Chronicle and Sandwell Chronicle, all distributed to areas where Midland News publishes their own trademarks to such t…
items.why: disguising party political material as genuine local news undermines the public's ability to distinguish trustworthy information from partisan messaging.
links: Byline Times research has found two thirds of Conservative voters want the fake newspaper practice banned

items.h: Half of UK voters consider UK government as institutionally corrupt
items.b: Earlier this year the UK achieved its worst ever level in Transparency International’s Global Corruption Perceptions Index , with only four other countries — Qatar, Myanmar, Azerbaijan and Oman — seeing their rankings decline by as much. According to a new poll for the Byline Times , a majority of voters (53%) now believe the Sunak Ministry is ‘institutionally corrupt’. 57% said they believed the level of corruption in government had increased in their lifetime and only 7% said it had decreased instead.
items.why: widespread public perception of institutional corruption and declining trust reflects on the accountability and integrity of government.
links: Transparency International’s Global Corruption Perceptions Index

items.h: Global philanthropists consider $500m global fund for local journalism
items.b: A group including the MacArthur Foundation, Knight Foundation and others are considering to put a seriously large dent into the global problem of a depleted local news sphere. Such a fund could be announced as early as this month .
items.why: funding for local journalism affects the plurality and availability of public-interest information that citizens rely on to hold power to account, including in the UK.
items.note: Global initiative treated as comparative/relevant evidence for UK local journalism decline.

items.h: Reflecting on PINF’s Local News Map research
items.b: Joe Mitchell and the team have published their reflections on the Local News Map . Launched earlier in the summer the map constitutes the first ever comprehensive mapping of local news journalism in the UK. Following feedback from various quarters , they’re reopening the map for people to add any media outlets they may have missed, and they’re going to review their methodology, in conversation with interested parties throughout the autumn.
items.why: it maps and tracks the state of local journalism, which underpins the public's access to a plural information environment about local public affairs.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building (a research/mapping tool) for local journalism, not organisational admin.
links: published their reflections on the Local News Map

items.h: Democracy Network AI & Democracy WhatsApp Group to begin regular meetings
items.b: Are you interested in applying or experimenting with the new AI large language model tools? Concerned about the impact of AI on democratic processes? Join the Democracy Network’s new WhatsApp Group , Isabella Roberts is organising new regular catch ups starting soon on Thursday afternoons.
items.note: A discussion/networking group announcement is sector logistics rather than a new means of democratic participation.

items.h: EU report finds participation in cultural activities enhances civic engagement
items.b: The report published by the European Commission analyses the link between democracy and culture , finding that those who participate in cultural activities are far more likely to engage in the civic and democratic life of their community. Thanks to Yvonne Murphy for recommending this one!
items.why: it presents evidence on what drives people's engagement in civic and democratic life, bearing on the conditions for participation.
items.note: International (EU) research offered as general comparative evidence rather than UK-specific.
links: analyses the link between democracy and culture

items.h: Constitution Unit asks, is confrontational questioning good or bad for democratic politics?
items.b: Ruxandra Serban, Associate Lecturer in Democratic and Authoritarian Politics at UCL, examines the role of contentious styles of debate in legislative bodies modelled on the Westminster System and whether the aggressive and confrontational cultures that surround these democratic bodies are desirable.
items.why: it examines whether the confrontational culture of legislative questioning helps or hinders effective parliamentary scrutiny of the executive.
links: examines the role of contentious styles of debate in legislative bodies modelled on the Westminster System

View the database here — Have we missed something? Add it here !
A screenshot of Zac Down’s volunteer run Online Postal Vote site, soon to be retired
items.why: it concerns the retirement of a volunteer tool that helped voters access and understand postal voting, a mechanism of electoral participation.

items.b: Monthly news, jobs, grants and gossip from across the democracy sector, brought to you by James Moulding and Max Roche of the UK Democracy Network . Read by 400+ democracy organisations. We read everyone’s newsletters & research so you don’t have to. If you want us to cover yours, let us know : hello@democracynetwork.org.uk

Editor’s note: We are making some changes to the Democracy Map, Jobs, Events and Funding Airtable lists over the next month, whilst those changes are underway, the jobs and events lists may appear out of date, apologies for the inconvenience.

Thanks to everyone who joined us last week for our Democracy Check-In . We were joined by Myf Nixon — mySociety, Katy Rubin — Legislative Theatre, Artem Zhiganov — Harmonica, Carly Walker-Dawson — Involve, Mohammed Afridi — Civic Power Fund, Zsofia Banuta — Unhack Democracy, Tim Hughes — Open Government Partnership, Ruth Hannah — The People’s Powerhouse, Kathie Conn — Extinction Rebellion UK, Peter Keeling — Democracy Club, Joe Mitchell — Public Interest News Foundation and Edward Saperia — Newspeak House.

items.h: Welsh Government introduces Senedd Cymru (Members and Elections) Bill
items.b: The new Bill will deliver reforms increasing the size of the Senedd from 60 to 96 members and shore up the Senedd’s scrutiny function. Additionally, the Welsh Government has proposed changing its electoral system to a closed proportional list system . Whilst welcoming the long awaited changes, the Electoral Reform Society highlights the problems of the closed list system, as opposed to STV, in their analysis of the new Bill.
items.why: it changes the size, scrutiny capacity and electoral system of the Senedd, altering how Welsh voters choose and hold representatives to account
items.note: Devolved legislature structure and electoral system change is classified under elections & decision making per the boundary rule on regional government.

items.h: Welsh First Minister Mark Drakeford sets out progressive laws to strengthen Welsh democracy
items.b: In addition to the new Senedd Cymru Bill (above), Mark Drakeford outlined a number of bills expected to be put forward in the coming months , including a bill to increase representation of women in the Senedd via gender quotas, another bill to improve electoral administration and increase the numbers of those registered to vote in Wales. The First Minister also committed to establishing an Electoral Management Board for Wales. Read the full analysis by Jess Blair on the Institute for Welsh Affairs blog.
items.why: it proposes gender quotas, electoral administration reform, voter registration improvements and a new Electoral Management Board that directly shape who can stand and vote in Welsh elections
links: number of bills expected to be put forward in the coming months

items.h: Trade Unions agree to resist ‘anti-strike laws’
items.b: Earlier this month, delegates at the Trades Union Congress in Liverpool almost unanimously backed a “non-compliance” motion put forward by the Fire Brigades Union and NASUWT. The motion means the TUC will hold a special conference to ‘explore options for non-compliance and resistance’.
items.why: it concerns trade unions' freedom of association and their capacity to organise and take collective action against restrictive legislation
items.note: Freedom of association for unions is classified under rights, freedoms & civic space per the boundary rule.

items.h: Online Safety Bill approved by Lords, awaits Royal Assent
items.b: The Online Safety Bill was approved by the House of Lords on 19 September and now awaits royal assent before becoming law. The legislation will give Ofcom the ability to issue fines of up to £18 million for media and tech companies who fail to remove harmful or illegal content. MPs David Davis and Caroline Lucas made an 11th hour attempt to help further protect end-to-end encryption, a longstanding issue of controversy within the bill .
items.why: it gives a regulator new powers over online content moderation, shaping the information environment in which public debate takes place, while raising encryption and privacy concerns
items.note: Encryption debate touches individual liberty but the core mechanism is regulation of the information environment.

16th November 2.30pm, Democracy Offers & Needs Market, Register

items.h: Democracy Network party conference events listing
items.b: Thanks to all of your input, the Democracy Network has published this page to track party conference events at all the major conferences this year. If we’ve missed anything let us know at hello@democracynetwork.org.uk .
items.note: A listing page tracking events is sector logistics, not a mechanism affecting democratic participation.

items.h: Democracy Network offering free places on new Leadership Programme by Axialent
items.b: In partnership with the Democracy Network, Axialent is running leadership training for 6 weeks from October 19th for 10 Democracy Network members. Apply for the training now by contacting Louise . See more info about the course program . Applicants must be Democracy Network Members to participate, sign up here .
items.note: Leadership training is for existing democracy sector staff/members, not a new means of public participation.

items.h: Democracy sector organisations meet with new Labour democracy spokesperson
items.b: Nine democracy sector organisations were fortunate enough to meet Florence Eshalomi MP recently in one of their first meetings with outside organisations. Florence Eshalomi is the newly appointed Labour democracy spokesperson, replacing Alex Norris MP. The discussion covered a wide range of issues and hopefully is the start of a close working relationship, remarked one of the participants.
items.note: A meeting between sector groups and an MP is networking, with no reported change to power or process.

items.h: UK model of democracy creates gulf between citizens and government, argues Tim Hughes
items.b: As part of the Bennett Institute for Public Policy and the Institute for Government’s Review of the UK Constitution work, Tim Hughes, Democracy & Participation Lead at the Open Government Partnership, has written a new paper on UK democracy, its discontents, and potential paths forward for better engaging citizens in democracy. The paper argues that the UK’s model of democracy and government does not put citizens at the heart of decision making — it should. Read the new paper here .
items.why: it presents new analysis and proposals for how citizens could be given a more meaningful role in UK decision-making, bearing on participatory and deliberative democratic mechanisms.
items.note: Touches on deliberative/decision-making reform as well as general citizen engagement, so could plausibly sit under elections_decision_making.

items.h: Join Participedia’s next Teaching Cafe!
items.b: Are you an academic looking to learn more about collaborating with democracy practitioners? Are you working at a democracy organisation or on a democracy project, and want to understand more about how you can interact with, learn from and share resources with democracy academics? Join Participedia on Weds October 11th 5pm for a special session — register here .

items.h: People Powered launch their new Participation Playbook
items.b: Launched last week, the new guide by People Powered aims to better help communities and local governments implement participatory programmes, opening up decisions to meaningful and equitable community participation. Check out the Playbook .
items.why: it creates a new practical resource intended to help local governments and communities implement genuine participatory decision-making processes.

items.h: This Is The North 2023 coming to Preston
items.b: People’s Powerhouse’s annual convention will be coming to Preston this November. PPH’s Chair Edna Robinson said: ‘We’re incredibly excited to bring the This Is the North Convention to Preston this November. The people of the North will gather to raise their collective voice across this brilliant city to demand a North that is fit for our future.’ Register now for tickets or fill out this EOI form if you’d like to deliver a workshop, talk or other sessions.
items.note: Event/conference listing, sector logistics not a democracy story.

items.h: My Life My Say prepare for Next Gen Conference 2023
items.b: My Life My Say’s Next Gen Conference is a globally recognised summit aimed at connecting young people with leading policymakers and empowering them to explore solutions to some of the greatest challenges facing society. Sign up now .
items.note: Conference sign-up notice, sector logistics not a new participation mechanism.

items.h: Polish Migrants Organise hiring for three amazing roles
items.b: POMOC are hiring for three roles, a new London Organiser, Liverpool Organiser and a new WeVote Campaign Coordinator. The October 9th deadline is fast approaching so get your applications in soon — apply now .
items.note: Job advert, organisational admin.

items.h: Involve appoint new Director of Climate Programmes in strategic shift to climate
items.b: Sarah Allan has been appointed as Involve’s new Director of Climate Programmes as part of a new strategic focus on public engagement on climate. Carly Dawson-Walker will be their new Director of Capacity Building & Standards.
items.note: Staff appointment news about an organisation.

items.h: Coming soon: The Reith Lectures
items.b: This year’s BBC Radio 4 Reith Lecturer is Ben Ansell, Professor of Comparative Democratic Institutions at Nuffield College, University of Oxford. Ben will be recording four lectures in their Our Democratic Futures series. The 2023 lectures will be recorded live in front of British, American and German audiences.
items.note: Announcement of a lecture series, not a mechanism of public power or new participation tool.

items.h: Young people remain doubtful about merits of democracy, new poll finds
items.b: A major new report, Can Democracy Deliver? by the Open Society Foundation has found 82% of people in the UK believe it is important to live in a democracy. Young people however, fall significantly short, with just 54% espousing a firm belief in democracy, and with more than 22% supporting some form of military rule in the UK.
items.why: This matters democratically because public and generational support for democratic government underpins its legitimacy and durability.
items.note: Survey evidence on popular support for democracy falls under participation & civic life per EIU anchors.

items.h: Women and Girls Network hiring for several roles
items.b: These five fantastic roles with the Women and Girls Network are only open to female applicants, apply here .
items.note: Job advert, organisational admin.

items.h: Friends of Indian Democracy looking for a great new campaigner
items.b: Friends of Indian Democracy (working title) is a newly established campaign group in the UK working to become a diaspora-led voice in the UK for preserving and promoting democracy in India and amplifying support for India’s democratic foundations. They are looking for a new campaigner, salaried at £50,000, deadline 9th October — Apply now .
items.note: Job advert for campaigner role concerning Indian, not UK, democracy.

items.h: Access to free legal advice via LawWorks for not-for-profits
items.b: LawWorks is a charity working in England and Wales to enable access to justice through free legal advice, and their not-for-profit programme brokers free legal advice for smaller not-for-profit organisations. If your organisation is facing a legal issue and you would like free legal advice, you can find out more about how LawWorks might be able to help, including details on the eligibility requirements and how to apply for support, on their website .
items.note: Sector service notice about an organisation's own programme, not a change to democratic participation.

items.h: Catalyst publish list of third sector funding opportunities
items.b: Catalyst has published a full list of third sector funding organisations — check it out now.
items.note: Funding listing, sector logistics.
links: published a full list of third sector funding organisations

items.h: Churchill Fellowship open to applications
items.b: The paid Churchill Fellowship enables successful applicants to spend 4–8 weeks meeting and working with innovators in your field, anywhere in the world, in person or online, helping you develop your learnings into practical outputs for your community or sector. Find out more .
items.note: Fellowship funding call, sector logistics.

items.h: New GOV.UK online portal for postal votes / proxy votes is coming, 31st October
items.b: Utilising a similar design to that found on the new Voter Authority Certificate site, the new GOV.UK ‘Apply for a postal vote’ ‘Apply for a proxy vote’ sites will not require a passport photo, but simply a photo of a handwritten signature. With the news, this means that the long standing www.onlinepostalvote.uk website, built by Zac Downs as a volunteer project in just a few days 7 years ago can now, finally, be retired.
items.why: this changes the administrative mechanics of postal and proxy voting, affecting how accessible and secure exercising the franchise is.

items.h: By-elections set for 19th October to replace Dorries and Pincher
items.b: Both elections are set to be tight votes, with Labour and Lib Dems hoping to repeat their recent by-election victories over the beleaguered Tories.
items.why: by-elections are a mechanism by which representatives are chosen and political competition is tested.

items.h: New research demonstrates null effect of social media advertising on voter registration
items.b: Research by Asli Unan, Peter John, Florian Foos and Vanessa Cheng-Matsuno finds ‘no evidence consistent with digital campaigning meaningfully affecting voter registrations’. Download the research on SocArXiv.
items.why: the research bears on voter registration, a core mechanism of electoral participation, and touches on the role of digital campaigning in the information environment.
items.note: Voter registration research is classed under elections per the turnout/registration anchor even though it involves campaign advertising.

items.h: Bates Wells, NEON & Stone King to run Q&A on rules around joint campaigning, Oct 17 5.30pm
items.b: The second in their series of webinars, the next session looks at what counts and what steps to take to make sure your engagement with allies doesn’t get classified as joint campaigning, if that’s not your intention. Register now .
items.note: Event listing/webinar on compliance rules, sector logistics rather than a democracy story itself.

items.h: Electoral Commission publish their final reports on the English and NI 2023 local elections
items.b: The Electoral Commission reports for England and Northern Ireland look at how the May 2023 elections were run, how voters and campaigners found taking part, and what lessons can be learned for the future.
items.why: official post-election reports assess how well local elections were administered, bearing on electoral integrity and voter experience.

items.h: LGIU Local Democracy Research Centre publishes their report on voter ID impacts
items.b: The 47 page report, The Impact of Voter ID: The Views of Administrators published by the Local Government Information Unit’s Local Democracy Research Centre analyses the perceptions of administrators, their reports on the increased pressure voter ID places on the electoral system, the likelihood of potential serious disruptions due to voter ID at GE polling day and more. Read the full report .
items.why: it examines whether voter ID rules create administrative strain that could disrupt the well-running of elections.
links: The Impact of Voter ID: The Views of Administrators

items.h: DLUHC publish evaluation plan for Electoral Integrity Programme
items.b: Back in December 2022, the UK Government committed to appointing external evaluators to analyse and research the measures being conducted through the Elections Act 2022, with a report due in November 2023. The published plan outlines their evaluation design, overview and research questions .
items.why: it concerns how the government will evaluate whether new electoral integrity measures are working as intended.
links: published plan outlines their evaluation design, overview and research questions

items.h: Councils put on alert for spring election, insiders say
items.b: Local authorities have reportedly been told to expect an election within months. Polling guru Isaac Levido has also rejoined CCHQ and Sunak’s election team after vacating Truss’ team during the collapse of their government last year.
items.why: the timing and preparation for a general election affects the machinery through which citizens choose their representatives.

items.h: Electoral Commission state up to 8 million missing from electoral rolls
items.b: In a new report last month, the Electoral Commission detailed that over 8 million people are incorrectly registered and are at risk of missing out on their right to vote. The report states that while 87% of White people are correctly registered, only 80% of Asian people and 72% of Black people are.
items.why: inaccurate electoral registers, unevenly affecting racial groups, directly threaten people's practical ability to exercise the franchise.
items.note: Racial disparity in registration is filed under elections per the franchise/registration anchor rather than rights.

items.h: Involve and the Citizens’ Convention on UK Democracy host special event on citizens’ assemblies
items.b: Last Monday, Involve and CCoUKD held a series of roundtable discussions with senior civil servants, parliamentary officials, MPs and civil society organisations to promote awareness and understanding of citizens’ assemblies. Speakers included Art O’Leary and Iain Walker of newDemocracy Foundation .
items.why: citizens' assemblies are part of the machinery of collective decision-making beyond elections, and building official understanding of them affects their future use.
items.note: Citizens' assemblies are anchored to elections & decision making per the boundary rule, not participation.

items.h: Democracy and Constitution APPG finds voter ID led to discrimination at polling booths
items.b: The new report by the APPG remarks that the recent voter ID legislation is a ‘poisoned cure’, disenfranchising voters more than it protects against fraud. The APPG is calling for amendments to be made to the legislation, including a greater range of ID documents, following evidence suggesting that significant numbers of voters suffered racial and disability discrimination at polling booths based on the need for ID.
items.why: evidence that voter ID rules disproportionately disenfranchise certain groups goes to whether elections are genuinely inclusive and accessible.

items.h: Efforts to improve gender equality in Parliament have made too little progress, report says
items.b: Open House: Where Next for Gender Equality in Parliament is the first ever audit of a decade’s worth of reports into gender equality in the UK Parliament, compiled by the APPG on Women in Parliament , Fawcett Society and the Global Institute for Women’s Leadership . Of 92 recommendations, across 36 different themes, which have been made to 29 different bodies since 2014, only a handful have actually been implemented.
items.why: the representativeness of elected institutions, including gender balance in Parliament, bears on whether elected bodies reflect the electorate.
items.note: Gender equality in Parliament is treated under elections as representativeness of elected institutions rather than rights.
links: Open House: Where Next for Gender Equality in Parliament

items.h: Labour publish full policy document condemning First Past the Post
items.b: Earlier in the summer, Labour’s National Policy Forum agreed policy stating the party views ‘First Past the Post as part of the problem’. Now, for the first time, the Labour Party has released the full policy document condemning First Past the Post.
items.why: a major party's formal stance on the electoral system shapes future debate over how votes translate into seats.
links: Labour Party has released the full policy document

items.h: Scottish Lib Dem Deputy Leader calls for electoral reform
items.b: Wendy Chamberlain, Deputy Leader of the Scottish Liberal Democrats has called for reforms to the First Past the Post system, writing, ‘If voting is the cornerstone of democracy, first past the post perverts that entirely’.
items.why: it concerns the design of the electoral system through which representatives are chosen.
links: called for reforms to the First Past the Post

items.h: Scottish Government publishes their electoral reform consultation analysis
items.b: Published back in late July, the Scottish Government’s paper outlines their findings from their 2022/23 Electoral Reform Consultation — check out the findings .
items.why: it reports government evidence-gathering on reforming the electoral system.

items.h: Lord’s reform will be ongoing headache for Labour, says Institute for Government Director
items.b: Implementing reform of the House of Lords will pose a significant challenge for Keir Starmer should Labour form the next government, argues Hannah White, Director of the Institute for Government , writing in the FT. White notes that any bill which forces the Lords to contemplate their own future will seriously distract them from scrutinising and enacting Labour’s core legislative programme.
items.why: it concerns the structure and functioning of a legislative chamber and its capacity for scrutiny.
items.note: Lords reform treated as government/Parliament scrutiny rather than elections since the chamber is unelected.
links: pose a significant challenge for Keir Starmer

items.h: Institute for Government publish their final report on the UK constitution
items.b: The final report in the 18-month Review of the UK Constitution by the Institute for Government and Bennett Institute for Public Policy is complete. They conclude that the UK constitution has been tested to its limit and is in urgent need of reform. Read the report .
items.why: it assesses whether constitutional checks and conventions still constrain and hold accountable those exercising public power.

items.h: Unhack Democracy prepare for the polish elections
items.b: Unhack Democracy are working towards developing a network for civil society organisation resilience through hope-based leadership in Poland, Hungary and Bulgaria. Ahead of the 15th October elections in Poland for the Sejm and Senate, they’ll be heading over for an election observation study trip with the European Platform for Democratic Elections . Contact Zsofi to find out more.
items.note: Reads as an organisational activity/contact notice rather than a UK-relevant democracy story.

items.h: Legislative Theatre wrap up successful projects with Greater Manchester & Trafford Council
items.b: Katy Rubin and the team at Legislative Theatre have just completed their project on ‘Right to the Streets’ with two local authorities, addressing public safety for women and girls, and all residents, in public spaces and transport across the region. Katy Rubin recently published an article on Legislative Theatre practice and how every citizen can be a policy analyst , for the Political Studies Association.
items.why: it creates a new means for residents to directly shape local policy through participatory theatre practice.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new participation mechanisms.
links: how every citizen can be a policy analyst

items.h: Government ‘flying blind’ on the scale of corruption and fraud, say Public Accounts Committee
items.b: A report by the Commons’ Public Accounts Committee has revealed that, apart from the £16.4 billion estimated tax and benefit fraud found by the National Audit Office last year, ministers have no idea about the level of fraud in the rest of government. Present estimates suggest that this could amount to anything from an additional £2.5 billion to £28.5 billion, leading to claims from MPs that the government is ‘flying blind’ on the true scale of corruption and fraud.
items.why: it reveals that government lacks the information needed to be held accountable for the scale of fraud and corruption in public spending.

items.h: Extinction Rebellion UK hosting discussion with KNOCA on how climate NGOs should engage with climate assemblies
items.b: Kathie Conn of XR UK shares news of their upcoming webinar on 11th October bringing together climate assembly experts, including Alina Averchenkova of the Knowledge Network of Climate Assemblies (KNOCA) to discuss the importance of the urgent requirement for a citizens assembly on climate and ecological justice.
items.note: Event/webinar announcement rather than a report of a new participation mechanism or decision.

items.h: IMPRESS writes to political parties over fake newspapers circulated by CCHQ
items.b: Lexie Kirkconnell-Kawana, Chief Exec of IMPRESS , the regulator of the independent press, has written to representatives of each major political party over the use of party leaflets dressed up to look like newspapers. The letter urges the leaders to review this practice amid the ‘crisis of trust’ in both journalists and politicians citing the very real consequences such tactics may have on UK democracy. For more information on this see Democracy Bulletin issue #54 .
items.why: disguising party political material as independent journalism deceives voters and undermines the public information environment they rely on to make political judgements
links: written to representatives of each major political party

items.h: Elon Musk fires half of X, formerly known as Twitter, Election Integrity Team
items.b: This one’s a bit of a mess , but the short version is that Musk fired half the team responsible for election misinformation monitoring, in addition to this Musk’s team disabled the button used to report election misinformation .
items.why: cutting the team and reporting tools that monitor election misinformation weakens the platform's capacity to protect the integrity of the information environment around elections
links: This one’s a bit of a mess
disabled the button used to report election misinformation

items.h: Editors call for greater action on SLAPPs
items.b: A chorus of news editors from The Times, Telegraph, FT, Guardian and the Chief Exec of ITN have called for greater action to address the use of SLAPPs , stating that though anti-SLAPP provisions have been included in a recent amendment to the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Bill , this was ‘only a partial victory’ and the next step must be ‘a standalone anti-SLAPP bill to extend protections to everyone who speaks out in the public interest’.
items.why: SLAPPs use legal threats to silence public-interest journalism, chilling the press's ability to inform public debate and hold power to account
items.note: SLAPPs are anchored to information_debate under the framework's press-freedom territory.
links: called for greater action to address the use of SLAPPs
Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Bill

items.h: Slump in UK Corruption Index rating due to ‘noisy reporting’, claims Cabinet Office
items.b: Cabinet officials are blaming the UK’s slump in the global Corruption Perceptions Index on ‘noisy reporting’ , their argument being that the media’s coverage of the COVID-19 scandals has contributed to decline in the UK’s international standing. Byline Times covers the story here .
items.why: government blaming media scrutiny for a fall in corruption perceptions, rather than addressing the underlying conduct, bears on how corruption and accountability are perceived and contested

items.h: Dembrane wins $100k OpenAI grant
items.b: Last month we announced that Recursive Public , a joint UK project between Chatham House and vTaiwan had won one of the 10 OpenAI grants as part of their Democratic Inputs to AI fund . Now we can announce that Dembrane , has also won the award. Dembrane is a partnership between Sortition Foundation and a number of dutch organisations and businesses. Dembrane seeks to better map insights from large scale participatory processes, check it out .
items.why: funding a new tool to synthesise insights from large-scale participatory and deliberative processes creates new capacity for deliberative decision-making machinery
items.note: Deliberative process tooling is anchored to elections_decision_making rather than participation.

items.h: Democracy Network AI & Democracy WhatsApp Group to begin regular webinars
items.b: Are you interested in applying or experimenting with the new AI large language model tools? Concerned about the impact of AI on democratic processes? Join the Democracy Network’s AI & Democracy WhatsApp Group , Bella Roberts, Founder of Antiparty , is organising new biweekly evening webinars starting on 26th October, more on this soon — or join the WhatsApp Group to find out more.
items.why: launching a recurring webinar and network space on AI and democracy creates a new means for people to engage with and understand democratic issues
links: Democracy Network’s AI & Democracy WhatsApp Group

items.h: New Harmonica chatbot to enable quick sensemaking in participatory processes
items.b: Harmonica is a new project developed by Newspeak House Fellow Artem Zhiganov. The Harmonica chatbot, currently in beta on Discord, enables very fast deliberation between large groups, conversing with Chat GPT, synthesising key learnings quickly. Email Artem for an invite to the Harmonica prototype on Discord.
items.why: a new chatbot tool for fast large-group deliberation adds capacity to the machinery of participatory and deliberative decision-making
items.note: Deliberative process tooling is anchored to elections_decision_making rather than participation.

items.h: Ade Adeyemi unpacks the potential for AI and its impacts for electoral campaigning
items.b: Ade Adeyemi, formerly of Chatham House, provides a broad overview of the potential for Labour to utilise AI tools to leapfrog the Conservative Party on campaigning at the next election. Worth a read , if only for the nugget that Keir Starmer’s son has been teaching them to use ChatGPT! If you’re interested in technology and campaigning, make sure you check out Campaign Lab , who run regular hackathons in London and online.
items.why: speculation about parties using AI tools to gain campaigning advantage bears on how AI-generated political information could shape political competition
items.note: Borderline: this is speculative commentary on AI's potential campaign use rather than a reported change.

items.h: This Inequality Does Not Exist, generates images of housing in London
items.b: This website built by Aleksi Knuutila is an experiment in how generative AI could be used to study social phenomena such as the visual aspects of social processes in cities. The demo tool uses thousands of images of housing in London and associated health and income data to display synthetic, generated images, based on user parameters, abstracting social processes.

items.h: Targeting the German Bundestag is quite complicated
items.b: In this short post, Fix The Status Quo outline just how difficult it is to pull off a successful Bundestag -wide political campaign, due to the complexity of the German political system — thanks to Edward Saperia for this one.
items.note: Offbeat commentary on foreign campaign logistics without clear bearing on UK democratic mechanisms.

items.h: The Influence Industry Explorer
items.b: Peter Keeling sent this one in, The Influence Industry Explorer unpacks the myriad ways companies play a role in political elections around the world, including… Antarctica?
items.why: This matters democratically because it maps how commercial and political influence operates within electoral campaigning and party financing systems worldwide.
items.note: Global comparative tool touching campaign finance/lobbying, only loosely tied to UK democracy.

items.h: Online Safety Act a threat to civil liberties, says Big Brother Watch
items.b: The legislative behemoth that was the Online Safety Bill has completed passage through Parliament and is now set to become law, but whilst many will welcome the legislation, Big Brother Watch highlights five aspects of the bill that threaten civil rights . The Bill is a ‘Frankenstein’s monster of a Bill that will set free expression and privacy back decades in this country,’ they write.
items.why: This matters democratically because new legislation reshapes the legal limits on privacy and free expression that citizens can exercise in digital spaces.
items.note: Online Safety Act touches both civil liberties (privacy) and the information environment (platforms/free expression); classified under rights given the civil-liberties framing.
links: aspects of the bill that threaten civil rights

items.note: Event listing/webinar announcement, not a substantive democracy story.

items.h: Democracy Network Conference save the date
items.b: Join the UK Democracy Network for our two day annual conference in London on the 9th and 10th January. Please save the date — there’s even rumours of a ‘Democracy’s Got Talent’ special evening event! Here’s a little reminder of what we got up to last year .
