items.note: Photo caption about an awards ceremony, organisational.

items.h: Migrant Democracy Project launch new MPower Political Leadership Programme
items.b: In a watershed moment for the campaign, Migrant Democracy Project are kicking off their new MPower leadership training programme, aiming to provide key knowledge and skills to 10 first-generation migrants to become candidates and stand in local elections across the UK — the deadline for submitting applications to the programme is Friday 17th November 2023 — spread the word and share with your networks to share with as many first generation migrants as possible — email Teo Benea , MDP’s new Training Organiser, with any questions
items.why: it creates a new pathway for an underrepresented group to gain the skills and support needed to become election candidates, affecting candidate access and representativeness in local elections.
items.note: Training programme aimed at producing election candidates places it in candidate access under elections, though it also builds civic participation capacity.
links: spread the word and share with your networks to share with as many first generation migrants as possible

items.h: Engage Britain merges with Demos
items.b: Demos, the leading cross party thinktank, and Engage Britain, a charity pioneering participatory policy-making, formally merged on 1st November 2023, with the following statement: “Our charities share a mission to put people at the heart of policy-making. We are both driven by a desire to show that participatory policy-making is a solution to our democratic challenges, can renew people’s trust in the political process and improve the quality of policies. “By coming together, we hope to turbo-charge our impact, making the case for involving people in the decisions that affect their lives and en…
items.note: Organisational merger of two sector bodies, not a change to democratic participation itself.

items.h: mySociety to celebrate 20 years next week
items.b: Next Wednesday mySociety will celebrate 20 years bolstering our democracy, creating the foundations for stronger communities and civic culture, and a more transparent politics, through their impressive suite of tools for journalists, local officials, campaigners, activists, researchers and more. They’ll celebrate their successes by highlighting and awarding the amazing work of everyone they helped along the way .
items.note: Anniversary celebration of an organisation, not a substantive democracy story.

items.h: This Is The North 2023 coming to Preston, 29th November
items.b: People’s Powerhouse’s annual convention will be coming to Preston this November. PPH’s Chair Edna Robinson said: ‘We’re incredibly excited to bring the This Is the North Convention to Preston this November. The people of the North will gather to raise their collective voice across this brilliant city to demand a North that is fit for our future.’ Register now for tickets .
items.note: Event/conference listing rather than a new mechanism for participation.

items.h: Access to free legal advice via LawWorks for not-for-profits
items.b: LawWorks is a charity working in England and Wales to enable access to justice through free legal advice, and their not-for-profit programme brokers free legal advice for smaller not-for-profit organisations. If your organisation is facing a legal issue and you would like free legal advice, you can find out more about how LawWorks might be able to help, including details on the eligibility requirements and how to apply for support, on their website .
items.note: Routine service notice for organisations' own legal needs, not a democratic mechanism story.

items.h: Centenary Action Group launch new joint campaign to reinstate funding for Disabled candidates
items.b: Elect Her , Disability Rights UK , Disability Policy Centre and Centenary Action Group published their joint statement, backed by over 30 democracy sector organisations. The statement calls on the UK Government to urgently reinstate an Access to Elected Office Fund to support Disabled candidates to contest elections. But that’s not all — don’t miss CAG’s #GenderEqualParliament Pledge .
items.why: this matters democratically because it concerns whether disabled citizens can practically access candidacy for elected office, a core condition of electoral competition.
items.note: Candidate access to elected office falls under elections & decision making rather than participation.

items.h: 50:50 Parliament prepare for Ask Her To Stand Day 2023
items.b: This November 21st 50:50 Parliament aim to inspire women across the UK to #SignUpToStand. Frances Scott and the team are holding a big event in Parliament that evening, so register now and don’t miss out.
items.why: this matters democratically because it seeks to increase women's representation among electoral candidates, affecting the representativeness of elected institutions.
items.note: Campaign encouraging candidacy is treated as elections & decision making (candidate access) rather than general participation.

items.h: Citizens in Power call for a national cultural network for citizen-led decision making
items.b: David Jubb and the team at Citizens In Power are testing interest in a new UK-based network for a transition to citizen-led decision making. The proposal outlines the network benefits of such an approach, from peer learning, professional development, coordinated advocacy, deduplication improved access to funds, resources and more. If you are interested, read the proposal and respond to the proposal by the 11th December .
items.why: this matters democratically because it proposes new infrastructure to coordinate and expand citizen-led deliberative decision-making across the UK.
items.note: Deliberative/citizen-led decision-making networks are anchored to elections & decision making per framework rules.
links: respond to the proposal by the 11th December

items.h: More than 500 Republic protesters turned up to protest the King’s Speech yesterday
items.b: Yesterday more than 500 republican protesters gathered on Whitehall to show their displeasure at King Charles’ State Opening of Parliament. Republic says that this is a sign of a ‘growing republican movement’ in the UK. Earlier this year saw more than 52 republicans arrested for protesting Charles’ coronation, including Republic Chief Exec Graham Smith. Meanwhile, their petition demanding a public vote on the future of the monarchy is close to reaching its target of 25,000 signatures.
items.why: this matters democratically because it evidences citizens' willingness to publicly demonstrate and campaign for a referendum on the constitutional order.
items.note: Framed as evidence of growing willingness to protest, so classed under participation rather than rights/civic space; the petition for a public vote touches elections & decision making.

items.h: Titus Alexander organising new Edinburgh Reith Lecture Reading Group
items.b: The new reading group will meet in Atholl Crescent, West End on the 7th, 21st November and 5th, 19th December. The group will discuss Ben Ansell’s Reith Lectures based on their book Why Politics Fails: The Five Traps of the Modern World and How to Escape Them , email Titus if you’re interested in joining the new group. Tickets may still be available for the third lecture, in Sunderland on 14th November.
items.note: A reading-group event listing about a book, not a new participation resource or organisational news.

items.h: Unlock Democracy launching new Automatic Voter Registration campaign
items.b: This week Grace Barnett and the team at Unlock Democracy kick off their new Automatic Voter Registration campaign in Parliament on the 8th November at 4pm.
items.why: automatic voter registration campaigns directly affect who is able to exercise the franchise, a core electoral administration mechanism

items.h: LGIU warn against newly launched and half-finished absentee vote application service
items.b: Last week a new web service for postal and proxy votes came online. Previously electors had to fill in a paper form and send it away to receive their absentee ballot. However, many electoral administrators think the new system has been rushed into service . The pre-existing service for processing paper ballots has been shut down, whilst paper ballots are still in use, forcing election officials to process new ballots one by one until the full switchover to online proxy ballots in January, Local Government Information Unit note.
items.why: a rushed rollout of the postal and proxy vote system risks disenfranchising or delaying eligible voters, a core election administration issue
links: many electoral administrators think the new system has been rushed into service

items.h: May elections highlight systematic barriers for disabled voters, say My Vote My Voice
items.b: Problems with access at the local elections in May combined with new voter ID laws and a lack of information in accessible formats highlights the systematic issues facing disabled voters , according to My Vote My Voice . They’re campaigning for greater support at the general election for disabled voters to ensure there isn’t a repeat of the local elections and no one is denied the right to vote.
items.why: barriers to accessible voting and ID requirements determine whether disabled citizens can exercise their franchise
items.note: Accessibility of voting mechanics is filed under elections; disability equality is a secondary rights angle.

items.h: Electoral Commission highlight recommendations and challenges following latest recall petition
items.b: Earlier this year, constituents in Rutherglen and Hamilton successfully triggered a recall petition with more than 10% constituents signing before the 31 July deadline, Margaret Ferrier was duly ousted and Labour MP Michael Shanks elected in their place. However, the Electoral Commission notes a range of areas in which the recall petition process can be improved and refined , such as locating adequate venues for signing places and ensuring extended opening hours for petitioners.
items.why: recall petitions are a mechanism of electoral accountability whose administration affects whether constituents can effectively remove an MP
links: Electoral Commission notes a range of areas in which the recall petition process can be improved and refined

items.h: New research demonstrates null effect of social media advertising on voter registration
items.b: Research by Asli Unan, Peter John, Florian Foos and Vanessa Cheng-Matsuno finds ‘no evidence consistent with digital campaigning meaningfully affecting voter registrations’. Download the research on SocArXiv.
items.why: evidence on whether digital campaigning affects voter registration bears on the effectiveness of participation mechanisms and campaign practices
items.note: Turnout/registration research is always filed under elections per framework rule.

items.h: FPTP leaves SNP vulnerable at upcoming GE, according to IfG research
items.b: First Past The Post has served the SNP well in recent elections due to divisions in the unionist vote, winning the vast majority of seats with a vote share of between 34–54%. However, according to new from the Institute for Government, FPTP now makes the SNP vulnerable according to pollster Peter Kellner who highlights that an 8.5% swing to Labour wins Labour 12 seats and a further swing of just 4.5% would win Labour 12 more seats giving them a majority in Scotland.
items.why: the electoral system's mechanical effects on party representation determine how votes translate into seats and political competition
links: FPTP now makes the SNP vulnerable

items.h: The Politics Project plan new GE Strategy Day
items.b: Hattie Andrews and the team at The Politics Project are planning another General Election Strategy Day. Their last, held on Jan 25 this year, was an amazing success and confluence of a wide and diverse range of civic education stakeholders from across the nations of the UK — we look forward to hearing more details about this soon.
items.note: An announcement of a planned future event without details, akin to sector logistics rather than a concrete new participation resource.

items.h: National Voter Registration Week — 4th March 2024
items.b: Democracy Classroom and their partner organisations have agreed a date for their collaborative National Voter Registration Week (NVRW), commencing on the 4th March 2024 — this is an opportunity for those running voter registration campaigns to focus efforts, work together, and amplify the reach of the various campaigns. NVRW will run in collaboration with National Voter Registration Day that is planned for April and is being led by My Life My Say .
items.why: This matters democratically because coordinated voter registration campaigns directly affect who can exercise their right to vote in elections.
items.note: Voter registration campaigns fall under elections per the turnout/registration rule, not participation.

items.h: The Politics Project launch student design competition #WhyVote
items.b: Creative Conscience, Democracy Classroom and The Political Project (TPP) have teamed up to host a new student design competition to support young people to develop creative resources in the run up to the elections next year. Winning entries will receive £200 and will be used as part of national campaigns to engage young people in next year’s elections — judges of the designs include Baroness Nicky Morgan, Alistair Campbell and Trevor Robinson OBE among others. TPP invite democracy orgs to share this competition with their audiences, schools and networks .
items.why: This matters democratically because a campaign designed to encourage young people to vote bears directly on electoral turnout and participation.
items.note: Campaigns to raise turnout are classified under elections regardless of the youth-engagement framing.
links: student design competition to support young people to develop creative resources

items.h: Democracy Classroom launch new website
items.b: Democracy Classroom’s new online hub is designed to make it easier for teachers, youth workers and democracy practitioners to access the suite of collective support available through their website, from teacher guides to games — and listing their full range of programmes and resources. Check it out now .
items.why: This matters democratically because the new hub creates concrete resources that expand teachers' and youth workers' capacity to help young people participate in democratic life.

items.h: Constitution Unit host discussion on results of two year democracy inquiry
items.b: UCL’s Constitution Unit has been examining public attitudes to democracy in the UK as part of a two year inquiry. On November 27th, they’re launching their new report drawing together the findings — including from two large-scale surveys and a citizens’ assembly — reflecting on what kind of democracy the UK wants and what policy makers can do about it. Register for the launch event now .
items.why: This matters democratically because the inquiry's findings on public attitudes toward democracy, gathered partly through a citizens' assembly, inform how confident and willing people feel to take part in democratic life.
items.note: Citizens' assembly component nods toward elections_decision_making, but the overall focus is public attitudes/support for democracy.
links: Register for the launch event now

items.h: Public debate on sentencing is ‘stuck in a dysfunctional and reactive cycle’ Justice Committee warns
items.b: In a new report by the Justice Committee in partnership with Involve , the cross-party committee of MPs have concluded the persistence of the view among the public that justice is not severe enough, represents a long term public policy challenge that needs to be addressed. In addition to a public poll of more than 2,057 people, Involve ran a deliberative engagement exercise with the Committee, with 25 adults across three half-day sessions to discuss the current justice system and sentencing approach.
items.why: This matters democratically because it examines a deliberative engagement exercise used to inform parliamentary committee decision-making on justice policy, testing a form of citizen deliberation in governance.
items.note: Deliberative engagement processes are mapped to elections_decision_making per framework rule, despite the justice-policy topic.
links: new report by the Justice Committee

items.h: Scrapping Voter ID laws could save £120m, says Unlock Democracy
items.b: In a submission to HM Treasury, Unlock Democracy has called on the government to scrap the Voter ID legislation saying it could save £120m. Director of Unlock Democracy, Tom Brake, says it is an unaffordable and unnecessary cost given there has been hardly any cases of voter impersonation fraud over the last decade.
items.why: This matters democratically because it concerns whether Voter ID requirements serve as a proportionate safeguard for electoral integrity or an unnecessary barrier to voting.

items.h: Labour backtracks on Lords reform amid criticism
items.b: Keir Starmer is reportedly watering down the party’s plans for an elected second chamber over fears of a backlash from the House of Lords. Last year’s Gordon Brown Commission raised the prospect of major Labour Party reform of the House of Lords, however this looks to be shelved in order to prioritise key legislative objectives.
items.why: This matters democratically because reform of the House of Lords concerns the structure and electoral legitimacy of a chamber of Parliament.
items.note: Classified under elections_decision_making because the reform concerns making the chamber elected, though it also touches legislative structure.
links: Keir Starmer is reportedly watering down the party’s plans

items.h: Government rejects calls to criminalise lying in Parliament
items.b: Two petitions involving nearly 250,000 signatures resulted in a parliamentary debate on whether the Government should criminalise deliberate lying to Parliament. The SNP’s Owen Johnson proposed setting up a Truth Commission to fact check MPs, but legislation has been shot down by the Government over fears that it could restrict freedom of speech in Parliament.
items.why: This matters democratically because it concerns whether MPs can be held legally accountable for dishonesty in Parliament, a core standards-in-public-life mechanism.
items.note: Petitions triggering the debate touch participation, but the core issue is executive/parliamentary accountability.
links: 250,000 signatures resulted in a parliamentary debate

items.h: Successful Full Fact campaign brings changes to Parliamentary correction system
items.b: Over 50,000 Full Fact supporters have been campaigning since April 2022 to amend the way the corrections system works in Parliament. MPs voted to change the system following the groundswell of support, meaning that if an MP now makes a mistake when speaking in Parliament and wants to make a correction, they will now be able to do so. Full Fact is hailing the change as a ‘really important day for our democracy’.
items.why: it changes a parliamentary accountability mechanism governing how MPs correct the official record, affecting scrutiny of what ministers and MPs say in Parliament.
links: amend the way the corrections system

items.h: Darren Jones, MP for Bristol North West, holds Constituency Assembly
items.b: Labour MP Darren Jones held a Constituency Assembly earlier this month in his seat in Bristol North West. The assembly involved 50 local constituents and gave them an opportunity to discuss and debate important issues with one another as well as with their MP. The initiative has been proposed by Compassion in Politics to help strengthen civic involvement in politics.
items.why: it creates a new deliberative forum linking constituents directly to their MP, which the framework treats as decision-making machinery rather than general participation.
items.note: Deliberative/assembly format is classed under elections & decision making per framework rule, not participation.

items.h: No major constitutional or electoral change without referendum, argue Policy Exchange
items.b: Ian Mansfield, Director of Policy Exchange , has argued Labour must not be allowed to push forward with plans to change the parliamentary franchise or constitutional makeup of the UK without a referendum. In an article for ConservativeHome they argue that any ‘major changes to parliamentary democracy should not be made without the clear support of the British people’.
items.why: it concerns whether changes to the franchise or constitutional structure require direct popular authorisation via referendum, a core decision-making mechanism.

items.h: Growing state intolerance towards protest related to the Israel-Hamas War
items.b: Liberty and the Network for Police Monitoring have raised the alarm over recent comments by UK Government ministers and by conditions imposed on protests. In recent weeks Home Secretary Suella Braverman sowed confusion over law relating to waving Palestinian flags or expressing support for Palestine . The London-based Met Police have placed serious conditions on protests, one of which prevented ‘ any person participating or associated with ’ the protest from deviating from the route, or else they may face arrest — effectively intimidating protesters and providing the police carte blanche for m…
items.why: it concerns state restriction, policing conditions and intimidation curbing citizens' ability to assemble and protest on a political issue.
links: sowed confusion over law relating to waving Palestinian flags or expressing support for Palestine

items.h: UK Government moves to dramatically curtail freedom of expression in leaked plans
items.b: Officials have drawn up plans to expand the definition of extremism to include anyone who ‘undermines’ UK values and institutions, according to documents reportedly seen by the Observer newspaper . The Dept. for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities started a review of non-violent extremism earlier this year. Dozens of civil liberties groups including Liberty and Index on Censorship, rallied against the plans as an ‘unwarranted attack on freedom of expression’. Amnesty International UK’s racial justice director, Ilyas Nagdee, said ‘this definition must not be accepted or implemented’.
items.why: an expanded definition of extremism used by government would curb individuals' freedom of expression and association on political grounds.
links: according to documents reportedly seen by the Observer newspaper

items.h: Liberty to sue Home Secretary over anti-protest legislation
items.b: Liberty is taking Suella Braverman to court over their decision to introduce anti-protest measures to the Public Order Act that had previously been voted out of the bill due to their draconian nature. Braverman was later able to introduce the amendments as secondary legislation without consulting Parliament.
items.why: the executive used secondary legislation to reinstate anti-protest powers Parliament had rejected, bypassing legislative scrutiny.
items.note: Primary mechanism is bypassing parliamentary scrutiny via delegated powers; litigation and protest rights are secondary.
links: Liberty is taking Suella Braverman to court

items.h: Justice for Bristol Protesters call for public inquiry into #KillTheBill protests
items.b: During the Bristol protests against the Police, Crime and Sentencing Bill on 21 March 2021, more than 100 people were injured by police. Police deployed pepper spray, beating, attack dogs and the controversial tactic of riot shield blading . Campaigners argue Mariella Gedge-Rogers, currently serving a 5.5 year sentence for riot for their part in the protests, was pinned to the ground by 3 officers and had their hand stamped on in an unprovoked police attack — yet no single officer has been questioned or called to account for their actions that day. Sign the petition and find out more .
items.why: campaigners are seeking a public inquiry as a redress mechanism for alleged unaccountable police violence against protesters.
items.note: Public inquiry framed around redress for victims, placing it in rule of law rather than accountability scrutiny.
links: Police deployed pepper spray, beating, attack dogs and the controversial tactic of riot shield blading

items.h: Government orders UKRI to sack advisers over ‘extremist’ views
items.b: One month on after UK Secretary of State for Science Michelle Donelan attached the ‘creep of wokeism’ in science, initiating a review into the sex and gender questions in scientific research, Donelan last week ordered UKRI Chief Exec Ottoline Leyser to disband a newly formed equality, diversion and inclusion panel over accusations of members sharing ‘extremist’ views and thereby contravening the Nolan Principles.
items.why: a minister directing an arms-length public body to dismiss advisers over their views raises questions about political interference with independent bodies and standards in public life.
links: disband a newly formed equality, diversion and inclusion panel

items.h: International coalition of human rights groups call for UK and worldwide halt on facial recognition technology
items.b: 180 rights groups and tech experts have warned of significant human rights threats associated with facial recognition technology. In a joint letter to legislators, the collection of organisations across six continents urged for a ban on the use of the technology at a time when the UK government is considering expanding its use in policing. See Big Brother Watch’s recent work for more in depth analysis .
items.why: expanding facial recognition surveillance by police affects citizens' privacy and freedom from unjustified state surveillance, a core civil liberty underpinning civic space.
items.note: Surveillance/privacy framed as rights issue rather than information environment.
links: warned of significant human rights threats
See Big Brother Watch’s recent work for more in depth analysis

items.h: Help us populate our sector funding list
items.b: The Democracy Network is part-way through refurbishing our resources and directories, including the UK Democracy Map and funding list. This is the current list of active democracy grant funds in the UK, please review and tell us if anything is missing , or if we’ve made an error — alternatively, add any grant funds we’ve missed via this form .
links: tell us if anything is missing
add any grant funds we’ve missed via this form

items.h: UK Democracy Network, Compass and Unlock Democracy submit joint JRRT bid for new campaign project
items.b: The Democracy Network has this week submitted a bid for funding the coalition campaign efforts voted for by the sector, brought together through the recent sector-wide development days. Unlock Democracy and Compass joined the bid to continue the Powering Up project and work more closely alongside sector organisations in the run-up to the election.
items.note: Organisational funding bid/admin news, not a change to what people can do.

items.h: Nuffield Foundation present their general election analysis and briefing fund
items.b: The Nuffield Foundation have funded a number projects and institutions ahead of the general election, including the Fraser of Allander Institute, the IFS, the National Institute for Economic and Social Research, the Social Market Foundation, the Education Policy Institute and London Economic, to a total tune of £526,000. Read more about the projected outcomes and aims of the fund .
items.note: Funding announcement for think-tank election analysis is sector funding news, not a participation mechanism.
links: Nuffield Foundation have funded a number projects and institutions

items.h: The New Institute is looking for Future of Democracy Fellows
items.b: The Hamburg based fellowship is fully funded. See here for more information .

items.h: Catalyst publish list of third sector funding opportunities
items.b: Catalyst has published a full list of third sector funding organisations — check it out now.
links: published a full list of third sector funding organisations

items.h: Churchill Fellowship open to applications
items.b: The paid Churchill Fellowship enables successful applicants to spend 4–8 weeks meeting and working with innovators in your field, anywhere in the world, in person or online, helping you develop your learnings into practical outputs for your community or sector. Find out more .

items.h: New Economy Organisers Network apply for further funding to extend their electoral law programme
items.b: In recent months, the New Economy Organisers Network (NEON) have been running a programme of high quality briefings on electoral law for campaigners and charities ahead of the 2024 General Election, together with Bates Wells and Stone King. Now they’re looking to extend their electoral law briefings and workshops as the election nears — do you know any relevant funds, can you help fund these important activities?
items.why: the programme creates new capacity-building resources helping campaigners and charities lawfully participate in electoral activity ahead of a general election.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new means of participation, not mere organisational funding admin.

items.h: Campaign Lab develops new electoral law chatbot prototype for charities and campaigners
items.b: Campaign Lab ’s Lefke Kerr and Jethro Reeve are developing an AI powered document search chatbot to assist campaigners, activists and charities make sense of electoral law documentation from the Electoral Commission, and so far so good. Last month they held a successful testing session, now they’re looking for funding to take the work further, can you help?
items.why: This matters democratically because it builds a new tool to help campaigners and charities understand and comply with electoral law, strengthening their capacity to take part in political campaigning.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating a new means of participation, per the framework's capacity-building rule.

items.h: Climate Emergency UK launch their Council Climate Action Scorecards
items.b: In what is possibly the biggest and first local government accountability exercise of this size and scale, Climate Emergency UK’s new transparency tool surfaces information on all 388 UK councils, gathered from more than 4,000 freedom of information requests — amounting to the first ever complete assessment of council climate action. Join their upcoming sessions exploring how to use the tool or contact Annie Pickering , CE-UK’s CEO, for more information.
items.why: This matters democratically because it creates a transparency tool, built from freedom of information requests, that lets citizens hold every UK council accountable for climate action.
items.note: FOI used as an accountability mechanism to scrutinise local institutions.
links: Climate Emergency UK’s new transparency tool

items.h: Scottish indy poll no longer dominates national politics, according to Tony Blair Institute
items.b: New research by The Tony Blair Institute reveals that almost a decade on from the independence referendum, the constitutional question no longer dominates Scottish politics. Whilst 45% want independence, one third of the indy vote agree that independence is not a priority right now due to more pressing matters.
items.note: Polling on issue salience does not identify a democratic mechanism being exercised, constrained or contested.

items.h: Labour councillors publish report on the case for greater devolution and community power
items.b: Working with New Local , seven Labour councillors from across England have written the report A Labour Vision for Community Power , setting out an agenda for Britain which is driven by the principles of participation, prevention and devolution. With public services and public finance in crisis, the report argues that devolving power to a local level will allow communities to meet local challenges whilst rebuilding trust in a political system that is widely seen as broken.
items.why: This matters democratically because it argues for devolving decision-making power to local communities, proposing a change to the structures through which collective decisions are made.
items.note: Devolution structure/powers placed under elections & decision making per boundary rule; participation themes are secondary.
links: A Labour Vision for Community Power

items.h: Public Interest News Foundation Forum convenes indy news publishers
items.b: Late last month, dozens of indie news publishers descended on Bristol for a day of speed dating, networking and working together on collective challenges. Jaldeep Katwala and the PINF team showcased their Local News Map and News For All campaign, the new Scottish Beacon team deep dived into their new business model and the afternoon was spent in invigorating open space discussions on a range of topics , from the upcoming election to how to hold local authorities accountable.
items.note: Event/networking report about an organisation rather than a new tool, resource or mechanism affecting participation.

items.h: Three companies control 90% of national news, according to Media Reform Coalition report
items.b: Media Reform Coalition has published their 2023 annual report; Who Owns the UK Media? They find that just three companies — DMG Media , News UK and Reach PLC — dominate 90% of the UK’s national newspaper market, whilst 71% of the local newspaper market is controlled by six companies. Urgent reform is needed, they say, to end ‘decades of failed regulation and political inaction on concentrated media ownership.’
items.why: This matters democratically because concentrated ownership of national and local news outlets narrows the plurality of political information and debate citizens can access.

items.h: Newspeak House awarded funding for new GE2024 Election Tech Handbook
items.b: Edward Saperia and the team at Newspeak House, the London College of Political Technology , have been awarded a new tranche of funding by the Joseph Rowntree Reform Trust to develop and launch a GE 2024 Election Tech Handbook. Newspeak House organised the 2017 and 2019 Election Tech Handbooks , providing a project board, data library and community organising space for the UK civic tech community during those election cycles.
items.why: This matters democratically because the funded handbook will build a shared resource and organising infrastructure that helps the civic tech community engage with the 2024 general election.
items.note: Distinguished from mere organisational funding news because the grant funds creation of a concrete participation resource.
links: Newspeak House, the London College of Political Technology

items.h: Who Targets Me mull AI election risks
items.b: In their latest Full Disclosure newsletter (highly recommend, subscribe here ) the team at Who Targets Me assessed the latest government rhetoric around ‘frontier AI risk’ to elections, noting that we’re already struggling with rampant misinformation and disruptive, undemocratic content and risk — so to focus on AI as presenting a new and specific threat is to miss the point — that we should focus on protecting elections and the security of the ballot full stop , by the technical, legal, political and structural protections available to us, i.e preparing for the future, but focusing on the her…
items.why: This matters democratically because it argues for prioritising concrete technical, legal and political protections for the security and integrity of UK elections over abstract AI-risk framing.
items.note: Discussion of disinformation risk to ballot security anchors it to elections rather than purely the media environment.

items.h: Democracy Network & ANTIPARTY AI & Democracy Webinars
items.b: Are you interested in applying or experimenting with the new AI large language model tools? Concerned about the impact of AI on democratic processes? Join the Democracy Network’s AI & Democracy WhatsApp Group , Bella Roberts, Founder of ANTIPARTY , is organising new biweekly evening webinars, join the WhatsApp Group to find out more, join the next webinar tomorrow — or watch our previous events on YouTube — How Can Collective Intelligence Empower Our Democracy? & Using Collective Intelligence to Govern AI
items.why: it creates a new network and recurring forum through which people can engage with and shape debate about AI's impact on democratic processes.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building (new network/programme) rather than a mere event listing.
links: Democracy Network’s AI & Democracy WhatsApp Group
How Can Collective Intelligence Empower Our Democracy?
Using Collective Intelligence to Govern AI

items.h: Institute for Government analyse ‘game-changer’ by-elections in new podcast
items.b: Last month the Labour Party overturned significant Conservative majorities in two by-elections, as well as defeating the SNP in the recall election in Rutherglen and Hamilton West. The Institute for Government deep dived into the results in a new podcast with a view to what this could mean for 2024.
items.why: by-election results reflect shifts in political competition, party support and the realistic prospect of a change of government.
links: The Institute for Government deep dived into the results in a new podcast

items.h: Leave voters more satisfied with democracy, according to UK in a Changing Europe
items.b: Following the 2016 EU referendum those who voted to leave became a lot more satisfied with the way democracy works in the UK, whilst those who backed remain saw a large drop in their level of satisfaction, according to new analysis from UK in a Changing Europe .
items.why: public satisfaction with how democracy works is a direct measure of popular support for and confidence in democratic institutions.
links: new analysis from UK in a Changing Europe

items.b: Monthly news, jobs, grants and gossip from across the democracy sector, brought to you by James Moulding and Max Roche of the UK Democracy Network . Read by 400+ democracy organisations. We read everyone’s newsletters & research so you don’t have to. If you want us to cover yours, let us know: hello@democracynetwork.org.uk
Join the UK Democracy Network’s WhatsApp Community here — there are currently several active groups on topics ranging from AI & Democracy to Democracy Academics Collaboration.

We were joined by Yvonne Murphy — Omidaze Productions (Democracy Box), Ruth Hannan — People’s Powerhouse, Mohammed Afridi — Civic Power Fund, Rebekah McCabe — Involve, Adam Mendum — Involve, Patti Garcia — Demos, Rosie Trevill — Elect Her, Lyanne Nicholl — 50:50 Parliament, Alastair Binnie-Lubbock — Sortition Foundation, Josiah Mortimer — Byline Times, Lord Chris Rennard, Myf Nixon — mySociety, Pip Eldridge — Voice of the Listener & Viewer, Madison Hammonds — CitizenCard, Laurie Moulton-Ulrich , Martyn Harris — North Warks…

items.h: Migrant Democracy Project require policy change costing assistance
items.b: Migrant Democracy Project (MDP) work to ensure every resident of the UK has equal access to democratic participation in the UK. The MDP team need semi-urgent specialist assistance with how to cost the implementation of a policy change, in this case, Residence-Based Voting Rights (RBVR). Contact Lara Parizotto if you can assist .
items.note: A request for costing assistance on a policy idea is sector logistics, not a reported change to franchise or suffrage.
links: Contact Lara Parizotto if you can assist

items.h: Are you thinking about deliberation and participation through a design lens? Brian Morgan wants to know
items.b: Brian Morgan is currently undertaking a PhD at Ulster University. They’re particularly interested in exploring who, if anyone, is working on citizens’ assemblies and deliberative practices through a design lens. If you know anyone, or would like to discuss, contact Brian .
items.note: PhD researcher networking request, not a new participation mechanism or reported change.

items.h: Martyn Harris offers subject matter expertise around electoral law & practice
items.b: Your friendly neighbourhood elections administrator, Martyn Harris , Head of Elections at North Warks & Nuneaton and Bedworth Councils, is kindly offering their advice and guidance on electoral law and practice, and their experience of working in a polling station or observing an election count. If either of these are helpful, please contact Martyn .

items.h: Ruth Hannan of People’s Powerhouse offers the chance to join their community map of the North
items.b: Are you an organisation working to make change happen in the North of England? Peoples’ Powerhouse invites you to join their community map and growing network. Last week People’s Powerhouse brought together the network at their amazing #ThisIsTheNorth Conference — the largest pan-Northern conference of the year.
items.note: Invitation to join an existing organisational network map, not creation of a new participation mechanism for the public.

items.h: Together We Can, Democracy Network Conference tickets now on sale
items.b: Last year at our inaugural conference more than 100 organisations, elected representatives, civil society leaders, campaigners and journalists came together for two days of stimulating discussion, collaboration and connection. Join us next month at our annual democracy gathering as all eyes turn to the prospect of a general election, featuring panel discussions, workshops, networking lunches and even a ‘Democracy’s Got Talent’ evening dinner. Register now on Eventbrite , bursaries are available for travel and ticketing costs.
links: Join us next month at our annual democracy gathering

items.h: Networking for People of Colour in the democracy sector
items.b: Operation Black Vote , The Black Equity Organisation , The Politics Project and the Civic Power Fund are working on an event specifically for people of colour with decision-making power in their organisation who are working on or organising around the 2024 election. If this is for you or you want to nominate someone to attend please contact mohammed@civicpower.org.uk

items.h: All Island Network for Better Democracy launching soon
items.b: Rebekah McCabe, Head of Northern Ireland at Involve , has recently been awarded funding by the St Stephens Green Trust to develop a new network for democracy covering the island of Ireland. The Network for Better Democracy is a new initiative to bring together people interested in ways to enable high quality, impactful participation and deliberative democracy on the island of Ireland. Find out more, contact Rebekah .
items.why: a newly funded network is being created to build capacity for deliberative and participatory democracy across the island of Ireland, expanding the means available for people to take part
items.note: Launch of a new capacity-building network counts as a participation story per the sector capacity-building rule.

items.h: Demos and Engage Britain undertake merger
items.b: Last month, Engage Britain merged with Demos , pooling resources and expertise to help make the case for participatory policy making. Their new chapter will start with a people-powered policy making programme which they will run ahead of the general election. In a statement, Demos highlighted their shared mission to put people at the heart of policy-making, championing participatory policy-making as a solution to our democratic challenges, saying that ‘by coming together, we hope to turbo-charge our impact, making the case for involving people in the decisions that affect their lives and ensur…
items.note: Organisational merger news, not a change to participation mechanisms yet.

items.h: Back the call to reinstate the Access to Elected Office Fund for Disabled candidates
items.b: Elect Her , Disability Rights UK , Disability Policy Centre and Centenary Action Group published their joint statement, backed by over 30 democracy sector organisations. The statement calls on the UK Government to urgently reinstate an Access to Elected Office Fund to support Disabled candidates to contest elections. Supportive organisations can share this Write to MP tool here , and raise awareness on social media .
items.why: the campaign concerns whether public office and candidacy are practically open to disabled citizens, bearing on the representativeness and accessibility of elected institutions

items.h: The Democracy Box publish their report and proof of concept
items.b: After four years of research and two years of writing the report, the Democracy Box report is now live! Democracy Box trained recruited and trained 61 young people as co-creators of the project, with more than 600 young people participating in events & focus groups as part of the project — totalling 9,000 visits to The Talking Shop trials. Yvonne Murphy and the team have published two versions of the report, an abridged version and an extensive version — don’t miss it.
items.note: Publication of a project report reads as organisational output rather than the creation of a new participation mechanism at this point.

items.h: Rise in hate crime against LGBTQ+ people continues, Stonewall slams UK Government inaction
items.b: New hate crime statistics released by the Office for National Statistics last month show that England and Wales continue to become an increasingly less safe place for lesbian, gay, bi and trans people. Increase in hate crimes against trans people increased 11% last year and by 186% in the past five years, the report states. Stonewall , Europe’s largest LGBTQ+ charity, argue this comes against a backdrop of central government withdrawing support for trans people and the growth of divisive and demonising rhetoric about trans people in society. Read the report .
items.why: rising hate crime and government inaction on protecting a group's safety and freedom from discrimination undermines equal protection and personal security under the law.

items.b: 50:50 Parliament’s #AskHerToStand 2023 (Photo credit: 50:50 Parliament)
items.note: Photo caption with no substantive content.

items.b: Lyanne Nicholl, the newly hired CEO of 50:50 Parliament , celebrates their recent #AskHerToStand Day in the House of Commons, where hundreds of women joined up to stand for office in the upcoming elections. ‘I couldn’t have asked for a warmer, or more inspiring, welcome to 50:50’ Lyanne said. If this piques your interest, don’t miss their monthly bitesize events, or their upcoming ‘Be A Councillor’ event with the LGA on the 7th December, as well as their programme of support for women standing for office across the UK — sign up to find out more now .
items.why: encouraging and supporting women to stand for elected office affects who can access candidacy and the representativeness of elected institutions.
items.note: Framed partly as organisational news but substantively about candidate access, which sits under elections.
links: sign up to find out more now

items.h: Sortition Foundation launch new Europe operation, hiring new Head of Press & Comms
items.b: Based out of Budapest, Sortition Europe aims to run democratic lotteries for European Citizens’ Panels and other transnational European citizens’ assemblies — see more about this on their blog . They’re also hiring a new Head of Press & Comms , find out more here — deadline 20th December.
items.note: Primarily a hiring announcement for a European operation with no clear UK democratic bearing.

items.h: Patchwork Foundation host MP of the Year Awards
items.b: Last week Patchwork Foundation held their annual MP of the Year Awards , celebrating MPs for their work on a range of areas from MPs championing young people, to cross-party collaboration, advocating for rural communities and supporting vulnerable communities.
items.note: An awards ceremony celebrating MPs is organisational activity, not a reported democratic mechanism.

items.h: Twitter posing challenges for comms leads
items.b: Democracy Network’s Comms Lead Adam is scratching his head at the increasingly restrictive algorithm on the platform formerly known as Twitter and wondering what other channels people might be using or considering as an alternative. Contact Adam to discuss . Relatedly, if you’re a comms or digital lead , we highly recommend you join Duane Raymond’s Electronic Campaigning Forum (ECF) community for all the latest chatter and gossip on matters such as this!
items.note: Informal internal musing about comms channels and a networking group invite, not a reported change to the information environment.

items.h: Elect Her offering new Digital Self-Defence and Self Care training
items.b: In partnership with Glitch UK , Elect Her are now offering new training and support for Digital Self-Defence and Self-Care. Any women in Britain can register to access their support here .
items.why: a new training resource helping women protect themselves online expands practical capacity to participate safely in political life, including standing for office.
items.note: Counted under the sector capacity-building rule as a new means of participation.

items.h: mySociety looking for new board members, celebrates 20 years with awards ceremony
items.b: Last month mySociety celebrated their 20th anniversary with an awards ceremony in central London. Myf Nixon, Marketing & Communications Manager at mySociety, reveals all, including the award winners on their blog . But that’s not all, they’re now looking for a new Trustee and Non-Executive Director for SocietyWorks — find out more here , deadline for applications is 15th January.
items.note: Organisational anniversary and board recruitment notice, not a democracy story.

items.h: Innovation in Politics Awards busy judging for latest awards submissions
items.b: Now on their 7th annual edition of the Awards, the Innovation in Politics Institute Awards work to celebrate and highlight courageous political work across Europe, including the UK. Take a look at their awards in recent years for a flavour of the type of projects they have selected as best practice examples. Whilst submissions for the latest round closed on the 8th Dec, IiPA have indicated they are open to late submissions past the deadline, for the keen beans — you can do so here .
items.note: Awards submission and judging process is sector admin, not a democracy mechanism.

items.h: UK GovCamp 2024 is coming
items.b: Every year the team at GovCamp run a free unconference for people who want to improve government . Next year’s conference is going to be a 500 attendee in-person event in central London. If this is the first time you’ve come across GovCamp, check out their video explainer .
items.note: Annual unconference event listing rather than a new participation mechanism or resource.
links: GovCamp run a free unconference for people who want to improve government

items.h: New Systemic Justice toolkit empowers communities to take the law into their own hands
items.b: The new toolkit for movements and communities outlines an approach for strategic litigation, using legal action as a tool to better fight racial, social and economic injustice. Check out the new resources and guide by System Justice and apply it in your work .
items.why: this matters democratically because it creates a new resource enabling communities to organise and use strategic litigation to challenge injustice, expanding practical means of civic participation.
items.note: New toolkit counts as sector capacity-building creating means of participation, though it operates via legal mechanisms.
links: Check out the new resources and guide by System Justice and apply it in your work

items.h: Medact looking for new Executive Director
items.b: Medact works to bring together health workers to fight for health justice. They’re now hiring a new Executive Director to develop their next five-year strategy and build on their previous five years of success and growth, bringing lasting victories in their campaigns for health justice. Apply now , deadline 2nd January.
items.note: Staff recruitment notice for an organisation, not a democracy mechanism.

items.h: Stronger Things 2024 returns
items.b: Stronger Things returns next summer bringing together 1,600 changemakers from the local government, healthcare, voluntary and community sectors. Run by New Local , the annual festival offers the opportunity to be part of an expansive network setting the community power agenda.
items.note: Recurring annual festival event listing, not a newly created participation tool.

items.h: UK Government increases election spending limits by 80%, attracts ire of Electoral Commission
items.b: Earlier this year Secretary of State Michael Gove announced that campaign spending limits for Westminster elections were to be increased. As Justin Fisher explains for the Constitution Unit Blog , since the last time spending limits were set through PPERA , these numbers have never been adjusted for inflation and as a result is approx 50% lower in real terms than when it was introduced. The latest change increasing limits by 80% mean that the Conservative Party General Election spend could top £36 million, £17 million more than their 2019 total. The Electoral Commission reported they had not s…
items.why: this matters democratically because raising campaign spending limits changes the competitive conditions of elections and the transparency safeguards the Electoral Commission oversees.
links: Justin Fisher explains for the Constitution Unit Blog
concerned that the proposals risk damaging the transparency of political donations

items.h: Byline Times highlight ‘massive hike to election spending limits’
items.b: Writing for the Byline Times Josiah Mortimer provides some context to the spending limit changes outlined above, that in the last year alone the three largest donations to political parties were given to the Conservative Party, including two individual donations of more than £5m. Labour left-winger Lord Prem Sikka called for the Govt to consider introducing a law which would require political parties to state what they’ve promised in return for donations. Rejecting the suggestion, Conservative frontbencher Baroness Penn said the Government had ‘no plans to limit the size of donations that are …
items.why: this matters democratically because large political donations and raised spending limits affect the fairness of electoral competition and the transparency of party financing.
items.note: Campaign finance and donation transparency sit at the boundary of elections and accountability; classified primarily as elections given the spending-limit focus.

items.h: Get set for The Politics Project General Election Strategy Day, 2nd Feb 2024
items.b: Building on their strategy day earlier this year bringing together more than 80 civic education organisations from across the Democracy Classroom Network , The Politics Project team are planning a new event on 2nd Feb 2024 to collectively plan and coordinate activities in the run up to the various, local, regional and national elections taking place in 2024. The event will include workshops with subject matter experts on key issues orgs are likely to face next year, as well as key networking opportunities, joint planning and collaboration. If you are interested in coming along, please contact …
items.note: Event listing for sector coordination ahead of elections, not itself a new participation mechanism or reported change.

items.b: That’s not all from Democracy Classroom, they’re also organising those interested in working around hustings. Join them on the 15th January 1–2pm, contact sian@thepoliticsproject.org.uk for more details.
items.note: Event/logistics notice with no substantive democratic mechanism described.

items.h: National Voter Registration Week — 4th March 2024
items.b: Democracy Classroom and their partner organisations have agreed a date for their collaborative National Voter Registration Week (NVRW), commencing on the 4th March 2024 — this is an opportunity for those running voter registration campaigns to focus efforts, work together, and amplify the reach of the various campaigns. NVRW will run in collaboration with National Voter Registration Day that is planned for April and is being led by My Life My Say .
items.why: it creates a coordinated campaign push to increase electoral registration, directly affecting who can exercise the franchise.
items.note: Turnout/registration campaigns are always filed under elections per the standing rule.

items.h: CitizenCard gear up for their No ID No Vote campaign launch
items.b: CitizenCard is a non-profit organisation focused on administering PASS cards, which is a voter ID option. Stevie Wren & Madison Hammonds share that they are now gearing up for a January launch of their No ID No Vote voter information campaign — they’re keen for others to reach out and team up, find out more here .
items.why: it addresses whether voter ID requirements create barriers to casting a ballot, a core electoral access mechanism.

items.h: Polimapper publishes new report on the next generation of MPs
items.b: The report by Polimapper, All Change at Westminster! Meet the Class of 24 , looks at the current crop of candidates standing for election in 2024. Though the data presents a dire picture, only 39% of prime candidates (those in target seats or successor candidates) are women and just 10% are from an ethnic minority background. Polimapper’s report marks the first detailed aggregate analysis of those set to make up the next House of Commons.
items.why: it provides new evidence on the representativeness of the candidates who will make up the next Parliament.
links: All Change at Westminster! Meet the Class of 24

items.h: Democracy Club launch their prospective parliamentary candidate tracker
items.b: In preparation for next year’s General Election, Democracy Club has launched a prospective parliamentary candidate tracker here . They have also created a widget that generates a timetable for any given election date allowing you to prepare better your election activities.
items.why: it creates a new tool improving public and campaigner access to information about candidates standing for election.
links: widget that generates a timetable for any given election date

items.why: it builds a new tool to help campaigners and activists understand and comply with electoral law, affecting electoral administration and access.

items.h: Vote for Policies is supporting campaign organisations who want to help their members vote on the issues that matter to them
items.b: For the last four general elections, Vote for Policies has run a manifesto-comparison survey to help people make an informed choice when they vote. For the next election they are also creating custom versions for campaign organisations. You can host it yourself and promote it independently. Here’s an example they did for private renters . Ahead of the election VfP hopes this can also provide a useful tool to gather data on policy popularity, enabling organisations to develop dialogue with political parties accordingly. For any questions or info please email matt.cm@voteforpolicies.org.uk
items.why: it creates a new civic tool enabling voters and organisations to compare policies and engage more meaningfully in political decision-making.
items.note: Sector capacity-building tool for civic engagement, with an informational dimension.
links: Here’s an example they did for private renters

items.h: UK exposes attempted Russian interference in political and democratic processes, say UK Government
items.b: The UK Government and her international allies have called out sustained and unsuccessful attempts to interfere in UK politics and democratic processes since at least 2015, GCHQ reports. The threats originate from Centre 18 of Russia’s Federal Security Service, they say. Malicious activity by Russia has included the hacking and leaking of UK-US trade documents ahead of the 2019 General Election, the hacking of the Institute for Statecraft and a range of other targets, including university, journalists, NGOs, CSOs and public sector organisations. High risk individuals, including politicians and…
items.why: foreign state hacking and leaking of political material ahead of elections and targeting of journalists, NGOs and public bodies is a foreign information operation aimed at undermining the integrity of UK political debate and electoral processes
items.note: Classified under information_debate as foreign information operations, with electoral integrity as a secondary concern given the pre-election hacking.
links: UK Government and her international allies have called out sustained and unsuccessful attempts to interfere in UK politics and democratic processes

items.h: Sadiq Khan criticises voter ID laws which they claim could disenfranchise 900,000 Londoners next year
items.b: London Mayor Sadiq Khan has struck out against the Voter ID legislation that will be in place for the first time in London at next year’s Mayoral Election. Khan called it a ‘cynical attempt to make it harder for people to vote’ as 900,000 Londoners could be silenced. Their figures come from Labour-commissioned Opinium polling which found that 15 percent of Londoners do not have voter ID.
items.why: voter identification requirements directly affect who can exercise their right to vote in a competitive election
links: struck out against the Voter ID legislation

items.h: Meta discuss their approach to elections in 2024
items.b: Nick Clegg, President of Global Affairs at Meta and former UK Deputy Prime Minister, sets our Meta’s vision and role in the various upcoming elections across the globe in the next 12 months.
items.why: a major platform's policies on political content and moderation shape the plurality and reliability of information voters encounter around elections
links: sets our Meta’s vision and role

items.b: The Democracy Network is part-way through refurbishing our resources and directories, including the UK Democracy Map and funding list. This is the current list of active democracy grant funds in the UK, please review and tell us if anything is missing , or if we’ve made an error — alternatively, add any grant funds we’ve missed via this form .
