items.h: Civic Power Fund hiring, publish new research on funding justice, launching new youth organising alliance
items.b: Mohammed Afridi, Civic Power Fund’s Director of Organising, reports that they’re launching a new Alliance for Youth Organising — a new intergenerational collective that’ll work together to invest in spaces, networks and organisations to support youth organising in the UK, funded by Civic Power Fund (CPF), Paul Hamlyn Foundation, Esmée Fairbairn Foundation, and the Blagrave Trust. To this end they’re hiring a new Youth Organising Lead and up to nine new Members of the new alliance. 5th January deadline for both of these, apply now and share the word about these excellent opportunities . In addi…
items.why: launching a new funded alliance to support youth organising creates new infrastructure and networks that enable young people to take part in civic and political life
items.note: Hiring and research-publication elements are organisational admin, but the alliance launch qualifies as sector capacity-building.

items.h: Polish Migrants Organise for Change & Civic Power Fund report back on their New York learning exchange
items.b: With funding from Unbound Philanthropy , Paul Hamlyn Foundation and This Day Foundation , POMOC and Civic Power Fund brought together 14 community organisers and 5 funders to head over to the US for a knowledge exchange with their American counterparts. In their blog, Martha Mackenzie, Executive Director of the Civic Power Fund, unpacks eight key takeaways from their recent trip .
items.note: A report-back on a learning exchange trip is organisational activity, not a new means of participation created.
links: unpacks eight key takeaways from their recent trip

items.h: Civic Innovation Fund now open for applications
items.b: The CIVICS Innovation Hub , an NGO supporting civic education in Europe, have opened calls for their Civic Innovation Fund , a new pooled fund aimed at pioneering new ideas in civil society. Apply here and find out more , CIF are offering €10,000 for piloting, incubation and scaling, for a period of 12 months — deadline 25 Jan 2024.
items.note: A funding call is explicitly sector logistics, not a democracy story.

items.h: Changemakers for Democracy selecting Fellowships
items.b: Supported by the Open Society Foundation, the Changemakers for Democracy Fellowship is a 12 month programme supporting up to 15 Europe-based practitioners and representatives of innovations, movements and collectives working on democratic renewal and new economic paradigms. The Fellowship is specifically aimed at supporting activities to radically improve democratic renewal. Whilst the deadline closed last week, you can find out more here .
items.note: An announcement about fellowship selection for practitioners is sector/opportunity admin rather than a new means of public participation.

items.h: The New Institute is looking for Future of Democracy Fellows
items.b: The Hamburg based fellowship is fully funded. See here for more information .
items.note: Fellowship funding advert, sector logistics not a democracy story.

items.h: Catalyst publish list of third sector digital funding opportunities
items.b: Catalyst has published a full list of third sector funding organisations — check it out now.
items.note: Listing of funding opportunities is sector logistics.
links: published a full list of third sector funding organisations

items.h: Churchill Fellowship open to applications
items.b: The paid Churchill Fellowship enables successful applicants to spend 4–8 weeks meeting and working with innovators in your field, anywhere in the world, in person or online, helping you develop your learnings into practical outputs for your community or sector. Find out more .
items.note: Fellowship funding call, sector logistics.

items.h: New Economy Organisers Network apply for further funding to extend their electoral law programme
items.b: In recent months, the New Economy Organisers Network (NEON) have been running a programme of high quality briefings on electoral law for campaigners and charities ahead of the 2024 General Election, together with Bates Wells and Stone King. Now they’re looking to extend their electoral law briefings and workshops as the election nears — do you know any relevant funds, can you help fund these important activities?
items.note: Primarily a funding appeal to extend an existing programme, not the launch of a new capacity-building resource.

items.h: Major political reform could secure key Labour target voters, Compass and Unlock Democracy study suggests
items.b: A YouGov survey conducted for Unlock Democracy and Compass has revealed a strong appetite amongst Labour’s two key target groups ‘Workington Man’ and ‘Stevenage Woman’ for major political reform . The focus groups emphasised the lack of trust in politicians to deliver on reform, but the findings signal a vote-winning opportunity for political parties, especially Labour, if they indicate they are serious about political reform.
items.why: it reports survey evidence on public trust in politicians and appetite for political reform, which reflects underlying support for and confidence in how democratic power is exercised.
links: revealed a strong appetite amongst Labour’s two key target groups ‘Workington Man’ and ‘Stevenage Woman’ for major political reform

items.h: Nesta’s Centre for Collective Intelligence Design launches new report on democratic innovations
items.b: Lewis Westbury, Senior Developer at Nesta , reports that they have just published their latest Collective Intelligence through Digital Tools for Democratic Innovation (COLDIGIT) report, Making Democratic Innovations Stick . The report explores the barriers to innovations, the prevailing reasons to use innovations and perceptions on involving the public in decision making — read the report here .
items.why: it studies the barriers and enablers to embedding deliberative democratic innovations that give the public a role in collective decision-making.
items.note: Deliberative democratic innovations are classified under elections & decision making per the framework's boundary rule.

items.h: Northern Ireland Affairs Committee urge the UK Government to establish an NI Citizens’ Assembly
items.b: Last week the Northern Ireland Affairs Committee (NIAC) published their report into the effectiveness of the institutions of the Good Friday Agreement . In the report, the NIAC ‘urge the Government to begin preparations for establishing a Northern Ireland Citizens’ Assembly’. In this short blog Involve unpacks the recommendations they made to the NIAC back in 2020 .
items.why: it recommends establishing a citizens' assembly, a new deliberative decision-making mechanism, to address governance issues in Northern Ireland.
items.note: Citizens' assemblies fall under elections & decision making, not participation, per the framework's boundary rule.
links: report into the effectiveness of the institutions of the Good Friday Agreement
unpacks the recommendations they made to the NIAC back in 2020

items.h: Involve asks, could involving citizens help unlock true English devolution?
items.b: Calum Green and Maddie Gough at Involve are developing a new set of proposals around how deliberative and participatory processes could help to better deliver English devolution and tackle the democratic deficit through greater involvement of citizens. Read the blog announcing this new tranche of work by Involve and reach out to Maddie to find out more or contribute to the project .
items.why: it develops proposals for deliberative and participatory processes to shape the structure and decision-making powers of English devolution.
items.note: Deliberative processes tied to devolution structures are classified under elections & decision making.
links: reach out to Maddie to find out more or contribute to the project

items.h: Cameron’s reappointment prompts fresh calls for House of Lords reform
items.b: A plethora of MPs and campaigners have criticised David Cameron’s appointment to the House of Lords claiming it makes a mockery of the honours system. CEO of campaign group Republic , Graham Smith, said the move is a reminder of ‘the urgent need to ditch the Lords in favour of an elected upper house’ whilst Naomi Smith, CEO of Best for Britain , said Cameron’s appointment is ‘another Tory VIP lane, only this time for unelected has-beens.’
items.why: this matters democratically because it concerns the integrity of public appointments and the honours system used to populate a chamber of the legislature.
items.note: Framed as an appointments/standards controversy rather than an electoral reform proposal, though calls for an elected Lords touch elections_decision_making.
links: criticised David Cameron’s appointment to the House of Lords

items.h: Constitution Unit publishes latest round up of constitutional developments
items.b: The Constitution Unit has published their latest issue of the Monitor . Their thrice-yearly bulletin provides a round-up and analysis of constitutional developments over the preceding four months. In this latest edition, they cover the controversies over the government’s attitude to parliamentary scrutiny, recent decisions over the alleged misconduct of parliamentarians, demands for reform of House of Lords appointments, the Electoral Commission’s report on the impact of voter ID legislation, and much more .
items.note: An announcement that a round-up publication exists, without itself reporting a specific democratic development.

items.h: Where next for English devolution? Institute for Government investigate
items.b: In a special episode of the Inside Briefing podcast , Akash Paun from the Institute for Government travels across England to find out whether a ‘devolution revolution’ is really taking place. The podcast explores how power is being devolved to the East Midlands, and brings together an expert panel to make sense of England’s evolving devolution settlement.
items.why: this matters democratically because it examines whether power and decision-making authority are genuinely being transferred to sub-national tiers of government.
items.note: Devolution structure and powers are filed under elections_decision_making per the boundary rule on local/regional government.

items.h: ANTIPARTY planning their first campaign advocating for direct and deliberative democracy
items.b: Isabella Roberts, Founder of ANTIPARTY , is looking to set up and facilitate citizens’ assemblies and citizens’ panels in collaboration with other organisations and projects working on direct and deliberative democracy — get in touch with Bella to find out more .
items.why: this matters democratically because it creates new deliberative and direct-democracy machinery (citizens' assemblies and panels) for taking collective decisions.
items.note: Citizens' assemblies and deliberative processes are classified under elections_decision_making, not participation, per the revised framework.

items.h: Commission on Political Power exploring responses to corruption
items.b: Frances Crook and the team at the Commission on Political Power are soliciting ideas about improving the UK legislation, transparency, behaviour and accountability in relation to corruption. Submissions to the Commission should be directed to info@commissionpoliticalpower.uk . A briefing on corruption and political funding will be published in the New Year.
items.note: A call for submissions to a commission, akin to sector administrative logistics rather than a reported development.

items.h: Senior politicians are attempting to wholly bypass constitutional norms, report Constitutional Monitoring Group
items.b: The latest report from the Constitution Monitoring Group covering the six month period from Jan — June 2023, found that senior politicians, including a former Prime Minister, have violated basic constitutional and ethical principles. The report states ‘there is evidence of a desire on the part of some to wholly bypass or even remove barriers to the violation of constitutional norms.’
items.why: this matters democratically because it reports evidence that senior politicians are seeking to bypass constitutional constraints on executive power.
links: latest report from the Constitution Monitoring Group

items.h: New report from Carnegie UK highlights ‘perilous state of democracy’
items.b: New research from Carnegie UK has found a widespread lack of trust across all age groups in the UK’s political systems and institutions. The survey found that almost three quarters (73%) of people in the UK feel that they cannot influence decisions that affect the UK as a whole, whilst 52% said they have a low level of trust in the Government.
items.why: this matters democratically because widespread perceptions that people cannot influence decisions affecting them reflect low political efficacy, a condition for genuine participation.
items.note: Trust in government also touches government_accountability, but the dominant framing is public efficacy and influence.

items.h: Liberty condemn 630 climate activist arrests in one month alone
items.b: In November alone UK police arrested more than 630 peaceful climate protesters campaigning against new oil and gas production in the UK. Liberty condemns the statistics as ‘staggering and shocking’ . Some accounts of what activists have faced in recent weeks:
items.why: this matters democratically because mass arrests of peaceful protesters concern the state's use of coercive power to restrict freedom of assembly.
items.note: Framed as policing and state coercion of protest, so filed under rights_freedoms_civic_space rather than participation.
links: UK police arrested more than 630 peaceful climate protesters
Liberty condemns the statistics as ‘staggering and shocking’

items.b: A 23-year old protester was arrested within 5 minutes of joining a demonstration and held for 56 hours in custody before being presented before court on an accelerated schedule.
items.why: this matters democratically because it shows police using new powers to restrict a citizen's right to protest through rapid arrest and prolonged pre-court detention.
items.note: Protest policing and state coercion falls under rights & freedoms rather than participation.

items.b: A 46-year old nursery school teaching assistant, and father of two sons, was remanded to HMP Pentonville indefinitely after marching for two minutes in the road.
items.why: this matters democratically because indefinite remand for a brief act of protest signals a disproportionate state response that could chill the exercise of assembly rights.
items.note: Protest policing and state coercion falls under rights & freedoms rather than participation.

items.b: A 19-year old was similarly held in a London prison for 4 nights before their court hearing, and then allegedly unlawfully held for a further 3 nights when they should have been released.
items.why: this matters democratically because unlawful extension of a protester's detention beyond the legally required release point undermines due process and predictable enforcement of law.
items.note: Part of a series on protest policing; also raises rule-of-law concerns about unlawful detention.

items.b: Police have been making these arrests under Section 7 of the new Public Order Action 2023 . A spokesperson for Climate Action Support Pathway said ‘this was the first real test for these new Section 7 powers…and it became quickly clear the police would use them readily’.
items.why: this matters democratically because it documents the first operational use of new statutory powers that expand police authority to restrict protest and assembly.
links: Section 7 of the new Public Order Action 2023

items.h: Riot police raid London Kurdish community cultural event
items.b: Dozens of Metropolitan Police Territorial Support Group officers attempted to raid the Kurdish People’s Democratic Assembly event at the Kurdish Community Centre in Haringey, London, last month. Members of the community later reported that officers failed to produce a warrant and indicated ‘no legitimate reason’ for the aggression and violence that they conducted themselves with against a community of civilians celebrating a cultural event. The Kurdish Community Centre is now pursuing legal action against the Metropolitan Police.
items.why: this matters democratically because a warrantless police raid on a community cultural event represents state interference with a civic organisation's freedom of association.
items.note: Freedom of association for a civic/cultural body falls under rights & freedoms.
links: attempted to raid the Kurdish People’s Democratic Assembly event
Members of the community later reported that officers failed to produce a warrant and indicated ‘no legitimate reason’

items.h: Children at risk of being deported by Home Office, say Human Rights groups
items.b: Human rights groups have warned that unaccompanied minors could be deported under the Rwanda scheme as more than 1,000 minors have been mistakenly identified as adults by the Home Office. According to a Refugee Council study of initial age-disputed decisions in 2021, 94% of Home Office assessments were incorrect.
items.why: this matters democratically because systemic errors in state age-assessment processes risk unlawful deportation of children without adequate due process or redress.
items.note: Framed around wrongful administrative decisions and lack of due process rather than a rights claim alone.
links: warned that unaccompanied minors could be deported

items.h: Majority of voters say think tank funding should be more transparent
items.b: A majority (59%) of the British public believe think tanks are not transparent , Deltapoll polling for the Centre Think Tank and Millbank Think Tank has found. The polling forms part of a new report by the think tanks into the state of think tank transparency in which they analysed over 100 think tanks and found that 22% of think tanks did not display a total income and only 32% of think tanks revealed all funders over £7,500.
items.why: this matters democratically because opaque funding of influential policy organisations undermines the public's ability to hold decision-influencing bodies accountable.
links: public believe think tanks are not transparent

items.h: Voice of the Listener & Viewer developing new coalition, hold their 40th Annual Autumn Conference
items.b: Pip Eldridge of Voice of the Listener & Viewer , says they are currently building a new coalition to campaign for the government to make changes to the draft Media Bill to ensure more effective regulation to safeguard against disinformation and ensure access to media regardless of bandwidth constraints. Last week they held their 40th Annual Conference celebrating Public Service Broadcasting and honing in on what is being done to preserve it — see more over on VLV’s socials .
items.why: this matters democratically because a coalition campaigning to strengthen media regulation and safeguard against disinformation affects the plurality and reliability of the public information environment.
items.note: Coalition-building for policy advocacy is treated as sector capacity-building rather than mere organisational news.

items.h: Public Interest News Foundation developing new NewsMatch style matchfunding programme
items.b: Public Interest News Foundation are currently across many pies at the moment, from LTN disinformation research, surveying UK newsrooms, improving their local news mapping, working on the digital media advocacy bill, hatching a plan for an Indie News Day and developing a new NewsMatch matchfunding programme for non profit news in the UK — if any of this sounds relevant to you, chat to Joe for more information — oh, and they quit Twitter too .
items.note: This is organisational news about a democracy-focused organisation's various activities, not a specific reportable change to participation mechanisms.

items.h: Society of Editors welcomes new plans to protect media freedom and journalists
items.b: New plans unveiled by the government to promote media freedom and protect journalists have been welcomed by the Society of Editors . The new protections will see enhanced training for police officers on the rights of journalists to report from protests, a new online portal for journalists to report abuse, as well as a new industry taskforce on keeping staff safe.
items.why: new government measures to protect journalist safety and police training on press rights at protests affect the practical safety and functioning of journalism as part of the public information environment.
links: welcomed by the Society of Editors

items.h: Networks 4 Democracy launches
items.b: A new Horizon Europe-funded initiative to establish a new European network of practitioners and researchers in the fields of democracy, civic deliberation, participation and citizenship education has kicked off in Brussels . Networks for Democracy (Nets4Dem) aims to spread knowledge and best practice about democratic innovation and civic participation throughout Europe and globally.
items.why: the launch of a new network to spread knowledge and practice on democratic innovation, civic deliberation and participation creates new capacity-building infrastructure for civic engagement.
items.note: Sector capacity-building counts as a participation story per framework rule, though the UK link is indirect via a European network.

items.h: Involve offering new online training masterclasses
items.b: The sessions offered by Involve include training in facilitation skills, understanding of public engagement, and equitable engagement, exploring issues of power and privilege in engagement processes. Find out more and sign up here .
items.why: this matters democratically because it creates new training capacity that helps people and organisations engage more effectively in public participation processes.
items.note: Sector capacity-building (new training resource) counts as participation per the special rule.

items.h: Democracy Club seeking £10k funding to improve their Election Leaflets site in time for upcoming elections
items.b: Democracy Club’s Election Leaflets site is the UK’s primary source for election leaflet data, with more than 18,000 leaflets archived on the portal. Peter Keeling and the team at Democracy Club are looking to improve the site and explore its use in the upcoming elections, but they need £10k to hire a developer to work on it — can you help?
items.why: this matters democratically because the tool archives campaign leaflets, supporting transparency and scrutiny of electoral campaigning material ahead of elections.
items.note: Borderline between campaign transparency (elections) and information environment; funding call rather than a completed launch.

items.h: Migrant Democracy Project looking for orgs in St Albans
items.b: Alex Bulat and the Migrant Democracy Project team are on the lookout for any democracy organisations working in St Albans — do you know anyone? They are looking to engage with migrants for organising a tour of Parliament for that constituency area.
items.why: this matters democratically because it seeks to build civic engagement capacity by connecting migrants with Parliament and organisations that support their participation.
items.note: Sector capacity-building aimed at expanding participation for an underrepresented group.

items.h: Byline Times VoteWatch project on the hunt for stories
items.b: Josiah Mortimer at Byline Times is looking to collaborate with democracy organisations for their VoteWatch project , which they’re partly crowdfunding. They’re interested in any and all projects and stories on dis/misinformation, deep fakes, election spending/donations and dodgy campaigning. Got a scoop? Email Josiah .
items.why: this matters democratically because it builds investigative journalism capacity to expose disinformation, deepfakes and dodgy campaign spending that distort the public information environment around elections.

items.h: Talk Shop looking to experiment with Win-Win Workouts on contentious local issues
items.b: Perry Walker and the Talk Shop team have spent the last couple of years developing their Win-Win Workout tool, designed to help small groups find common ground. Check out the new video explaining the format now . Talk Shop are working to identify contentious local issues, particularly transport and planning, through which they can develop a way forward. Got any suggestions? Email Perry Walker .
items.why: this matters democratically because it develops a deliberative tool intended to help communities reach collective decisions on contentious local issues.
items.note: Deliberative process development is filed under elections & decision making per the revised framework.
links: new video explaining the format now

items.b: Martyn Harris , Head of Elections and North Warwickshire Borough Council, is seeking feedback on their elections pages .
items.note: A feedback request on an existing council elections webpage is sector admin rather than a change to what people can do.

items.h: New Economy Organisers Network OrgBuilders programme open for applications, deadline 17th March
items.b: OrgBuilders , NEON’s 12 month programme that enables leaders to build winning strategy, structure, and culture into your organisation, is designed for social justice organisations at early and growth stages or those in a period of transformation who are looking to make changes and improvements to ways of working. The programme involves training, coaching and opportunities to link with other organisations facing similar challenges. Applications close on 17 March — Apply now .
items.why: This matters democratically because it builds the organisational capacity of civil society groups to organise and take part in political and civic life.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building for civil society under the participation beat.

items.h: Launch of the All-Island Better Democracy Network
items.b: The All-Island Better Democracy Network is a community of individuals and civil society organisations working to build a healthier democracy, more active citizenship and stronger civic voice across the island of Ireland. The Better Democracy network is a project of Involve and has been made possible by a grant from St Stephens’ Green Trust . Don’t miss their launch event in Belfast as part of the Imagine! Belfast Festival .
items.why: This matters democratically because the launch of a new civic network creates fresh means for citizens to build active citizenship and civic voice.
items.note: Launch of a network explicitly aimed at strengthening civic participation counts as capacity-building under participation.

items.h: Demos launching Collaborative Democracy Network
items.b: On the 13th of March, Demos is launching a new network — the Collaborative Democracy Network — bringing together politicians, policymakers and civil society to discuss innovations that put people at the heart of policy making. Sign up for the launch event now which will feature Florence Eshalomi MP, Shadow Minister for Democracy, and Martin Wolf CBE, Chief Economics Commentator at the Financial Times.
items.why: it creates a new cross-sector network aimed at embedding participatory, people-centred approaches into policy making, expanding the means available for civic engagement.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating a new participation mechanism rather than a mere event listing.

items.h: Centenary Action host event on the power of women’s votes this election year
items.b: This women’s history month Centenary Action are thinking about the power of women’s votes. 100 years ago not all women could vote, they say. In this special event they will explore insights from women leaders on how to make the most of the election year — Register for the online event now

items.h: Newspeak House open for Fellowship applications
items.b: Newspeak House, the London College of Political Technology , is a residential college in East London. Participants spend a year immersed in civic communities of practices with the opportunity to meet thousands of people and participate in a wide range of in-person events. The programme is designed to support mid-career technologists to develop a holistic understanding of the civic landscape in the UK, in order to found groundbreaking new projects or seek strategic positions in key institutions. Apply now .
items.why: it creates a new capacity-building programme intended to help participants understand and act within the UK's civic and political landscape, expanding practical means of democratic participation.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building under the participation beat rather than organisational news.

items.b: Working across Migrant Democracy Project’s voter registration, voting rights advocacy work and community organising, the new full time position is open to applications on a rolling basis, so apply now !

items.h: Understanding Society publish new landmark Insights 2024 report
items.b: The Insights 2024 report by Understanding Society is the largest longitudinal study of its kind. This year’s report focuses on behaviour and attitudes around youth voting, the upcoming general election, climate change, levelling up and inequality in the UK. Read the report now .
items.why: it presents new longitudinal evidence on youth voting behaviour and attitudes ahead of a general election, bearing directly on electoral participation and turnout.
items.note: Turnout and youth voting attitudes are classified under elections per the standing rule even when framed as research.

items.h: I Have A Voice launch their Politics4All and Justice 4 You reports
items.b: Last month Rebecca Deegan and the I Have A Voice team took to Parliament to launch Politics4All — their academically rigorous feasibility study on the possibility of developing a measure of political literacy, the first of its kind — Read the Political Literacy Survey Report now . The parliamentary launch also saw the publication of their Justice 4 You report, as part of a campaign to eradicate racial inequality in education — read the survey report Does racism exist in the English education system? Check out IHAV’s Twitter for the reactions to the launches .
items.why: it develops a new academic measure of political literacy intended to assess and strengthen people's capacity to engage in political life.
items.note: Focused on the political literacy report; the education-racism report is not clearly a democracy mechanism.

survey report Does racism exist in the English education system?

items.h: Climate Emergency UK hosting Scorecards Successes Conference this month
items.b: Annie and the team at Climate Emergency UK behind the Council Climate Action Scorecards project , are hosting a new conference on March 21st exploring the enablers of local climate action, from private financing for council climate action, to questions around what good local climate governance looks like — Register now .
items.note: Event listing about climate governance conference, not a democratic mechanism story.

items.h: Joint Committee on the National Security Strategy (JCNSS) calls for evidence on Defending Democracy Inquiry
items.b: Organisations are invited to submit evidence to the Defending Democracy inquiry by 18th March. JCNSS is launching its inquiry into ‘Defending Democracy’ to better understand how threats to the UK’s democracy may evolve and be addressed. This will primarily focus on the work of the National Security Council’s Defending Democracy Taskforce. Email the committee for more information .
items.why: a parliamentary committee is scrutinising how the state identifies and responds to threats to UK democracy, a core accountability function.
links: submit evidence to the Defending Democracy inquiry
Email the committee for more information

items.h: Speed networking for people of colour working on elections
items.b: Last month The Politics Project , Operation Black Vote and Civic Power Fund collaborated to bring together more than sixty activists, campaigners and organisers of colour who will be driving change at the next general election, to meet, drink and build relationships that will help renew our democracy.
items.note: Report on a past networking event rather than creation of a new participation mechanism or resource.

items.h: ISWE make the case for a Global Citizens’ Assembly, launch People Powered Politicians campaign
items.b: Over the next few weeks, the team at ISWE , working with The UN Foundation , are making the case for a Global Citizens’ Assembly — stay tuned for more. They’re also launching their Good Help report with Rochdale Council on participatory practice in local service provision. But that’s not all, ISWE are launching their new People Powered Politicians programme — find out more .
items.why: new programmes and participatory practice resources are being created to expand how people can engage in local and political decision-making.
items.note: Citizens' assembly element falls under elections & decision making per framework, but the wider programme launch is capacity-building for participation.

items.h: Uptick in hires and job roles available across democracy community
items.b: There has been a significant pick up in availability of job roles and hiring across the democracy community in recent months, with several organisations such as the Electoral Commission, Migrant Democracy Project, The Politics Project, mySociety, Citizens UK and others expanding their capacity significantly.
items.note: Sector employment news about organisations, not a change in democratic participation or power.

items.h: Democracy Classroom kick off Voter Registration Week
items.b: Voter Registration Week is a collaborative effort from partners across Democracy Classroom to empower as many people as possible to register to vote. With #VoterRegistrationWeek comes the first #ElectionCountdown of the year by The Politics Project ahead of the May 2nd elections — sign up for tailored learning resources , template emails, posters, blogs and more to help young people better navigate the upcoming elections. See more coverage of voter registration week .
items.why: a coordinated campaign is being launched to increase voter registration and turnout among young people ahead of elections.
items.note: Turnout and registration campaigns are always classified under elections & decision making.
links: more coverage of voter registration week

items.h: Democracy Network members can now take advantage of a new discount of up to 25% off a Nationbuilder subscription
items.b: In the run up to the General Election, Nationbuilder is offering a 25% discount for their platform to Democracy Network members. Contact the Democracy Network for more details .
items.note: Commercial discount offer for a software subscription, sector logistics rather than a democracy mechanism.
links: Contact the Democracy Network for more details

items.h: The Politics Project partner up with the Association of Colleges for further education voter resources push
items.b: Last week The Politics Project launched a new bank of resources to directly support the Association of Colleges , as part of Colleges Week 2024, to provide critical voter information resources for further education students across the country — so far they’ve reached over 1,000 schools and colleges !
items.why: new voter information resources are being distributed to thousands of colleges to help students register and participate in elections.
items.note: Voter information and registration resources fall under elections & decision making regardless of the participation framing.

items.h: Who Targets Me political ad spend data suggests unlikely we’ll see May election
items.b: In their latest Full Disclosure newsletter Who Targets Me unpack recent political advertising spend data and whether or not this indicates pre-election build up. Sam Jeffers and the team at Who Targets Me deep dive into the spend data, arguing that current spend is stable and not increasing week by week (as you’d expect before an election), the parties aren’t using geotargeting at the moment which indicates little targeted campaigning, as well as a lack of active candidate pages or consistent messaging on socials — all four combined, they argue, point in the opposite direction to ‘imminent ele…
items.why: this matters democratically because political advertising spend patterns are a signal of campaign activity and transparency in the run-up to elections, which shapes political competition.
items.note: Concerns campaign finance/advertising data as evidence about election timing, filed under elections rather than information given its campaign-finance framing.

items.h: Norfolk Community Advice Network launch new voter education campaign
items.b: Ruth Stokes at Norfolk Community Advice Network (NCAN) , a network of more than 60 VCSE orgs across the Norfolk region, are launching their new voter education campaign. They’re also speaking to council elections teams across the region to coordinate election plans, as well as working with disability rights organisations to build a picture of disabled people’s experiences with voting locally. Contact Ruth to find out more .
items.why: this matters democratically because voter education and coordination with election administrators, including addressing disabled people's access to voting, directly affects who can exercise their vote.
items.note: Voter education/turnout campaigns are always filed under elections per the turnout rule.
links: Contact Ruth to find out more

items.h: South Devon Primary launches UK’s first community-led political primary
items.b: Running this month until 16th March, South Devon Primary are hosting 7 town hall events to help choose a candidate for the upcoming general election. South Devon Primary say they aim to unite the progressive majority around one candidate at the general election, to oppose the incumbent Conservative MP Anthony Mangnall. This will be the first time a community-led political primary has been organised in the UK, they argue.
items.why: this matters democratically because a community-led primary is a new mechanism for candidate selection that affects political competition and voter choice in the constituency.
links: South Devon Primary are hosting 7 town hall events to help choose a candidate

items.h: 7.6m eligible voters missing from electoral roll, says Electoral Reform Society
items.b: New analysis from the Electoral Reform Society finds 7.6m eligible voters are missing from the electoral roll . This year sees general, local and mayoral elections taking place, prompting fears that this registration gap will have widespread implications on local and national democracy. The constituency with the highest level of unregistered voters is the Cities of London and Westminster where one fifth of the eligible population is currently unregistered.
items.why: this matters democratically because millions of unregistered eligible voters represent a gap in the franchise that limits people's ability to take part in elections.
links: 7.6m eligible voters are missing from the electoral roll

items.h: Open Elections — an online archive of over 9,000 election leaflets
items.b: Did you know that Prof Caitlin Milazzo and their team of researchers, funded by the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council , have produced a new exhaustive archive of UK election leaflets? Open Elections hosts more than 9,000 election leaflets in an effort to boost the transparency of election campaigning.
items.why: this matters democratically because an archive of election leaflets increases transparency of campaign communications and supports scrutiny of electoral competition.
items.note: Sector capacity-building tool specifically for election transparency, filed under elections rather than information given its electoral campaigning focus.
links: Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council

items.h: UK and Denmark establish voting rights treaty
items.b: The new agreement allows for British and Danish citizens to stand and vote in local elections in each other’s countries . The new treaty restores the right of British citizens to vote in Danish elections and vice versa, as has been the case prior to Brexit on the 31st January 2020. Denmark is the fifth country to sign a voting rights treaty with the UK, following treaties signed with Poland, Spain, Portugal and Luxembourg.
items.why: this matters democratically because the treaty extends suffrage rights, allowing citizens of each country to vote and stand in the other's local elections.
links: British and Danish citizens to stand and vote in local elections in each other’s countries

items.h: Zero Hour to launch their general election campaign, March 12th
items.b: Zero Hour , the campaign behind the Climate & Ecology Bill , are launching their general election campaign to raise the salience of climate action in Parliament ahead of this year’s elections. The Climate & Ecology Bill includes a commitment to hold a citizens’ assembly on climate and nature to help the UK Government and Parliament develop an emergency strategy. Join Chris Packham and the Zero Hour team for their launch here .
items.note: This is advocacy to raise the political salience of a climate policy issue rather than a story about how democratic power is acquired, exercised or contested.
links: Join Chris Packham and the Zero Hour team for their launch here

items.h: Election Tech Handbook launches for 2024!
items.b: The 2024 Election Tech Handbook has launched ! Back in 2019 the Handbook collected hundreds of data sources and projects, providing a key resource and signpost for election tech projects to scale, collaborate and reach a broader audience. The 2024 project has been funded by JRRT to build upon previous successes of the project, improve the provision of and discoverability of new election tech tools, data and digital volunteers throughout the election period. Subscribe to their newsletter , join the ETH WhatsApp , attend their first meetup and bookmark the Election Tech Handbook in your web brow…
items.why: this matters democratically because the handbook creates new means for election tech projects, data and volunteers to support the running and scrutiny of elections.
items.note: Sector capacity-building resource specifically tied to elections, filed under elections rather than general participation.

items.h: mySociety launch Local Intelligence Hub
items.b: Launched in partnership with The Climate Coalition , the new mySociety Local Intelligence Hub is designed to support people and organisations campaigning around climate and nature with the information they need to focus their campaigns on the areas that can have the greatest impact. Check it out now , read the supporting blog or join the upcoming webinar explainer on Tuesday 26th March .
items.why: it creates a new tool that helps campaigners and organisations focus civic engagement on the areas where it can have the greatest impact, expanding the practical means of participation.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building: a new resource that expands means of participation.
links: upcoming webinar explainer on Tuesday 26th March

items.h: Campaign Lab host showcase of election and civic tech projects
items.b: Last month Campaign Lab held a special showcase event of their recent hackathon projects, including the powerful Council Gateway tool (below), a new prototype doorknocking bot to train election doorstep canvassers, an (unofficial) bot summarising Electoral Commission guidance on the upcoming election, constituency boundary converter tools, MP newsletter analysis , in-depth research into political leafleting and much, much more . Do you have a campaign challenge for Campaign Lab volunteers to tackle?
items.why: it showcases newly built civic tech tools (canvassing aids, election guidance bots, transparency tools) that expand people's practical capacity to engage in campaigning and elections.
items.note: Some tools (doorknocking bot, election guidance) touch elections_decision_making but the overall story is capacity-building for participation.

items.h: mySociety’s civic tech TICTeC Conference now open for proposals and early bird tickets
items.b: mySociety’s TICTeC, or the Impacts of Civic Technology Conference , will be returning for its 7th edition on 12th and 13th June 2024, in London and online. TICTeC is the foremost civic technology conference globally, focused on sharing research, knowledge and experiences to better understand the impacts of civic tech and better strengthen democracy, public participation, transparency and accountability across the world. You can answer the Call for Proposals here and register for the conference now .
items.note: Conference call for proposals/tickets is an event listing, not a reported change in democratic capacity.
links: TICTeC, or the Impacts of Civic Technology Conference
answer the Call for Proposals here

items.h: Movement Industries develop new Council Gateway portal to access & summarise council minutes and data
items.b: James and the team at Movement Industries , through Campaign Lab’s hackathon collaborations, have developed a powerful new tool to query council data and minutes dating back to the dawn of council digitisation in the 1990s. Their team have scraped council minute databases for every UK council, allowing their new AI-powered Council Gateway tool to search and summarise council discussions and debates. The new tool when complete will be a gamechanger for local journalists and campaigners.
items.why: it creates a new tool that gives journalists and campaigners easier access to council minutes and data, strengthening capacity to scrutinise and engage with local government.
items.note: Sector capacity-building tool; also touches local-journalism access to information.

items.h: Code the City hosting Democracy Hackathon, 16–17th March
items.b: Aberdeen-based Code the City use tech and data for the civic good. Their next hackathon is focused on democracy — transparency of levels of government, accountability of officials and representatives, identifying sources of political data and more. Sign up now .
items.note: An event listing (hackathon) rather than a launched tool or resource.

items.h: Help us populate our sector funding list
items.b: The Democracy Network is part-way through refurbishing our resources and directories, including the UK Democracy Map and funding list. This is the current list of active democracy funds in the UK, please review and tell us if anything is missing , or if we’ve made an error contact us via james@involve.org.uk
links: current list of active democracy funds
tell us if anything is missing

items.h: Join the new Democracy Funding group on WhatsApp
items.b: At this year’s Democracy Network Conference several sessions were held around the big question of funding democracy organisations and initiatives. Following this a group has convened around exploring various avenues to boost both the levels of funding available within the sector as a whole and on ways to more closely integrate and pool resources, for example back office functions. Join the WhatsApp Group or message Jessie Joe Jacobs to get involved.

items.h: Labour would introduce citizens’ assemblies, Sue Gray says
items.b: The Labour leader’s chief of staff, Sue Gray, said the assemblies will get the public directly involved in deciding contentious issues such as constitutional reform, devolution and housing. Gray also remarked that ‘civil servants will not like this, because they have no control’. Following the announcement Labour rowed back on the remarks , saying the announcement was not formal policy. Involve’s Calum Green, Director of Advocacy and Communications, welcomed Labour’s suggest they are exploring citizens’ assemblies , remarking that assemblies can help rebuild trust, and deliver clear and practi…
items.why: it concerns a proposal to introduce citizens' assemblies, a deliberative mechanism for direct public involvement in binding or contentious collective decisions.
items.note: Citizens' assemblies are classified under elections_decision_making per the revised framework, not participation.
links: said the assemblies will get the public directly involved in deciding contentious issues
Labour rowed back on the remarks
celebrated the prospect of greater citizen engagement

items.h: Support for the monarchy reaches historic low
items.b: A recent poll has revealed a shift in opinions away from the monarchy, amid allegations of sexual assault by members of the royal family. For the first time, support for a monarchy in Britain has dropped below 50% , now sitting at 48%. Graham Smith, CEO of Republic said, ‘this is huge. Royalists have spent years saying the monarchy has the support of the country — that’s clearly no longer the case’.
items.why: this matters democratically because it signals shifting public consent for the hereditary basis of the head of state and pressure for constitutional reform toward an elected alternative.
items.note: Monarchy is not itself an elected institution but the story concerns constitutional legitimacy and calls for reform, so treated as a government accountability/constitutional conventions issue.
links: support for a monarchy in Britain has dropped below 50%

items.h: Being more open is good for government, says Institute for Government
items.b: 2024 is an opportunity to reset the government’s approach to transparency, says the Institute for Government , after the UK fell from 3rd — in 2014 — to 24th place in the OECD’s open data rankings . Their new report — The Benefits of Transparency — draws on six case studies, including Transport for London’s open data regime and the Scottish public appointments process, to show how being more open can not only benefit outside observers, but government itself too.
items.why: this matters democratically because open government data and transparency are mechanisms by which citizens and watchdogs hold government answerable.

items.h: Unlock Democracy call for a ban on MPs accepting gifts
items.b: Unlock Democracy is calling for a ban on MPs accepting gifts following the news that Michael Gove failed to declare a gift from a donor he’d helped secure lucrative PPE contracts for. The ban would help clean up Westminster politics, they argue, as it would prevent any conflict of interests arising when MPs accept ‘freebies’ from large companies.
items.why: this matters democratically because rules on gifts to MPs govern conflicts of interest and standards in public life, core to holding representatives to account.
links: calling for a ban on MPs accepting gifts

items.h: UK Government considers ban on MPs engaging with pro-Palestine and climate groups
items.b: Former Labour MP, and now crossbench peer and Government Adviser on Political Violence and Disruption, John Woodcock , has presented plans to the government to employ a ‘zero tolerance approach’ to groups that use disruptive tactics, including marches. The plans include instructing MPs, councillors and elected representatives to not engage with — or communicate — with anyone from climate or pro-Palestinian groups , amid threats to politicians. The plans put forward by Lord Walney made no mention of far-right extremism. Jun Pang, Policy and Campaigns Officer at Liberty, said ‘any government tha…
items.why: this matters democratically because government plans to bar elected representatives from engaging with certain protest groups would restrict freedom of association and civic space under a new security justification.
items.note: Framed as government invoking new threats to curb civil liberties, so classified under rights and freedoms rather than participation.
links: instructing MPs, councillors and elected representatives to not engage with — or communicate — with anyone from climate or pro-Palestinian groups

items.h: Government pushes through Electoral Commission strategy, raising concerns over independence
items.b: The controversial Elections Act 2022 included provisions for the government to issue a strategy and policy statement for the Electoral Commission . The government has said the statement is necessary to improve public confidence in the commission. A range of organisations, including the Electoral Commission , have opposed the statement, calling it incompatible with the commission’s independence . Lord Rennard, a Liberal Democrat peer and vocal opponent of the Elections Act, has sharply criticised the move .
items.why: this matters democratically because government control over the Electoral Commission's strategy threatens the independence of the body that administers elections.
links: strategy and policy statement for the Electoral Commission
opposed the statement, calling it incompatible with the commission’s independence

items.h: Government broke law with new protest powers, Liberty argues
items.b: New legal action by Liberty challenges Government decision to sign off on anti-protest laws previously rejected by Parliament. The High Court has been urged by Liberty to quash the legislation that gives police almost unlimited power to shut down protests it deems as causing a ‘more than minor’ disturbance’. Liberty argues the Government has deliberately circumvented the will of Parliament and unconstitutionally breached the principle of separation of powers by using a statutory instrument to change the Public Order Act last year, despite having an amendment to do the exact same thing rejected…
items.why: this matters democratically because the legal challenge concerns whether the executive unlawfully bypassed Parliament and the separation of powers to expand protest restrictions.
items.note: Focus is on legality of executive action via judicial review rather than protest policing itself, so filed under rule of law.
links: Government has deliberately circumvented the will of Parliament

items.h: Parliament descends into chaos as Commons Speaker breaks with precedent
items.b: Late last month House of Commons Speaker Lindsay Hoyle broke with established parliamentary precedent to select a Labour amendment on an SNP opposition day, causing a walkout of Conservative and SNP MPs. Since that time 93 submissions of no confidence in the Speaker have been submitted, an event without precedent itself. Hannah White of the Institute for Government analyses and unpacks the parliamentary spectacle in this blog .
items.why: this matters democratically because a breach of parliamentary precedent by the Speaker affects the impartial functioning of legislative scrutiny and procedure.
links: 93 submissions of no confidence in the Speaker

items.h: New laws mean UK is vulnerable to ‘dirty money and foreign influence’, says Spotlight on Corruption
items.b: In December last year, Spotlight on Corruption wrote to the National Crime Agency warning that the UK is currently ‘exposed to dirty money and foreign influence’ . The warning came as the Commons waved through new regulations outlined under the Elections Act 2022, that allow for a huge expansion in overseas voters with few checks. As many as 3.4 million overseas citizens will be brought onto the electoral roll, and with them ‘foreign money entering our democracy’, remarked the Labour front bench prior to entering a Motion of Regret on the issue.
items.why: this matters democratically because expanding the overseas electoral roll with weak checks affects franchise integrity and opens channels for foreign money to enter UK elections.
links: warning that the UK is currently ‘exposed to dirty money and foreign influence’

items.h: Democracy is being targeted by extremists, says Prime Minister
items.b: During an impromptu speech outside Downing Street last week, Prime Minister Sunak argued extremists are trying to tear us apart . Sunak’s statement came after George Galloway’s shock election victory , garnering 39.7% of the vote on a byelection turnout of 39.7%. The veteran MP’s campaign prioritised support for Palestine, amidst the ongoing war and humanitarian disaster in the Occupied Palestinian Territories . Policy Exchange has called the PM’s speech a ‘striking intervention ’ which was ‘justified by events.’ The PM’s comments follow days after their prior comments of ‘mob rule replacing d…
items.why: This matters democratically because government rhetoric framing dissent and protest as 'mob rule' or extremism risks being used to justify curbing civil liberties such as freedom of expression and assembly.
items.note: Byelection turnout is mentioned but the story's substance is rhetoric about civil liberties, not electoral mechanics.
links: Prime Minister Sunak argued extremists are trying to tear us apart
ongoing war and humanitarian disaster in the Occupied Palestinian Territories
Policy Exchange has called the PM’s speech a ‘striking intervention

items.h: Lawyers Are Responsible to host full day event to understand the role of the justice system in civil rights crackdown
items.b: In a new all day event on April 12th in London, Lawyers Are Responsible are convening lawyers, barristers and the wider legal and campaigns community to better understand why the criminal justice system is responding in such extreme ways to the exercise of fundamental democratic rights and freedoms, they argue. The British civil rights crackdown in recent years has been described by a UN Special Rapporteur as terrifying , with peaceful protesters jailed for lengthy periods of time or forced to wear electronic tags for simply holding up placards or communicating with members of direct action gr…
items.note: This is an event listing/call to sign up, treated as sector logistics rather than a reported democracy story.
links: Sign up for the event now

items.h: Devolved government restored in Northern Ireland
items.b: After a 2-year hiatus, power sharing has been restored in Northern Ireland , following a decision by the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) . The DUP had previously boycotted the Northern Ireland Assembly over a breakdown in relations with the UK Government over post-Brexit trade arrangements. The DUP has now agreed to re-enter the institutions after a deal with the UK Government. The new NI Executive saw Sinn Féin’s Michelle O’Neill becoming Northern Ireland’s first nationalist first minister.
items.why: This matters democratically because it restores the functioning of a devolved legislature and executive, re-establishing power-sharing government and representative decision-making in Northern Ireland.
items.note: Devolved government structure and restoration is classified under elections & decision making per the framework's treatment of devolved institutions.
links: power sharing has been restored in Northern Ireland

items.h: Scottish electoral reform Bill published
items.b: Legislation which aims to enhance Scotland’s democratic processes has been published in the Scottish Parliament . The Bill includes provisions for piloting digital polling cards, provides powers for elections to be rescheduled in emergencies, foreign nationals living and working in Scotland on a time-limited visa would become eligible to stand as candidates in Scottish Parliament and local government elections — in addition to their existing voting rights. The legislation also proposes to ban people from being MSPs if found guilty of intimidating campaigners and election officials and changes …
items.why: This matters democratically because the Bill changes who can vote and stand for election, how elections are administered, and safeguards against intimidation and foreign spending in Scottish elections.
links: Democracy Club’s Peter Keeling reviewed the changes in their blog last month

items.h: 50 Ideas For The North
items.b: Tris Brown and Patrick Hurley launched their book 50 Ideas For The North . Based on a range of workshops and sessions across the North of England in 2021, the suggestions included in the book have been sourced directly from the minds of people who live in those communities. Find out more and grab yourself a copy here .
items.note: This is a book launch/promotional item rather than a new participation mechanism or reported democratic change.

items.h: Press Forward to award more than $500 million to revitalise local US news outlets
items.b: As you know, we don’t usually cover international stories through the UK Democracy Bulletin , but if you’re working in the indy news space in the UK and looking for inspiration, cast your eyes across the pond where 22 donors recently announced their intention to back a major new national initiative in the USA to strengthen local news through an injection of more than half a billion dollars over the next five years — a major achievement by any reckoning.
items.note: International story about US local news funding presented as inspiration, not shown to bear directly on UK democracy.
links: major new national initiative in the USA to strengthen local news

items.h: Public Interest News Foundation launch Local News Fund in Newry, focus on big tech legislation impacts on indy news
items.b: Joe Mitchell, Deputy Director at Public Interest News Foundation (PINF), highlights their work on developing new pooled Local News Funds to support local news and information ecosystems across the UK. They are starting this process through their pioneering Local News Found in Newry, Northern Ireland . In other news, Hani Barghouthi provides an update on PINF’s News For All campaign to get a fair deal for indy news from the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Bill currently passing through Parliament.
items.why: This matters democratically because it creates new funding infrastructure for local journalism and campaigns on legislation affecting the economic viability of independent news, both central to a plural information environment.
links: developing new pooled Local News Funds
Local News Found in Newry, Northern Ireland
update on PINF’s News For All campaign

items.h: Concern over Data Protection and Media Bill
items.b: Concern is mounting over the Data Protection and Media Bill progressing through the Commons. Open Rights Group provided a summary of the changes as they were outlined when it was initially introduced . Public Law Project warns that the Bill in its current state will weaken important data protections and safeguards, reduce transparency and put individuals at risk of unfairness and discrimination.
items.why: This matters democratically because weakening data protection safeguards and transparency exposes individuals to unfairness and discrimination and reduces accountability over how public and private power handle personal data.
items.note: Despite the 'Media Bill' title, the substance concerns data protection, privacy and discrimination risk rather than the media information environment.
links: Public Law Project warns that the Bill in its current state

items.h: Civil servants taught legislative process through Legislate board game
items.b: Back in 2023, the Office of Parliamentary Counsel helped deliver a series of workshops at Civil Service Live, the government’s annual, cross-dept learning event, teaching civil servants the legislative process through a boardgame! Who knew?
items.note: Whimsical item about internal civil service training, not a mechanism of public democratic power.
links: teaching civil servants the legislative process through a boardgame!

items.h: Brussels to consult citizens on European AI strategy
items.b: As part of their 2024 presidency of the European Council, Belgium is holding a citizens’ assembly on the use of AI in the area. 16,200 invitations have already been sent out to Belgian residents, giving them the chance to help shape the EU’s approach to AI in the 2024–2029 intergovernmental period. See you next time, add to your calendar
items.note: EU citizens' assembly on AI has no demonstrated bearing on UK democracy, and the item is framed as offbeat trivia.
links: Belgium is holding a citizens’ assembly on the use of AI

items.h: Democracy Network launch new Democracy Resource Hub
items.b: This month the Democracy Network launched the new Democracy Resource Hub featuring the Democracy Map — an 800+ directory of democracy organisations and projects across the UK, new Democracy Jobs and Democracy Funding boards, as well as a home for the network’s webinars, guides and free training videos/resources. Missed the launch? Watch the deep dive into the Resource Hub on YouTube. Check out the Democracy Resource Hub now — find your organisation, share your jobs and explore the new funding lists. Have we got something wrong, got anything to add or contribute? Let us know via the Map or via …
items.why: it creates new practical means for people and organisations to find, coordinate with and support each other in democratic and civic work, including jobs, funding and training resources.
items.note: Sector capacity-building rule applies: launch of a new hub/tool for civic participation counts as a democracy story.
links: Missed the launch? Watch the deep dive into the Resource Hub on YouTube.

items.h: Democracy Network to hold annual Steering Group election — vote now
items.b: The Democracy Network’s Steering Group elections are running until tomorrow Weds 17th April 9am — the Steering Group is the elected board of the Democracy Network and works to guide, develop plans and strategy for the Network and helps support this community in myriad ways. Find out more and use your vote!
items.note: Internal steering-group election for a sector organisation, not a public democratic institution or mechanism.

items.h: Today is National Voter Registration Day!
items.b: Coordinated by My Life My Say , National Voter Registration Day (NVRD) is an annual collective effort to ensure every eligible individual is registered to vote. NVRD is officially recognised by all major UK political parties too — get involved now , contact Dan Lawes at My Life My Say to find out more.
items.why: it is a campaign to increase voter registration, which directly affects who can exercise the franchise.
items.note: Turnout and registration campaigns are always classified under elections & decision making.
links: Dan Lawes at My Life My Say

items.h: British Youth Council closes down permanently
items.b: After more than 75 years of championing the voices of young people, the British Youth Council (BYC) has decided to permanently close down. In their press release, Zara Khan, Chair of the BYC, suggests ongoing financial challenges as the reason for the decision . The news has come as a shock to both those among the democracy sector who have been working closely with the BYC across its many programmes, and for generations of those who had invested much of their time in the youth voice movement through the British Youth Council.
items.note: Organisational closure news is treated as sector admin rather than a change to democratic mechanisms, even for a youth-voice organisation.

items.h: All-Island Better Democracy Network launches in Belfast
items.b: The All-Island Better Democracy Network launched last month as part of the Imagine! Belfast Festival. The new network is a community of individuals and civil society organisations working to build a healthier democracy, more active citizenship and stronger civic voice across the island of Ireland. The Better Democracy network is a project of Involve and has been made possible by a grant from St Stephens’ Green Trust .
items.why: a new civil society network is being created to build capacity for civic voice and active citizenship.
items.note: Launch of a civic-society network is capacity-building that creates new means of participation.

items.h: Collaborative Democracy Network launches
items.b: The Collaborative Democracy Network is a new network created by Demos . Launched last month, it is a new space for politicians, policymakers and civil society to come together to discuss innovations that put people at the heart of policy making. Missed the launch event? Watch it now on Youtube .
items.why: a new network is being created to connect civil society with policymakers on participatory approaches to policymaking.
items.note: Launch of a network counts as new civic infrastructure under sector capacity-building rules.

items.h: I Have A Voice open applications for this year’s Training and Internship Scheme
items.b: The scheme run by I Have A Voice is aimed at those between 16–25 years looking to learn about careers in policy research, public affairs and communications. Over the last two years they’ve had more than 35 trainees, with over 18 now permanently employed (13 are still in education). The training is completely free and includes two weeks of on the job training in different offices across London, before being invited for one of several paid hosted internships. The deadline to apply is the 26th April — share the application form .
items.why: a new training scheme is created to build young people's capacity to take part in policy and public affairs work.
items.note: Sector capacity-building programme creating new means for participation in civic/policy life.

items.h: More than 12 organisations now signed up to the National Campaign for Proportional Representation
items.b: The National Campaign for PR is gearing up, they’re currently interviewing for their two new positions — Campaign Convenor & Campaign Coordinator — to power the campaign over the months ahead. The campaign is now more than 12-organisations strong, including Compass , Electoral Reform Society , Labour Campaign for Electoral Reform , Lib Dems for Electoral Reform and Make Votes Matter , among others.
items.note: Sector staffing/growth news about a campaign organisation, not a new participation mechanism.

items.h: Newspeak House open for Fellowship applications
items.b: Newspeak House, the London College of Political Technology , is a residential college in East London. Participants spend a year immersed in civic communities of practice with the opportunity to meet thousands of people and participate in a wide range of in-person events. The programme is designed to support mid-career technologists to develop a holistic understanding of the civic landscape in the UK, in order to found groundbreaking new projects or seek strategic positions in key institutions — Apply now .
items.note: A fellowship application call resembles routine event/programme listing rather than a new means of participation.
links: Newspeak House, the London College of Political Technology

items.h: Collective Intelligence Project launch new Roadmap to Democratic AI report
items.b: Flynn Devine of The Collective Intelligence Project , reports that their new publication ‘ A Roadmap to Democratic AI’ lays out a framing, plan and recommended actions for those interested in ‘democratising’ AI’ with the aim of generating shared understanding of priorities for efforts in 2024.
items.note: An advocacy report on AI framing is a technology/publication story, not a concrete mechanism of public power.

items.h: mySociety launch Local Intelligence Hub
items.b: Launched in partnership with The Climate Coalition , the new mySociety Local Intelligence Hub is designed to support people and organisations campaigning around climate and nature with the information they need to focus their campaigns on the areas that can have the greatest impact. Check it out now and read the supporting blog .
items.why: This matters democratically because it launches a new resource that helps campaigners and citizens target civic action more effectively, expanding practical means of participation.

items.h: Oli Whittington developing participatory process to determine democratic campaigning priorities
items.b: Oli Whittington, Strategic Design Director at Shift Design , is busily interviewing people across the democracy sector at the moment regarding their new project proposal, to run a participatory assembly process with UK democracy organisations to develop a shared understanding and agreement on substantive democratic reforms — get in touch with Oli to discuss their ideas in more detail.
items.note: A proposal still in the interviewing stage, akin to a call for engagement rather than a launched participation mechanism.

items.h: Unlock Democracy and Compass publish new report on devolution
items.b: Power to the People: the route to english devolution charts the course for a radical approach for radical devolution. The report assesses five key proposals that could inspire and guide an incoming government to act in this area as part of a wider movement towards a new 21st century democratic settlement — Read the report here .
items.why: This matters democratically because it addresses proposals for the structure and powers of English devolution, which determine where decision-making authority sits.
items.note: Devolution structure and powers fall under elections & decision making per the framework's boundary rule on local/regional government.
links: Power to the People: the route to english devolution

items.h: mySociety note a massive drop in the number of All Party Parliamentary Groups
items.b: Over the past month there has been a 39% decrease in the number of APPGs, from 722 to just 444. In their latest blog Julia Cushion at mySociety details why this has happened, namely due to rules changes brought in on 31st March 2024 that required APPGs show increased financial reporting, ban APPG funding from foreign governments, require increased reporting and changes to the composition of the groups. Read Julia’s blog to find out more or dig into the data .
items.why: This matters democratically because new transparency and funding rules for All-Party Parliamentary Groups affect lobbying influence, foreign interference risk, and standards in public life.

items.h: Shared Future CIC & Katy Rubin to run day of participatory democracy workshops at Sheffield Festival of Debate
items.b: Katy Rubin and the Shared Future CIC team are presenting a day of fun and workshops at the Festival of Debate in Sheffield on Saturday 25th May, from 1030. They’ll be running both a Legislative Theatre workshop and the City of Empavilla game on Participatory Budgeting — Find out more .
items.note: A one-off festival workshop listing is sector event promotion rather than a change to participation infrastructure.

items.h: Voice for Change England hosting online panel discussion on cost living crisis and the local elections
items.b: The Voice for Change panel discussion on the 25th April aims to focus on the intersection of the cost of living crisis and the local elections this May, how the crisis is affecting communities, vulnerable groups and how it is exacerbating other social problems. Register now .
items.note: Event listing/panel notice, not a change to democratic mechanism.

items.h: New report launch on technological capability of UK trade unions, May 8th
items.b: Organise Lab are launching their new report on the levels of digital training and ability across the UK trade union sector. The report is based on more than 100 interviews with shop stewards, health & safety reps and industrial representatives across a range of unions and sectors. The launch panel event will include contributions from GMB , Campaign Lab and Newspeak House — sign up now , and receive the report when it launches here .
items.note: Report launch event on union digital capacity, sector logistics rather than a democracy mechanism story.

items.h: The Khan Review recommends deliberative democracy methods
items.b: The new review by Dame Sarah Khan into social cohesion and resilience recommends ‘local authorities should consider adopting deliberate democracy models to help encourage greater citizen participation and engagement in the democratic system . This includes the setting up of a local cohesion and democracy forums or citizens assembly to support these objectives’.
items.why: This matters democratically because it recommends new citizens' assembly and deliberative democracy structures as mechanisms for local collective decision-making.
items.note: Deliberative democracy and citizens' assemblies are classed under elections & decision making, not participation, per framework rules.
links: new review by Dame Sarah Khan
