items.h: Democracy Club ready for the May elections, hosting hustings event listings
items.b: Each year, Democracy Club’s amazing volunteer community collates thousands of nomination papers (Statement of Persons Nominated) published on council websites, which are then manually added to the Democracy Club database in an annual effort known as SoPN Day, this year DC volunteers uploaded more than 2000 ballots. This year 10,662 candidates are standing for election across 2,015 individual ballots in England and Wales on 2 May, including principal councillors, mayors, Police and Crime Commissioners, London Assembly Members, and one MP. See the full election briefing here . Democracy Club are…
items.why: This matters democratically because collating candidate nomination data and hustings listings supports electoral administration and voters' ability to access information about who is standing.
items.note: Candidate/nomination data collation sits in election administration; hustings listing also touches civic participation.

items.h: Common Knowledge launch new Mapped tool for organisers
items.b: The organising platform developed by Common Knowledge allows campaigners and organisers to pull in data from their various databases and plot their people and supporters on a UK map, overlay rich information layers from constituency boundaries, past election results, missed rental payment data, poverty distribution data — and even, with agreement. Promising stuff — whether you’re a canvasser, campaign strategist or fundraiser — try it now .
items.why: This matters democratically because it creates a new organising tool that expands campaigners' and organisers' practical capacity to mobilise and engage supporters.
items.note: Sector capacity-building tool for organisers counts as a new means of participation.

items.h: House of Commons Library looking for feedback on new election results pages
items.b: The House of Commons Library team are looking for feedback on their new election results information and data site . You read more about the development and roadmap of the pages here .
items.why: This matters democratically because it develops a new official public resource for accessing and understanding election results data.
items.note: Election results data sits primarily under election administration, with an information-access dimension.

items.h: Operation Black Vote developing Black Manifesto, convening faith groups ahead of election
items.b: Operation Black Vote (OBV) and Black Equity Organisation , supported by the Joseph Rowntree Reform Trust , are developing the UK’s first Black Manifesto for the upcoming General Election. OBV also recently met with the National Church Leaders Forum and Muslim Council of Britain with the aim of organising large scale hustings ahead of an autumn election and the development of a multi-faith manifesto.
items.why: This matters democratically because it builds new means for Black and faith communities to organise, be heard and increase their political voice ahead of a general election.
items.note: Minority voice and mobilisation capacity is classed as participation, with an election-timing link to elections & decision making.

items.h: Demos’ new report highlights the possibility of gendered election disinformation
items.b: In their new report Generative AI: the new frontier for gendered disinformation? , Ellen Judson focuses on the spectre of gendered misinformation, a new form of online violence weaponising gendered stereotypes to abuse, demonise and undermine people in public life, with a disproportionate targeting of Black, LGBT+ and other minoritised women — Read the new report now .
items.why: gendered disinformation using AI can be used to abuse and drive minoritised women out of public life, distorting who can participate in political debate and stand for office.
items.note: Disinformation targeting candidates is filed under information/debate rather than rights, though gender-targeting also engages civic space.
links: Generative AI: the new frontier for gendered disinformation?

items.h: Campaign Lab prepares new hacknights for the May elections
items.b: The London-based community of progressive political technologists and electoral innovators are planning their next pre-election hacknight for April 22nd and post-election follow up event ‘Let’s Get Local’ here . They’re also running a training session to help people lobby politicians effectively — get in touch with Daniel Rockman to find out more.
items.why: new training and events that help people organise campaigns and lobby politicians create additional means for citizens to take part in political life.
links: get in touch with Daniel Rockman

items.h: Young Citizens’ create new voter resources aimed at 18–24 year olds
items.b: The new Young Citizens’ resources offer an introduction to voting, elections, laws, taxes and many more topics, including interactive resources such as Mock Parliament and Be Your Own Councillor. Oliver Walkden at Young Citizens also highlights that they are seeking volunteers from the legal sector to deliver The Big Legal Lesson in local schools. Email Oliver to find out more.
items.why: new voter education resources aimed at young people are designed to raise understanding of and engagement with voting and elections.
items.note: Voter education aimed at encouraging turnout is filed under elections per the turnout rule.
links: seeking volunteers from the legal sector to deliver The Big Legal Lesson

items.h: Runnymede Trust launch new report on immigration and racism ahead of the General Election
items.b: In their new report Creating a crisis: Immigration, racism and the 2024 General Election for the Runnymede Trust , Aurelien Mondon and Aaron Winter, show how the mainstreaming of far-right ideas and narratives by major UK political parties is predicated on the exclusion of people of colour, and is eroding public confidence in the political system and harming UK democracy .
items.why: mainstreaming of exclusionary narratives by major parties bears on equal treatment and inclusion of racial minorities and on public confidence in the political system.
links: Creating a crisis: Immigration, racism and the 2024 General Election

items.h: 50:50 Parliament to run How To Get Involved in the Election events
items.b: Lyanna Nicholls, CEO of 50:50 Parliament is running a new session on 22nd April for getting involved in the upcoming elections as a volunteer, even if you’re not standing. The event will focus on sharing knowledge on what women can do in the run up to the election to support their Party and gather valuable experience and networks should they be thinking of standing in the future. Interesting? Email the 50:50 Parliament team for more information.
items.why: new sessions helping women build experience and networks to eventually stand for office expand the practical opportunities for underrepresented groups to take part in political life.

items.h: Conservative council candidates seemingly invalidate themselves for election
items.b: Thirteen prospective Conservative candidates are no longer due to contest the elections at Castle Point Borough Council due to admin errors . It is understood that an old nomination form may have been used for the candidates’ applications.
items.why: administrative errors in candidate nomination processes can remove candidates from the ballot, directly affecting electoral competition.
links: no longer due to contest the elections at Castle Point Borough Council due to admin errors

items.h: Election Tech Handbook gears up for a General Election
items.b: The 2024 Election Tech Handbook launched last month. Back in 2019 the Handbook collected hundreds of data sources and projects, providing a key resource and signpost for election tech projects to scale, collaborate and reach a broader audience. The 2024 project has been funded by JRRT last to build upon previous successes of the project, improve the provision of and discoverability of new election tech tools, data and digital volunteers throughout the election period — and it’s growing to encompass all manner of digital projects and websites working in and around GE2024. Check it out now — Sub…
items.why: a shared resource collecting election tech tools and data helps organisations and volunteers support the administration and conduct of the election period.
items.note: Election-period tech infrastructure is filed under elections rather than general participation capacity-building.

items.h: Joseph Rowntree Charitable Trust recruiting Interim Chief Exec & new committee members
items.b: The Trust are recruiting and co opting several new roles including for their Chief Exec (on a rolling deadline) and for four positions on their Power & Accountability Committee (deadline 9th May) — Apply now .
items.note: Organisational staffing and committee recruitment, not a change to democratic practice.

items.h: Help us populate our sector funding list
items.b: The Democracy Network has launched a new Resource Hub (above) including a new list of democracy funders in the UK. Take a look at the new funder list and see if there’s any grants that match your needs — Please do review the directory to improve this resource for everyone , and let us know if we have missed anything, please report any errors via hello@democracynetwork.org.uk
items.note: Sector funding directory for democracy organisations, not a mechanism affecting public political power or participation.

items.h: Join the new Democracy Funding group on WhatsApp
items.b: At this year’s Democracy Network Conference several sessions were held around the big question of funding democracy organisations and initiatives. Following this a group has convened around exploring various avenues to boost both the levels of funding available within the sector as a whole and on ways to more closely integrate and pool resources, for example back office functions. Join the WhatsApp Group or message Jessie Joe Jacobs to get involved.
items.note: Internal sector coordination on funding pooling, not a democracy mechanism.

items.h: Research for Action secure long term funding, developing their citizen auditors network
items.b: Gloria Dawson and the team at Research for Action have secured long term funding for their worker co-op for three years, congratulations! As a result of this, they now have improved resources to keep growing and supporting their network of citizen auditors. This nascent network of citizen auditors is made up of local people who work to hold local government to account, journalists, civil society organisations and members of the public — Email the team for more information .
items.note: Story is framed as an organisation securing its own long-term funding, which is excluded even though the org's mission touches accountability.
links: Email the team for more information

items.h: ‘Right to acquit’ defendant Trudi Warner facing court this week
items.b: Campaigner and Quaker Trudi Warner is to face contempt proceedings in court this week for allegedly holding placards notifying jurors of their ability and ‘right to acquit’ defenders based on their conscience, outside a trial of Insulate Britain protesters last March. The charge against the 68-year old holds a maximum sentence of two years imprisonment. Leading barristers have said ‘she appears to be simply stating the law’ , whilst Defend Our Juries add this is a ‘united front from the public’ and presents the Solicitor General, the police and the courts ‘with a dilemma’ . The ancient right o…
items.why: contempt proceedings over informing jurors of their historic right to acquit on conscience threaten the fairness and independence of jury trials and the ability to inform citizens of legal rights within the justice system.
items.note: Also touches freedom of expression/protest but the core mechanism is the jury trial right and contempt law.
links: face contempt proceedings in court this week

items.h: Raphael Schlemback launches their new book on Spycops
items.b: Spycops: Secrets and Disclosure in the Undercover Policing Inquiry by Dr Raphael Schlemback, Principal Lecturer in Criminology at the University of Brighton, is the first academic analysis of the activists experiences and their attempts to find answers and accountability through the Undercover Policing Inquiry. Register for the book launch at Leeds Beckett University on the 13th May as part of the Social Movements and Activism symposium.
items.note: This is an event/book launch listing rather than a report on the inquiry itself.
links: Spycops: Secrets and Disclosure in the Undercover Policing Inquiry

items.h: Liberty publish new guidance and analysis on Prevent
items.b: With the recent widening of the definition of extremism by the UK Government last month, there are fresh concerns that these changes have the potential to further stifle and suppress legitimate political expression, particularly amongst marginalised communities such as Muslims and Palestinian groups. The new Liberty advice provides information on what happens if you are referred to prevent and what are our rights under the new Prevent definitions. Prevent has long been a concern of civil rights groups in the UK with organisations such as Liberty and Amnesty claiming Prevent threatens the estab…
items.why: widening the government's definition of extremism under Prevent risks curbing lawful political expression and association, particularly for marginalised communities, under the guise of a new security threat.
links: recent widening of the definition of extremism
new Liberty advice provides information on what happens if you are referred

items.h: MP Watch experiment with citizen-led focus groups
items.b: In a bid to learn more about how their messaging and campaign lands with the public, the team at MP Watch have been working with local focus groups based around particular interests to help refine their approach and decide where to focus their energies. Their first group was with ‘soft Conservatives’ in NE Somerset, the next will be with women-focused groups in High Wycombe, followed by a third group of people from Pakistani backgrounds. So far they report success and that the groups like their approach.
items.note: Internal campaign messaging research by an advocacy group, not a new means of public participation or decision-making.

items.h: Public Interest News Foundation coordinating world’s first Indie News Week this June
items.b: The inaugural week long event from 3–9th June will be the world’s first , Joe Mitchell, Deputy Director at the Public Interest News Foundation , reports. Under the banner of No News is Bad News, Indie News Week will comprise an online, print and in-person rollout with community events run by independent and independent local news outlets up and down the UK. The campaign will give communities an opportunity to meet their local journalists and find out more about who’s behind their local indie outlet and what goes into accurately and fairly covering the lives of their fellow residents. Sign up f…
items.why: a coordinated campaign to raise public awareness of and engagement with independent local journalism strengthens the plural local information environment citizens rely on to hold power to account.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new means for the public to engage with local journalism, not mere organisational promotion.
links: inaugural week long event from 3–9th June will be the world’s first

items.h: Meta moves to cease promotion of political content across their platforms
items.b: Tama Leaver, Professor of Internet Studies at Curtin University, highlights a set of sweeping changes to the way Meta platforms both define and recommend political content on their feeds. The changes will mean Instagram, Threads and possibly Facebook users will cease to see any political content on their feeds , relegating the ability to see news/political content as an opt-in feature. The change signals Meta’s retreat from politics but also news more generally is likely to both have a chilling effect on political discourse on the platforms and challenges any sense that these platforms are goo…
items.why: This matters democratically because a major platform's decision to suppress political content reshapes the public information environment through which citizens encounter political debate.
links: Instagram, Threads and possibly Facebook users will cease to see any political content on their feeds

items.h: Games Transformed is back for 2024
items.b: The one day festival brings together game developers, trade unionists, activists, campaigners and more to explore the intersection of games and progressive politics — register now for the June 22nd London event .
links: register now for the June 22nd London event

items.h: Doc Society to launch new Democracy Story Unit
items.b: The Doc Society works to support documentary film makers and empower them to make great films to tell the tales of our age. With the success of their Climate Story Unit , the new Democracy Story Unit will work to develop, empower and work with documentarists specifically around the issue of democracy — stay tuned for more.
items.why: This matters democratically because a new programme to support documentary storytelling about democracy could expand the range of public-interest content available for civic debate.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building affecting the information environment, though the announcement is speculative and org-focused.

items.h: New journalism schools sets out to improve diversity in UK journalism
items.b: The school, based in Beckenham, south London, will teach children about news reporting, video editing and illustration . According to the Sutton Trust, 80% of editors went to private school; only 11% of journalists are from working-class backgrounds, and only 0.2% of journalists are Black — this new school aims to change that.
items.why: This matters democratically because widening access to journalism training for underrepresented groups affects who can produce and shape the public information environment.
items.note: Classified as capacity-building for media plurality rather than mere organisational news.
links: will teach children about news reporting, video editing and illustration

items.h: Involve’s Ruth Hart crowned 2024 Mastermind Champion
items.b: Ruth Hart, Engagement Lead at Involve , won the 2024 edition of Mastermind! This was the first time she’d ever been on TV and scored a perfect 15/15 in her specialist subject, the artist Francis Bacon. You can watch Ruth’s big win on BBC iPlayer now — congratulations Ruth! See you next time, add to your calendar
links: watch Ruth’s big win on BBC iPlayer now

items.why: This matters democratically because a crowdsourced resource helping technologists build election-related tools creates new practical means for people to engage with the electoral process.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new means of participation around the election.

items.b: Election Hackspace The London College of Political Technology, Newspeak House, has opened its doors from now until the election for all those working across the election. Drop in and co-work from 10am till 7.30pm every day.
items.note: A co-working space for election workers is sector logistics, not a resource that changes public participation.

items.b: Democracy Classroom Key resources include posters, template emails, a handbook for employers, manifestos and everything you need to engage young people in the election.
items.why: this matters democratically because it creates new resources to help young people engage with and understand the electoral process.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building that creates new means of civic participation.

items.b: Democracy Club is the go to place for voter information, whether for candidate information or polling station information. mySociety’s TheyWorkForYou, Freedom of Information tools and Local Intelligence Hub provide key information for you and your election projects.
items.why: this matters democratically because these tools give voters practical information needed to identify candidates and polling stations, and give citizens means to scrutinise Parliament and public bodies.
items.note: Voter information tools fall under elections access; FOI/TheyWorkForYou touch accountability.

items.h: Just Register
items.b: Small Axe’s Just Register project provides wrap around personalised support for those registering to vote.
items.why: this matters democratically because it directly helps people overcome barriers to electoral registration, a precondition for exercising the franchise.

items.h: Fix The Glitch 3.0 Election Toolkit
items.b: The Glitch team created a toolkit and facilitation guide to combat digital misogynoir during election periods as part of their Be Safe Online campaign.
items.why: this matters democratically because it addresses online discrimination and harassment that can deter women, particularly Black women, from participating in electoral campaigns.
items.note: Classified under rights as it concerns discrimination/harassment rather than resource distribution.

items.h: RNIB resource on how to campaign accessibly
items.b: The Royal National Institue of Blind People want to make this General Election the most accessible election campaign ever — download their guide to accessible campaign communications now
items.why: this matters democratically because it aims to make election campaign communications accessible to disabled people, widening who can meaningfully engage with the election.
items.note: Accessibility of campaigning is anchored to elections under the framework's accessibility-of-voting scope.

items.h: National Voter Registration Day — 18th June
items.b: National Voter Registration Day (NVRD) is coming up fast on 18th June, the deadline to register to vote in the upcoming national poll. Find out more .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it publicises the deadline and mechanics for electoral registration, which determines who can exercise the franchise.
items.note: Voter registration mechanics fall under elections & decision making, in line with the turnout rule.

items.h: Special event Democracy Drinks: Election Edition next week, June 20th in Central London
items.b: Next week at the Wellcome Collection, the Democracy Network , JRRT and The Civic Power Fund are hosting a special evening drinks reception for all those working across the general election, with a particular focus on voter registration and GOTV. The event will be an informal affair and an opportunity for those working on the election to share what they’ve been working on, seek help and assistance and just to let their hair down for an evening among fellow travellers. Sign up for the event here .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.note: Social/networking event listing for sector workers, not a democracy story.

items.h: Votes at 16 confirmed in Labour Party manifesto
items.b: Thanks to tireless campaigning efforts by democracy organisations from the Electoral Reform Society , National Union of Students , to the Scottish Youth Parliament and British Youth Council, Body Shop , Intergenerational Foundation and many more — votes for 16 and 17 year olds are now confirmed in the UK Labour Party manifesto . Scotland and Wales already have votes at 16, but this has not been the case for the Westminster Parliament. By committing to this policy, the Labour Party joins the Liberal Democrats , Plaid Cymru, SNP and the Green Party offer Votes at 16 in this election for Westmins…
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: extending the franchise to 16 and 17 year olds changes who is entitled to vote in UK elections.

items.h: Democracy Classroom offer key resources to orgs engaging young people in election activities
items.b: Democracy Classroom have now engaged over 2500 teachers and youth practitioners and are working with over half of the FE Colleges in the UK. They are offering critical resources to engage young people , FAQs for voter registration , a handbook for employers and are also tracking all hustings events across the UK , not to mention Our Generation Our Vote . Democracy Classroom’s #ElectionCountdown includes a huge array of resources for voter registration efforts from an array of partner orgs — sign up to their emails now .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it creates new resources and tools that help young people and organisations engage in election activities, expanding practical means of participation.
items.note: Capacity-building resource for civic engagement, with a voter-registration component tying it to elections.
links: tracking all hustings events across the UK

items.h: New Economy Organisers Network running General Election digital drop-ins
items.b: The sessions run by NEON are open sessions taking place online every Thursday from 0945–1145 and can provide assistance with digital content creation, project development, election strategies and content feedback. The next one is on Thursday 20th June — book your slot using this Calendly Link .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: the drop-ins build organisational capacity for campaigning and digital engagement, expanding the practical means available for participating in the election.
items.note: Borderline sector training service treated as capacity-building since it helps orgs take part in election campaigning.

items.h: 120 organisations back #SheVote24 Open Letter to put women and girls at the heart of the election
items.b: Centenary Action Group and the Fawcett Society are coordinating an Open Letter from women’s sector organisations calling for women and girls to be put at the heart of the election. With more than 120 signatories from women’s organisations across the UK, representing more than 10.5 million women and girls as members, supporters and service users — they are the largest ever assembled coalition coming together in the interests of women and girls.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.note: This is advocacy for policy content (women's issues in the election), not a democratic mechanism of representation or participation.

items.h: Just 30% of candidates standing are women, say Elect Her
items.b: Whilst there are more than 62 Marks, 62 James’, 61 Chrises, 54 Andrews, 51 Richards… standing for election, just 30% of candidates standing this year are women. Are you a woman standing this year? Get in touch with Elect Her now or check out their election resources to support women candidates , wherever they are and whoever they are standing for. Elect Her’s new How to: Get Involved In The Election Toolkit can help you get politically active in the run up to the vote.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: the proportion of women standing as candidates bears directly on the representativeness of elected institutions.
links: Get in touch with Elect Her now or check out their election resources to support women candidates

items.h: 79 candidates have taken Jo Cox Foundation & Compassion in Politics’ Civility Pledge
items.b: The 2024 General Election Civility Pledge has been created in partnership between The Jo Cox Foundation and Compassion in Politics . With 79 pledging candidates, CIP & JCF urge all parliamentary candidates from across the political spectrum to take the Civility Pledge and share their commitment to a respectful election campaign.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: candidate abuse and incivility can deter people from standing for office, undermining fair political competition.
items.note: Treated as elections/decision-making because it concerns conditions for candidacy rather than civic-society capacity.

items.h: Operation Black Vote launch Vote For Your Life
items.b: Vote For Your Life , launched by Operation Black Vote (OBV) in collaboration with the Black Equity Organisation (BEO) , is a new voter registration campaign aimed at ensuring the voices of Black communities are heard and advancing their demands for equality, justice, and reform in the corridors of power.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: a new voter registration campaign directly affects who is able to exercise the franchise.
items.note: Turnout and registration campaigns are always classified under elections & decision making per framework rule.

items.h: Black Equity Organisation running Black Britain’s Mandate Poll
items.b: Black Equity Organisation and Operation Black Vote want to hear your thoughts on what will help Black individuals of Caribbean and African heritage thrive in the UK. Share the poll now on X . They say: ‘Ensuring Black communities can engage in political processes up and down the country is vital to achieving equity. This engagement is also part of our mission and ongoing work to dismantle systemic racism to ensure equity for all. ‘The views and ideas you share in this poll will then be collated with hundreds of other responses from across the UK to create the first Black Britain’s Mandate, whi…
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: a new consultation mechanism aims to gather and amplify community demands to put to government, expanding avenues for civic voice.
items.note: This is a consultative poll rather than formal decision-making machinery, so filed under participation not elections.
links: Share the poll now on X

items.h: United Response and My Vote My Voice highlight disability exclusion in the election
items.b: My Vote My Voice is on a mission to encourage people with learning disabilities and autistic people to vote in the 2024 General Election. Before the election they worked with Channel 4’s Ruben Reuter to highlight the exclusion of Disabled People from the Electoral Commission’s voter registration campaign . Now they’re providing new resources and easy read voter information for autistic people and people with learning disabilities — check it out now ( and get your free accessible voting badge here ). Watch their new campaign video .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: new accessible resources and campaigning address barriers that exclude disabled people from exercising the franchise.
links: highlight the exclusion of Disabled People from the Electoral Commission’s voter registration campaign
and get your free accessible voting badge here

items.h: Royal National Institute of Blind People encouraging campaigners to campaign accessibly
items.b: Liz Williams at RNIB Cymru is writing to campaigns to campaign accessibly over the next few weeks and ensure accessibility for Blind people. They’re running an ‘Alt-Text Day’ this Saturday raising the importance of using Alt-text in campaigner communications — Alt text paints pictures for those who can’t see . RNIB are currently working with the Electoral Commission on a guide for Blind and Partially Sighted voters, particularly around voter ID.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: new guidance and campaigning on accessible campaigning and voter ID directly affect whether blind and partially sighted people can vote.
links: Alt text paints pictures for those who can’t see

items.h: Jo Cox Foundation says ‘Candidate abuse unacceptable’ after repeated attacks on Reform Leader
items.b: The Jo Cox Foundation (JCF) has called the recent attacks on Nigel Farage , newly appointed leader of Reform UK , an ‘affront to democracy’. Su Moore, CEO of JCF, said it was ‘shocking and completely unacceptable’ and is a ‘really serious issue’. ​​The Jo Cox Foundation was launched after Batley and Spen MP Ms Cox was killed by far-right terrorist Thomas Mair in June 2016.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: threats and attacks against candidates can deter people from standing and campaigning, undermining free political competition.
items.note: Classified under elections because the harm targets a candidate's ability to campaign, though personal security is also engaged.

items.h: More than 50 organisations sign up as accredited UK Voter Champions
items.b: Citizens’ UK have brought together more than 50 organisations as voter registration ‘champions’ , these now-accredited organisations include the Church of England, dozens of schools, colleges, universities, charities, community groups and businesses. Demonstrate your commitment to encouraging non-partisan engagement in democracy by accrediting as a Voter Registration Champion now .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it expands voter registration infrastructure that determines who can exercise their right to vote in elections.
items.note: Voter registration/turnout is always classified under elections per the framework's turnout rule.

items.h: My Life My Say’s Give An X voter registration campaign ratchets up ahead of the election (free ice cream alert!)
items.b: My Life My Say Give An X campaign , laser focused on getting young people to register to vote in droves ahead of next thursday’s deadline, has announced a major new partnership with Ben and Jerry’s UK — together they will be serving free ice cream in the centre of town in Manchester and Birmingham to get out the vote — find out more .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it is a campaign to increase voter registration and turnout ahead of a general election.
items.note: Turnout campaigns are always classified under elections & decision making regardless of framing.

items.h: Young people can now apply for a free Citizen Card, ends 20th June
items.b: Citizen Cards are an accepted form of voter ID in polling stations and can be used as regular ID, for pubs, buying age restricted goods etc. Use the code DEMOCRACY at checkout to receive a CitizenCard for free. The deadline to apply for a free CitizenCard in time for the general election is Thursday 20th June.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it affects whether young people can meet voter ID requirements and cast a ballot.

items.h: Poverty Alliance’s Vote Your Values campaign highlights inequality in this year’s election
items.b: Scottish Community Development Centre shine a light on The Poverty Alliance’s Vote Your Values campaign which is working to register more than 300,000 people on lower incomes at risk of losing their vote this year because they’re not registered. They’ve created posters and resources to share and post up in community centres to encourage people to register to vote.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it targets electoral registration gaps that risk disenfranchising low-income citizens.
items.note: Registration/turnout drives are classified under elections even when framed around inequality.
links: The Poverty Alliance’s Vote Your Values campaign

items.b: Candidate data for past elections from the House of Commons Library .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it provides public data on electoral candidacy that underpins transparency about political competition.

items.h: Democracy Club — the most data held on candidates ever!
items.b: Democracy Club’s amazing volunteer community ( Join the Slack community ) have collected the details of every candidate standing in the 2024 UK general election — you can access this data and view your ballot paper on WhoCanIVoteFor . Democracy Club have also identified that the 2024 UK general election will see a record number of candidates . 4,515 candidates have been nominated to stand on 4 July, beating the previous record of 4,150 set in 2010.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it documents candidate competition and provides voters with the information needed to choose representatives.
links: 2024 UK general election will see a record number of candidates

items.h: mySociety tools to help your organisation face the election
items.b: mySociety’s Julia Cushion has pulled together a handy suggestion of how mySociety tools can help your organisation navigate the election. These include: TheyWorkForYou — MPs voting record and register of interests, including new General Election pages with up to date lists of candidates — thanks to Democracy Club ’s WhoCanIVoteFor. Local Intelligence Hub — for loads of detailed data on your constituency new and old, from opinion polls to nearby campaigning groups.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it aggregates tools that let citizens and organisations track candidates, MPs' records and constituency data to engage with an election.
items.note: Combines election navigation tools with an MP-accountability tool (TheyWorkForYou), so elections is treated as primary given the election-focused framing.

items.h: Sortition Foundation launches new 858 Project
items.b: It’s been 858 years since Henry II introduced juries and now Project 858 seeks to put citizens at the helm of politics as part of an umbrella campaign to ‘finish the job Henry II started’ and upgrade Britain’s institutions, replacing the House of Lords and the legacy of feudalism, they argue, with a new House of Citizens.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it proposes replacing an unelected legislative chamber with a sortition-based citizens' body, altering the machinery of collective decision-making.
items.note: Citizens' assemblies/sortition proposals are anchored to elections & decision making per the framework's boundary rule, not participation.

items.h: Tory women hit out at ‘Boys Club’ candidate selection
items.b: Female Tory candidates claim they lost out in the last-minute rush to fill vacancies , alleging Rishi Sunak’s allies oversaw a ‘jobs for the boys’ operation. The party was working under emergency rules to select candidates for 160 seats nationwide in preparation for the 4 July General Election. Women2Win have been working to elect more Conservative women and helping them to stand in the rushed proceedings for this year’s snap election — find out more .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: it concerns whether internal party candidate selection processes are fair and open, affecting who can stand for office and the representativeness of elected institutions.
items.note: Candidate selection within a political party falls under elections & decision making per the parties/candidate access anchor.
links: claim they lost out in the last-minute rush to fill vacancies

items.h: Tactical voting tools are back for GE2024
items.b: This year’s election features a set of various anti-Tory tactical voting tools. Movement Forward have updated their anti-Tory tactical voting tool StopTheTories.vote with the latest data and polling ahead of the upcoming vote, fronted by Carol Vorderman who has been helping the team promote the tool. Tactical.vote is another tool produced by the Tactical Voting Coalition. Best for Britain have also produced their own tactical voting tool, GetVoting.org .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: tactical voting tools shape how citizens exercise their vote under the electoral system, directly engaging the mechanics of electoral choice.

items.h: Alliance Now UK produce resources and a voting checklist
items.b: Alliance Now UK , a coalition of organisations working to upgrade democracy, have released a set of resources to help their supporters and the public navigate the elections.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: providing resources and a voting checklist helps citizens navigate the practical mechanics of casting their vote.
items.note: Voting-navigation resources are treated as elections & decision making per the turnout/access-mechanics rule.

items.h: Steve Endacott ‘AI Steve’ is running as an AI powered candidate
items.b: Brighton businessman ‘AI Steve’ or Steve Endacott is running as a candidate in Brighton , though they say they will merely be a ‘conduit’ for the generative AI model, which, they say, will make the policy decisions — Wired has the story . Last year Democracy Network member Andrew Gray ran as the UK’s first AI-powered candidate , who planned to use Pol.is to help drive policy decisions. Please see here for the full range of candidates running in Brighton Pavillion .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: a novel AI-driven candidacy raises questions about who and what can stand for election and how policy positions are formed for voters to choose between.
links: Brighton businessman ‘AI Steve’ or Steve Endacott is running as a candidate in Brighton
Democracy Network member Andrew Gray ran as the UK’s first AI-powered candidate
Please see here for the full range of candidates running in Brighton Pavillion

items.h: Demos running ongoing ‘citizens’ conversation’ on attitudes to trust in the pre-election period
items.b: Trustwatch 2024 is a new project by Demos , a live ongoing citizens’ verdict on the election campaign. The panel, made up of 32 people from across various backgrounds, will share their thoughts on key campaign moments as they happen throughout the short campaign.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: a live citizens' panel deliberating on the election campaign constitutes a deliberative process feeding into public understanding of the democratic contest.
items.note: Deliberative/citizens' panel processes are classified under elections & decision making per the framework's boundary rule.

items.h: Voter confidence at record low — new British Social Attitudes survey report by NatCen
items.b: Trust and confidence in the UK’s political and election system has never been lower according to new research by the National Centre for Social Research , with analysis by senior psephologist Sir John Curtice. The report Damaged Politics? The impact of the 2019–2024 Parliament on political trust and confidence finds 45% would ‘almost never’ trust the government to put country before party, the highest proportion ever, with more than 53% polled favouring more proportionate voting systems fairer to smaller parties.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: record-low trust in government to act impartially and rising support for electoral reform reflect the public's confidence in the accountability and design of the political system.
items.note: Trust-in-government findings map to the government & accountability anchor on public confidence, while the PR preference touches elections.

items.h: Republic lobbying candidates, digital action evening 17th June
items.b: Anti-monarchy campaign Republic are asking their members to contact their parliamentary candidates about the case for a Republic and they’re kicking this work off with a digital action evening next Monday 17th June at 7pm — find out more .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: a campaign mobilising members to directly lobby parliamentary candidates is an exercise of civic participation in shaping political debate.

items.h: Society of Editors tracking fake newspapers, again
items.b: The Society of Editors are concerned with new reports of fake newspaper titles promoting candidates, in the latest case Lib Dem candidate Munira Wilson. Last year Private Eye noted that the Conservative Party made widespread use of fake local newspaper titles in rural areas. The SoE has written to all political parties asking them to refrain from using fake newspapers to correspond with the public in the run-up to the election. Society of Editors have also unpacked the manifestoes for their positions on media reform . Last but not least, the SoE’s Media Freedom Awards are now open for nominati…
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: the use of fake newspaper titles to promote candidates distorts the public information environment voters rely on to make informed choices.
links: unpacked the manifestoes for their positions on media reform

items.h: Scottish Refugee Council’s Refugee Festival Scotland starts tomorrow, calls for a new plan for refugees
items.b: Amidst the election, the Scottish Refugee Council calls upon politicians across the UK to take action for a kinder, fairer and more effective refugee system — find out more here . Check out more than 150 events forming the Refugee Festival Scotland .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.note: Advocacy call and event listing for refugee policy, not a democratic mechanism story.
links: Check out more than 150 events forming the Refugee Festival Scotland

items.h: The Ferret launches For Fact’s Sake Podcast
items.b: Scotland’s leading independent investigative journalism paper The Ferret has launched a new weekly podcast for the duration of the election — For Fact’s Sake — highlighting the role of misinformation, the culture war, dark money and fact-checking ahead the vote — listen here . If you’ve not come across The Ferret before, check their work out now .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: This matters democratically because it creates a new public resource devoted to fact-checking, misinformation and dark money during an election, supporting a more informed electorate.

items.h: Professor Sir John Curtice to drop his take on the election in upcoming lecture
items.b: On Weds 26th June, Professor Curtice, the UK’s leading psephologist breaks down the polls and politics with just a week and a day to go until polling day — Register on Eventbrite .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.note: Event listing for a lecture, not a reported change or mechanism.

items.h: Cross-party Compass campaign backing 30 MP candidates for electoral reform
items.b: Compass are campaigning to elect a caucus of anti-Tory pro-PR MP candidates across various parties, including 11 candidates from Labour, 17 from the Lib Dems and 2 from the Green Party. The candidates have been endorsed by local Compass groups who are now campaigning on their behalf.
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: This matters democratically because it is an active campaign to elect candidates committed to reforming the electoral system (proportional representation), directly engaging electoral competition and system design.
links: elect a caucus of anti-Tory pro-PR MP candidates

items.h: Hundreds of peers could be forced to retire under Labour plans
items.b: Today’s Labour Party manifesto launch set out plans for an age cap for peers of 80 , reducing the size of the upper house and removing hereditary peers. Labour appear to have backtracked on earlier commitments to abolish the Lords and replace it with an elected Assembly of the Nations and Regions, though have kept this ambition in place, naming it in their manifesto . Tory peer Lord Norton, a member of the Campaign for an Effective Second Chamber cross-party group, described Labour’s decision to reform the Lords using an age cap as ‘a bit odd’ considering Labour would lose ‘quite a lot of Labo…
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: This matters democratically because it concerns proposed reform of the House of Lords, affecting legislative scrutiny, composition and checks on the executive.
items.note: Mentions an elected second chamber option, touching elections, but the core story is Lords reform and accountability.
links: set out plans for an age cap for peers of 80

items.h: Protecting All We Care About — new report by Unchecked UK
items.b: New report Protecting All We Care About by UK regulation campaigners Unchecked sound alarm on failure by UK regulators to sanction companies flagrantly in breach of rules on pollution, workers rights and other violations — key issues during the present election. Byline Times covered the story here .
items.sec: ⚡ Latest news and updates this week ⚡
items.why: This matters democratically because it documents regulators' failure to enforce rules against companies, undermining a key accountability check on public and private power.

items.h: Conservative Party manifesto democracy plans outlined
items.b: The Conservative Party manifesto promises to deliver greater accountability within the devolved parliaments and centralisation within Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland to ‘ensure decisions are made as close to the communities they serve as possible’. They pledge to remain steadfast in their their support for the First Past the Post system for elections and that they will not change the voting age from 18. They will maintain rules to ‘tackle voting fraud’, including the requirement to show ID. They will also introduce a new Minister for British Citizens Overseas, having delivered on their ea…
items.why: This matters democratically because it sets out the party's electoral system preferences (FPTP), voting age, voter ID rules, overseas franchise, and devolved decision-making arrangements.
items.note: Devolution accountability elements are secondary to the core electoral and franchise commitments.

items.h: New changes outlined in Labour Party manifesto plans
items.b: Labour’s manifesto launch includes commitments to strengthen relations between the Nations of the UK through a new Council of the Nations and Regions, strengthen free speech protections for devolved representatives, commitments to improve voter registration (automatic voter registration perhaps?) and address voter ID inconsistencies — and strengthening rules around political donations and ethics codes. In addition to Votes at 16 and Lords reform, Labour also commits to deepening devolution settlements for Combined Authorities and strengthening devolved arrangements in general.
items.why: This matters democratically because it proposes changes to voter registration, voter ID, the voting age, and devolution settlements that govern who can vote and how devolved power operates.
items.note: Donations rules and ethics codes are secondary accountability elements within a primarily electoral manifesto section.

items.h: Liberal Democrats launch new manifesto plans for democracy
items.b: In between rollercoaster rides at Thorpe Park , the Lib Dems launched their manifesto committing to introducing PR (STV), scrapping voter ID, Automatic Voter Registration, Votes at 16, overhauling ministerial codes, enable overseas citizens to vote in separate overseas constituencies, establishing national and local citizens’ assemblies, reforming the Lords ‘with a proper democratic mandate’, capping donations to parties and preparing for the transfer of power away from Westminster, both through a written constitution and a convention for a federal United Kingdom.
items.why: it sets out proposed changes to electoral systems, voter identification, registration, party finance, citizens' assemblies and the machinery of devolution that determine how people choose representatives and take collective decisions.
items.note: Campaign finance and citizens' assemblies are filed under elections & decision making per framework anchors; ministerial code reform is secondary government accountability.

items.h: Green Party, Plaid Cymru and Reform manifesto democracy commitments at a glance
items.b: The Green Party manifesto commits to defending the Human Rights Act, bringing in PR, replacing the Lords with an elected second chamber, Residence Based Voting Rights and Votes at 16 — as well as scrapping the Police, Crime Sentencing and Courts Act and the Public Order Act and ending the Prevent Programme. Plaid Cymru pledge to create a National Commission to improve the health of Welsh democracy and prepare the way for Welsh independence, removing the Secretary of State for Wales and devolving their powers to the Welsh Government, a new Government of Wales Bill to protect the Senedd’s powers…
items.why: the parties' manifestos propose changes to electoral systems, the Lords, postal voting and devolution structures alongside rights protections and anti-corruption measures that shape how power is acquired and constrained.
items.note: Human rights/ECHR and Equalities Act commitments are secondary rights beat; anti-corruption unit is secondary accountability.

items.h: Make this a zero-misogyny election
items.b: Back in February the Fawcett Society and the APPG on Women in Parliament asked parliamentary candidates to pledge a zero-tolerance approach to misogyny and racist mysogyny (mysogynoir) during the upcoming election.
items.why: a campaign to secure candidate pledges against misogyny and racist misogyny addresses discrimination and harassment that can deter people from standing for or participating in political life.

items.h: Runnymede pre-election report on immigration, racism and the 2024 election
items.b: Reflecting again, in January 2024, Runnymede Trust published a detailed report detailing the situation and choices facing political parties, elites and media organisations ahead of an election, whether public figures continue to ‘manufacture crises and moral panics’ and ‘mainstream far-right ideas’ or choose an alternative path. Well worth a read for those that missed it earlier this year.
items.why: the report examines how political parties, elites and media frame race and immigration ahead of an election, bearing on the quality and plurality of public political debate.
items.note: Recap of an earlier report rather than new news.

items.h: France wanted to get in on the action too
items.b: Just in case you missed it, our cousins across the channel are having a wild time of it. Take a look at what’s been happening in the French elections this week . That’s all for this now, if you’d like to send us your news for next week please email james@involve.org.uk UK Democracy Network
items.sec: And now for something completely different …
items.note: Offbeat pointer to French elections with no substantive claim about UK democracy.
links: Take a look at what’s been happening in the French elections this week

items.note: Event/co-working space listing for election workers, not a new means of public participation.

items.b: Democracy Classroom Key resources include posters, template emails, a handbook for employers, manifestos and everything you need to engage young people in the election.
items.why: this matters democratically because it creates new resources to help young people understand and engage with the election process, expanding practical means of participation.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new means of participation rather than an organisational notice.

items.h: Fix The Glitch 3.0 Election Toolkit
items.b: The Glitch team created a toolkit and facilitation guide to combat digital misogynoir during election periods as part of their Be Safe Online campaign.
items.why: this matters democratically because it equips people to counter online misogynoir during elections, protecting the conditions under which women can safely campaign and participate.
items.note: Toolkit is a new capacity-building resource; also touches rights against discrimination and online abuse.

items.h: RNIB resource on how to campaign accessibly
items.b: The Royal National Institute of Blind People want to make this General Election the most accessible election campaign ever — download their guide to accessible campaign communications now
items.why: this matters democratically because it provides tools to make campaign communications accessible, expanding blind and partially sighted people's practical ability to engage with the election.

items.h: Highest number of people register to vote on a single day ever, say Politics UK
items.b: A new record number of 629,875 people registered to vote on June 18th , ahead of the voter registration deadline — the highest amount in a single day ever, according to Politics UK .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: a record number of new registrations directly affects the size and composition of the electorate able to vote in the election
items.note: Voter registration/turnout is always classified under elections per the framework's standing rule.

items.h: Can you help circulate Disability Policy Centre’s voter accessibility survey
items.b: With the close of voter registration, Chloe Schendel-Wilson and the team at the Disability Policy Centre want to better understand how disabled people and people with learning difficulties found the experience and process of registering to vote. Please consider sharing their survey form , or share via X .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.note: A call to share a survey, not a reported finding or change; treated as sector logistics.

items.h: Fawcett Society announce big win: Labour, Lib Dems, Greens and SNP would make misogyny a hate crime
items.b: Labour, the Lib Dems, the Greens and the SNP have all said they would make misogyny a hate crime during an election debate on women’s safety . In 2021, the murder of Sarah Everard by a serving police officer led to renewed efforts to tackle violence against women and girls, with campaigners arguing misogyny is one of the ‘root causes’. See here for the Fawcett Society’s tweet sharing the news .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.note: Reports party policy pledges rather than a mechanism of democratic process or public power.
links: have all said they would make misogyny a hate crime during an election debate on women’s safety

items.h: Electoral Reform Society call for AVR as more than 5 million missing from voter rolls
items.b: Despite record numbers registering to vote this week, there still remains approximately 5 million people missing from voter rolls following the close of the registration deadline. In response, Electoral Reform Society are arguing the UK should follow Wales in introducing Automatic Voter Registration (AVR) at the earliest opportunity. Legislation on AVR is currently proceeding through the Senedd, see here for more information on the Elections and Elected Bodies (Wales) Bill and a breakdown of the Bill .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: a call for automatic voter registration, backed by ongoing Welsh legislation, addresses who is included on the electoral roll and thus who can exercise the franchise
items.note: Voter registration reform falls under elections/turnout per the standing rule.
links: still remains approximately 5 million people missing from voter rolls

items.h: Can I Vote? helps voters check their eligibility to vote at the general election
items.b: It’s not just UK citizens who can vote in UK elections — people from 56 Commonwealth Countries may also be eligible to vote. Can I Vote? a new online resource from Citizens UK , Just Register and Migrant Democracy Project allows individuals to check on their eligibility so no one misses their chance to vote.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: a new tool helping people determine their eligibility to vote directly affects practical access to the franchise
items.note: New resource aimed at voting eligibility falls under elections despite being framed as a capacity-building tool.

items.h: Democracy Classroom highlight voter registration on BBC news & radio
items.b: The Democracy Classroom team have published their hustings map , covering 130 hustings across the UK. They are running four Youth Hustings in Wales and have also collated all of the manifestoes and Party Political Broadcasts in one place. Ian Pope, The Politics Project Head of Programmes made it onto BBC Radio Wales yesterday to highlight the voter registration deadline, whilst Harriet Andrews, their Director, made it onto Radio 5Live .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: it publicises hustings and highlights voter registration deadlines, directly affecting turnout and electoral participation.
items.note: Turnout and registration always sit under elections per the framework's fixed rule.

items.b: Put People First, the Democracy Network coalition campaign, went live this week. The campaign has three strands — Include Everyone, Clean Up Politics and Devolution. The campaign partners are Campaigning Members of the Democracy Network and each strand is led by a partner organisation. We will soon have a website where you can find our key messages but in the meantime, please check the Democracy Network X and LinkedIn pages for the latest news — or join as a Campaigning Member now . items.h: UpVote engaging employers, launching new ‘voter tripling’ app
items.b: Rebecca Baron and the UpVote team are primarily working with brands, musicians, influencers etc to get people to register to vote — and now — to turn up and vote. With voter registration in the back mirror, they’re now turning to ‘Time to Vote’ an initiative similar to that run in the USA, consisting of getting employees to give employees time off to vote on election day. Patagonia and Oatly are hosting a roundtable event tomorrow, June 20th about it — Are you an employer? Email Rebecca for the details . The other initiative is Triple the Vote , again a successful initiative used by organisati…
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: new tools and employer initiatives aimed at increasing voter turnout directly affect electoral participation.
items.note: Turnout mechanics and willingness-to-vote campaigns are always classified under elections.

items.h: Good Law Project take aim aim at digital dark arts this election
items.b: Good Law Project’s new campaign Stop Targeting Me! highlights political parties’ dodgy use of data this election. The campaign calls upon the main UK parties to stop using personal data in their election campaigns — find out more and get involved .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: microtargeted use of personal data by parties shapes the political information environment voters encounter during campaigns.
items.note: Framed as political advertising/data targeting rather than pure privacy rights, so filed under information & debate.

items.h: Patchwork Foundation engaging underrepresented communities during the election
items.b: Patchwork’s #GetInvolved programme aims to engage the UK’s underrepresented communities in the lead up to the election. If you know people looking for ways to get more involved in the election but don’t know where to start, their #GetInvolved programme is aimed at those wanting to build their engagement with mainstream politics. Their sessions are tailored towards those with little to no prior experience or knowledge of politics — check it out now . They are also working to highlight the UK’s community leaders, through their Community Champions Award, alongside their MP of the Year Award. Find…
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: a programme built to help underrepresented communities engage with mainstream politics expands practical opportunities for participation.

items.h: Association for Citizenship Teaching need hustings videos, running impartiality workshops
items.b: Zoe Baker , Head of Education and Professional Development at the Association for Citizenship Teaching (ACT) , is looking for any videos of hustings, to be used in education resources and citizenship teaching, just 30 seconds to a minute’s footage is enough. ACT have been running political impartiality workshops for school leaders, teachers and youth workers, with a focus on sharing practical tools to help educators engage with young people in this election.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: educational resources and impartiality training build young people's and educators' capacity to engage with democratic processes.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new means of civic engagement.

items.h: Democracy is for everyone yet millions have no say in who represents them, say Migrant Democracy Project
items.b: Josiah Mortimer of the Byline Times spoke with the Migrant Democracy Project about the disparity of voting rights in the UK and their current work to correct this, highlighting how many non-British workers living in the UK feel deliberately politically excluded and disenfranchised .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: it concerns the extension or denial of suffrage to non-British residents, a core question of who can choose representatives.
items.note: Franchise/suffrage disparities are explicitly elections-beat territory.

items.h: Independent Social Research Foundation hold event tonight on disability & political representation
items.b: Independent Social Research Foundation (ISRF) to host event book launch event today from 5–6.30pm online and in London, the event features discussion with the authors of a new treatise exploring how and why representative politics are failing disabled people — register now or share via X .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.note: A book-launch discussion event is sector promotion, not a new participation mechanism or accountability change.

items.h: mySociety focus on post-election period
items.b: With their various tools running in the background for campaigners and activists, such as the Local Intelligence Hub , TheyWorkForYou , etc — mySociety have turned their gaze to after the election, creating new briefing packs for the new MPs. The packs will provide key information on their electorates and constituents — and you can help too! They are looking for data that is organised and categorised by the new constituency maps. Anyone that can help with this would be appreciated and should reach out to Julia via Julia@mysociety.org
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because creating constituency briefing resources for new MPs is a form of civic-tech capacity-building that helps representatives understand and be accountable to their constituents.

items.b: The London College of Political Technology, Newspeak House , who are hosting the ongoing 7 day a week election hackspace until the 5th July, are topping off their election activities and convening efforts with a non-partisan (political party workers/canvassers welcome) election results watch party from 8pm until late in Shoreditch, London — Sign up now .

items.h: Votes at 16 Northern Ireland put pressure on NI Executive to legislate Votes at 16
items.b: Emily Crudden McIlhatton of Politics in Action , working with the Votes at 16 NI team, report that the timing of the General Election announcement threw their plans somewhat, they are hoping to use the election opportunities to put pressure on the Northern Irish political parties to ask for the powers to be devolved so that the NI Executive can legislate on Votes at 16, rather than waiting on Labour to legislate at a UK wide level — sign and share their petition now .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because it concerns extending the franchise (votes at 16) and which level of government holds the power to decide suffrage rules.
items.note: Suffrage extension and devolved legislative power both sit in elections & decision making.

items.h: Generation Rent engage in final big push on voter registration
items.b: The team at Generation Rent , an organisation focused on tackling unfair evictions and pushing for a better deal for private renters, have been working to sign up their supporters — and young voters in particular — and get them registered to vote ahead of yesterday’s deadline.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because voter registration drives directly affect who is able to exercise the franchise and cast a vote.
items.note: Turnout and registration campaigns are always classified under elections & decision making per framework rule.

items.h: Give Food working to raise UK over reliance on emergency food banks with candidates
items.b: Jason Cartwight at Give Food has built a tool to contact MP candidates in each constituency as part of their campaign to ensure new MPs are aware of the scale of the problem of people relying on emergency food parcels.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because the tool creates a new channel for constituents to raise a policy concern directly with prospective MPs, expanding avenues for civic engagement.

items.h: Sense About Science ask party leaders to pledge on evidence based policy
items.b: David Schley and the team at Sense About Science are asking political parties to commit to following the rules on giving the public the evidence behind their policies . The campaign follows a recent review that showed the damage to public trust and confidence when government departments try to bury their findings or when ministers fail to share their rationale for decisions. The Liberal Democrats, SNP, Plaid and Green Party have signed the pledge. If you think you can help, or have useful political contact / able to make an intro — contact David Schley .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because pledges on evidence-based policy relate to transparency about the rationale behind government decisions, a core accountability mechanism.
items.note: Focus is on parties committing to transparency about policy evidence, an accountability mechanism rather than the information environment itself.

items.h: More in Common & UCL Policy Lab explore role of respect at upcoming election in new report
items.b: More in Common and the UCL Policy Lab have published the first in a series of briefing papers on the importance that voters place on politicians respecting them in the lead up to the general election. The research reveals that one of the biggest drivers of those who have switched from Conservative to Labour since 2019 is a feeling that Keir Starmer and Labour are more likely to ‘respect voters like them’.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: the report examines how voters' trust and sense of being respected by parties shapes vote-switching, which bears on electoral competition and public confidence in parties.
items.note: Borderline as this is voter-sentiment research rather than a mechanism of democracy itself.

items.h: Democracy Classroom and Operation Black Vote publish free posters encouraging voter participation
items.b: Democracy Classroom has created a number of posters and flyers which can be downloaded, printed out and used to encourage young people to vote. Operation Black Vote has also created a number of posters designed to encourage marginalised communities to vote in the election.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: new resources encouraging young people and marginalised communities to vote directly affect electoral turnout and participation, which the framework treats as always belonging to elections.
items.note: Turnout-related campaigns are classified under elections regardless of framing.

items.h: AI voice cloning is threatening electoral integrity, says new report
items.b: A new report from The Centre For Countering Digital Hate , Attack of the Voice Clones , explores how AI can be manipulated to create convincing fakes of high profile politicians’ voices. Six leading generative AI audio tools complied with CCDH researchers’ prompts to produce false statements mimicking the voices of high-profile political figures in 193 of the 240 test runs (80%).
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: AI-generated fake political audio undermines the public's ability to trust the information environment they rely on to make electoral decisions.
items.note: Framed as an electoral integrity threat but the mechanism is disinformation in the information environment.
links: The Centre For Countering Digital Hate

items.h: Large numbers of brits are still misinformed about voter ID, according to new poll
items.b: Polling for the Byline Supplement reveals that more than 4 in 10 (44%) of adults in Britain believe that a polling card alone will allow them to vote at the upcoming election. The research shows that age has a large determining factor, with 62% under the age of 40 wrongly assuming a polling card will suffice, compared to just 32% above the age of 40.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: widespread misunderstanding of voter ID rules risks disenfranchising eligible voters at the polling station, directly affecting electoral access and participation.

items.h: PolicyMogul launch manifesto comparison tool
items.b: PolicyMogul has launched a free manifesto comparison tool which allows you to see where the main parties stand on any issue of interest. A comparison of the various parties’ policies on ‘elections’ brings up a lot of interesting results!
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: a new tool letting voters compare party manifesto positions expands the public's access to plural information needed to make informed electoral choices.

items.h: Full Fact check claims made in party manifestos
items.b: Full Fact has been working hard in recent weeks to fact check all the live TV debates and the manifestos of major parties. They’ve checked the Labour manifesto , Conservative manifesto , Lib Dem manifesto , Green manifesto and Plaid Cymru manifesto for signs of misleading claims.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: fact-checking manifesto and debate claims helps voters access accurate information about competing political arguments ahead of an election.

items.h: The Constitution Unit to host conference on post-election constitutional reform priorities
items.b: The next government will have a number of constitutional reforms to consider, but which are the most pressing and most easily implemented? On the 24th and 25th of June, The Constitution Unit is hosting an online conference to debate these questions with sessions running on parliamentary standards, House of Lords reform, devolution in England, and more.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: debating post-election priorities on parliamentary standards, Lords reform and devolution concerns how executive and legislative power will be constrained and structured.
items.note: Event spans multiple beats; classified by its emphasis on parliamentary/constitutional scrutiny.

items.h: Conservative manifesto is light on pledges to improve democracy, says Electoral Reform Society
items.b: The Tory manifesto is light on commitments to improve our democracy , according to analysis by the Electoral Reform Society . Whilst they commend the plans to devolve more power to communities, ERS found little further evidence in the manifesto for reform. ERS welcomed Labour’s proposals , to extend the voting age to 16 and 17 year olds, to reform the House of Lords and to address the inconsistencies around Voter ID, but called on them to uphold their commitment to reforming First Past the Post.
items.why: the analysis concerns manifesto commitments on suffrage extension, voter ID, House of Lords reform and electoral system change, all of which shape how representatives are chosen and power transferred.
links: The Tory manifesto is light on commitments to improve our democracy

items.h: SNP manifesto pledges to deliver independence from the United Kingdom
items.b: The SNP manifesto commits to devolving employment rights to the devolved nations, protect the right to strike, reverse Brexit, secede from the Union via a new referendum, repeat the Internal Market Act, support the abolition of the House of Lords, transition to a new proportional voting system, extend voting rights to 16 & 17 year olds, as well as those with refugee status and international students. They also pledge to scrap voter ID, defend the ECHR and enhance LGBTI rights.
items.why: This matters democratically because the manifesto sets out competing proposals for how power is acquired and contested (referendums, voting systems, suffrage, voter ID) alongside constitutional and rights reforms.
items.note: Multiple beats covered; elections/voting reforms dominate the pledge list.

items.h: Constitution Unit undertake blog series on the manifestoes and what they mean for public participation in 2024
items.b: For more indepth analysis of the various parties pledges on democracy and constitutional matters, please see Alan Renwick’s blog series from the UCL Constitution Unit on this here .
items.note: Announcement of an external analytical blog series, not itself a reported democracy development.

items.b: Demos’ next Collaborative Democracy Network event will feature Taiwanese politician and free software programmer Audrey Tang, chief architect of Taiwan’s digital democracy policies, who served as the first Minister of Digital Affairs of Taiwan from August 2022 to May 2024 — during the session they will explore the intersection of technology and democracy. items.h: Labour commits to introducing Automatic Voter Registration
items.b: The Guardian has learned that Labour plans to implement Automatic Voter Registration (AVR) should they gain a majority in next week’s poll. While the UK Labour Party’s manifesto mentioned that it will ‘improve voter registration’ , until now Labour officials had previously dismissed that this would mean introducing AVR.

items.why: automatic voter registration directly affects who is enrolled and therefore able to exercise their right to vote
items.note: Voter registration policy falls under elections/turnout mechanics per the standing turnout rule.
