items.h: UpVote engaging employers, launching ‘voter tripling’
items.b: Rebecca Baron and the UpVote team are primarily working with brands, musicians, influencers etc to get people to register to vote — and now — to turn up and vote. With voter registration in the back mirror, they’re now turning to ‘ Time to Vote ’ an initiative similar to that run in the USA, consisting of getting employees to give employees time off to vote on election day. Are you an employer? Email Rebecca for the details . Their other key initiative is Triple the Vote , again a successful initiative used by organisations around the world, UpVote will launch a new text prompt tool that messa…
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because campaigns to boost employer-supported voting time and peer-to-peer turnout mobilisation directly affect electoral participation.
items.note: Turnout campaigns are always classified under elections per the standing rule, regardless of the willingness/mobilisation framing.

items.h: Demos and Power to Change call for more community power post-election
items.b: A new Green Paper published by Demos and Power to Change, Taking Back Control , calls on the incoming government to implement a set of proposals to increase ‘foundational power’ within communities. Demos and Power to Change want a change in how the next government approaches this question — what next after Levelling Up?
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because proposals to build 'foundational power' in communities concern the distribution of power and resources that shape people's practical ability to take part in civic life.
items.note: Framed as community empowerment rather than formal local government structure, so classified under participation not elections.

items.h: The Democracy Network’s campaign coalition kick-off community engagement work
items.b: The Put People First campaign aims to connect with community groups across the country to meet people where they are on issues of democracy. Together with The Haringey Community Action Network , Community Organisers , Sortition Foundation and Quakers UK , the Democracy Network kicked off the work in Tottenham this week in a lively discussion on the need to ‘clean-up politics’, ‘include everyone’ and ‘shift power’. The lively session discussed the impact of these issues on people’s lives, priorities for change, and how to support people to get involved in the campaign — check out these vox pop …
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because launching community engagement work to build relationships and mobilise civil society membership creates new means for people to take part in democratic life.
links: check out these vox pop videos from the session!

items.h: Weaponisation of prejudice as tactic of division in election period must end, say Democracy Network
items.b: Helen Wishart, Power & Voice Lead at the UK Democracy Network , argues in their new blog that actions from across the political spectrum during the election period that have targeted people and groups affected by intersecting forms of inequality is dangerous for democracy. Helen highlights ongoing work by members of The Democracy Network to address these issues as a cause for hope, and calls for us to be stubborn in our insistence that people in the UK — and our democracy — are better than our ‘politics’ often makes us look.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because targeting groups affected by intersecting inequalities during an election period concerns equal protection and freedom from discrimination as conditions for democratic participation.

items.b: Labour ‘pushing the big go button’ on their digital ads on Meta last week, according to Who Targets Me. Credit — Who Targets Me
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because monitoring of political digital advertising bears on transparency and plurality in the campaign information environment.

items.h: Get live updates on how candidates and parties are using digital political ads this election, via Who Targets Me
items.b: Who Targets Me run a browser extension app monitoring political ads on websites and social media sites installed on more than 100,000 people’s devices. This affords a huge amount of information and insight into how parties are deploying digital political advertising — install the browser extension , follow Who Targets Me for updates on how the campaigns are using digital ads, or subscribe to their Full Disclosure newsletter for a full and regular lowdown on all things political ad spend.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because tracking how parties deploy digital political ads provides public insight into the campaign information environment.
links: subscribe to their Full Disclosure newsletter

items.h: Kevin Keith argues for open government as way to build trust, in piece for Civil Service World
items.b: Open government is a governance model based on the principles of integrity, accountability, transparency and the involvement of citizens, argues Kevin Keith, Chair of the UK Open Government Network , which coordinates civil society input into the UK National Action Plan for Open Government. Read the article on Civil Service World .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: this matters democratically because open government principles of transparency, integrity and citizen involvement are mechanisms for holding institutions answerable.
links: Read the article on Civil Service World

items.h: Campaign Lab develop tool to fast track petition data entry
items.b: A new tool developed by Campaign Lab is about to make campaigners’ lives a lot easier! Instead of manually entering data from physical petition sheets, the Handwritten Petition Scanner allows campaigners to snap a quick photo and have their data ready in seconds.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: it creates a new practical tool that lowers the burden of collecting and processing petitions, a mechanism for citizens to seek redress of grievances.
items.note: Sector capacity-building tool for petitions counts as participation under the framework's rule on new means of participation.

items.h: Byline Times reveal more than 130 Reform UK candidates ignoring election finance rules
items.b: 136 Reform candidates have raised tens of thousands of pounds on crowdfunding platforms without explaining how they will vet their donors, Byline Times’ Adam Bychawski finds. Only 21 of the 157 Reform candidates made clear that they need additional details from donors on their funding pages, despite the 136 raising over £99k through the sites. Electoral Commission rules require candidates to state on funding pages that they will check donations are from a permissible source. Read the article on Byline Times .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: transparent vetting of campaign donations is a core safeguard against illicit money influencing electoral competition.

items.h: Channel 4 News uncover racism and homophobia within Reform UK’s Clacton campaign
items.b: An undercover team working for Channel 4 News has revealed shocking racist and homophobic behaviour by Reform campaigners and canvassers in Clacton-on-Sea. They also witnessed Reform’s campaign manager ‘joking’ about potentially breaching election spending limits. Watch the footage now .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: exposure of a campaign casually discussing breaching spending limits bears directly on the integrity and fairness of electoral competition.
items.note: Racism/homophobia within the campaign also touches rights and discrimination, but the spending-limits admission anchors it to elections integrity.
links: revealed shocking racist and homophobic behaviour by Reform campaigners and canvassers

items.h: Electoral Reform Society call for guardrails on AI use during election campaigns
items.b: An open letter signed by Electoral Reform Society , Demos , Full Fact , Martin Lewis, and others, calls on political parties to agree a set of guidelines and guardrails for how to use AI during the election campaigns. Their demands include: not using generative AI tools to create misleading audio or visual content, clearly labelling where AI has been used to create content, and not amplifying misleading material — find out more .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: unregulated AI-generated political content during campaigns threatens the plurality and reliability of the information environment voters rely on.
items.note: AI in campaigns is classed as an information-environment issue rather than election administration.
links: calls on political parties to agree a set of guidelines

items.h: Democracy Club collate list of former MPs standing for election
items.b: With one week to go, Democracy Club has created a list of former MPs standing in the current election . They have also identified 40 manifestos published by parties across the country and included them in their WhoCanIVoteFor tool.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: aggregating candidate and manifesto information helps voters make informed choices in a competitive election.
links: created a list of former MPs standing in the current election
identified 40 manifestos published by parties across the country

items.h: Electoral practice and law — Constitution Unit discuss what’s changed since 2019
items.b: A lot has changed in electoral law and practice since the 2019 general election. A new blog from Sanjana Balakrishnan at UCL Constitution Unit outlines all the changes; from Voter ID to oversight of the Electoral Commission. Also, don’t miss their recent article on Labour’s plan for a new Ethics & Integrity Commission .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: tracking changes to voter ID rules and Electoral Commission oversight since 2019 concerns the machinery and integrity of elections.
links: recent article on Labour’s plan for a new Ethics & Integrity Commission

items.h: Record number of women MPs to enter parliament, according to Survation
items.b: Survation MRP modelling has mapped projected results on July 4th and concludes that the UK could be on the verge of electing a record number of female MPs (40%) to the House of Commons, meaning the UK would move into the top 30 countries for gender representation. A Labour victory would also see the ‘most gender balanced cabinet in British history’ including the country’s first female chancellor, they state. However, Survation note there is still a long way to go to ensuring parliament is fully representative of the gender composition of the electorate — check Elect Her and 50:50 Parliament fo…
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: the gender balance of elected representatives is a direct measure of the representativeness of the elected legislature.
links: UK could be on the verge of electing a record number of female MPs

items.h: Route Research build new tool to identify whether your constituency has ever had a woman MP
items.b: Centenary Action Group highlight the work of audience research body Route Research, who have developed a tool and interactive map uncovering the history of women’s representation in Parliament since universal suffrage was established.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: mapping historical representation of women in Parliament illuminates the representativeness of elected institutions over time.
items.note: A new research tool tracking representation, treated as capacity-building tied to representativeness of elected office.

items.h: General election coverage dominated by male voices, claims new research by Loughborough University
items.b: Academics from Loughborough University’s Centre for Research in Communication and Culture have conducted news audits for every election since 1992. Since campaigning began on 30 May, only seven of the top 20 most prominent figures in election coverage have been women . In the past week, that figure fell to six. Dr Jilly Kay, senior lecturer in communication and media, said: “We’re seeing the continued dominance of men’s voices, which has been an established pattern throughout the campaign.”
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: This matters democratically because unequal media prominence for women shapes the plurality and diversity of political voices citizens encounter during an election campaign.
items.note: Treated as media plurality/diverse coverage rather than gender rights, since the story's mechanism is news coverage patterns.
links: only seven of the top 20 most prominent figures in election coverage have been women

items.h: Questioning parliamentary candidates on women’s inequality, new guide published
items.b: The Women’s Budget Group has published a pre-election guide to help voters understand women’s economic inequality in the UK and their prospective candidates’ plans to tackle it. The briefing provides key stats and info on the economic inequality facing women, alongside some suggested questions which voters can ask to probe parliamentary candidates on this agenda.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: This matters democratically because the guide gives voters new practical means to scrutinise and question candidates on a policy issue ahead of an election.

items.h: Millions in UK unable to vote due to immigration status, say Migrant Democracy Project
items.b: In a new piece by Emiliano Mellino of the The Bureau of Investigative Journalism , Lucrezia Bosio highlights the millions of people, doctors, civil servants and elected members of local government who have lived in the UK for decades, think of themselves as British, but cannot vote on 4th July due to their immigration status. Migrant Democracy Project are highlighting these stories and campaigning for a change to electoral law — find out more and read the article now .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: This matters democratically because it concerns who is legally entitled to vote, a core question of inclusive suffrage.

items.h: We’re Right Here have a message for the main parties this election
items.b: We’re Right Here launch a new campaign film this election calling on the next government to empower local communities and community leaders, saying that whilst politicians are out pounding the pavements for these few weeks, ‘community leaders are always in touch with their communities — we’re right here, and we’re here to help’. Get in touch about the new campaign and how your organisation can support them.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: This matters democratically because the campaign seeks to expand the role of community organising and local voice in shaping government decisions.
items.note: Could touch local government structure, but the mechanism here is community campaigning rather than a specific institutional change.

items.h: MP Watch launch new campaign targeting climate denying MPs
items.b: The new campaign aims to target the top 10 ten climate denalists in Parliament and highlight the top 10 best climate candidates on the ballot in this Thursday’s election, as judged by a team of panellists at DeSmog, including Baroness Boycott, Prof. Mike Berners-Lee, Brian Eno, Lucy Siegel, Laline Paull and MP Watch citizens.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: This matters democratically because the campaign mobilises citizens to scrutinise candidates' records and engage with an election issue.
links: new campaign aims to target the top 10 ten climate denalists in Parliament and highlight the top 10 best climate candidates

items.h: JustPark offer 30 minutes free parking near polling stations this Thursday
items.b: A survey of 2,100 drivers for the firm found that more than a quarter of respondents are planning to drive to cast their vote, with cars being their second preferred mode of transport to the polls, after walking. The parking allocation app company JustPark are planning to offer 30 minutes free parking near polling stations on Thursday. Thanks to Josiah Mortimer at Byline Times for pointing this out!
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: This matters democratically because reducing practical barriers to reaching polling stations bears on voter turnout and access to voting.
items.note: Turnout and voting-access mechanics are always classed under elections per the framework rule.

items.b: Make Votes Matter Manchester dressing up as chartists as part of their drive for PR. Credit — Make Votes Matter
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: This matters democratically because it depicts campaigning for proportional representation, a matter of electoral system design.
items.note: Thin caption content but topic concerns electoral systems reform.

items.h: Make Votes Matter campaigning to get candidates to sign up to backing PR
items.b: From Portpatrick to Pimlico Make Votes Matter campaigners have been out knocking on doors, postering and making the case for PR and calling on candidates to take the #PledgeForPR, as Andrew Marr admits he thinks ‘PR or voting reform is going to be one of the really big issues in the next Parliament’ and Labour, Green and Lib Dem candidates come forward to take the pledge. See more over on Make Vote Matter’s X feed .
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: This matters democratically because campaigning to change the electoral system directly concerns how votes translate into representation.
links: Andrew Marr admits he thinks ‘PR or voting reform is going to be one of the really big issues in the next Parliament’

items.h: Tory warnings of impact of Labour supermajority do not add up, say Institute for Government
items.b: Whilst the Conservatives have been warning of the dangers of a Labour supermajority, Hannah White at the Institute for Government argues their fears don’t stack up , arguing instead that ‘a government’s attitude to scrutiny is more important than the size of its majority’.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: it concerns whether Parliament and civil society can hold an executive with a large majority to effective scrutiny and account.
links: Institute for Government argues their fears don’t stack up

items.h: Shout Out UK team up with Ofcom and the Electoral Commission to tackle election misinformation
items.b: A new campaign launched by Shout Out UK in collaboration with Ofcom and the Electoral Commission , Dismiss , is boosting awareness of misinformation / disinformation tactics to enable young people make an informed decision on July 4th. The campaign highlights a number of areas voters should be aware of including deep fakes, bot accounts, echo chambers and data manipulation.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: it addresses whether voters can access accurate information free from disinformation tactics ahead of an election.
items.note: Election-specific misinformation campaign classified under information environment rather than elections machinery.

items.h: Alistair Campbell predicts proportional reform to feature heavily in coming weeks
items.b: The Labour Party’s former Director of Communications, Alistair Campbell, remarks that he expects proportional voting reform to jump up the agenda in the coming weeks as a result of the disproportionality of the expected results. Meanwhile, the Labour leader last week defended First Past The Post as ‘the right system’ in a TikTok interview.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: it concerns whether the electoral system produces proportionate representation of votes cast.
links: he expects proportional voting reform to jump up the agenda in the coming weeks
Labour leader last week defended First Past The Post

items.h: Conservative Party on lowest seat total in British electoral history, according to YouGov MRP poll
items.b: A new MRP poll from YouGov suggests the Conservatives could be on track for their lowest seat share in their 200 year history. According to their latest model, Sunak could win just 108 seats with Labour winning 425. Britain Elects has their live poll aggregator pegging the Conservative Party at just 96 MPs.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.note: Pure horse-race polling on seat projections without a democratic mechanism at stake.

items.h: Three quarters of voters think politics needs to improve significantly, poll finds
items.b: Polling by the Electoral Reform Society finds three quarters (76%) of the public feel that politics needs to improve significantly , with 48% of respondents saying that politics needs ‘a great deal of improvement’. Conservative voters were the least likely to agree with this statement, but a majority (58%) still thinks an improvement is needed. Only 4% of the 2,226 polled said no improvement is needed.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: it reflects public confidence in the political system, an explicit indicator of institutional accountability and legitimacy.
links: three quarters (76%) of the public feel that politics needs to improve significantly

items.h: Poll finds unprecedented appetite for tactical voting to unseat the Conservatives
items.b: A new Best for Britain poll of more than 22,000 people finds that at least a third of voters in 558 constituencies are prepared to vote tactically on July 4th to orchestrate a change of government. In 234 seats that number increases to 40%, and in 31 seats more than half are ready to vote for a different candidate to their first choice in order to unseat the current Government.
items.sec: Latest election news and updates this week
items.why: it concerns voters' willingness to exercise their vote strategically to shape electoral competition and outcomes.
links: prepared to vote tactically on July 4th

items.h: Google is launching a new €15M fund for European democratic resilience
items.b: The initiative is aimed at bolstering civil society organisations across Europe, with a focus on election integrity and misinformation, through the use of emerging technologies. Google is looking for high impact proposals leveraging technology in innovative ways , as well as coalitions of organisations working together to leverage solutions. So, if you’re working on election integrity, disinformation, cybersecurity in the civic space, digital literacy training for voters, civic information platforms or deliberative or decision making tools and systems — check it now .
items.note: Treated as a funding call under sector logistics rather than a created participation tool.
links: Google is looking for high impact proposals leveraging technology in innovative ways

items.h: Reprieve, IPPR, Best for Britain, Republic and more hiring
items.b: Reprieve are looking for a new Head of Unlawful Detentions, IPPR are on the hunt for a new Head of Advocacy, Republic for a new Labour-focused supporter officer, and Best for Britain for a new Head of Fundraising, and many more besides — check the Democracy Jobs board for more information .
items.note: Job listings are organisational admin, not a democracy story.
links: check the Democracy Jobs board for more information

items.h: Stop Funding Hate & Civic Power Fund run new Bad Actors sessions
items.b: The series of sessions organised by Stop Funding Hate and Civic Power Fund are focused on Bad Actors in the migration sector. Their first session will be training focused on how to campaign against corporations, sign up here .
items.why: it creates new training capacity to help people organise and campaign, expanding practical means of civic participation.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building under participation per the framework rule.

items.h: Care Full celebrate their first 6 months!
items.b: Ruth Hannan and the team at Care Full celebrate their 6 month birthday today since taking the leap to build a new organisation to explore what a new caring economy could look like — go check them out now and give them a follow !
items.note: Organisational anniversary notice, not a change in democratic participation.
links: go check them out now and give them a follow

items.b: Nivek Thompson at the All-Island Better Democracy Network coworking day. Credit — Involve Foundation
items.note: Photo caption only, no substantive content.

items.h: All-Island Better Democracy Network host in-person network day
items.b: The Democracy Network’s sister organisation, also hosted by the Involve Foundation, the All-Island Better Democracy Network , is a new initiative made up of organisations from every corner of Ireland working or interested in participation, civic voice, deliberation and citizen-centred democracy. Last week they hosted an in-person network day including co-working, offers and needs and a learning seminar by Nivek Thompson of Real Democracy Now , even finishing off with Democracy Drinks. Join the Network here!
items.why: it builds a new cross-border network and shared capacity among organisations working on civic voice and deliberation, expanding the sector's ability to support participation.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building rather than a specific deliberative process.
links: Nivek Thompson of Real Democracy Now

items.h: Senedd Elections and Elected Bodies (Wales) Bill progresses to Stage 3 next week
items.b: The Elections and Elected Bodies (Wales) Bill currently working its way through the Senedd would introduce Automatic Voter Registration, make it an offence for a Senedd member or candidate to engage in political lying, improve the diversity of the Senedd and local government democratic structures, create a new requirement for a voter information platform, reform electoral financing, as well as disqualifying town and community councillors from serving in the Senedd. The Bill is currently at Stage 3 with proceedings taking place on Tuesday 2 July — find out more .
items.why: it changes electoral registration, candidate conduct rules, electoral financing and the structure of Senedd and local government elections.
links: The Elections and Elected Bodies (Wales) Bill

items.h: Compassion in Politics call on Welsh public to contact their MS to support new law to end deliberate lying by politicians
items.b: Compassion in Politics are calling on their supporters and people in Wales to call on their MS and urge them to #endthelies and back Section 46 of the Elections and Elected Bodies (Wales) Bill and vote against Amendment 6.
items.why: the campaign seeks to influence a specific legislative provision governing electoral candidate conduct, and mobilises public contact with representatives.
items.note: Campaign concerns a specific clause of the Elections and Elected Bodies Bill.
links: calling on their supporters and people in Wales

items.h: Mick Antoniw MS raises fears over Senedd lying ban
items.b: Counsel General for Wales, Mick Antoniw, has raised concerns over a lack of parliamentary scrutiny regarding the ‘suddenly bolted on’ changes to the the Elections and Elected Bodies (Wales) Bill , namely the amendment to make it an offence for a Member of the Senedd to lie in the chamber. The Counsel General argues the changes may have serious unintended consequences if not allowed proper time for scrutiny , highlighting that the Welsh Parliament does not have a revising second chamber to make such changes and offer scrutiny.
items.why: it concerns whether a legislature scrutinises significant amendments to law with adequate process and revising checks.
items.note: Focus is on parliamentary scrutiny process, not the electoral content itself.
links: argues the changes may have serious unintended consequences if not allowed proper time for scrutiny

items.h: mySociety welcome new cohort of trustees
items.b: It’s all warm welcomes and fond farewells over at mySociety as they welcome six new trustees onto the mySociety board, find out more information here .
items.note: Organisational governance/staffing news, not a democracy story.

items.h: Civic AI Observatory working to better inform civic organisations on their use of generative AI
items.b: The Civic AI Observatory , a project delivered by Newspeak House and funded by Nesta, aims to support civic organisations plan and adapt to the rapidly evolving field of generative artificial intelligence. Read the latest issue of their newsletter and join their WhatsApp Community to find out more.
items.note: A project newsletter/community launch about AI tooling for civic orgs, not a direct change to participation mechanisms.
links: Read the latest issue of their newsletter

items.h: Demos’ Collaborative Democracy Network hosting new discussion with Taiwan’s Audrey Tang
items.b: Demos’ next Collaborative Democracy Network event will feature Taiwanese politician and free software programmer Audrey Tang , chief architect of Taiwan’s digital democracy policies, who served as the first Minister of Digital Affairs of Taiwan from August 2022 to May 2024 — during the session they will explore the intersection of technology and democracy. Register now for the special evening event on 16th July, tickets are likely to sell out fast.
items.note: Event listing/registration notice, not a substantive democracy story.
links: Register now for the special evening event

items.h: Just Stop Oil activists and employees face raids, house searches and arrest
items.b: Police have utilised new clauses within the Public Order Act introduced in 2023 relating to persons interfering with key national infrastructure to raid the homes of more than 27 Just Stop Oil activists and employees , with arrests continuing over the weekend. Just Stop Oil organisers have suggested this is a suspected ‘intelligence gathering’ operation.
items.why: this matters democratically because police use of new infrastructure-protection powers to raid and arrest protest activists tests the legal limits on freedom of assembly and state coercion of civil society.
items.note: Protest policing under new statutory powers falls under rights/civic space, not participation, since the story is state coercion rather than willingness to take part.
links: raid the homes of more than 27 Just Stop Oil activists and employees

items.h: ANTIPARTY to launch on election night
items.b: There’s elections on, but they’ve got better things to do, they say. Join Isabella Roberts and the ANTIPARTY team for their launch event, featuring musicians, artists, DJs and talks on a range of community-driven projects, including ‘What are citizens’ assemblies?’, ‘​​How can Blockchain technology support decision-making?’ and ‘What is Participatory Budgeting?’ — Register here .
items.note: Launch/event listing rather than a reported change or new participation mechanism.

items.h: Need something to do whilst waiting for the results to roll in this Thursday?
items.b: Jessica Metheringham, Chair at Unlock Democracy , recommends their friend’s new ‘roll and write’ election strategy game — check it out!

items.h: Paul Hamlyn’s Ideas and Pioneers Fund reopens
items.b: Paul Hamlyn Foundation’s Ideas and Pioneers Fund has reopened offering grants up to £20k for individuals, groups and small organisations who want to explore a new idea for social change. Apply now .
items.note: Generic social-change funding call, not specifically tied to democratic participation.
links: Paul Hamlyn Foundation’s Ideas and Pioneers Fund

items.h: Welsh Government Democracy Engagement Grant is now open for applications
items.b: Each year £300,000 is made available by the Welsh Government to support and improve democratic engagement in Wales. £40,000 of this pot is still available for grants — the deadline for applications is 16th August 2024. See more about this opportunity now .
items.why: the grant directly funds efforts to improve democratic engagement among the Welsh public, creating new resources for participation.

items.h: Footwork launch programme to support community innovators
items.b: The new programme by Footwork works to support people in their community to deliver long term change for neighbourhoods, connecting community builders with mentors and other community connectors. Footwork will cover mentor fees and field trips as well as an unrestricted grant of £5k to each project. Find out more information .
items.why: the programme creates new capacity for community organising and civic action, expanding practical means for people to take part in shaping their neighbourhoods.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building for community organising under participation & civic life.

items.h: Also in funding news:
items.b: Helen Moulinos appointed interim chief executive of the Joseph Rowntree Charitable Trust, the trust has given out million in democracy funding via its Power and Accountability Program. You can find out more about Helen here . Lush, a long time funder of radical democracy work and campaigning is no longer accepting applications for funding as it reviews its giving strategy. The company says no new funds will be given until next year at the earliest.
items.note: Organisational appointment and funder business decisions, not a democracy mechanism.

items.h: TEDx London launch Democracy Bootcamp — applications open
items.b: TEDx London is running a special one day Democracy Bootcamp aimed at upskilling the next generation of storytellers and exploring how politics can work better for young people. Applications are open until 16th August — and the event will take place on the 12th October — Apply now and share the news .
items.why: the bootcamp builds skills and resources for young people to engage in political storytelling and civic participation.
items.note: Sector capacity-building programme aimed at expanding civic participation.
links: TEDx London is running a special one day Democracy Bootcamp

items.h: Input into the Democracy Network’s Annual Members Survey and receive a £15 voucher
items.b: The Democracy Network is currently running their annual survey, asking members of the growing Network for their input and feedback on their work. Participants will receive a £15 voucher. Take the survey now .
items.note: Internal member survey, organisational admin rather than a democracy mechanism.

items.h: All-Island Better Democracy Network hosting full network day, August 8th
items.b: The full day networking event organised by Marianna Mooney and Rebekah McCabe of the All-Island Better Democracy Network includes a coworking day event, a workshop on DIY Democracy, an in-person Network Meeting and even Democracy Drinks in the evening — Register now !
items.note: Primarily a sector networking and social event rather than a new means of public participation.

items.h: Liberty to publish civil society letter to the Home Secretary regarding sentencing of climate protesters
items.b: Liberty , Greenpeace and Amnesty UK are coordinating a joint civil society letter to the Home Secretary, Yvette Cooper, following the sentencing of 5 Just Stop Oil protesters to 4–5 years in prison last week for planning a protest. They are aiming to mobilise a broad coalition of civil society and community group support to reverse the recent civil rights crackdown. See the content of the letter and sign here .
items.note: This is a call-to-action letter-signing campaign rather than reporting on the underlying sentencing decision itself.
links: See the content of the letter and sign here

items.h: Open Government Network publish joint letter to the new Prime Minister
items.b: The UK Open Government Civil Society Network have drawn together 60 civil society organisations to support an open letter calling upon the government to proceed with open government reforms. View the open letter .
items.note: A call to sign an open letter is sector logistics rather than a reported change to open government practice.
links: UK Open Government Civil Society Network

items.h: Read the UCL Constitution Unit’s latest Monitor
items.b: The Monitor is a quarterly bulletin published by the UCL Constitution Unit highlighting in detail the most important democratic and constitutional issues facing the UK — well worth a read .

items.h: Join the Democracy Network for their AI & Democracy Webinar on empowering community voices
items.b: The next Democracy Network AI & Democracy webinar , this time will focus on Fora, ​an AI-supported sense-making platform developed by Cortico and the MIT Centre for Constructive Communication (MIT CCC). Fora is a community-powered, human-led and AI-supported digital approach to making sense of shared experiences. Find out how Fora makes it easier to amplify real voices and share the insights generated in deliberative forums, both large and small. Register now . Democracy Network are also organising a new Reimagining Political Parties AI & Democracy workshop, featuring contributions from Prof. …
items.note: Event/webinar listing, not a reported change to democratic practice.
links: next Democracy Network AI & Democracy webinar
recent paper by Dr Kate Dommett

items.h: Women-led grassroots democracy orgs make the Stylist
items.b: Last month, just before the election, the Stylist ran a piece on the women-led grassroots political orgs you should know about — and of course, they highlighted the diligent and amazing work of Naked Politics , Migrant Democracy Project and The Politics Project .
items.note: Media coverage of organisations as organisations, not a mechanism story.
links: Stylist ran a piece on the women-led grassroots political orgs

items.h: New AI-powered powered tool Whatsard makes Hansard more accessible
items.b: Developed by Jethro Reeve, a resident of Newspeak House — the London College of Political Technology — Whatsard is a new tool mimicking WhatsApp that takes Hansard records from TheyWorkForYou and publishes them in a more relatable, easy to read and accessible ‘chat’ format. Check it out here — Whatsard are looking for funding to promote and develop the tool, can you help?
items.why: this matters democratically because it creates a new, more accessible means for people to follow and engage with what their elected representatives say in Parliament, lowering barriers to civic engagement.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new means of participation rather than a media-plurality story.
links: Newspeak House — the London College of Political Technology
Whatsard is a new tool mimicking WhatsApp

items.h: MP Office Manual onboards hundreds of MPs
items.b: Edward Saperia, Hannah O’Rourke, Tom Steinberg, Lauren Botsford and the wider team at MP Office Manual have been working over the past several weeks to onboard hundreds of new MPs via their 102-page document packed with best practice and advice drawn from months of user research and analysis with MPs and their office staff. The MP Office Manual helps new MPs & their staff establish and run their offices effectively.
items.why: this matters democratically because it builds the operational capacity of newly elected MPs and their staff, supporting the effective functioning of Parliament as a democratically authorised institution.
items.note: Capacity-building for elected officials' offices falls under effective-parliament accountability rather than general civic participation.

items.h: Migrants Organise celebrate the launch of new book ‘A World Without Racism’
items.b: Edited by organiser Joshua Virasami, the new book A World Without Racism: Building Antiracist Futures features contributions from Migrants Organise, Healing Justice London, Voices That Shake, Sisters Uncut, and many more across a range of subjects such as migrant justice, women’s liberation, land and food struggles, policing and prisons. Migrants Organise offer a 20% discount code — just use WORLD20 when you order from Pluto Books .
items.note: Book launch/promotional item, not a mechanism story about public power.
links: A World Without Racism: Building Antiracist Futures

items.h: NEON National Spokesperson Training applications open
items.b: The New Economy Organisers Network trains and supports people to speak on television and radio, aiming to substantially boost the number of progressive, diverse voices in the campaigning space and boost coverage of underrepresented issues. The training runs from 15–17th October and includes two half days of online training and a full in person day of training — afterwards participants will join as members of the NEON Spokesperson Network, with the opportunity to be promoted to media outlets to speak on issues relating to them and their organisation on a regular basis — Apply now .
items.why: it creates a new pipeline of trained spokespeople to increase diverse voices participating in public debate and campaigning.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new means of participation rather than organisational news.

items.h: Trade union organiser Jane McAlevey passes away
items.b: Jane McAlevey was an American trade union organiser, author, Senior Policy Fellow at the UCA Berkeley Institute for Research on Labor and Employment And commentator on workers’ rights and struggles, before passing away earlier this month. Jane was a powerful organiser with a formidable track record and a deep commitment to labour organising, whose work impacted upon thousands of organisations across hundreds of countries. Read Rosa Luxemburg Stiftung’s obituary for Jane .
links: Read Rosa Luxemburg Stiftung’s obituary for Jane

items.h: Danny Sriskandarajah launches new book on people power
items.b: Chief Executive of the New Economics Foundation and former CEO of Oxfam, Danny Sriskandarajah has released a new book on the power of citizen action. Danny spoke with Unlock Democracy last week and toured the airwaves on Compass’ It’s Bloody Complicated podcast , talking about the new book.
items.note: Book launch and media tour is organisational/personal news, not a mechanism change.
links: Danny spoke with Unlock Democracy last week

items.b: Citizens White Paper recommendations (credit: Demos and Involve)
items.why: it depicts recommendations for embedding citizens' assemblies and panels into government decision-making machinery.
items.note: Caption accompanying the Citizens' White Paper story; classified consistently with it.

items.h: Demos and Involve launch new Citizens’ White Paper
items.b: The Citizens’ White Paper published this week by Involve and Demos sets out why and how the new government can embed participation in its decision-making. The paper recommends citizens’ panels to feed into the new government’s Mission Boards, embedding participation across the civil service, introducing a programme of citizens’ assemblies and setting standards to ensure best practice and standards to ensure citizen participation is independent and rigorous. Read the Citizens White Paper .
items.why: it proposes new deliberative and citizens'-assembly mechanisms to be embedded in government decision-making structures.
items.note: Citizens' assemblies and deliberative processes are classified under elections & decision making per framework rule.

items.h: Involve pen new thought leadership series on participation under the new government
items.b: The series by Involve aims at discussing and exploring possibilities for a new relationship between everyday people and the state under the new Labour Government. Read their first blog here .
items.note: A thought-leadership blog series is discursive commentary, not a new participation mechanism or resource.

items.h: Migrant Democracy Project — Report on the MPOWER Political Leadership Program
items.b: MDPs report highlights the impact of its flagship training program that prepares migrants to run for office. You can read the report here.
items.why: it trains migrants to seek public office, affecting who can access candidacy and representation.
items.note: Candidate access for underrepresented groups falls under elections & decision making rather than general participation.
links: You can read the report here.

items.h: Sortition Foundation criticise Starmer’s inaction on House of Lords reforms
items.b: Despite pre-election proposals to scrap the House of Lords altogether, the King’s speech contained limited action on this agenda. Labour did promise that no more hereditary Peers would sit in the upper chamber, but the Sortition Foundation criticised Starmer for these timid reforms and for already appointmenting eight new retiring MPs to its ranks.
items.why: it concerns the composition and reform of the House of Lords, a legislative chamber central to checks on executive power.
items.note: House of Lords reform concerns legislative structure/accountability rather than elections per se.

items.h: Labour to prioritise audit reform
items.b: The Government plans to create a new regulator , the Audit, Reporting and Governance Authority (ARGA). Labour will bring forward legislation previously shelved by the last government, within which will include power to investigate and sanction company directors for serious failures in relation to their financial reporting and audit responsibilities. This will mean directors will face consequences for putting forward any dodgy accounts. Thanks to Research for Action for highlighting this.
items.note: Audit regulation of company directors is corporate governance, not the exercise of public democratic power.
links: plans to create a new regulator

items.h: Justice Minister provides update on SLAPPS
items.b: Lord Ponsonby, a Labour justice minister in the House of Lords, remarked he could not commit to bringing forward standalone legislation on strategic lawsuits against public participation (SLAPPS) , or set out a timetable for tackling the issue. He said the government would be conducting a review and recognised ‘an urgent need for legislation’ on the matter.
items.why: SLAPPs are lawsuits designed to intimidate journalists and campaigners into silence, chilling public-interest reporting and debate about power.
items.note: SLAPPs are explicitly filed under information & public debate as they affect the public information environment.
links: he could not commit to bringing forward standalone legislation on strategic lawsuits against public participation (SLAPPS)

items.h: Voting rights for 16 and 17 year olds still a priority despite not being in King’s Speech, says Commons Leader
items.b: Despite promising signals that Labour would lower the voting age to allow 16 and 17 year olds to vote, no such legislation made it into the King’s Speech. However, Commons Leader, Lucy Powell, said they were hopeful young voters would be allowed to participate at the next general election as the policy remains a commitment for Labour.
items.why: Lowering the voting age would expand the franchise, directly affecting who can choose representatives.
links: said they were hopeful young voters would be allowed to participate at the next general election

items.h: Do you use art-based or creative participation methods? INSPIRE want to hear from you
items.b: Are you a democratic practitioner/scholar? INSPIRE (Intersectional Space of Participation: Inclusive, Resilient, Embedded) is a new Horizon Europe-funded project starting in April 2024 that aims to strengthen intersectional inclusion within participatory deliberative processes. They are seeking information on processes involving art-based or creative methods. If you use such methods or know processes that do — Get in touch via this form .
items.note: A research project's call for information/participants is sector logistics rather than a new means of participation being created.

items.h: Labour for a New Democracy discuss electoral reform with Andy Burnham
items.b: Labour for a New Democracy teamed up with Politics for the Many earlier this week to discuss the development of the campaign for proportional representation and the opportunities the change of government brings. Long standing supporter of democratic reform, Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham, was also on hand to discuss the next steps for electoral reform — check out what they had to say .
items.why: The discussion concerns proportional representation, a change to the electoral system determining how votes translate into seats.
links: check out what they had to say

items.h: Criminal Justice Alliance welcomes new chair, join the Race Equality Expert Group
items.b: The Criminal Justice Alliance is a network of 170 organisations working towards a fair and effective criminal justice system, this week they welcome their new Chair of Trustees Dr Gemma Birkett . Join Gemma for CJA’s Time for Change report launch next Tuesday — Register now . Recent consultations with CJA members highlighted a steep decline in race equality progress within the criminal justice system — in a bid to reverse this decline they formed the Race Equality Expert Members Group, if you or a colleague is interesting in joining, please email CJA Policy Manager, Mark Blake: mark.blake@crim…
items.note: New chair appointment and group membership call is organisational admin, not a change to what people can do.
links: Chair of Trustees Dr Gemma Birkett

items.h: Lord Rennard raises need for fundamental root and branch democracy reform
items.b: Writing in the Byline Times this week, member of the Democracy Network, Lord Chris Rennard argues for the Labour Government to scrap and replace new voter ID rules , restore and strengthen the independence of the Electoral Commission once again, review the proposals of the Committee on Standards in Public Life and work to ensure effective civic education for young people.
items.why: The op-ed calls for reversing voter ID restrictions and restoring Electoral Commission independence, both directly shaping electoral integrity and access.
items.note: Spans several reform proposals; primary beat chosen as electoral administration and franchise mechanics dominate.
links: Committee on Standards in Public Life

items.h: Proposals in King’s Speech must amount to ‘devolution’, not ‘delegation’, says SOLACE
items.b: Matt Prosser, president of the Society of Local Authority Chief Executives and Senior Managers (SOLACE), praised proposals in the King’s Speech to strengthen devolved decision making. They cautioned however that councils must not be ‘put on the hook for delivery, whilst left outside of the room on strategy’, and called for the reintroduction of a robust standards system for local government to strengthen local democracy.
items.why: The story concerns the structure and powers of devolved local government decision-making versus central delegation.
items.note: Local/regional government structure and powers are filed under elections & decision making per boundary rules.
links: Society of Local Authority Chief Executives and Senior Managers

items.h: The Yorkshire Society host forum on the future governance of Yorkshire
items.b: Simon Duffy of Citizens’ Network highlights the upcoming public discussion hosted by the Yorkshire Society as part of their Big Yorkshire Conversation project , an open forum on the options for the future governance of Yorkshire. Check it out .
items.why: This matters democratically because it concerns public deliberation on the future structure of regional and local government in Yorkshire.
items.note: Deliberative forums on regional governance structure fall under elections & decision making, not participation, per boundary rule.

items.h: Just Stop Oil activists handed down extensive 4–5 year prison sentences
items.b: Last Thursday at Southwark Crown Court in central London, Judge Hehir handed down 4–5 year prison sentences to the five Just Stop Oil activists charged with conspiracy to cause a public nuisance , marking the most punitive sentences for nonviolent political protest in modern British political history. They will join Amy Pritchard who was sentenced in June to 10 months in prison for breaking a window of the world’s largest fossil fuel funder, JP Morgan. Sir David King, the government’s former Chief Scientific Adviser, said: “This is so disgraceful. We are all hoping that the change in UK Govt w…
items.why: This matters democratically because unusually severe prison sentences for nonviolent political protest raise concerns about state coercion restricting the space for civic dissent.
items.note: Focus is on state restriction of protest as a civil liberty, with judicial sentencing process as secondary.
links: 4–5 year prison sentences to the five Just Stop Oil activists charged with conspiracy to cause a public nuisance
Share Just Stop Oil’s 54,000 strong petition to ‘stop jailing those telling the truth’

items.h: Extinction Rebellion’s Media Tell The Truth campaign highlights inconsistent application of justice
items.b: Judge Hehir, who presided over the Just Stop Oil sentencing last week, is the subject of this Twitter thread by XR’s Media Tell the Truth campaign — who point out the alleged inconsistent application of sentencing guidelines across the range of cases he has presided over.
items.why: This matters democratically because alleged inconsistent application of sentencing guidelines by a judge undermines predictable and equal enforcement of the law.
links: Twitter thread by XR’s Media Tell the Truth campaign

items.h: Bond publish their annual at-a-glance report on UK civic space
items.b: The new report by Bond monitors trends among protest rights, charity campaigning and public scrutiny. This report highlights increasingly strict anti-protest laws, restriction of protest defendant rights in court, charity campaign tone-policing, increased pressure on migrants’ rights campaigns, increased use of Henry VIII clauses and vetting or banning experts who are critical of government policy from public events and conferences related to the government — Explore the report .
items.why: This matters democratically because it tracks legal and institutional restrictions on protest rights, charity campaigning and civic scrutiny that affect people's ability to organise and challenge power.
items.note: Report spans protest rights and delegated-powers concerns; classified under rights/civic space as the dominant theme.

items.h: Liberty agree to adjourn court hearing against Home Secretary over anti-protest legislation
items.b: Byline Times reports that government officials are currently deciding whether to continue the appeal against the previous government’s anti-protest legislation, as a result Liberty have agreed to stay the hearing against the Home Secretary and the legislation to allow for talks to proceed. Katy Watts, lawyer at Liberty said: “We are glad the new Government are taking a moment to reconsider, as this case has immense implications for our democracy and the potential unchecked power of ministers.” See more here .
items.why: This matters democratically because a legal challenge to anti-protest legislation tests whether executive power to restrict protest is subject to judicial constraint.
items.note: Story centres on the court process and its adjournment, so filed under rule of law rather than the underlying protest right.

items.h: Defend Our Juries campaigners arrested outside Crown Court despite Trudi Warner case
items.b: Back in April a High Court judge threw out the case against Trudi Warner , a climate activist who was charged with contempt for holding a placard reminding jurors of their right to acquit based on conscience. Judge Hehir, the same as that responsible for the extensive sentencing, instructed police to arrest the 11 members of Defend Our Juries despite the actions of the High Court , labelling them ‘trouble-makers’.
items.why: This matters democratically because police arrests of protesters, despite a prior High Court ruling in their favour, raise concerns about state coercion restricting the right to protest.
links: a High Court judge threw out the case against Trudi Warner
instructed police to arrest the 11 members of Defend Our Juries despite the actions of the High Court

items.h: Full Fact calls on Labour to ‘restore trust in politics’
items.b: Full Fact is calling on Labour to improve standards across public and political life and to restore trust in politics. To do this, they’re suggesting that Labour makes the ministerial code statuary, that they improve parliamentary mechanisms to better hold MPs to account, and that they increase resources for media literacy to help the public spot misinformation more effectively.
items.why: This matters democratically because making the ministerial code statutory and strengthening parliamentary scrutiny would improve mechanisms for holding the executive and MPs to account.
links: calling on Labour to improve standards

items.h: Deteriorating state of civic freedoms signal failure of SDGs, say CIVICUS
items.b: The annual High-Level Political Forum (HLPF) to review progress on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is taking place, CIVICUS report . At the forum, states report on their implementation of the 17 goals meant to bring ‘peace and prosperity for all’. But the SDGs are badly off track, not least SDG16, which includes commitments to protecting fundamental rights — Read on . CIVICUS also calls for the new UK Government to respect civic space and reset relationships with civil society, calling this a ‘chance for change’.
items.why: This matters democratically because it documents deterioration in civic freedoms such as association, assembly and expression that underpin democratic participation.
links: calls for the new UK Government to respect civic space and reset relationships

items.h: July 4th most disproportionate election on record, say Electoral Reform Society
items.b: Electoral Reform Society has called July 4th the most disproportionate election on record after Labour won 64% of available seats on just 34% of the vote. Meanwhile, Reform UK and the Green Party — both supporters of electoral reform — won just 9 seats between them with a combined vote share of over 20% — check out below how the election results would have looked under PR . Meanwhile, Compass , Make Votes Matter and Unlock Democracy have launched a joint online petition to call for an end to the current voting system.
items.why: it concerns how proportional the electoral system is in translating votes into seats, a core measure of electoral fairness and representativeness.
links: how the election results would have looked under PR

items.h: Two thirds of public felt informed enough to make their decision on July 4th, according to Demos
items.b: Polling conducted by Demos found that 65% of the electorate felt they were informed enough to make their decision on July 4th, with 46% saying the manifestos helped them decide and 39% saying the TV debates helped. Meanwhile, a quarter of voters said they had avoided talking about politics because they didn’t feel they understood it well enough — something most acutely felt amongst Gen Z voters where the number rose to 41%.
items.why: it concerns whether voters had access to and understood the information needed to make an informed electoral choice.
items.note: Borders participation (political efficacy/discussion) but centres on the information environment around the campaign.

items.h: Voter turnout at general election was worst on record since 2001
items.b: Analysis from Vote for Policies reveals how just 51.6% of eligible voters cast their ballot on July 4th (graph below), making it the lowest turnout since 2001, and the second lowest since 1918. A new report from the Institute for Public Policy Research — Half of Us — discusses the poor voter turnout in greater depth and outlines four possible pathways for increasing participation at future elections.
items.why: low turnout affects how representative and legitimate the elected government is.
items.note: Turnout is always classed under elections & decision making per framework rule.

items.h: Glitch celebrate most black women ever elected to Parliament
items.b: July 4th marked an historic moment for UK political diversity with the election of the highest proportion of Black women ever in parliament. Seventeen Black women were elected in total across Labour, Conservative, and the Scottish Greens. Glitch celebrated the news but said they remained concerned however by the ‘lack of support, prevention and action to stop the abuse Black women candidates and MPs faced during their campaigns.’
items.why: the representativeness of who gets elected to Parliament is a core measure of democratic inclusiveness.
items.note: Concerns about abuse of candidates touch on rights & civic space as a secondary issue.

items.h: Democracy Volunteers produce final report on the 2024 General Election
items.b: Democracy Volunteers deployed more than 200 observers, experts and support staff during the election to more than 204 constituencies, attending 1,173 polling stations, observing polling venue processes and monitoring the integrity of the process, for every polling station, witnessing more than 20,289 voters. This report shares their feedback and recommendations following this work — Read the report .
items.why: independent observation of polling and election administration underpins confidence in electoral integrity.
links: Democracy Volunteers deployed more than 200 observers, experts and support staff during the election

items.h: Campaign Lab to host election results review event in London
items.b: The Election Results Review special event being organised by Campaign Lab will feature Paula Surridge, Professor of Political Sociology at the University of Bristol, and Christabel Cooper, Director of Research at Labour Together, as panel speakers. It bodes for an interesting evening — sign up now .
items.note: Event listing/sector logistics, not a democracy story in itself.

items.h: Home Secretary lambasts ‘disgraceful’ intimidation of political candidates in election
items.b: The new Home Secretary, Yvette Cooper, has announced she will chair a new Defending Democracy Taskforce, in response to ‘ the growth of US-style aggressive confrontation and intimidation ’ in British politics throughout the election, highlighting the fear that such behaviours could fuel further political murders, such as those of MPs Jo Cox and Sir David Amess in 2016 and 2021. The Democracy Network’s Power & Voice Lead Helen Wishart also highlighted the discrimination and attacks on minoritised candidates during the election period in their recent blog .
items.why: intimidation of candidates threatens the security and fairness of electoral competition, undermining who is willing to stand for office.
items.note: Also touches rights & civic space via personal security and discrimination against candidates.
links: the growth of US-style aggressive confrontation and intimidation

items.h: 400,000 may have been prevented from voting, according to poll
items.b: A survey by More in Common found that 3.2% of voters were turned away at least once from a polling station on July 4th for lacking an appropriate ID, with minority ethnic groups more than twice as likely to have been affected. Reflected across the UK, that would mean 850,000 had been turned away at some point, with large numbers reporting they did not return to try again.
items.why: voter ID requirements affect people's practical ability to exercise their right to vote, particularly among minority groups.

items.h: Association of Electoral Administrators welcomes plans to strengthen integrity of elections
items.b: The King announced new measures in their parliamentary address to ‘strengthen the integrity of elections and encourage wide participation in the democratic process’. Chief Executive of the Association of Electoral Administrators , Peter Stanyon, said members looked forward to hearing concrete details of the plans but cautioned that any changes must be taken well in advance of the next election to avoid confusion.
items.why: This matters democratically because changes to electoral law and administration directly affect the integrity, accessibility and trustworthiness of the voting process.
links: members looked forward to hearing concrete details of the plans

items.h: Reform UK win second place in student election run by Association of Citizenship Teaching
items.b: During the General Election, the Association of Citizenship Teaching (ACT) ran a ‘Parallel Election’ in which nearly 30,000 students in schools across the country cast their vote. Labour won the election with 32.1% of the vote, whilst the Conservatives dropped to fifth place on just 8.3%. Meanwhile, Reform secured second place with 18.8%. See you next time,
items.why: This matters democratically because civic education exercises like parallel elections build young people's engagement with and understanding of democratic participation.
items.note: Treated as civic engagement/education rather than a real electoral contest.

items.h: Democracy Network Statement
items.b: The past week has seen an unprecedented wave of rioting and racist and Islamophobic violence in communities across the UK. The fear that these attacks create for Black people, People of Colour, Muslims, and asylum-seekers in the UK who are being directly targeted is not new: it builds on lifetimes of experiences of discrimination and abuse in our society. These assaults are not inevitable and do not occur in isolation: they are exacerbated by deep economic inequalities and the political weaponisation of the distress caused by these realities. The demonisation and scapegoating of racialised com…
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.why: This matters democratically because racist and Islamophobic violence undermines the equal protection and personal security that targeted communities need to participate safely in public life.

items.h: Stand Up To Racism call national demonstration against the far right this Saturday in towns and cities across the UK
items.b: Stand Up To Racism (SUTR) have called a national demonstration in every town and city across the UK this Saturday . Demonstrations include a London protest outside Reform UK’s London HQ, linking arms around Finsbury Park Mosque in London and demonstrations in York, Cardiff, Newcastle, Calderdale, Portsmouth and many more. See more information now — Help amplify the call for the National Demonstration via X .
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.why: This matters democratically because a call for mass demonstrations reflects citizens' readiness to mobilise and take part in political action.
items.note: Classified as participation because the story concerns willingness to demonstrate, not legal restriction or policing of protest.
links: called a national demonstration in every town and city across the UK this Saturday
Help amplify the call for the National Demonstration via X

items.h: Anti-fascists turn out in their thousands in opposition to the riots across England & NI, Aldershot and other areas face continued attacks
items.b: More than 10,000 anti-racists gathered to challenge the threat of the far-right in Walthamstow last night, according to the police and organisers, with thousands gathering in Brighton , Bristol , Liverpool , Peterborough , Newcastle , Northampton and right across England. Far-right unrest continues as Aldershot, Belfast , Blackpool and other areas were rocked by violence and far-right activity yesterday, with the Police Service of Northern Ireland requesting reinforcements from Great Britain to bolster its response, as Stormont is also recalled .
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.why: This matters democratically because it reports large-scale public mobilisation against far-right violence, showing citizens' readiness to take civic action, amid ongoing threats to community safety.

items.h: Black Lives Matter condemns race riots, calls for communities to come together and organise
items.b: Black Lives Matter have reacted to the race riots taking place across the UK, condemning the racist violence and highlighting the inflammatory role of politicians such as Nigel Farage MP in recent days. Black Lives Matter have shared a Telegram channel ‘Fight Fascism Callouts’ with their supporters, for latest news and updates on organising against the far-right.
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.why: This matters democratically because it reflects civil society organising and mobilisation in response to racist violence.
links: condemning the racist violence and highlighting the inflammatory role of politicians

items.h: Hope Not Hate monitoring far-right organising, launch new campaign Hold Onto Hope
items.b: Hope Not Hate are currently monitoring possible far-right targets over the next week and weekend . They have also launched a new campaign Hold Onto Hope , aiming to build a movement of hope and community action, in the wake of the racist attacks.
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.why: This matters democratically because launching a new campaign to build community action creates a new means for people to participate in civic life in response to a democratic threat.
links: currently monitoring possible far-right targets over the next week and weekend

items.h: Red Flare highlight far-right groups have access to list of immigration and asylum services
items.b: Anti-fascist research unit Red Flare have published findings that far-right Telegram channels are circulating a list of 39 immigration and asylum charities, solicitors and services , which is now circulating online through far-right and fascist organising channels. The Bureau of Investigative Journalism also noted yesterday that bomb-making instructions and calls for genocide in the UK have been circulating in these same channels , alongside calls for assassination of leading UK public figures.
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.why: This matters democratically because exposing far-right targeting of immigration and asylum services highlights threats to the personal security and operating space of civil society organisations and the communities they serve.

items.h: New Economy Organisers Network have developed a new messaging guide on far-right violence
items.b: The far-right violence messaging guide produced by New Economy Organisers Network produced in partnership with the Runnymede Trust covers messaging framing principles, facts that tell a story, words that work, common attacks and where the public are at — Read it now .
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.why: it creates a new resource strengthening civil society organisations' capacity to communicate and campaign effectively in response to far-right violence.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building for civic organising rather than a media/information story.

items.h: Migrants’ Rights Network hosting safeguarding and collective care forum
items.b: In light of attacks on Muslims, migrants and refugees, and racialised people, Migrants’ Rights Network is offering to facilitate a space to discuss a safeguarding and collective care response, on the following dates:

In addition, MRN invite attendees to share best practices on protecting staff and service users both in the immediate future and going forward.
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.note: Continuation of internal support call, not a democracy mechanism.

items.h: Green & Black Cross publish master thread of Know Your Rights information
items.b: Green & Black Cross (GBC) have re-shared their 5 key messages megathread on attending demonstrations safely — see their Know Your Rights advice . GBC are the primary organisation organising Legal Observers for protest and actions — find out more about how you can train and volunteer as a Legal Observer .

items.why: it equips people with legal knowledge and observer support needed to safely exercise their right to protest.

items.h: Tell MAMA — an independent and confidential support service for those who face anti-Muslim hatred
items.b: Tell MAMA — Measuring Anti-Muslim Attacks , support victims of anti-Muslim hate in the UK through their case workers and support teams. Please amplify the work of Tell MAMA now, at this urgent time. Find out more information here .
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.note: Promotion of an existing victim-support service rather than a new democratic mechanism or change.

items.h: Network for Police Monitoring publish resources on staying safe during anti-fascist organising
items.b: The Network for Police Monitoring works to produce analysis and shared resources for campaigners, activists and citizens to organise successfully and resist police surveillance . Their new resource hub Netpol Solidarity provides information on being aware of police surveillance at public events and demonstrations and actions you and your group can take to limit the risks to yourself and others .
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.why: it creates a new resource hub helping campaigners resist police surveillance while exercising their right to organise and protest.

items.h: Healing Justice Ldn highlight healing and grounding resources for activists
items.b: Healing Justice Ldn have pooled several resources for aftercare and healing for activists and members of the public dealing with the impacts of the far-right attacks. You can view the resources on their website .
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.note: Aftercare/healing resources support activist wellbeing rather than creating new means of democratic participation.

items.h: Extinction Rebellion offer online de-escalation training resources
items.b: How might you de-escalate a tense situation with someone who disagrees with you but is in dialogue with you? Extinction Rebellion have experience in dealing with responses to their own demonstrations and have shared these via online videos and training resources, with dedicated de-escalation and nonviolence teams and resources rooted in Nonviolent Communication (NVC)..
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.why: This matters democratically because sharing de-escalation and nonviolence training builds activists' capacity to take part safely in protest and dialogue, a core form of democratic participation.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building resource enabling participation, per the framework's carve-out for courses/resources/tools.

items.h: More than 100 politicians, celebs, music artists, trade union leaders and anti-racists urge Unity Statement
items.b: The Unity Statement brings together national figures, from Kate Nash and Paloma Faith to Billy Bragg and Dianne Abbot, to England cricketer Azeem Rafiq and Jerry Dammer, founder of the Specials, along with trade union leaders and campaigners from across the political spectrum. Sign the national Unity Statement here .
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.note: A call-to-sign statement without a specific democratic mechanism at stake falls under excluded sector logistics.
links: Sign the national Unity Statement here

items.h: Runnymede Trust and 80+ anti-racist and migrants rights organisations request PM recalls parliament
items.b: Runnymede Trust and the signatories call on Keir Starmer to recall Parliament to address the scale of this crisis . In case you missed it, Runnymede published their ‘Creating a Crisis: Immigration, racism and the 2024 General Election’ report detailing how the mainstreaming of far-right narratives in British politics is predicated on the exclusion of people of colour and is harming UK democracy — Read the report .
items.issue: UK Democracy Network Far-Right Response, 8th August 2024
items.why: This matters democratically because recalling Parliament to address a national crisis is a core mechanism of legislative scrutiny and executive accountability.
items.note: Focus is on the parliamentary accountability mechanism, not simply a signature campaign.
links: call on Keir Starmer to recall Parliament to address the scale of this crisis
