items.h: Hope Not Hate launches their new BID-BUILDER
items.b: BID-BUILDER is a new tool developed by Hope Not Hate as part of their new Hopeful Towns project . The resource includes a range of tools, datasets, guidance and advice to support community stakeholders and local authorities in identifying and accessing funding opportunities.
items.why: this creates a new resource that helps community stakeholders and local authorities access funding and engage in local civic and economic decision-making, expanding practical means of participation.
items.note: Sector capacity-building tool counted as a participation story per guidance.

items.h: John Ellerman Foundation pen new strategy for 2025–2030
items.b: The new John Ellerman strategy involves focusing on supporting changemaking organisations with a clear understanding of their roles within existing systems / new systems, and a clear strategy on how they intend to make change — they are also opening up funding beyond their old three category limit of Arts, Social Action and the Environment. Read on for more information .
items.note: Organisational funding strategy change, not a new means of participation or democratic mechanism.
links: new John Ellerman strategy involves focusing on supporting changemaking organisations

items.h: The Democracy Network needs a host organisation — could it be you?
items.b: The Democracy Network is at a key stage in its development. We have had a lot of success over the last few years in bringing together hundreds of democracy organisations, and now we are looking to start a new exciting chapter under a new host organisation. Please do get in touch if you are interested in talking about this exciting opportunity — Deadline for expressions of interest 3rd July. See more information and view the Expression of Interest info sheet here .
links: See more information and view the Expression of Interest info sheet here

items.h: Sarah Castell steps down as CEO of Involve
items.b: Sarah Castell, CEO of Involve , stepped down this month, saying they are ‘incredibly proud’ of what has been achieved at Involve . Involve are currently considering next steps following this change in the organisation, Carly Walker-Dawson and Steph Draper have been appointed as interim Chief Executives in Sarah’s place. See here for Involve’s statement on the changes .
items.note: Organisational staffing change, not a change to democratic mechanisms.
links: ‘incredibly proud’ of what has been achieved at Involve

items.h: RECLAIM has now closed as of end of May
items.b: RECLAIM has officially shut down as of the 31st of May. The organisation which was set up to challenge inequality and champion working class voices says they are ‘incredibly proud of the work [they] have done’, promising that the spirit of RECLAIM will live on.
items.note: Organisational closure, not a democracy story per se.

items.h: Research for Action looking for contacts in Slough, Croydon and Woking areas, can you help?
items.b: Research for Action is looking to talk to people (scoping interview, off the record) about their experiences of Westminster interventions at Slough, Croydon and Woking councils. They would like to talk to councillors, officers, journalists, campaign/community groups and trade unions. Do you work in any of these places or have good contacts there? Email info@researchforaction.uk
items.note: A call for research contacts is sector logistics rather than a reported democratic change.

items.h: Our House prepping to run their first public event on 18th July
items.b: Oli House, Salma Perveen and the team at Our House are preparing for their first public event, Power to the People: Shaping a People’s Charter . The online session will introduce the project and how people can shape their budding movement by developing people’s charters in their communities. Stay tuned for more!
items.why: this matters democratically because the project is creating a new mechanism (people's charters) for communities to shape and express collective demands, expanding means of civic participation.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new means of participation.
links: Power to the People: Shaping a People’s Charter

items.h: Scottish Government apologises for treatment of GRT people
items.b: The Scottish Government has issued a formal apology to Gypsy, Roma and Traveller communities and the Scottish Parliament for its role in the Tinker Experiment and historical policies affecting those groups. The Tinker Experiment was a UK Government programme to ‘integrate’ GRT people into so-called mainstream society, between 1940–1980, by forcing their children into care. Traveller Movement celebrated the announcement — find out more about their important work .
items.why: this matters democratically because it addresses government responsibility for historical discriminatory policy against an ethnic minority group, bearing on equal protection under public power.
links: The Scottish Government has issued a formal apology to Gypsy, Roma and Traveller communities and the Scottish Parliament
find out more about their important work

items.h: Migrant Democracy Project looking for researchers
items.b: Migrant Democracy Project is looking for researchers who can help build evidence on residence-based voting rights and its practical implementation in Scotland and Wales. They are looking for practical evaluation as well as storytelling on the impact of extending the franchise on migrant voters. Ideally, we would love to work with researchers with lived experience of migration in Scotland and Wales but we are flexible!
items.note: A researcher recruitment call is sector logistics, not itself a reported change to franchise or participation.

items.h: Not1More shine a spotlight on environmental defenders and the right to protest, in Parliament next week
items.b: Not1More and Wera Hobhouse MP will be hosting an event in Parliament at 5pm 9th July presenting several years of research on environmental activists in the UK and their experiences facing violence, invasive surveillance, racism and disability discrimination at the hands of the police. The event aims to bring together Parliamentarians, activists, legal experts and those who’ve been imprisoned for taking peaceful action — to develop new connections and identify paths forward to work to restore and strengthen the right to protest in the UK. Email Fran@not1more.org to RSVP for this special event.
items.why: this matters democratically because it concerns policing, surveillance and legal treatment of protesters, bearing directly on the freedom to assemble and dissent.
items.note: Protest treated under rights/civic space as the issue is policing and state coercion, not willingness to participate.

items.h: New Campaign Lab research reveals the importance of personalised messages for campaigners
items.b: New research by Campaign Lab and Lenard Mettson of LSE looks at how campaign organisations can use personalised messages and supporter data to mobilise action and drive engagement. The research used a ‘pressure group campaigning for proportional representation’ as a case study and explored how different messages resonated better or worse with their supporters. Check out all the findings from this key piece of research: video , slides and transcript .
items.note: Research findings shared with campaigners are sector knowledge-sharing, not a new means of participation created.
links: New research by Campaign Lab and Lenard Mettson of LSE

items.h: Are you Act Build Change’s next Head of Business Operations?
items.b: Steph Wong and the team at Act Build Change are looking for a new member of their team to help transform community organising in the UK — Apply now .

items.h: New podcast: Doing Democracy Differently
items.b: Hosted by Professor Keith Hyams and Jessica Sutherland, Doing Democracy Differently launches July 4th — they’ll be talking with inspiring guests about why democracy has been slow to respond to the climate crisis, about the rise of populism, the impact of AI on democracy, and more. Check it out now and watch the trailer .
items.note: A podcast launch discussing democracy topics is sector media content, not a created mechanism for participation or accountability.

items.h: I Have A Voice run new event on Diversity in Politics
items.b: Amelia Christie and the team at I Have A Voice have teamed up with Elect Her , and speakers from Labour, the Conservatives, Liberal Democrats and the Greens, to explore careers in politics in a new event aimed at engaging 18–25 year olds on 14th July in London — Register for the event here .
items.why: the event creates a new opportunity for young people to engage with political careers and cross-party political life, expanding the pipeline of participation.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating a new avenue for civic/political engagement among young people.

items.h: UCL Policy Lab upcoming drinks on defending democracy
items.b: On 2nd July, UCL Policy Lab will be welcoming civil society practitioners to join them for an evening discussing countering authoritarian populism and defending democracy, with the Lab’s Director Marc Stears and Refugee Council CEO Enver Solomon.
items.note: A discussion drinks event is an event listing rather than a created mechanism affecting participation.

items.h: Centenary Action to host event on championing women in politics from rural areas
items.b: The upcoming event by Centenary Action , at 9–11am on the 9th July, will see a keynote from writer Lynne Franks and a cross-party panel of MPs highlighting the voices, leadership and challenges of rural women in politics in the UK. appointed four young people to their board

items.h: John Lubbock explores the history of Black History Month
items.b: John Lubbock recently met Addai Sebo, who fled Ghanaian government paramilitaries to escape to the UK in the 1980s, where he played a key role in the development of Black History Month . In the interview Addai unpacks the early development of what became Black History Month, and why October is such an important month for African societies. Read the interview here .
items.note: A historical interview about the origins of Black History Month does not engage a current UK democratic mechanism.
links: played a key role in the development of Black History Month

items.h: Talk Shop considering designs for a European Festival Democracy
items.b: The Talk Shop event will take place this autumn, stay tuned for more information. Last week Talk Shop ran an online event as part of York Festival Ideas, but experienced low participation numbers, something the festival reported more widely — Perry Walker requests any insights / ideas on drumming up interest for online events, email them here .
items.note: Discussion of low turnout at an online event and future festival planning is sector logistics rather than a democracy story.

items.h: Care Full launch provocation paper on exploring a care solidarity movement
items.b: The paper, CARE, for each other , penned by the Care Full team, explores the potential of a solidarity movement across care, what it could mean, and why we need a collective approach to care. Read the paper here .

items.h: Sutton Trust creates Opportunity Index Interactive Map
items.b: The new tool allows users to visualise access to opportunities for young people across the UK. The map is based on the Sutton Trust’s Opportunity Index , which ranks constituencies according to a range of measures, including school attainment, access to higher education, employment status and earnings of young people eligible for free school meals (FSM) at secondary school. Check it out now .
items.note: Tool visualises socio-economic opportunity rather than democratic participation or power.

items.h: Anti-arms groups claim new nuclear deterrent plans ‘undermine democracy’
items.b: The UK Government announced plans to buy 12 new tactical-nuclear capable F35A strike fighters, and the deployment of US tactical nuclear weapons, as part of a broader defence spending package as NATO countries push to re-arm amidst the growing threat of a Russian attack on the NATO military alliance and the ongoing full scale invasion of Ukraine by Russia. The Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament called for the largest protests in a generation against the plans at RAF Marham last Saturday , saying: ‘this is being done without any parliamentary debate or vote and completely undermines British democ…
items.why: campaigners argue a major defence and nuclear deployment decision was made without parliamentary debate or vote, raising questions about executive accountability to the legislature
items.note: Protest element is present but the core claim concerns bypassing parliamentary scrutiny.
links: growing threat of a Russian attack on the NATO military alliance
Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament called for the largest protests in a generation against the plans at RAF Marham last Saturday
Protesters held placards and banners at the gates of the RAF station

items.h: Petition to block Donald Trump from addressing the House of Commons gains 130,000 signatures
items.b: More than 130,000 signatures have amassed behind a petition to prevent the President of the United States from speaking in Parliament. The petition says ‘Trump’s hate fuelled rhetoric has no place in our parliament’, and argues that if Trump were to address the Commons it would be a ‘national embarrassment’.
items.why: the petition mechanism lets citizens formally register grievances and seek redress through Parliament

items.h: Demos praise ‘quiet revolution’ on devolution promised in Chancellor’s Spending Review
items.b: Demos has praised the Spending Review for ushering in radical changes to public service provision . The Chancellor promised a significant transfer of power to local communities to manage public services at a local level, something hailed by Demos as having the potential to fundamentally transform the relationship between citizen and state. And for more on the ‘devolution revolution’, The Constitution Unit is hosting a webinar to explore prospects and challenges on the 10th of July.
items.why: the story concerns a structural transfer of decision-making power to local government tiers
items.note: Devolution of powers to local government falls under decision-making machinery per framework rule.
links: praised the Spending Review for ushering in radical changes to public service provision

items.h: Government’s plan to create ‘mega-councils’ strongly rejected by councillors, poll shows
items.b: Government ministers are reportedly considering merging councils to create ‘mega-councils’ of over 500,000 people. Unlock Democracy has strongly criticised the proposals saying they are ‘the opposite of devolution’ . What’s more, of the over 800 councillors who responded to their survey, only 20% were optimistic that the Government’s proposed reforms will improve local government, and just 17% of councillors believed that a minimum of 500,000 people is the right size for local councils.
items.why: proposed council mergers change the structure and scale of local government decision-making bodies
items.note: Local government structure changes are classified under elections & decision making.
links: Unlock Democracy has strongly criticised the proposals saying they are ‘the opposite of devolution’

items.h: Climate Emergency UK launch local council climate actions scorecards
items.b: Climate Emergency UK and mySociety have launched their 2025 Council Climate Scorecards showing the progress all local councils are making around their climate goals. And as this is the second edition of Scorecards, the data allows users to compare their local councillors score to last year. They are also fundraising for the next iteration — please consider donating or sharing the crowdfunding link to your networks .
items.why: the scorecards create a public tool for holding local councils answerable for their performance on climate commitments
items.note: Treated as an accountability tool for local government rather than a climate policy story.
links: please consider donating or sharing the crowdfunding link to your networks

items.b: Council Climate Scorecards (photo credit: Climate Emergency UK)

items.h: Centre for Governance and Scrutiny look into hyperlocal governance
items.b: Centre for Governance and Scrutiny (CFGS) are talking to local and central government about how to make the processes and support for scrutiny more robust as the landscape of local democracy changed in England. If you’re interested in hyperlocal governance and how governance at a neighbourhood level is changing, get in touch with Andrew Brightwell at CFGS .
items.why: it concerns how scrutiny mechanisms hold local decision-makers accountable as governance structures below the council level evolve.
items.note: Local government scrutiny sits at the boundary of accountability and local democratic structure.
links: get in touch with Andrew Brightwell at CFGS

items.h: Just 1 in 10 trust the government to put the country first, according to extensive new polling
items.b: The latest edition of the British Social Attitudes Survey takes an in-depth look at attitudes towards democracy and shows a worrying decline in levels of satisfaction and trust in the state. Just 10% now trust the government to put the interests of the nation over their own party — a record low. Additionally, just 19% think the system of governing needs little or no improvement. Meanwhile, the appetite for electoral reform has reached an all time high, with 60% saying they want to change the system compared to 36% that want to keep it the same. Check out all the findings from this key report o…
items.why: it reports new evidence on public trust and confidence in government, and shifting public appetite for changing the electoral system.

items.h: Scottish Parliament votes to embed deliberative democracy in its work
items.b: The Scottish Parliament has voted to support the Citizen Participation and Public Petitions Committee’s blueprint recommendations to embed deliberative democracy in its work. The blueprint lays out plans for the creation of four ‘People’s Panels’ at the next parliament session which will be guided by collaboratively developed processes. Demos ’ Polly Curtis has praised the result as a ‘significant step forward in democratic innovation.’
items.why: a parliament formally adopting deliberative democracy structures like People's Panels changes how binding collective decisions are shaped.
items.note: Deliberative democracy is anchored to elections & decision making per framework rules.

items.h: UK Government postpones new parliamentary session to next May
items.b: Insiders claim the delays are due to key planks of Labour legislation being held up by ‘difficult’ members of the House of Lords, due to the proposed reform of the upper house. The hereditary bill, which will remove peers who inherited their position, is currently making its way through parliament.
items.why: the scheduling and delay of a parliamentary session, tied to contested House of Lords reform, affects Parliament's capacity to scrutinise and legislate.
links: delays are due to key planks of Labour legislation being held up

items.h: Commission on Political Power publishes briefing paper on Cabinet Reform
items.b: In a recently published options paper, The Commission on Political Power has laid out six changes to the Cabinet to make it fit for a 21st Century democracy. These include; making the role and decision making responsibilities of the Cabinet more clearly defined, addressing the problem of leaks, improving overall transparency, and more.
items.why: proposals to clarify Cabinet decision-making powers and reduce leaks bear directly on executive accountability and transparency.

items.h: Politics for the Many sets out the trade union case for democratic reform
items.b: With support for proportional representation growing amongst the trade union movement in recent years, a new report from Politics for the Many sets out why a rewiring of our voting system is key to building a just society and a democratic economy. Currently the trade unions with a policy supporting proportional representation are; ASLEF, BFAWU, FBU, Musicians Union, PCS, Prospect, UCU, Unison, Unite, USDAW, TSSA.
items.why: it advocates changing the electoral system, which determines how votes translate into representation.

items.h: Climate Outreach new report — 14 case studies of public engagement on climate change
items.b: The new report by Climate Outreach outlines 14 inspirational examples demonstrating the power of public engagement. Download the report .
items.note: Generic climate public-engagement case studies do not identify a specific democratic mechanism at issue.

items.h: Government to launch steering group to improve the representation of disabled people
items.b: ElectHer and their partner organisations are celebrating a major campaign win, the government has announced they will be launching a new steering group to champion disabled people in elected office. The steering group will rely on those with lived experience to guide a set of recommendations on how they can level the playing field and improve representation across the UK.
items.why: a new government steering group aimed at improving disabled people's representation in elected office affects the representativeness of elected institutions.

items.h: APPG for Fair Elections say public support for electoral reform at all time high
items.b: 60% of people now support a change to the electoral system, according to the APPG for Fair Elections . In recent years support for reform has surged from around 25–35% to 60%.
items.why: public support for changing the electoral system reflects citizens' assessment of how competitive and representative UK elections are
links: according to the APPG for Fair Elections

items.h: Make Votes Matter to hold rally for Proportional Representation on July 5th
items.b: People will be taking to the streets on July 5th as part of the Democracy Action Weekend coordinated by Make Voters Matter . To commemorate the anniversary of ‘the most disproportionate election in history’, the organisation is hoping to gather 100,000 on the streets across the UK to demand real change to our democracy. Find out about an event in your area and get involved .
items.why: people's readiness to demonstrate for electoral reform reflects willingness to take part in political life
items.note: Protest coverage is filed under participation because the story is about willingness to demonstrate, not policing or restriction.

items.h: 1,000 people put their name forward to participate in first ever ‘House of the People’
items.b: The lottery has now closed for participation in the country’s first ever ‘ House of the People ’, with more than 1,000 people signing up from all over the UK. On July 20–22, 100 of them will gather in London to listen, deliberate, and write the People’s Charter — a mandate for action across the UK to tackle the interwoven crises that are affecting all of us. If you want to help support the organisation of this important event, there are plenty of opportunities to volunteer .
items.why: a citizens' deliberative assembly is part of the machinery of collective decision-making beyond elections
items.note: Deliberative processes are filed under elections & decision making per framework rule, not participation.

items.h: Compassion in Politics joins calls to introduce Automatic Voter Registration
items.b: Calls for the Government to introduce Automatic Voter Registration (AVR) are on the rise, and now Compassion in Politics has added the name to the list of organisations calling for the change. They say that AVR could be crucial to supporting young renters, ethnic minority communities, disabled people and others who are disproportionately missing from the register today. Take their survey to let them know if you agree.
items.why: automatic voter registration affects who is able to exercise the franchise and vote

items.h: 250,000 sign petition calling for House of Lords Reform
items.b: A petition from The Electoral Reform Society calling for a smaller, elected second chamber has amassed over a quarter of a million signatures! They are aiming for 275,000 at least — so spread the word and share the petition.
items.why: making the second chamber smaller and elected changes how legislative power is authorised and held accountable
items.note: Election of the second chamber is treated as elections & decision making since it concerns making the body elected.

items.h: Unlock Democracy to launch new campaign looking beyond ending Hereditary Peers
items.b: The new campaign by Unlock Democracy aims to encourage peers to back wider reforms on the House of Lords, not just the removal of Hereditary Peers — would your organisation be interested in joining or partnering on the campaign? If so, email Tom Brake .
items.why: reforming the composition and functioning of the House of Lords affects checks and balances within Parliament
items.note: Filed under government & accountability since the campaign concerns broader legislative reform, not just making the chamber elected.

items.h: Demos launches the Epistemic Security Network
items.b: Demos has launched the Epistemic Security Network — a new initiative to protect democracy by strengthening our information supply chains, supported by regular cross-spectrum events, targeted policy proposals, and a weekly newsletter sharing the latest research and insights. To get involved, contact network lead hannah.perry@demos.co.uk.
items.why: strengthening information supply chains against disinformation affects the public's ability to obtain meaningful information about public affairs

items.h: Survey of UK independent news providers finds significant audience growth
items.b: The Public Interest News Foundation has crunched the numbers from their fifth annual survey of independent UK news providers. They find that indy news providers experienced a significant increase in news traffic and email subscriptions with the average outlet attracting over 489,000 unique visitors in 2024, and nearly 4,000 email subscribers. This suggests that most people in the UK now get at least some news from independent providers — you can see this news picture via their local news map .
items.why: growth in independent news providers affects media plurality and the public's access to varied political information

items.h: Voice of the Listener and Viewer takes aim at politicians presenting news shows
items.b: Pip Eldridge of Voice of the Listener and Viewer is submitting a response to Ofcom’s consultation on politicians presenting news and current affair programmes . They welcome other organisations to join them, copy and paste the submission and submit their own.
items.why: who is permitted to present news programmes bears on the plurality and independence of the information environment citizens rely on for political judgement
items.note: a regulatory consultation response about broadcast content, not sector logistics alone
links: Voice of the Listener and Viewer
response to Ofcom’s consultation on politicians presenting news and current affair programmes

items.h: Traditional media continues to lose ground to social media, says new report
items.b: The Reuters Institute has published their 2025 Digital News Report which shows traditional media platforms are struggling to maintain readership levels in the face of increasingly popular online platforms — specifically video channels such as The Joe Rogan Experience, as well as other YouTubers and Tik Tok channels.
items.why: shifts in where citizens get news affect the plurality and reliability of the information environment underpinning political debate

items.h: UK journalists face growing personal threats and say media freedom is at risk
items.b: The Reuters Institute has published a new report exploring UK journalism in the 2020s. The report is built on a survey of 1,130 journalists and finds that 48% of those surveyed think truth is shaped by power, whilst 43% said the UK news ecosystem has ‘some’, ‘little’ or ‘no media freedom at all’. Meanwhile just 18% of journalists said they have never experienced safety threats through their work. Check out all the findings from this extensive report .
items.why: threats to journalists and perceived erosion of media freedom directly affect the public's ability to obtain plural, meaningful information about public affairs

items.h: Media Reform Coalition report highlights significant corporate ownership of UK media
items.b: The Media Reform Coalition has released their latest annual report — Who Owns The UK Media — which looks at the concentration of news ownership in the UK. They find that just three companies — DMG Media, News UK and Reach — control 90% of UK national newspaper circulation, a 20% increase in market concentration since 2014. A similar story plays at a local level where two companies own 51% of the UK’s 882 local titles. They also find significant market control of the online platforms used to access news, as 7 of the top 15 platforms are owned by Meta, Google and X Corp.
items.why: concentrated ownership of news outlets and platforms narrows the plurality of political viewpoints citizens can access

items.h: Public Interest News Foundation petition urges Government to support regeneration of local journalism
items.b: PINF has launched a new petition calling on the government to support local journalism by backing six key measures. These include a £15m Local News Stimulation Fund, incentives for philanthropists to support local news, a new deal for local news providers to level the playing field with big tech, and more. Sign the petition to build awareness behind this key issue!
items.why: the sustainability of local journalism affects whether citizens can access meaningful information about local public affairs
items.note: framed as a petition/call to sign but substantively about local media plurality
links: new petition calling on the government to support local journalism

items.h: Index on Censorship launch ‘Am I facing a SLAPP’ tool to help journalists
items.b: Strategic lawsuits against public participation (SLAPPs) continue to plague public interest journalism, shutting down investigations and intimidating journalists. Index on Censorship has campaigned for government legislation to prevent this abuse and has recently created a tool to allow journalists to better understand whether they might be facing a SLAPP by answering their questionnaire .
items.why: a tool helping journalists identify SLAPPs strengthens their capacity to pursue public-interest reporting without unaccountable legal intimidation
items.note: sector capacity-building tool creating new means for journalists to protect public-interest reporting
links: created a tool to allow journalists to better understand whether they might be facing a SLAPP by answering their questionnaire

items.h: Society of Editors urge government not to de-fund media and journalism courses
items.b: The Society of Editors has written to the Education Secretary to oppose new guidance instructing the Office for Students to shift funding away from media and journalism courses toward STEM subjects, warning it will disproportionately harm disadvantaged students. They argue the move threatens diversity in journalism and contradicts the government’s stated support for the industry.
items.why: defunding journalism training could narrow the diversity and supply of future journalists who sustain plural public debate

items.h: Liberty defeats Government over ‘serious disruption’ legislation
items.b: Another major victory for campaigners as the government has dropped its defence of parts of the 2023 Public Order Act , potentially allowing activists convicted under the anti-protest legislation to have their convictions overturned. Human rights group Liberty had challenged the law, which allowed for police to arrest protesters causing ‘more than minor’ disruption, and hailed this latest development as ‘a victory for protest rights’.
items.why: the legal boundaries of protest policing determine whether citizens can freely assemble and dissent as a check on state power
items.note: protest story concerns legal restriction and policing, placing it in rights rather than participation

items.b: Palestine Action activists damage military cargo planes at RAF Brize Norton (photo credit: Palestine Action)
items.why: This matters democratically because the incident depicted led directly to a government decision to proscribe a protest group, raising questions about the limits of lawful dissent.
items.note: Caption is contextual to the proscription story rather than a standalone claim.

items.h: Palestine Action to be listed as proscribed organisation after vandalism of RAF jets
items.b: Home Secretary Yvette Cooper has lain a statement Parliament beginning the process of banning Palestine Action, in a move the group’s solicitors say is ‘unlawful, dangerous and ill thought out’ , given the considerable levels of public support for the pro-palestinian group. Hundreds joined protests in London against the ruling. The High Court has granted an urgent hearing to Palestine Action to stop the ban taking effect, the ‘first attempt in British history to criminalise direct action, political protest, as terrorism, mimicking many authoritarian regimes around the world who have used count…
items.why: This matters democratically because the state is using counter-terrorism powers to criminalise a protest group, directly narrowing the space for lawful dissent and civic action.
items.note: Protest policed via proscription falls under rights/civic space, not participation, per the boundary rule on state coercion.
links: High Court has granted an urgent hearing to Palestine Action

items.h: European Legal Support Centre requests support for legal against again PA proscription
items.b: The European Legal Support Centre are supporting a legal action against the proscription of Palestine Action and are gathering evidence from grassroots organisations regarding concerns groups may have with the proscription of Palestine Action. If your organisation is able to support with this, contact the ELSC with the following information, which will be submitted to court: They are asking for answers to 3 questions: (1) Who are you? What is your organisation and your mandate? How many members do you have? (2) What do you do? What kind of events/actions do you do in support of Palestine? (3) …
items.why: This matters democratically because civil society groups are mobilising legal evidence to challenge a state proscription that could curtail their freedom of association and protest.

items.h: Netpol oppose the ‘Statutory Right to Protest’ under scrutiny in Crime and Policing Bill
items.b: Although a number of high profile organisations and MPs have come out in support of the amendment to Labour’s Crime and Policing Bill to introduce a ‘Statutory Right to Protest’, Netpol has urged caution. They warn that a host of anti-protest measures will remain untouched by the bill and more broadly, they reject the idea that the state should not be allowed to determine the kinds of protest it sees as deserving of protection. Explore their full reaction as this important bill makes its way through parliament.
items.why: This matters democratically because legislative debate over a statutory right to protest concerns the legal boundaries of assembly and dissent.
items.note: Protest legislation is classed under rights/civic space as it concerns legal restriction rather than willingness to participate.

items.h: Fossil fuel giants exploit loopholes to force previous government to weaken climate policies
items.b: An investigation by InfluenceMap has found that the fossil fuel industry successfully lobbied to delay UK government action on the roll-out of heat pumps, the development of ‘sustainable’ aviation fuel and the granting of new oil and gas licences. The climate-focused think tank is calling for action to address the ‘major transparency gap’ which allows government lobbying to occur with minimal public scrutiny.
items.why: This matters democratically because undisclosed corporate lobbying shaping government policy undermines transparency and accountability in public decision-making.

items.h: Roots offers Countering Disinformation Fellowship
items.b: Roots are offering an intensive one-week training, aimed at empowering organisers with the tools they need to stop disinformation at the root. Find out more .
items.why: This matters democratically because the fellowship builds capacity among organisers to counter disinformation, strengthening the integrity of public political debate.
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating new means to protect the information environment.

items.h: The Guardian launches Secure Messaging tool to promote confidential story-sharing
items.b: Described as ‘a new whistleblowing innovation’, the Guardian’s new ‘Secure Messaging’ tool allows for anyone to share information and stories with their journalists via the Guardian app . According to the newspaper, the tech behind the platform conceals the fact that any messaging is taking place as the communication is indistinguishable from data sent to and from the app by regular users of the Guardian app.
items.why: This matters democratically because the tool expands safe channels for whistleblowing and public-interest journalism, supporting a plural and accountable information environment.
items.note: Whistleblower protection overlaps with rule of law, but the story centres on journalism infrastructure.
links: Guardian’s new ‘Secure Messaging’ tool allows for anyone to share information and stories with their journalists via the Guardian app

items.h: Drop Homeland: Red Flare Launches Campaign Urging Stripe to Cut Ties with Fascist Party
items.b: Anti-fascist investigative journalist outfit Red Flare are running a campaign to get Stripe to stop hosting the British fascist party Homeland on their payments platform . Homeland is the largest fascist organisation in the UK, after splitting from the neo-nazi group Patriotic Alternative in 2023 .
items.why: This matters democratically because pressuring a payment processor to deny services to a registered political party affects that party's freedom of association and capacity to organise.
items.note: Freedom of association for a political party is classed under elections & decision making per the boundary rule.
links: splitting from the neo-nazi group Patriotic Alternative in 2023

items.h: National Union of Students convene roundtable on dangers of disinformation for young people
items.b: The National Union of Students (UK) recently hosted a roundtable conversation alongside Lord John Mann to discuss the danger of disinformation and the growing risks of political disengagement. They explored the role of online conspiracies in shaping belief systems — particularly among young people — and discussed how this leads to growing mistrust in democratic systems.
items.note: This is an event/roundtable notice rather than a reported finding, resource or change.

items.h: Investigation finds Instagram intentionally demoted pro-Palestine posts
items.b: An investigation by nonprofit newsroom ‘ The Markup ’, has analysed hundreds of screenshots, videos, accounts and posts on Instagram in response to accustations that the platform censors pro-Palestinian support . Their analysis proved as much. They’ve shown that Instagram has routinely demoted non-graphic images of war, deleted captions and hid comments without notification, as well as suppressing hashtags and limiting the ability of account holders to appeal moderating decisions.
items.why: algorithmic suppression of political speech by a major platform can distort the range of information and viewpoints people encounter about contested public issues

items.h: Headline figures in Spending Review don’t tell the full story, says Full Fact
items.b: The Chancellor’s Spending Review promised departmental budgets will grow by 2.3% a year in real terms. However, Full Fact says this figure is misleading . The increase Reeves’ is referring to accounts for changes that began in 2023/24, and Full Fact says the increase between this financial year and 2028/29 is more like 1.5%.
items.why: correcting misleading official figures protects the accuracy of the information citizens rely on to judge government spending decisions
links: Full Fact says this figure is misleading

items.h: Incelosphere has doubled in size since 2022, says Centre for Countering Digital Hate
items.b: Research by CCDH in the wake of Stephen Graham’s hugely acclaimed new drama — Adolescence — shows that the world’s largest incel forum has nearly doubled in size to 30,000 members since their ‘ Incelosphere ’ report in 2022. The research also found that the forum reacted to the programme with a surge of violent rhetoric with more than 2.7m visits in the first quarter of the year.
items.note: Growth of an online extremist forum does not itself describe a mechanism of public power or democratic contestation.

items.h: Transparency International celebrate ‘World Whistleblower Day’ with twelve inspiring stories
items.b: The 16th of June marked World Whistleblower Day. To celebrate the occasion, Transparency International outlined twelve brave cases of global whistleblowing — from exposing healthcare corruption in Hungary to leaking information about river pollution in Lebanon — which led to awareness and action. Check out these inspiring stories .
items.note: A celebratory list of past whistleblower stories reports no institutional change or accountability mechanism.

items.h: Open Rights Group hosting round table on political parties use of data
items.b: With the integrity of elections in question over a lack of transparency around how people’s data is used during canvassing operations, Open Rights Group are co-hosting a roundtable discussion on party use of data, together with the Good Law Project. If you or your organisation has a particular interest in party use of data, get in touch to join the event: james.baker@openrightsgroup.org
items.note: This is an event invitation rather than a reported finding or new resource.
links: integrity of elections in question over a lack of transparency

items.h: Global Game Jam run a game jam to level up democracy
items.b: Over the course of the next month, Global Game Jam and One World or None are running a game jam to produce new games that embody the spirit of citizens assemblies, and can inspire people about the power of working together and finding common ground. Check it out and get your game on!
items.why: creating new participatory tools that embody the spirit of collective decision-making builds people's capacity and appetite to engage in civic life
items.note: Treated as sector capacity-building creating a new means of participation rather than as an actual deliberative process.
links: Check it out and get your game on!

items.h: Games Transformed to run anti-fascist game festival this month
items.b: Games Transformed run an annual festival celebrating games and radical politics, this year’s festival on Saturday 12th July explores how communities can undertake anti-fascist organising through games. Find out more .
items.why: a festival building skills and networks for community organising expands people's practical capacity to take collective political action

items.h: AI offering promising avenues to enhance citizen engagement in African democracies
items.b: The African Elections Project details 5 key ways AI is boosting citizen engagement through AI , from AI powered democratic education chatbots, to empowering electoral transparency to scan and address electoral irregularities in real time — including valuable lessons for UK democracy organisations assessing the potential of AI in their work.
items.why: this matters democratically because AI tools that boost citizen engagement and detect electoral irregularities expand and safeguard the practical means by which people take part in and trust democratic processes, with lessons transferable to UK practice.
items.note: International comparative case offered as evidence for UK democracy organisations.
links: The African Elections Project details 5 key ways AI is boosting citizen engagement through AI

items.h: DemocracyNext explore AI & Governance in latest paper
items.b: DemocracyNext’s new paper, Five Dimension of Scaling Democratic Deliberation , explores what scaling deliberation might mean, why it’s valuable and what’s the role of AI in delivering and enabling scaled democratic engagement. Read now .
items.why: this matters democratically because it examines how deliberative processes, which are part of the machinery of collective decision-making, might be scaled using AI.
items.note: Deliberation is filed under elections & decision making per framework rule, not participation.
links: Five Dimension of Scaling Democratic Deliberation

items.h: Poland’s presidential election campaigns faced unprecedented Russian interference, officials say
items.b: Lidia Kurasinska writing for Forbes, reports unprecedented large-scale Russian interference during its recent presidential election , with coordinated efforts by Russia and Belarus to spread disinformation, undermine public trust, and influence political outcomes in a democratic state, according to Polish Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski. He also noted that Russian military intelligence activity in Poland had doubled compared to the previous year. Poland’s Research and Academic Computer Network identified over 10,000 social media accounts disseminating disinformation aimed at swayi…
items.sec: And now for something completely different …
items.why: this matters democratically because foreign disinformation operations targeting an election corrupt the information environment voters rely on and threaten the integrity of the electoral contest itself.
items.note: Comparative international evidence bearing on the UK's own exposure to foreign election interference.
links: unprecedented large-scale Russian interference during its recent presidential election

items.h: Did you know there is a Democracy Network Boardgames Club?
items.b: Run by Patti Garcia and Jon Pritchard, the group meets regularly in London and the South East of England. Join the WhatsApp Group today and get playing democracy-inspired boardgames! See you next time,
items.sec: And now for something completely different …
items.note: Sector social/networking notice, not a mechanism of democratic participation.
links: Join the WhatsApp Group today and get playing democracy-inspired boardgames!

items.b: Blagrave Trust’s Challenge and Change Fund is back! The C&C Fund exists to support 30 young changemakers with direct lived experience of issues they are working to address — and to move power away from adult-led initiatives that end up speaking for and controlling young people’s ideas. Applications open soon .
items.note: Funding call announcement, sector logistics rather than a new means of participation being created.

items.h: Joseph Rowntree Charitable Trust next grant round deadline — 1st September
items.b: Katherine Knox at Joseph Rowntree Charitable Trust (JRCT) has written in to announce the next grant round deadline of 1st September — new applicants will need to register by Mon 18th August in order to apply. Find out more information here .
items.note: Grant round deadline notice, sector logistics.

items.h: JRSST-CT seeking new Chair & Trustee
items.b: JRSST-CT is an independent democracy focused grant making charity connected to the Joseph Rowntree Reform Trust. The fund supports inclusive political participation, civic education and reform, with a strong focus on those most excluded from democratic power, such as young people, migrants, renters and people from minoritised backgrounds. The fund is looking for a new Chair and Trustee . For more information see the job listings here — deadline 26th August.
items.note: Trustee recruitment notice, organisational admin not a democracy story.

items.b: The Civic Power Fund is recruiting an honorary treasurer to join their Board of Trustees. Find out more info and apply here .
items.note: Treasurer recruitment notice, organisational admin not a democracy story.

items.h: Two new groups to join Paul Hamlyn’s Youth Strategic Investment Fund
items.b: GirlDreamer and My Life My Say will join Paul Hamlyn Foundation’s Youth Strategic Investment Fund . These grants contribute £550,000 towards an organisation’s core costs, in addition to a package of expert support worth £175,000.
items.note: Grant funding to organisations is organisational news, not a new participation mechanism.

items.h: Welsh Government publishes evaluation of their recent Democratic Engagement Grant
items.b: The Welsh Government have also published their evaluation of the Democratic Engagement Grant here .
items.note: Publication of an evaluation report is sector admin, not a reported change to participation mechanisms.

items.h: UK Government announces 16 and 17 year olds to be able to vote at next election
items.b: In a major announcement, Rushanara Ali MP as the Minister for Democracy, has announced 16 and 17 year olds are to be given the right to vote through new election reforms . Harriet Andrews, Director at The Politics Project signalled that with this announcement ‘there’s real optimism that support for educators, practitioners and young people to ensure they have a meaningful vote and voice is finally on the horizon’.
items.why: expanding the franchise to 16 and 17 year olds directly changes who can choose representatives through elections.
links: 16 and 17 year olds are to be given the right to vote through new election reforms

items.h: Supplementary Vote to be restored, UK Government announces
items.b: The UK Government is to restore the Supplementary Vote system and scrap First Past The Post in PCC and English mayoral elections . SV was scrapped as part of the 2022 Elections Bill, a move vehemently opposed by the Electoral Reform Society , Make Votes Matter and other democracy organisations.
items.why: changing the electoral system used for PCC and mayoral elections alters how votes translate into representation.
links: The UK Government is to restore the Supplementary Vote system and scrap First Past The Post in PCC and English mayoral elections

items.h: V-Dem downgrade UK from Liberal Democracy to Electoral Democracy
items.b: Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) is a large-scale global research and monitoring effort run by the V-Dem Institute out of the University of Gothenburg in Sweden, comprising more than 19 staff members, 56 specialists, 134 country coordinators and 4200+ country experts. Last month they released their latest annual report, Democracy Report 2025 — Democracy Trumped? 25 Years of Autocratisation , in which the UK has been downgraded from a ‘Liberal Democracy’ to an ‘Electoral Democracy’.
items.why: a downgrade in the liberal democracy index reflects weakened checks on the executive and constraints on power that hold government answerable.
items.note: V-Dem's liberal/electoral distinction is anchored in v2x_liberal, which maps to government accountability and rule of law rather than elections.
links: Democracy Report 2025 — Democracy Trumped? 25 Years of Autocratisation

items.h: Stop Trump Coalition prepare for 17th September mass mobilisation
items.b: President Trump is due to visit the UK for a state visit on 17th September. The Stop Trump Coalition is preparing to welcome the U.S President with a large scale protest — see here for more information .
items.why: mobilising for mass protest reflects citizens' willingness to take part in political action.
items.note: Framed as readiness to demonstrate rather than legal restriction or policing, so filed under participation not rights.

items.h: Migrant Democracy Project & Elect Her team up through Migration Exchange
items.b: Migrant Democracy Project (MDP) and Elect Her are to partner on supporting those with lived experience of migration to enter politics, build narrative power and organise their communities. Sign up here to find out more about the development of the project.
items.why: the partnership creates new pathways for migrants to enter politics and organise, expanding practical means of civic participation.

items.b: Led by Donkeys unveil giant banner opposite Labour HQ — Photo credit: Led By Donkeys, via Twitter/X

items.why: a state ban on supporting a protest organisation directly restricts freedom of association and assembly, core mechanisms for civic dissent.
items.note: Protest and assembly is classified here as it concerns legal restriction, policing and state coercion, not willingness to participate.

items.b: Politicians ignore legal advice and back motion on banned Palestine Action
items.why: elected representatives disregarding formal legal advice on a proscription decision raises questions about predictable and lawful exercise of public power.
links: Politicians ignore legal advice and back motion on banned Palestine Action

items.b: Man arrested for holding Private Eye Palestine Action cartoon
items.why: an arrest for displaying satirical political material tests the boundary of individual freedom of expression under a proscription order.
links: Man arrested for holding Private Eye Palestine Action cartoon

items.b: Defend Our Juries lead protests again the Palestine Action ban
items.why: continued protest against a proscription order exercises and tests the legal space available for assembly and dissent.

items.b: Led By Donkeys unfurl giant banner depicting Gaza suffering outside Labour HQ
items.why: a public protest action against government policy is an exercise of freedom of expression and assembly, part of the civic space in which citizens contest power.

items.why: a High Court challenge to the proscription tests whether the ban is a lawful and proportionate exercise of executive power subject to judicial scrutiny.
links: Palestine Action terror ban made UK international outlier, High Court told

items.why: judicial criticism of police enforcement of a ban concerns whether state power is being exercised predictably and lawfully.
links: Police ‘getting it wrong’ when enforcing PA terror ban, says High Court Judge

items.why: mass arrests under terrorism law for protest activity concern the scope of state coercion against freedom of assembly and expression.
links: More than 300 terror arrests over Palestine Action ban protests

items.why: this matters democratically because police use of force against a peaceful protester over a political symbol restricts the freedom of assembly and expression that citizens need to contest public power.
items.note: This is about policing and state coercion of protest, not willingness to participate, so it sits in rights not participation.
links: Armed police threaten Kent protester for holding Palestinian flag

items.b: Police Scotland charge man for wearing ‘pro-Palestine t-shirt
items.why: this matters democratically because criminal charges over political clothing signal state coercion narrowing the space for lawful political expression.
items.note: Policing and legal restriction of expression places this in rights, not participation.

items.b: UN Human Rights Commission urge UK not to misuse terrorism laws
items.why: this matters democratically because misapplication of terrorism law to political dissent risks criminalising legitimate protest and speech, curbing civic freedoms.
items.note: Bordered rule of law (predictable enforcement) but the core issue is civil liberties being curbed by new legal threats.
links: UN Human Rights Commission urge UK not to misuse terrorism laws
