items.h: Liberties report a year of transition for Europe’s civil liberties network
items.b: Published last month, Liberties ’ Annual Report 2025 records a sixth Rule of Law report covering 21 EU countries, 200 media mentions and 12 million views, plus action against Hungary’s use of biometric surveillance to identify Pride participants. The network grew to 24 organisations across 21 member states, with Ilina Neshikj taking over as Executive Director from Balázs Dénes. Read the annual report here .
items.sec: And now for something completely different …
items.note: Reads as organisational news (annual report, leadership transition, network growth) rather than a reported democratic mechanism change.

items.h: Indian “cockroach” protest archive crowdsources photography, obscuring participants
items.b: Democracy by Design is crowdsourcing a visual record of India’s massive student protests over exam paper leaks and educational equity. The platform drew together a range of media — posters, placards and photographs — with every face automatically obscured before publication. It is the work of Dr Manmohan Singh Fellows through the arts and culture wing of the All India Professionals’ Congress , part of the Indian National Congress party. India’s youth-led “cockroach” protests forced the resignation of a government minister over exam paper leaks and state violence — students now report mass arre…
items.sec: And now for something completely different …
items.why: it documents state coercion and mass arrests following protests over exam integrity, illustrating restrictions on freedom of assembly and civic space, though the case is Indian rather than UK-specific.
items.note: International material included as offbeat comparative evidence on protest rights rather than direct UK relevance.

items.h: Goodbye Politicians saw 30 strangers picked by lottery to write their state’s pandemic policy
items.b: Goodbye Politicians Hello Democracy follows 30 Michigan residents, drawn by lottery from across the political spectrum, who met online for six weeks in 2020 to write pandemic policy for their state — no script, no actors and all filmed in their own homes. They sent 12 recommendations to Michigan politicians at every level and got one reply — a standard reply email. The nonpartisan nonprofit OF BY FOR put the 76 minute film online free on 4 July. Watch it here .
items.sec: And now for something completely different …
items.why: it documents a lottery-selected citizens' deliberative process producing policy recommendations, a form of decision-making machinery beyond elections.
items.note: Deliberative/citizens' assembly processes are classified under elections & decision making per framework rule, not participation.

items.h: NED board heads to Ukraine, reports on ‘extraordinary’ democratic resilience
items.b: A board delegation from the National Endowment for Democracy , a US pro-democracy grant maker, travelled to Kyiv, Lviv, Zhytomyr, Bucha and Rivne in June, meeting 32 partners alongside the Office of the President, the Verkhovna Rada and the Central Election Commission, to see how Ukrainian civil society and democratic resilience is holding together despite Russia’s continued aggression. Summarising their time in the country, they remark that the visit served as a powerful reminder that democracy endures not because it is inevitable, but because people choose to defend it. Read about the visit …
items.sec: And now for something completely different …
items.note: A descriptive account of an NGO board's travel and reflections without a specific reportable mechanism or change to democratic practice.

items.h: Generation Rent: Reforms to register more renters to vote
items.b: £39,159 over one year to maximise the potential of the Elections Bill and other government activity to increase voter registration rates among private renters.
items.why: this matters democratically because increasing voter registration among private renters directly affects who can exercise the franchise and take part in elections.
items.note: Turnout and registration mechanics are always classified under elections per the standing rule.

items.h: Politics Project: Votes at 16 Youth Strategy Day
items.b: £9,985 to coordinate an in-person youth day for young people across the UK campaigning for Votes at 16, and to support a parliamentary roundtable for young campaigners and MPs in parliament.
items.why: this matters democratically because campaigning to extend the franchise to 16-year-olds concerns who is entitled to vote.
items.note: Votes at 16 is a suffrage question, filed under elections rather than participation.

items.h: Joseph Rowntree Reform Trust publish new strategy and funding guide
items.b: JRRT has launched a new strategic plan focused on confronting the erosion of trust, political inequality, and systemic threats like disinformation and the influence of monied interests in UK democracy. The strategy prioritises institutional resilience, protest and expression rights, electoral reform, and measures to rebalance power — particularly for underrepresented groups. Over the 2025–2029 period, JRRT plans to redirect grantmaking toward these core democracy-strengthening goals while closing marginal programmes and refocusing on transparency, long-term funding, and intersectional racial j…
items.note: This is a funder's own strategic plan and funding guide, which counts as organisational news rather than a change in what people can do.

items.h: New Democracy Minister — Samatha Dixon MP
items.b: Democracy has officially joined the list of things the government thinks are a health and safety hazard. The UK Government last month appointed Samatha Dixon MP as the new Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Building Safety, Fire and Democracy.
items.why: this matters democratically because it identifies who in government holds ministerial responsibility for democracy policy, a matter of executive accountability.

items.h: Elon Musk tells protests to ‘fight back or die’ at UK’s largest far-right rally in decades
items.b: More than 110,000 people took to the streets of London last month for the ‘Unite the Kingdom’ march organised by far right activist Tommy Robinson. Attendees were addressed by a number of far-right speakers including; Robinson, Katie Hopkins, Lawrence Fox, Ben Habib (leader of the new Advance UK party), Ant Middleton, and Elon Musk, who joined via video link to tell attendees that ‘violence is coming to you. You either fight back or you die, that’s the truth’.. Labour initially drew strong criticism for failing to condemn the march after Peter Kyle said the march was proof that ‘free speech, f…
items.why: this matters democratically because it concerns the policing and political framing of a mass protest, incitement to violence, and government response to far-right mobilisation affecting civic space.
items.note: Classified under rights and civic space because the story centres on protest, coercion and the state's response rather than willingness to participate.
